This film will make a believer out of most people that go to watch it, and leave them wanting more like myself. I'm going tonight to see it for the second time, and let me tell you it won't be the last time. This is a true heavy weight in the long history of great films, and will go down as one of the biggest epics in movie history. I can't say enough about this movie but 10, 10, 10. A total perfect 10.

title: THE Best movie I've EVER seen! An exquisite masterpiece of art!
review:
Everything about this movie deserves the highest of praise. Being a consummate movie lover AND a fan of Tolkien's work, I truly believe this picture could not have been made better. It has a lyrical quality to it that surpasses most other fantasy films and is easily the most enchanting movie I've seen.

I just saw it for the third time and it was still every bit as captivating, from the poetic black-screen opening to the open-ended finale, setting up the next picture. This film has so much to teach us about ourselves and yet can simply be enjoyed for it's own sake as a well made piece of art.

Indeed, all the choices that director Peter Jackson had to contend with and the pressures that he was under to be true to the story give me a greater respect and appreciation for the filmmaking process and especially his masterful interpretation of the story, which so closely hit the mark for me it was uncanny.

The acting was magnificent, the musical score perfect, the choice of dialogue most appropriate, the cinematography beautiful...from one who has seen many, many movies, I recommend this above all others.

title: Ehhh - really, really good, basically.
review:
I'm one of the ones who really liked the film a whole load of much.

I'm resorting to the 'list of main reasons for liking it' format to avoid being tedious after all that's already been said.

1. The way in which the ring itself became the central bad guy through very imaginative filming and screen writing.

2. The savvy and sheer dynamism of aforementioned screen writing.

3. The degree of affection portrayed between the central characters.

4. The black riders scary-factor.

5. ALL of the touching/disturbing scene between Frodo and Bilbo in Rivendell.

6. Elijah Wood's performance from happy-go-hobbit to brave, tortured soul.

7.Ian McKellen's Gandalf, particularly the 'YOU SHALL NOT PASS' surely-soon-to-be-legendary cinema moment.

8. Arwen's enlarged role - a brave choice and a good one.

9. New Zealand.

10. Weeping hobbits newly emerged from Moria.

11. Sean Bean's heartbreaking, hugely sympathetic performance as Boromir.

12. Lots of other stuff.

As I said, I'm one of the ones who really liked this film a whole load of much.

title: This one has it all...
review:
...a great story, well-acted, and visually stunning in both location scenery and effects.

I was at first afraid the screenplay couldn't possibly measure up to the book, but my fears were unfounded. Very few liberties were taken with the story as told by Tolkien, and those lend themselves well to the screen.

Don't miss this one.

title: Breathtaking
review:
Die hard fans of the Tolkien books have torn apart this movie. All the comments are the same: DISGRACE TO TOLKIEN!!!, or NEVER HOW IT SHOULD'VE BEEN MADE!!! Please, stop!!!!! I've read the books many times, and sure, there are differences, but a movie that completely copies the reading material will utterly bore people to death. This was the best movie of 2001 and one of my all-time favorite adventure movies. And I don't care what anyone says, Peter Jackson captures the essence of the book better than anyone else could've ever dreamed. Nit-picky fans: YOU try to make a movie with more passion, excitement, adventure, and feeling! You know, I respect fans that don't think it fit with their vision of Middle-Earth, but come on!!! IT'S SO WRONG TO COMPARE A MOVIE TO THE BOOK IT'S BASED ON!!! Judge the movie on it's own!!! Oh well, people hating the movie based on book comparisons are at least better than when people complain: "That ending was so abrupt!" That annoys me to no end more than anything else.

Final Note: Anyone that would rather enjoy a movie for what it is on its own than nit-pick it to death for its differences to a book will love this brilliant movie. 10/10

title: Epic beyond belief
review: There's no other way to describe this film than utterly epic. It grabs you with a tense opening sequence and doesn't let go until nearly 3 hours later at the end, leaving you only wanting more. I honestly could not think of a better way to spend 3 hours of my life. The characters are all developed wonderfully, the acting is top-notch, the special effects leave you in awe, and yet don't distract you from the story.  I read the trilogy many years prior to seeing the film, and only until after seeing it did I re-read the books.  The film follows the story almost perfectly with a few minor ommisions that, if included, would only prolong the film unnecessarily. I have seen it twice now, and am planning on seeing it a third time, before it's gone from theaters.

title: The Greatest Film of the last 20 years
review:
Truly, Peter Jackson and crew have created in my opinion (and many others) the greatest film of the last 20 years. I believe that this film should win best picture and best director, best actor (Ian McKellan), and a sleuth of others for screenplay, score, etc. I've become somewhat of a Tolkien buff ever since I saw the trailer for the film almost 7 months ago, and when I saw the film it completely blew my mind. I was holding onto the seat the whole three hours, and the actors simply became the characters that I know and love.

The casting of Elijah Wood as Frodo was shear brilliance, even more so for Ian McKellan as Gandalf. As I said, McKellan deserves the oscar. Ian Holm was perfect as Bilbo, and Hugo Weaving was entirely believeable as Agent Smith, errr.. I mean Elrond. Cate Blanchett was foreboding as Lady Galadriel, as was Liv Tyler and Orlando Bloom. Overall the casting was excellent, and I'm glad that they did't cast and superstars like Haley Joel Osment or Brad Pitt. Imagine if George Lucas or Steven Spielberg got their over-zealous hands on this one? We would probably have gotten garbage. I'm glad that a true Tolkien fan was chosen to direct, and I must say his performance was awe-inspiring.

The scenery was magnificent, and now I've set New Zealand as my next vacation destination. Just imagine hiking through the closest thing to Middle-Earth in the world! The thought alone leaves me flabbergasted. The mines of Moria added an adreneline rush to the film, kudos to the CGI men who made it come alive. The scene where the Fellowship hears the drums and sees the fire of the Balrog almost made me die from anticipation! The Shire and it's details were also well done. An aspect of the film that many people forget (the length) is Isengard and Saruman. Christopher Lee is the most evil actor of all-time! Isengard was brilliantly done and I can't wait for the Two Towers, when the Ents smash it to kingdom come.

Although the story was slightly altered to remain politically correct and more widely appealing, it is still enjoyable to an immeasurable level. The characters of Glorfindel, Tom Bombadil, and Goldberry were left out for various reasons, but I'm hoping that they make an appearance on the DVD. The attack of the Wargs outside of Moria is also left out, as is various things from Lothlorien. Nevertheless the film remained extremely entertaining and at the same time having an air of greatness to it.

The real shame though is that the Academy probably won't give this film much regard, because of it's genre and for the most part unknown actors. Every year usually and overlong and boring film wins best picture (ie. The English Patient, Titanic, Dances With Wolves, Shakespeare in Love, etc...). I'm not saying that these films aren't good, they're just unnecessarily long or for the majority of the film quite boring. Granted FoTR is 3 hours long, but it keeps the viewer enthralled and entertained, interested and spooked, fascinated and terrified, for every minute of it. I will be extremely disappointed if this film doesn't win a substantial amount of oscars. I'll restrain from death threats if it doesn't win Best Picture (which it should), but I will be utterly enraged if it doesn't take home all of the technical categories, score, and adapted screenplay. I will punch a hole through my Sony Trinitron if I see Harry Potter or Shrek or some other stupid children's film win anything that FoTR deserved for any reason whatsoever. Thank-you for listening to my ramble, and if I may say so I will be positively beaming if in a few years I see one of those Oscar Statuates on the bottom left-hand corner of the DVD saying: "Best Picture 2001".

title: Great Movie
review:
The only reason I didn't see this movie twice was because I decided that instead, I'd rather have my second, third and fourth viewing of it all on the same day without going broke. It was a fabulous movie.

I compare it to the only other movie that came out this year that I've seen - Harry Potter. With only a week in between the time I saw each, I felt after Lord of the Rings, Harry Potter was a rip off.

My Dad was telling me a few days before I saw it that I should read the book while my friends were saying that a) The book ruined it and b) there were two many omissions. I didn't hear a word either group said- if Harry Potter gave me anything, it was a lesson, read the book afterwards. That is what seperated me from my friends.

Unfortunately, every rating service in this world has an annoying cap of giving a movie 100% (which translates into 10/10 or 5/5 or whatever). Personally, I have found there are several movies where the mark it deserves is above that limit. Lord of the Rings is not just one of those movies, but serpasses them all. If the world was my way, Lord of the Rings would get 35/10. I don't know, that may be a bit low.

Now to find out how badly it mutilated the books - I am going to read them.

title: Absolutely Amazing
review: The Lord of Rings was perhaps the most pleasurable movie-going experience of my life.  Having read the book before seeing the movie, I had great appreciation  for the story, and had been awaiting the movie with bated breath for months before its release.  It did not disappoint.  The movie captured almost every aspect of the book, save a few minor details not relative to the main plot, and the beautiful scenes of the shire, and Rivendell, and Amon Hen, combined with the emotionally stirring soundtrack, came together so marvelously to create my new favorite film. Kudos to Peter Jackson. I can't wait for Two Towers.

title: Special effects are really sensational with the story to boot...
review:
An outstanding movie, an outstanding piece of work. My wife and I started reading the book before the movie because we heard it would be a bit hard to follow. It wasn't at all. I only got through the first 2 chapters and she got close to the end before we decided to go. She wanted to refrain from reading the whole story so she would at least have a suprise ending. Just pay close attention to the story and you'll get it.

I really do believe that Ian McKellen could very well take best actor for Gandalf (At his age and for that work was just amazing) and Peter Jackson should get best director definately (to take the story of JRR Tolkein and breath life into the screen like that takes a master. . If you only see one movie, go and see "Lord of the Rings"

The only thing I disliked is that they really left you hanging in the end, but hey thats the story and there are two other movies to follow. This movie is just as worthy as status of classic as "Star Wars" Trilogy. Can't wait to see part 2!

title: This movie have met my expectations.
review: I shall say that this is a fantastically made movie. I've been studying Mr. Tolkien's writings for years. My opinion is that Tolkien had successfully accomplished his experiments with creation of myths. For those who want to start to read "The Lord of the Rings" Trilogy, I would suggest to start from "Hobbit." Of course for those who watched the "The Lord of the Rings" for many times, this movies is nothing more than a "very-cool-movie." These people must understand that Tolkien's books are highly philosophical. You ask me why? Well, I have to say one thing. Read his books more closely. I would also suggest reading the following books: BILBO'S LAST SONG; UNFINISHED TALES; THE SILMARILLION; THE HOBBIT; TOLKIEN: MASTER OF FANTASY by B. Green; MYTH MAKER: JRRT by Anne Neimark; TOLKIEN: A CRITICAL ASSESSMENT by Brian Rosebury; JRRT: THE ART OF THE MYTH-MAKER, Starmont House; ONE RING TO BIND THEM ALL: TOLKIEN'S MYTHOLOGY by Anne C. Petty.

title: That movie was the greatest!!!
review: I definitely recommend this movie to people.  You feel as if you're right there.  And, boy do I wish I was an elf.  I'd take Legolas home any day. Girls, you'll see what I'm talking about.  He is to die for.  And for you guys out there, don't worry.  There are some nice looking girls in it for you.  Enjoy the movie!!!

title: THE best fantasy movie ever made
review:
There is no doubt in my mind that Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring is the best fantasy movie ever made. Nothing else even comes close. That's sort of a left-handed compliment, considering that I can count the number of fantasy movies that I would consider good on one hand, but it's more than that. I would place LOTR: FOTR among the top science-fiction/fantasy/adventure movies ever made as well, which would include such notables as Raiders of the Lost Ark, Star Wars, Aliens et al.

The acting was incredible...Ian McKellan, Viggo Mortensen and most particularly Sean Bean simply defined their roles for a generation to come. When I read the Tolkien books from now on, I will imagine these faces attached to the names of Gandalf, Aragorn and Boromir.

The scenery was simply exquisite...if there were any way to more completely realize Middle Earth, I can't imagine it.

And I have to applaud the fine line Peter Jackson walked between being as faithful as possible to the book and making an excellent movie. This may go down as one of the best book-to-movie adaptions of all time.

title: Best movie of the year!
review: Lord Of The Rings is one of the best movies of the year and is worth watching it on the big screen....if not get a dvd if u can....trust me its the best movie u might have seen! I would give it 10 points for the best; direction, camera effects, action and all the best actors in the movie!

title: Liked it, but not according to the book
review: As a movie it goes very high on the scale, but still it could go along the story of the original a bit better. It also helped me imagine a couple of things I couldn't before. The battles are really great, the magic is all there, effects are also great. Can't beat it, great story, great movie!

title: Brilliant!
review:
When I heard about all the hype for this film, I knew I was in for something good here. My expectations were nowhere near as good as it turned out to be. The camera work was brilliant, with some spectacular views and incredible CG shots. I especially liked the scene in the cave with the collapsing steps and bridge - everything seemed so real. The acting too was brilliant, and emotions really came across effectively. Director Peter Jackson is added to my list of very worthy directors and I can't wait until the next film.

In short, if you haven't seen this, see it now!

title: Unspeakably awesome
review: You know how you read a book then go to see the movie and you're always disappointed?  Well, Lord of the Rings is the most breathtaking piece of fiction I have ever read, arguably the most breathtaking ever written. When I saw the film, I was, astonishingly, not disappointed.  I was awestruck. That anyone could take on such an ambitious project with such glorious results, especially given the material that needed to trimmed to keep it under 12 hours, is a tribute to there still being talent in the film industry. I won't go into describing the film; there are comments enough here already. I have never given a movie a vote of 10.  Until now. When i first heard of the filming of this movie i got a little worried, would the movie be able to capture the magic from the books. Even though he has made some quite good movies lately (the Frightners, Heavenly Creatures) He also has made Braindead and Bad Taste. Even though i liked those movies i didnt realy feel he was the man for the job.

(Some minor spoilers below) After have seen the movie three times i can say that my worries where uncalled for, the movie is truly a amazing epic adventure.

I will start with the actors. All main characters do a good job. Sean Been is perfect as Boromir and i like his character a lot more than the boromir from the books. Ian McKellen IS Gandalf no doubt, he was probably born for this part, at first i was dissapointed that Sean Connory didnt get the part but after having seen McKellen in action i can say that he couldnt have made a better job. Ian Holm is wounderfull as Bilbo, Viggo Mortensen is just as i have imagined Aragorn, Ellijha Wood is good but a litle too young i think. The other Hobbits where good. Legolas and Gimli where good. Sean Been and Ian McKellen both deserves an oscar for there preformance.

The scenery was truly amazing and breathtaking, New Zeeland was the perfect choice. The score is one of the best music scores i have heard, Howard Shore truly deserves an Oscar for this masterpiece.

Ok now for the spoiler parts. Some things have been changed and i really dont like all of them. The nazguls are a little too violent for my taste. The part where they without any aperent reason kills a man and when they ride down the gates of bree, i thought where a little unnececery.

The wizard battle was a lot better than i had thought, i had a nightmare scenario when Gandalf and Saruman where hurling balls of fire on each other. But i found this battle of the mind terrific.

I actually thought the Arwen thing was quite good, that glorfindel was replaced didnt matter at all for me (and it was one name less for the audience) and that arwen where there made sence. I was a little dissapointed at the ford that it where Arwen and not Gandalf and lrond that summoned the river. And the line " If you want him, come and claim him" was a little too much but otherwise i think it worked ok.

All the parts from here too lorien was wonderfull. I would have wanted more from Rivendell but hopfully we will get a lot of deleted scenes on the DVD. (Peters first cut was 4,5 hours instead of the 3 we have seen, and he has said that they will be on the DVD) Moria was absolutly breathtaking.

Lorien was the first down in the movie. Too much was cut and psycho galadriel was just silly. Please tone down the Special effects there untill the DVD if possible. The tempting of Gandalf in Bag end was much much better.

This is truly a masterpice and a modern epic, By far the best fantasy movie and this years best movie. Actully the best movie i have seen in the last years.

If this movie dont even get nominated for best picture and Ian for best actor i will lose the last respect for the Academy awards. i lost most of it when Gladiator won last year. I mean come on, it was a ok film with good fight scenes but worth best picture? No way.

This movie is the Star Wars of our generation

title: Great Movie that gets better after each viewing
review:
First off I read a comment on this movie and that person said they thought this movie didnt have an ending, yet they loved the books???!! Did that person even read the books? It had a much more abrupt ending than the movie, Hell *spoiler* Boromir didnt even die until the second book at the beginning, what kind of starting is that?

BTW I love the books and the movie because it is one long story like it is supposed to be. This is a 9 hour epic, not a trilogy like some people like to call it. The books were meant to be one story, just like the movies, cant wait for that 9-hour long DVD *starts salivating on himself*

Im sure everyone has explained why this movie is so great, so no need to copy them. It is a movie for people who can accept fantasy and enjoy it. If you dont like fantasy, dont watch the movie, and most of the people who dont like this movie are either Fantasy-haters or are too hung up on a different movie epic to give this one a chance. title: Great Movie
review: This movie is one of the greatest (if not THE greatest) fantasy movie I have ever seen.  Unlike many other movies that are based on novels, the "Fellowship of the Ring" does not distort or alter the original story. Indeed, in many places, it seems better than the original. For those of you who have not yet seen it, do so.  But if you have children that are under the age of 10, don't bring them.  Some of the scenes are incredibly intense and sometimes frightening. One of the great things about this movie is that you actually get to see the main villain, the Dark Lord Sauron.  In the books, he is simply portrayed as a malevolent presence, not an actual character.

title: Finally, a film version worthy of the "Book of the Century"!
review:
At long last we can lay Ralph Bakshi's 1978 version to rest. Here, at last, is the real film version of J.R.R. Tolkien's magnum opus, "The Lord of the Rings". I feel as though I've been amply rewarded for more than thirty years of patiently awaiting a film version I can be proud of.

I think this movie will go down with "The Wizard of Oz" as an all-time fantasy classic. Peter Jackson's skillful direction is very well complemented by brilliant performances, seamless cgi-effects, faithful attention to detail, and the excellent choice of New Zealand as a stand-in for Middle-earth. The opening installment of the Trilogy, "The Fellowship of the Ring" is as clear and brilliant as the Silmarils of Feanor. I found myself riveted to my seat for the entire length of the movie, and I was not alone in my rapture. Every other member of the theater audience was also carried away by this movie. I have no fear about the next two installments. They undoubtedly will be just as good.

There are two factors that make this movie work. First, Peter Jackson knew that he had to make a visual Lord of the Rings, so there were parts of the book that simply had to be cut to keep the audience engaged. Hence, the poetry, music, and extraneous episodes were all jettisoned. In their place, however, was a rich tapestry of sight and sound that gave even a person completely ignorant of Tolkien's work a sense of direction and purpose.

The other factor was the performances of the main characters. This was most important because otherwise we would have had another special-effects laden movie that would have been the cinematic equivalent of a slow boat to China. We find ourselves caring about the main characters in a personal way. The Quest is important, of course, but the other themes of friendship, power, bravery, and the like are manifested in different ways by the major characters, and this gives the story life that special=effects alone can never do.

I've seen the movie three times already, and wouldn't mind one or two more viewings. Of course, it goes without saying that I will get the DVD when it is released, but I am happy that finally, despite Bakshi, despite the refusal of the Tolkien estate to cooperate with Peter Jackson, Tolkien's work is finally getting the treatment it so richly deserves. The moviegoer who sees this film will be amply repaid not only with a work that will entertain him mightily, but will leave him aquiver with anticipation for the sequels.

review: This movie is excellent. Great Storyline. This movie is good for people who are either into dramas or action movies. The locations are just great and well designed. Characters are designed perfectely and the acting is at its very best. This MOVIE IS  BETTER THAN CROUCHING TIGER, HIDDEN DRAGON! LET'S PUT THOSE DULL/ROMANTIC TIGERS AND DULL DRAGONS TO SLEEP!

title: Brilliant acting and effects for one of the best books ever
review:
Going in to this film as a Tolkien purist, I had to force myself to view it as merely related to the book. In that context, I thought the film was fantastic. Sure, there was no Tom Bombadil, no Barrow-Downs, nor the Old Forest, but fortunately, there wasn't a XenArwen, either!

I thought Peter Jackson did a wonderful job of bringing the scope and sense of "epic" to Tolkien's brilliantly conceived yarn. The effects were amazing (except for the corny, video-game feeling of Legolas on the Cave Troll scene) and the acting was spot-on. In particular, Elijah Wood as Frodo and Sir Ian McKellen as Gandalf were terrific.

One thing I appreciated as a Tolkien junkie, although it appears that the Balrog has wings, one who has come down on the other side of the fence could probably still argue that they do not. I thought they were rendered as fairly insubstantial things, perhaps to make it slightly ambiguous.

All in all, a masterful film from Peter Jackson -- better even, then Heavenly Creatures.

title: Most Excellent Movie-Making AND Writing!
review: A faithful adaptation of the book and an amazing transition to the big screen.  It also has made great use of some limited creative license to capture the essence of the relationship between Aragorn and Arwen.  A most wonderful movie this is!

title: The Single Greatest Film Of All Time
review:
This film has greatness written all over it. Why it does not have a higher user rating is beyond me. C'mon everybody! Let's make it #1 again!

The film is adapted quite well from Lord of the Rings novels. It's definately a movie for someone who has read the books before, as a few key sequences were left out, but for time's sake, I'm sure (c'mon people, it's 3 hours long as it is!). However, this is not to say that a newcomer to the series cannot enjoy it. It is the most powerful film I've ever seen. I loved it from the opening sequence to the closing frames. It was well-directed (thanks to a long-time favorite director of mine, Peter Jackson), well-acted, well-written (I loved the books, and I loved the script), and incredibly well-edited. The effects are amazing. This is one of those films with justification for all the special effects, and they use them very wisely. They are not overdone in the least... they are very true to the book. And the music... wow. VERY powerful score by Howard Shore.

If you ever want to do an experiment on how a good director progresses, rent Bad Taste (Peter Jackson's first and another one of my favorites) then go see this while Bad Taste is still fresh in your mind. You won't believe your eyes. Beautiful!

I gave this a 10/10! How could I not?

title: Gets Better
review: First film I have ever watched twice. Now 3 times. Each viewing has just got more enjoyable as keep on noticing things have missed earlier. First viewing never noticed Peter Jackson, second viewing saw him. Third viewing noticed Legolas walks on top of the snow while the other wade waist deep. This is an epic movie well worth watching more than once. Will not see again at the movies but will be a DVD buyer as the extra footage will be interesting.

title: Excellent
review: The movie is my Lord of Fantasy Movies (now, obviously). It's my Lord of Movies too. If you did not read the book, read it and enjoy it. If you did not go to the movie, go and enjoy it. That's only my opinion, obviously. Galadriel's Temptation is 'my' nearly-60-seconds sequence in 'Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring'.

title: This film is like chocolate cake with extra icing... you crave the sequels.
review: "Lord of the Rings : The Fellowship of the Ring" is a roaring masterpiece. It has you sitting on the edge of your seat in suspense and laughing in the mean time. It's a wave of emotions rolled into one film. The actors in their roles are fabulous, especially Elijah Wood who does a breath taking job of portraying the character of Frodo Baggins, a small hobbit from the Shire of Middle Earth with a huge job on his hands. The film is true to Tolkien's literature and is magnificent. Everyone who sees this will never forget it. The two sequels: "The Two Towers" and "The Return of the King" are promising and if they are as good as this, we are in for a treat. Lord of the Rings deserves every bit of attention it has been getting.

title: the best movie i ever saw in the cinema
review:
well.. so i'm not usually a person to make great words about a movie. but this time i felt the urge to make an exception... even though i now talk about it in a language that is not my own.

i have seen this movie 3 times, once in german language and twice in english. (where i think the english version is quite alot better.. but maybe that's because i also have read the books only in english and not in my native language). and i still have not had enough of it. it lasts three hours, but that doesn't seem to long, since there is so much "energy" in the scenes. a fascinating story, great actors, a wonderful soundtrack, first class special effects, also to mention the great make-up and costumes - all that made this film the very best of all i have ever seen in the cinema.

i highly recommend it - if you have read the books or not, that does not matter, since the movie is a piece of art on its own.

title: Well worth waiting for!
review: I've waited for this film for 21 years, ever since I first read The Lord of the Rings. But it was well worth the wait! Okay, so it isn't exactly like the book, it's still a magical movie. It's closer to the book than I dared to expect, and the changes to the original story are understandable. After all, this is a film, not the book itself. It's a long film but it kept me in my seat till the very end, and even that came too soon for me. Absolutely magnificent, even after seeing it a couple of times. I can hardly wait for the DVD!

title: The Best Hollywood could do....
review: Fellowship of the Ring, was one of the best movies I've seen in years. There had been some complaints about how characters were changed, and/or left out.  I myself am a big Tolkien fan.  I read the book again before seeing the movie, and in the beginning I had a hard time paying attention because stuff had been changed.  But then I got my mind set and sat back to enjoy the movie.  I'm convinced that Mr. Jackson's masterpiece, was the best Hollywood could do in order to bring one of the greatest books of the 20th Century to life.  Of course he had to change it, the movie itself was 3 hrs long, imagine how much longer it would have been if everything was left in it.  It would have been six movies in stead of three.  I'm very pleased with the movie, and I can't wait for this December to see "The Two Towers".  My vote 10/10

title: simply perfect!
review: Let's talk about a masterpiece! I've already seen it three times and don't get tired of it, the more I see it the more I love it. I'm getting addict to this movie, it's turning into obsession. Pj is a real genius, he pulled the characters out of the books and put them into the movie, Sean Bean's Boromir is even better than Tolkien's one. Amazing photography, excellent screenplay. And a great cast of sublime actors (never seen so many TRUE tears on the screen before).

title: One of the Best!
review: After reading the Tolkien books for a class in school, I knew that as soon as the movie came out in theaters I would want to see it.  Since then I've gone to see the movie 'The Fellowship of the Ring' three times, and each time I consider it money well spent.  I consider this movie one of the best I've ever seen, and I would highly recommend it to anyone.  My only word of caution is that it received a PG-13 rating for a reason.  I wouldn't recommend parents take their young children to see it, as it does have a few scenes that may upset young children.  Instead I would encourage that parents allow their kids to see the children's cartoon version.

title: The best thing to happen to cinema in a long, long time
review:
To start with an interesting fact: Orlando Bloom (legolas) went to the school just down the road from me. Anyway.... This is genuinely a masterpiece of a film. I have read the lord of the rings (twice) and when i heard some of the alterations that Peter Jackson had made to the events depicted in the book i became very apprehensive, the main one was the the Arwen/Aragorn love interest theme. But after seeing the film i can safely say that the changes dont detract from the book one bit.

To start with the casting was PERFECT, i can not begin to imagine who could have played Frodo if Wood hadnt, i hadnt heard of Viggo Mortensen before LOTR and i thought casting him would be a disaster, but he pulled off one of the performances of the film. The other actors to accrue this accolade in my opinion were; Ian Mckellen - the powerful wizard Gandalf, Elijah Wood - the brave yet vulnerable hobbit and Cate Blanchett - the beautiful, immortal Galadriel. The other actors who had smaller parts but deserve a mention are; Hugo Weaving - the elf lord Elrond (when he says "the ring must be destroyed" you cannot help but think of a similar line he says in the Matrix), Ian Holm - the old but wise Bilbo (i do hope the Hobbit is made as a prequel to LOTR, he and Mclellen would be brillaint together),Astin, Boyd and Monaghan - Frodos companions were depicted brilliantly. Bloom and Rhys-Davies also give fine performances as members of the fellowship. Sean Bean was a superb choice to play Boromir. The special effects were unbelievable, the seemingly trivial matters such as making the hobbits 3 feet smaller than everyone was done seamlessly, not to mention the incredible make up used on the orcs. The battle at the beginning of the film is a fine example of how a good special effects department can add to the magic of the film. Lothlorien, the Shire and the mines of Moria were created exactly as how you would imagine them to be, absolutely perfect. I have know idea how one country could provide so much contrasting scenery, New Zealand is full of surprises, the scenery is utterly breathtaking. The music worked brilliantly with the film, im no Enya fan but its a nice song. People have complained at the length of the film, ever heard of the phrase 'time flies when your enjoying yourself' it truly applies in this case, the three hours shot by. There was so much to fit in that nothing else could have been removed from the final cut. Thats enough from me,but lastly a small prediction, after the return of the king is released the Lord Of the rings will claim its place as one of the greatest trilogies in cinema history.

title: Simply Amazing
review: See this movie...the special effects, incredible story, and terrific acting will leave you itching for more....and luckily enough you get it come December.  Ian McKellen is simply astounding...Christopher Lee's villanous Saruman absolutely DRIPS with evil...and a star is born in Viggo Mortensen.

title: Excellent
review:
I have seen this movie two times now. What has struck me the second time has been the underrating of the actors in the film. Perhaps this is most true when it comes to Sean Bean. I had seen him in one of the Sharpe episodes and Patriot Games ,but hadn't realised how good he is before this. He is an excellent actor and really needs to get a lot of credit for his portrayal of Boromir.

Despite the film striking out at the Golden Globes I have confidence that the academy will truely see this film for the masterpiece it is. And although I have a feeling that none of the actors will get recognized individually I think that part of the movie that prooves that they are all excellent was that they all handled the formulised dialogue of Tolkein without seeming silly (perhaps the best comparison would be the Star Wars movies, especially the Phantom Menace, where the stylized dialogue even gave Ewan McGregr a hard time) Perhaps that really shows the brilliance of Jackson, Walsh and Boyens for being able to take the dialogue and go beyond it.

If you haven't seen this film yet you are missing out on a truely unique and wonderful experience.

title: It was like reading the books for the first time again!
review: This film was an amazing experience. Perfectly paced, visually stunning, with changes that enhanced the story rather than taking away from it, this movie was easily the best I have ever seen. I can't wait to see it again, and I especially can't wait for the next two installments!!!

title: Brilliant
review: I think this film is a masterpiece of film making and here's why.  It was as faithful to the original story as it could given the 3-hour time constraint. In fact "faithful" is too weak a word - the film really did justice to Tolkien's world - the Orthanc scenes in particular.  As well as excellent technical qualities such as cinematography, special effects, costumes, and such the acting was for the most part excellent.  Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen, and Elijah Wood provide a strong core cast and the other players also shine, Sean Bean in particular (Orlando Bloom is very convincing as Legolas too).   Similarly the pace and tone of the movie, after the initial slow start, keep the audience's attention throughout the long running time. Somehow Peter Jackson has created a film that can render both die-hard Tolkien fans (well this one at least) and people who nothing of his work spellbound and transported to a different world.  And that's why this film is a masterpiece.

title: Excellent movie!!!!!
review: i absoulutely loved these books and the movie was soooooo enjoyable.  i was very impressed with how closely the movie was kept to the book.  the ending was shocking to see hollywood end a movie like that, but a pleasent surprise to see them stick with the story line as written by the author.  Can't wait to see the rest of the series!!!

title: A most excellent movie
review: The only Tolkien I ever read before watching this movie was The Hobbit, so I went into this movie not really knowing what to expect, which some people have told me is quite a benefit.  This was an amazing movie: the best I have seen in a long, long time, if not the best I've ever seen.  My brother and I have been into gaming and fantasy since we were around 13, so when we first heard about this movie, we made a point to go see it on opening day.  We were not dissapointed.  Anyway, I don't want to spoil it for anyone else, but this was an amazing experience.  Peter Jackson and his crew did excellent work.  10 out of 10.

title: A great experience in modern cinema
review:
Wow, I´ve read the books about 20 years ago, but now it seems like yesterday! Great stuff from good old Pete, he did a good, very good job!

It felt like reality, eons of time ago, just can´t wait for the second part!

title: The best film from a book I have ever seen.
review: I was really impressed by how they really made the book come alive in this movie. I didn't even have to be told what character was who, to know that that was who they were. And the dialog was almost perfect to what is in the book. And how they made the hobbits that small when all of them are 5'6 and all of the taller of the Fellowship are 5'11. It was just amazing how they did it. From the Fellowship to the cave troll and the orcs. They made everything look just how I had imagined it. My mother has been reading me the story from when I was in her tummy until now. And I was reading it by myself since I could read. I was really hesitant to watch this movie, because I was afraid of what was going to be done to it. I was afraid it wasn't going to be anything like the book, but I was wrong. I am really pleased at what Peter Jackson and the cast did they made all the characters come alive, from my mind.

title: Move over Skywalker, Aragorn's here!
review: Definitely a milestone for adventure/fantasy movies! How can one write about this movie? To me, it'd be like trying to sum up Egypt's history in one sentence. One can only imagine what sights we'll see in the next two years with the second and third installments of this amazing trilogy. Those who complained about this movie's slowness will be singing a different tune when they see the Ents sacking Isengard, or the utter hugeness (for lack of a better word) of the War of the Ring! Star Wars fans - move over! Star Trek fans - take a seat! There'll be no room for others when these films are complete.

title: what tremendous fun
review: the movie was a tremendous, thoughtful, and human event. i have read the trilogy many times, and listened to the recorded audio adaptations many times, and have seen the 1st installment of the trilogy 5 times and i simply can't wait for next next two films.  how could you not identify with this story, even if you've never read or heard the story before.  you have heroes great and small, and i don't mean stature.  there are so many qualities to identify with that it replays over and over in your mind. washing dishes after you've misbehaved, excellent compression, the fun loving mischief of merry and especially pippin much condensed but very effective, yes i would've liked less compression, but understand that it just wasn't practical.  thanks for taking us, or rather, bringing us middle earth.  it is a beautiful place.

title: GREATEST MOVIE EVER!
review:
wow! i am a huge fan of JRR Tolkien, and I could not wait for the movies to come out. When I first heard that Jackson was making the trilogy, I went nuts (i was one of the 100 million downloads in the first hour). if you have not seen this movie yet, i highly suggest that you do. The acting is great, the cinematography is immense, and it's well worth watching.

best movie since Citizen Kane and Saving Private Ryan (yes, quite a different variety, but those are great movies!)

title: Best Fantasy Movie of all Time
review: I've been waiting for 25 years for somebody to make this movie.  I first read the books 25 years ago and I've reread them about 15 times, I never get tired of the story.  They did a great job of bring it to the big screen and I can't wait for the other two parts

title: Wonderful
review: A wonderful adaptation of a wonderful book.  It amazes me that such a work is now possible.  Just 10 years ago, before Jurassic Park and Star Wars Episode I this movie would have been inconceivable.  This movie says to me that now all is possible.  If you can imagine it, computers can now make it real.  Think about it; any set, any special effect, any creature can now be created.  Tolkien himself sold the movie rights for a pittance in the '60s thinking that no movie adaptation would ever be possible.  He was right, until the computer came along.  Jurassic Park was revolutionary, Star Wars I was revolutionary, Toy Story was revolutionary.  This movie is evolutionary, it shows just what technology can do with a skilled director's guidance. That alone makes this movie worthy of its high rating.  Add to that Tolkien's incredible prose....and in MY book...you have nothing less than a 10.

title: This Movie Rules (them all)
review:
A great story, a great movie, a great cast of characters. Hats off.

I read the books more than 10 years ago and re-read them only recently in anticipation of the movie. I am pleased to report that the movie surpassed my expectations (already high due to the surrounding hype and positive initial reactions).

Clearly one of the best features of the film (if any one can be singled out) is the music. I do hope Shore keeps up the good work and the same motives throughout the trilogy (especially the "Concerning Hobbits" piece). Fitting music is the one thing that I missed when reading the books (of course).

As regards the cast of characters, the only choice that I could not endorse was the selection of Mr. Mortensen for the role of Aragorn. No insult meant, but Mr. Mortensen is not my idea of Elendil's heir and the future king of Gondor. Perhaps he will do better in the trilogy's next installments. On the other hand, I would like to stand up in defence of the much criticized Liv Tyler as Arwen. She seemed elvish enough for my taste and, standing at the fords with that little scar on her face delivering the "if you want him, come and claim him" line, she was just too cute for any criticism. McKellen's performance as Gandalf stands out together with that of the Hobbit gang (all of them were exactly as I wanted them to be). Hugo Weaving was excellent (although, as some commentators have noted, at the point where he discusses the future of the Ring with Gandalf, I almost expected him to say "It seems that you have been leading two lives Mr. Anderson...").

I look forward to the DVD version (which I hear will be much longer than the the 179 min. cinema version) and do hope that it will contain some parts that may have been cut out from the cinema version, like the attack of the worgs before Moria, the blindfolded Gimli part in Lorien and the gifts of Lorien (you may have noticed that a shot from the gifts of Lorien scene was in the trailer but not in the movie).

Having said that, bring on the Two Towers PJ !

title: They got it just right!
review:
Like all fans of the late, great JRR Tolkien, I was holding my breath: Would they get it right? The answer? A resounding YES. With an amazing touch for every little detail, I felt that this film really brought the domain of Middle Earth to life quite genuinely.

When the fellowship were in the Mines of Moria. I said "yes" audibly, for I knew that THIS was exactly how it should be. Somehow everyone, everything and every place was just right.

The acting was understated and purposeful. The direction was subtle yet precise. I would highly recommend this film to fans of Tolkien as well as those who may not generally count themselves as fantasy fans. This movie is a genuine classic already, and I can hardly wait to buy the entire set in a DVD boxed set in 2005.

Kudos to all those involved in putting LOTR together for us. I look forward to this winter when I can once again step into the mystical realm of Frodo and all his compatriots.

title: A fantastic movie and a promising trilogy
review: I finished watching this movie in the cinema and wondered what happened to the 3 hours that had passed, I didn't want it to end. I would highly recommend this movie for any age group. It has tremendous special effects, a completely original story line and to top it up, characters that you can relate to in seconds. I'll be looking forward to the 2nd and 3rd parts and trust me, you will too once you've seen this.

title: It was about an hour into the movie....
review:
I believe it was about an hour into the movie when the thought struck me: "This movie is ramping up to knock one of my top five favorite movies from their place." (current faves are held by: Braveheart, Remember the Titans, Deep Impact, The Natural, Titanic, Field of Dreams, The Karate Kid... ok, was that five?)

Now granted, this is from someone who's never read anything from Tolkien (only surrounded by crazed co-workers who are). Even so, I found the movie to be engaging at every turn, and was willing to forego some of the initial character development (Why? Because I know there's two more movies still to come!). I was able later to bounce questions off of my co-worker Tolkienites, and that has helped me enjoy the movie even more. The fact that Rings wasn't digestable in one sitting makes it all the more appealing to me. This only added to the movie's richness. How often does that happen with a film?

The music? Wow. Howard Shore's score perfectly matched the timbre of the on screen moments... choking me up on several sections. (there's just something about that Hobbit theme that gets me every time.) The haunting "May it Be" perfectly wrapped up the 3-hour adventure, leaving this 30-something guy quite stunned by the film's overall majesty and scope.

Action, Courage, Friendship, Devotion, Self-Sacrifice, (no profanity)... wonderful qualities to find in *any* film.

When it comes to rating this film... you won't find me giving it a low mark (as some seem to have done) because *their* favorite movie was "de-throned" from IMDBs #1 spot for a while. (can you say "The Godfather"?) Judge the movie on it's own merits alone.

My conclusion? The Fellowship of the Rings, is worth the highest mark it could receive. Bring on the "Two Towers"!

title: True to the Book
review: I enjoyed Lord of the Rings for several reasons. 1, it stuck to the book extremely well and 2, the graphics were the best i have ever seen. I read the books back in junior high and was able to not only follow along, but also remember people, places and details like that.

title: incredible
review:
i am such a tolkien geek, and i approve heartily. there were some details that i could go on about for hours, but they don't matter so much. peter jackson did such an incredible job that it doesn't matter that they left out 17 years, put arwen in, and left out the giving of the gifts from galadriel. it just doesn't matter.

IF YOU HAVEN'T SEEN IT YET, GO SEE IT NOW!!!

title: This movie is a spiritual experience!!!
review: That is all I have to say about this movie... a spiritual experience! I literally had trouble walking just after I saw it and also had to rush out to get some air. This movie has it all, and is without a doubt the best film I have ever seen. When watching it, I could feel that what was showing on the screen before me, was a piece of movie history. So, if you have not already seen it (which I find hard to believe) go see it!!!

title: Even if you're not a fantasy buff--go see this movie!
review:
I am afraid with all the kiddie-hype and marketing committed to "Harry Potter" last year and all the beautiful people (yes, I suppose they can act OK too, but do all mathematicians really look like Russell Crowe and Jennifer Connelly?) in "A Beautiful Mind," that this movie is now getting written off as another special effects fantasy film, and not getting the awards recognition it is due. And this movie should be one of the highest-grossing of all time, in the same club as the Star Wars and Indiana Jones movies, with a little touch of Titanic as well.

"The Fellowship of the Rings" has an extra measure of everything a movie should have--a great story, action, adventure, acting so good you don't realize it's acting, effects so good you don't know they're not real (unlike several cartoon-like sequences in Harry Potter), romance and beautiful cinematography. It is both exciting and funny as well as subtle and artistic. The only person who wouldn't enjoy this movie is one who has no imagination at all.

When the movie was over, a huge groan came from the sold-out audience I was part of--because we couldn't believe three hours had passed and we didn't want it to end.

title: THE BEST MOVIE I'VE EVER SEEN
review: Whenever a famous book is made into a movie, there's loads of hype - Harry Potter being an obvious example. These movies always seem to be better in the advert. But not The Lord of the Rings. The advert didn't really do it justice! I'd give this movie 10 out of 10. It's exciting, moving, and a tiny bit romantic (Arwen and Aragorn). It was so well done, I didn't lose interest once during the three hours. I cried twice - when Gandalf fell from the bridge in the Mines of Moria, and when Sam was prepared to follow Frodo, even though he couldn't swim. Sam, Merry, and Pippin are my favourite characters. The movie captured Sam's loyalty to Frodo. And if you were in unimaginable peril, Merry and Pippin could crack a joke and make it OK. This is the best movie I've ever seen. I can tell whenever I've seen a good movie - I'm dizzy when I leave the cinema. I can't wait for the Two Towers and the Return of the King to come out. Roll on 2003...

title: Completely blew me away
review:
Finally got to a cinema last night to see this incredibly hyped movie.

As somebody who doesn't normally warm to the Fantasy or even Science Fiction genre as I walked into the cinema I was wondering if I was about to add another 3 hours to my "waste of time" file.

Well what can I say now except that I was completely blown away by this film.

The three hours went by very quickly and I didn't look at my watch once (a sure sign of a good film experience for me). In fact, I didn't really want it to end.

As I sat in total awe of this movie experience I couldn't help but wonder if it's creator was the same Peter Jackson who directed the cheesy but nice "Bad Taste" movie (the last PJ movie I think I've seen).

So to borrow a well worn movie cliche, if you only see one movie this year, make it this one!

title: Best Movie Ever made!!!!
review: What is there to say about this monumental film?! It is honestly and without a doubt thee best movie ever ever ever made! Orlando Bloom is a God, Elijah Wood was sensational, Sean Astin had another succesful movie, Liv Tyler really brought oomph to the love story, Viggo Mortenson-who could have played better than him? No one! And all of the rest of them were stunning! The effects, like the RingWraiths and the orcs were awesome. The setting of New Zealand was amazing. Saruman was frightening and all of the special effects were spectacular!Every single element was amazingly spectaculary unbelievable! No other film, except for the upcoming Lord of the Rings movies, could be any better!!

title: Well done - big problem with Moria scene
review:
Lots of reviewers have written about how good or bad this movie is, but I have yet to see any that point out, IMO, its biggest problem - Gandalf's death. In the book, there's no possibility of help for Gandalf, but the movie makes Frodo and Aragorn look like cowards.

My wife, who is not a Tolkien or fantasy lover like I am (she hasn't even read the books), was enjoying the movie up until this point, and this scene completely soured it for her. I was looking past and accepting all of the earlier deviations, but this one stuck in my craw. I don't understand why Jackson changed it so.

Besides that, I loved the movie; acting is terrific, scenery beautiful, and I think it does convey the epic quality/feeling of the original story.

Can't wait for the 4-hour DVD with all of the additional footage.

title: Could the book have been adapted any better? No!
review: Before I saw this film I made sure to read the books over again from The Hobbit through The Return of the King b/c I wanted one last chance to fix my own mental images of the places and characters before Elijah Wood and Liv Tyler were permanently etched in my mind.  I need not have worried b/c everything in this film looks perfect.  I honestly believe that a better adaptation could not possibly have been done.  I cannot imagine how any fan of the books could fail to love this movie.

title: Catches the spirit
review: I first read the Lord of the Rings as a preteen many years ago, and have reread it more times than I can conveniently remember.  (Plus the Hobbit, the Silmarillion, and various of the volumes edited by Christopher Tolkien as well - so I brought a lot of additional lore of Middle Earth in with me!) When I went to see the film I was worried that it would be too different from how I had imagined that world for me to enjoy, or on the contrary that the film version would take over how I imagined characters, locations, etc. so that I could no longer envision things in my own way.  I am very pleased that neither was the case.  While there are certainly aspects of the film that I would have liked to have seen done differently (the hobbits Merry and Pippin should have much more to them than just comic relief), or choices in casting that I might disagree with (most notably Hugo Weaving as Elrond - I do not see the half-elven lord as quite so dour), I enjoyed the film unreservedly and await the next two installments impatiently.  One perhaps small point, carried through from the book, that is particularly well done is the fact that the characters express their affection for one another without fear or embarrassment, without even making a point of it - it is simply their natural emotion.  It is this that makes the story so wonderful - it is a saga of good and evil, yes, but the "human" (or elven, or whatever) aspect is what gives it life.  Tolkien was a true sub-creator, and the filmmakers have caught a good deal of that splintered light.

title: As much an Internal- as an External Epic
review:
I can probably summarize my review best with this quote from Martin Scorsese talking about Lawrence of Arabia. Because that's what The Fellowship is, as much a movie about emotions as it is one about spectacle. And on both levels, the movie succeeds in an amazing way. How does it work?

First of all, let me cover the internal side of this picture. It contains a lot of characters, but in this first part I say about four characters stand out, Frodo,Gandalf, Aragorn and Boromir. Each of these characters has his own conflicts, history and motivations. And again I see a similarity between L.o.Arabia and Fotr, and I'm referring to the similarities between Lawrence and Frodo. Frodo's story is about being taken out of the confines of a familiar culture, his own, and being placed among cultural strangers. Secondly it's about him having to carry a burden he is not sure he can handle (carrying and destroying the ring). These two aspects of Frodo's story are of course comparable to Lawrence's story in Lawrence of Arabia. Besides Frodo you've got the other three characters wich I will not cover so deeply, but it's to say they each have their own problems and conflicts they must try to overcome. How much time Peter takes to explore these emotions is significant, especially for such a large production wich, in Hollywood, almost always means, lots of effects and cardboard characters, and it has renewed my hope for feature Hollywood blockbusters.

And this brings me to the second aspect of Lotr, watching it as an External Epic. To put it mildy, the movie is breathtaking. Seamless CGI, wonderful sets, locations etc. etc. Visually it might well be one of the most amazing movies ever made. Nothing more to say about that.

So to sum it up. Lotr is indeed a movie wich works on a lot of levels, contains facinating characters, wonderful visuals, a rich soundtrack etc. It may be (and I know I said this already with Moulin Rouge, but it simply is the truth) the most complete cinematic experience imaginable. Keeping in mind you have to be open-minded enough to appreciate fantasy, there are very few faults to detect and it may well be one of the cinema's greatest epics!!

title: Very faithful!
review: This is now one of my favorite movies and I could see it over and over.  I loved Elijah Wood as Frodo and all of the other characters were exactly how I pictured them (give or take a little). By the way Elijah Wood has the most beautiful eyes and Orlando Bloom is very cute. The movie was very faithful to the book and I can't wait to see the next one. The land is so gorgeous that I hope to visit there some day. i reccomend that everyone read the book and see the movie!!

title: The movie world redeems itself
review:
My experience up until now has been that movie makers could only ever ruin a perfectly good, even great, story by translating it to the silver screen. For this reason, 40 years ago, I made a pact with my best friend that if they ever tried to make a movie of Tolkien's classic, we would pay good money to be allowed not to see it! How glad I am that we agreed, in the autumn of 2001, to set aside that pact.

Watching Peter Jackson's production, the feeling was one of finally getting to meet people whom I had only heard about before - most of them didn't look anything like my mental picture, but I recognized them instantly nevertheless. In particular, Ian Holme was the perfect Bilbo Baggins. The moment he appeared on the screen, I knew him at once, and Holme didn't just play Bilbo, he became him.

From the point of view of the actual action, my impression was of watching someone else telling the tale of an experience we had both shared. Some things I would have found important, he left out, some things I thought trivial, he left in, and some things he saw completely differently from the way I did, but he was nevertheless still talking about the same incident.

On the negative side, I was disappointed with the casting of Liv Tyler as Arwen. Personally, I had looked for a more ethereal beauty than Liv Tyler possesses. I also found that leaving out the entire confrontation between the Nine of the Fellowship and Galadriel meant that parts of the subsequent story must either also be omitted, or must be hard to understand for those who don't know the story line as well as I do. We shall see, as parts II and III come out, how Peter Jackson is going to cope with this.

Overall, I must say that in this film, Peter Jackson has redeemed the film-making industry. It was a stroke of genius on his part to require that all concerned re-read the trilogy before picking up the film script. By so doing, he made sure that any rank departures from Professor Tolkien's original intent would be immediately short-circuited. I hope that others will follow his example when their turn comes to translate classic works to the screen, and that from now on, producers, directors, actors and screen-writers will work together to preserve the artistic integrity of the original works, as Jackson has now shown us can be done.

title: One of the best films of 2001
review:
My hat is off to the producers, writers, actors and everyone else that made Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring one of the best films of 2001! I can't wait to see The Two Towers & The Return of the King!

My advice: don't miss this film on the big screen! I will definitely get a copy when it comes out on DVD.

title: Yes! The best movie ever!!!
review: Beautiful scenery, costumes, creatures, characters, story.   I loved the Cave Troll and the Balrog scenes.  The Mines of Moria site was very good. I heard there may be actually be up to an hour and a half of additional footage that was cut out of the theatrical release.  If this is true then a special director's cut served on DVD will make the DVD a HUGE success.  I cannot wait for the DVD!!!  FotR IS the best movie of all time, and it was only the first of a three part trilogy!  WOOOHOOOO!!!!!!!

title: A technical achievement and excellent adaptation of the book
review:
One important bit of advice when watching LOTR:FOTR is to find a comfortable theater. But having done that, I didn't notice that the movie was 3 hours long. I thoroughly enjoyed it.

From discussion with my friends, I found that everyone liked The Fellowship of the Ring whether they had read the book or not. It stands on its own as a great movie. But it's a faithful telling of the story from the book. Nearly all the dialog is right out of the book. It's out of sequence in a number of places but I see that as completely excusable since they still told the same story. It couldn't be exactly the same as the book and still be a great movie. The way the story unfolds keeps your attention.

The effort that went into this movie was tremendous. The directing, casting, acting, music and effects were all excellent. For example, things which were supposed to look old or ancient, did. Hobbits looked about half the height of men. Etc.

The graphics lead me to think this film is a landmark technical achievement too. In the 70's Star Wars raised the bar for non-computer effects and integrating music into the action. In the 80's Tron and The Last Starfighter introduced whole segments of the movie completely generated by computer. In the 90's Terminator 2 and Jurassic Park realistically mixed computer graphics with filmed footage. Now in what I think is raising the bar for a new decade, Lord of the Rings takes that integration to a new level whenever you see whole armies or large numbers of Orcs on the move, or other indoor and outdoor footage that I won't mention since they would be spoilers...

title: One of a kind
review: Many classic novels, like Frankenstein, have been made into a film several times. There were other interpretations of the book possible. After seeing this film I cannot imagine another film version of the Ring-Saga. It is an impressive opus. I'm looking forward to part two and three.

title: The best movie of 2001
review: This movie was simply, the best movie of the year.  When I heard the reviews for the movie becoming increasingly good all over the place (being a fan of the original trilogy of books) I could hardly control my excitement. Then the night that I went to see it, it hit me that my expectations might exceed the film. When the movie was over however, it was the movie that exceeded my expectations.  The movie put in one word is "spectacular."  Throughout the entire movie I was on the edge of my seat.  Even though I knew what was going to happen at every seen, I was always surprised. I had decided prior to watching the movie that if I liked it I would wait for all three of the movies to come out before I bought them.  When I stood up after the movie I couldn't wait to see it again which wasn't good because I didn't want to have to get it to watch it again. So, I went to see it again about three days later to get it out of my system.  About ten days later and four watchings of the movie, I still can't wait to see it again. I loved the good characters and hated the bad ones.  I cared what was going on, and not once through this three hour and fifteen minute movie did I look at my watch or talk or find myself bored. WATCH THIS MOVIE!

title: The Impossible-to-make Movie has been made into the Perfect Movie
review: Reading LOTR back in the dark ages of the early '70s, and loving every page, I concluded that this was the best book(s) I had ever read.  I still think that.  I also concluded that this was one story that HAD to be made into a movie - with one catch:  It is too BIG of a story to be a movie - it could simply not be told in one movie or three.  Do I still think that?  Not on your life!  Peter Jackson, we are not worthy...  What a fantastic job he has done. The only story that came close in my mind to LOTR was 'Dune'.  While I myself liked the job that was done with it, as I watched 'Dune', I knew that those who had not read 'Dune' had to be confused.  It was true to the book, but the explanatory material in it was too incomplete.  I saw people leaving the theater, asking, "What happened?  I didn't get it." Not so with LOTR.  I watched with 2 non-readers of LOTR, and they both understood everything perfectly.  The opening was so clear I was astounded. Those who have waited 30+ years for this movie to be made must understand how difficult of a thing it is to tell THIS story well for those who did NOT read it.  And how magnificent of a telling of LOTR this is.  Peter Jackson had the following choice: be true to EVERY aspect of the book, or tell the essential story with as many aspects as could FIT into 3 movies.  I CHALLENGE ANYBODY that faults his choices to do it better!! I walked out of the theater thinking I had just watched the first perfect movie I had ever seen.  I saw no flaws in the story, the script, the plot, the acting, the directing, the scenery (oh the scenery!), the cinematography, the music, the casting, the action, the pace, the special effects (I didn't think they could do the Hobbits to scale).  (Hmm - that's 12 items - maybe we should give it 12 stars.)  My 20-something daughter - who is used to 100-minute coming of age flicks, said, "It's so good, but it's too LONG!"  I have seen it twice, and the second time, the 3 hours went by in a flash. [At this writing, this movie on IMDB has a "weighted average" of 9.1, an "arithmetic mean" of 9.0, and a "median" vote of 10.0, and has dropped to #2, behind 'The Godfather'.  'The Godfather' has scores of 9.0, 8.6, and 10.0, yet it re-claimed #1.  I do not understand the IMDB scoring when 9.0 is higher than 9.1, and 8.6 is higher than 9.0.  By the way, LOTR has been scored a 10 by 24,160 voters, while 'The Godfather' has 24,163 - only 3 more, while LOTR has about 10,500 FEWER overall votes.  I am really curious about the math here.  But of course, the votes are not all in, and it is probable that LOTR will eventually fall to 2nd, even in my math.] I am really happy that this story that I have loved so well has been turned into such a remarkable movie, and that so MANY people love the movie! Yes, Professor Tolkien, Frodo lives!  And what a smile that has put on so many faces...  When 65.7 percent of the voters rate a movie a 10 out of 10, I think we can say Mr. Jackson did okay by T.R.R.

title: Have you ever wondered what the best movie ever made would be like?
review: Wow!!!!  That's all I can say.  This movie so clearly depicted evil and good and made the conflict between them so real, that any viewer can feel the constant tension.  The viewer is constantly having to calm himself down, fretting over the characters that are so easy to fall in love with, and the extreme odds that are set against them.  This is a fantasy with so much reality....there is NO hope in essence.  Everything looks so grim and terrible, and this is portrayed so magnificently that I'm sure even those who have read the books will be surprised when the Protagonists prevail in the coming movies.  Thanks to the director for the excellent job of making this movie.  It was by far the most stimulating, visually stunning, and all around best movie I've ever seen.  No doubt about it...that is until the next two come out maybe.  Perhaps that's just my bias talking, being a major Tolkien fan, but perhaps it's just the shear facts that absolutely no one can deny.  This movie is one EVERYONE must see.

title: Well worth the wait
review: The same guy held the rights to LOTR since the early 70's and has repeatedly blasted try after try to get this movie made.  Thank God he waited for Peter Jackson and Company. This movie is AUTOMATICALLY in my top 5 all time just because of it's visual effects. Add in the Supreme cast, excellent adaptation of the books to script and the over all production value and it's easy to see why this movie will become an instant classic. Can't wait for TWO TOWERS!  Bring on Treebeard and the Ents!!!!

title: Everyone should see this movie!!!
review: Definately the best I've seen all year... and close to being the best EVER!!! I'm going to be eagerly watching the Golden Globe Awards tomorrow to see if "Fellowship of the Ring" wins all the ones it's nominated for... it certainly deserves to! Great action, awesome battle scenes, good acting, amazing landscapes in New Zealand, WONDERFUL MOVIE!!! True, it doesn't stick to the book exactly, and some of the characters (like good old Tom Bombadil!) are cut out... but hey, it's better than a lot of other movies that are based on books! So, go see it, if you haven't already! And see it again, if you've already seen it! Anyone know when the DVD's coming out?  I'm dying to see all those deleted scenes! 11/10

title: One of the best movies ever.
review: The Lord of the Rings is one of my favorite movies of all time.  It followed the book really well, it had great special effects and the acting was good too.  The movie missed some parts but that isn't enough to mess with its score, it gets a 10 from me.

title: How can you wait for next Xmas?
review:
There is so much one could write about the first part of the LOTR trilogy. One could mention that accuracy, they "by the book" filming. Another would point out the excellent acting. The stunning visual effects would be another thing to praise, not to mention the fantastic work of the make up artists and the costume designers.

One could surely not find enough words to describe the phenomenal pace that movie goes on with - a pace that doesn't let one stare at the amazing detailed Middle Earth, a real incarnation of Tolkien's brilliant fantasy.

And one shouldn't hasitate to cheer the effort of the film director, a man carefully planning everything, taking the best out of the most famous myth of the anglo-saxon literature.

Oh, yes, words would pale if one'd try to describe the feeling that emerges from the screen, when the first time the Nazgul appear. Or the beauty of the Elven resorts. Or the convincing and complicated Moria world. Or the fabulously well done animations of the various monsters. Or...

Really, one could say so much about this film. One could write a book. Or one could only write one phrase:

I can't wait till next Christmass. I need the "Two towers" now. Presto. ASAP. GIVE ME THE SECOND PART, PLEASE!!!!!!

title: A Work of Art, A rare find
review: Lord of the Rings' first installment, "Fellowship of the Ring" Wasn't just a movie, but a Work of Art. The Year 2001 had movies about Famous War Events, Dinosaurs, Apes, Mummies, and Creepers, Life Stories, and Novels into Book Films. Yet, out of all of them, Fellowship seemed to be the complete and utter best. Yes, some you might say Harry Potter I is the Best, but when you look back, which movie looked the best? I'm not going to get into a debate about that, so I'll move on. FOTR seemed perfect in everything, Characters, Plot, Script, Effects, etc. Its very rare to find a movie like this, the Emotion, humor, action, romance, and utter fear is all here. I recommend this to anyone, it might be 3 hours of Tolkien's classic book, but in movie form, its astounding, just like the book.

title: Just as I imagined the book
review:
I an a diehard Tolkien fan having read LOTR, the Hobbit, the Silmarillion as well as all twelve books of the history of middle earth and I was so hyped about LOTR FOTR. And I for one am not in the least bit let down by the movie. The characters are all superbly cast especially Aragorn who looks sufficiently rugged but kingly as well and Legolas and Elrond who are both convincingly elvish. Hugo Weaving not only looks elvish but he looks like a Noldorin descendant and Orlando Bloom looks as i would imagine one of the dark elves.

See this movie. Whether you have read this book is irrelevant.

title: EXCELLENT!!!
review:
GREAT film! I've only read one of the LOTR books (Fellowship) but I can appreciate this movie just as much as a die-hard Tolkien fan can.

What's not to love about this film? It has action(ALOT of action actually), comedy(Merry and Pippin make for great comic relief), romance(Aragorn and Arwen), drama(Gandalf's death, Sam's neverending loyalty to Frodo), and all in all, everything with this film is perfect. The pacing is marvelous as the film is two hours and fifty eight minutes long yet at the end, it feels like an hour and a half went by instead of nearly three hours.

The directing is great, the writing is great, the acting is fantastic, the special effects are great, I mean anything that can be perfect in a film is perfect in LOTR. The translation from book to screen is near perfect. I say near perfect as some things were changed but that does not at all detract from the enjoyment of the film. The film follows the book closely and this is easily one of the best book to film adaptations I've ever seen.

Two thumbs up for LOTR!

title: the most popular tale is, now, the best movie
review: It's incredible as Jackson and his cast can act the Middle-Earth in this way. Excellent movie, where a love story and a epic tale are mixed with the right number of comic relief. There are not the right number of word to describe how fantastic this movie is. Please, see it. It's the best advice and the only thing I can say. and have fun!

title: Amazing
review: It is not the book, nor even half as good as the book, but allowing for everything one must admit the movie stands alone. I realize the omissions were necessary for the movie, ( good example for this would be Harry Potter which I found incredibly boring!). Thank you, Peter Jackson, for bringing my middle earth to life

title: Like the critics said, "A Ring to Rule the Screen!"
review: I was so impressed with this movie.  I went to see it without knowing much about it.  I had read the Hobbit and seen the animated version of it, but had never read the books.  All that changed in about three hours.  Some parts of the movie made me laugh, and others had me in sentimental tears. And it was so clean!  So many movies today seem to be made with the impression that it can't be a success if it doesn't have profanity or some sexual reference in it.  This movie had none of that, the PG 13 rating was for the violence, and even that wasn't so bad, mainly battle scenes.  This movie sends out positive messages on loyalty, friendship, resisting temptation, and self-sacrifice.  What a great film.  Bravo Peter Jackson!

title: As a fan of the books I was prepared for disappointment, but, I was thrilled with the first movie.
review: I think that a lot of fans of Tolkien were skeptical about anyone's ability to take these incredible books, really the standard by which all other fantasy novels are measured, and create movies that would even come close to the world that Tolkien created.  In scope and style, any director seems hopelessly out-matched by the novels from which this epic story must come. Having said all this, it is with even greater surprise, joy, relief, gratitude etc. that I admit that Peter Jackson has done this impossible task with an amazing style and craft that I could not have previously hoped for. It seems cruel now to have to wait a whole year for the next installment; even knowing what will happen in the next movie, I am still riddled with anticipation to see Jackson's rendition.  If you have yet to see this movie, go and see it soon while it is still in theaters, because like the novels, the film is an epic in its own right and the big screen is necessary to properly overwhelm the viewer.  You will be overwhelmed, whether or not you have read the books, you will leave the theater impressed and ticked off that you have to wait until next December for THE TWO TOWERS.

title: the best movie I've ever seen
review: This is by far the best movie I have ever seen. Anyone who didn't like this movie has something wrong with them. Peter Jackson did a wonderful job directed and shooting this movie and the editing was amazing. The special effects were awesome as well! I can not wait until The Two Towers is released!

title: As real and fantastic as the books themselves...
review:
For the 15-month effort of the actors, to the near decade effort for everyone else involved, I have to sit back in awe at this movie. The acting was amazing - it captured the different races and complex relationships - while the screenplay, script, soundtrack, and digital effects were mind blowing. This is truly a movie produced as well as it could ever be.

10/10

title: Great representation of the book.
review: Tremendous movie, a great tribute to the insight, dedication and understanding that Peter Jackson obviously has for the Trilogy.  Tolkien would be very proud to sit down and watch this, I'm sure.  I'm looking forward to the two sequels, as many are.  Can they make them even better? We'll see.

title: BEST MOVIE IN THE HISTORY OF FILM!!
review: Breathtaking,beutiful,scary,funny and excellent in every other way. If you don't see this it is a damn shame. If this movie dosen't win the oscar it will sadden anyone who has seen this marvelous film. I loved all of it. I absolutley can not wait for the two towers. I will be first there, last one out. 10/10
