title: Read it in 1969 and since. Film amazingly like what I had in mind.
review: I think you have to have read the book to appreciate the underlying story. I was taken back in time as I watched each scene playing out what I saw in my mind when I first read the book back in 1969. The natural scenery and the computer graphics created a Middle Earth worthy of the sixties scene I grew up in. And the way the two strands of culture - the low Hobbit with its earthy community humour, and the high Elvish with its cool altruism - was carried over to the film so well.  All round an excellent film - and two more to come!

title: As good a movie as I have ever seen!
review: I went in with very high expectations, mainly from it taking over #1 on the all time list here, but also because I loved the stories as a child.  I am a sci-fi nut, & I love fantasy, so I was so looking forward to this.  I have never seen a movie so complete & balanced in every way.  You can see they took no shortcuts, or cheap tricks here.  They went all out, cast, crew, special effects, & locations, everything was right on.  I felt like I was in middle earth.  Sets that you know for a fact are fake look totally real. The acting was on target not so overdone or gaudy that it took away from the scenery, but not so weak that it away from the character depth.  I don't know that everyone should give this a 10, but it at least deserves an 8 from just about everybody.  No movie ever made has been this anticipated & then surpassed all possible expectations.  I agree with a previous comment, "This is what we expected from Star Wars: Episode I".  All I add to that is this, "& hope to see from Episode II!"

title: A few words....
review: amazing, unique, excellent, breathtaking, everything about this was perfect for me....after reading all three books and knowing what to expect, I honestly thought that the scenery, the characters, the way they moved, the way they spoke and everything else in general was exactly how I had imagined it...don't think we'll see a better adaptation in a looooooong while.

title: This movie is haunting...
review: All I can say is that I have found the movie that will remain my favorite for the rest of my life, except for perhaps the next two installments. Every aspect of it was superb to the extreme.  Nothing I could say could possibly do it justice, so I will simply say that you MUST see this movie. No excuses allowed!  The only word I can think of that even begins to capture the essence of this movie is...haunting.

title: Complements the book
review:
Can't please everyone, is all I can say about those who complain about this movie being over-hyped and all that.

30k+ votes can't be wrong, just compare against Godfather votes, MANY MANY more think LotR is a full 10, whereas Godfather has many more 9's, and almost double the number of 8, 7, and 6s.

As for the movie. Brilliant. Amazing. I registered for this site just to vote it a 10/10, to rub it in on those who say it's only because it is hyped up. This movie IS the best of it's kind, by FAR.

Myself, I think the movie complements the book. It brings out in more fleshed out way things like Saruman's deception, which is VERY integral to the world's story itself but is not emphasized in the book. Also, where did they show Galadriel did NOT give Sam a present? All it does is hold to Frodo because of time constraints.

Of course, there were some scenes I had imagined differently myself. Like the setting of site where Frodo got stabbed, or the mountain pass over Moria, but I don't care about little silly things like those to say the movie sucks because it didn't fit MY view in all things. That is egoistic :)

And people complain about the weirdest of things... Saruman's army did have Uruk-hai's with names and details in the book too, I'm pretty sure Smeagol, while not spotted, was sensed already in Moria, etc. etc. It has been a decade or so since I read LotR, but in my view the movie was 99% truthful to the book. Arwen instead of Glorfindel is the 1%, but that's probably better this way :)

All in all, easily and by FAR the best fantasy movie I have ever seen. And I have seen many. As for best of all movies of all categories, well for me it is definitely one of the best. Along with Casablanca, Matrix and Usual Suspects. As a side note ... like it much more than Godfather ;)

title: One of the GREATEST FILMS EVER MADE!
review:
If you go see this movie, you will not be disappointed!

Not only does "The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring" remain true to the events in the first novel of J.R.R. Tolkien's world famous trilogy, but the movie is made with an exceptional quality that brings out the very real and wholesome epic qualities of the book and it succeeds over and over again!

The cast and crew gave performances that were nothing short of marvellous and they should all be proud of their work in this colossal movie! Everyone who was cast shows the true and real emotions that were originally intentioned by the author, focusing on the fear, determination, treachery, evil, love, fellowship, courage, wholesomeness and stoutheartedness that should be present in such an epic as this. Of all the actors that took part in this movie, I believe that all of the actors were perfectly cast for their roles and fit perfectly!

The soundtrack was nothing short of flawless, and "The Shadow of the Past" makes "Duel of the Fates" (in Star Wars 'Episode I') sound like a lullibye in comparison! :-) It was dark and very emotional where it should be, and flawless! Inviting Enya for specific themes was a stroke of genius, and it can only be hoped that she would return to provide her magical touch for the next two movies.

New Line Cinema has a new classic trilogy on their hands, and one that is timeless! This picture is every bit as big and has just as big a following as the Star Wars genre does, and I would hope that at least one of these movies could become the most popular movie of all time! I have seen this movie no less than 13 times, and I thoroughly enjoyed it each time!

But of course, you can only form your opinion if you go and see it as well! This movie deserves 4 stars out of a 4 star rating, and 10 stars out of a 10 star rating.

If you go see it, you will not be disappointed! This movie was written and produced by fans of the greatest fantasy epic series of all time, "The Lord of the Rings", by J.R.R. Tolkien.

title: Beautiful movie
review:
Peter Jackson made what every director should make when adapting a book into a film: he kept the essence of the story. This is what make Lord of the Rings a very good movie.

I have read the book and I think that it completes the film and vice-versa. Certainly, the book (as always) has more details. But it's possible to understand the film without reading.. As I said, one completes the other but, at the same time, they are independent. It has a fine production and the special effects are not over. They are so close and natural to the story that sometimes you can't feel it. And that is what make them so good. The actors are excellent, especially Christopher Lee as Saruman. Great actor! I think that the others movies should come soon. One year is too much time to wait. Why not six months or maybe, five, four,...

title: Breathtaking
review:
I went to see the movie yesterday. The cinema was crappy & old. The seats were terrible, the sound wasn't calibrated right, etc. But you know what? I didn't care! The story just overwhelmed me. The movie embraced me and I simply forgot everything around me.

This is the best fantasy/sf film I have ever seen!! THE BEST. I think I am addicted already. I want to see it again. And again and again.

I have not read the books yet, but I plan to. Some people say the books are better than the movie. Is that truly possible??

If you have not seen this movie yet, you missed the best adventure ever. Go see it!

title: Big budget Hollywood finds it's hero.......
review: In an era where spending over a $100 million dollars on movies such as the dreadful "Pearl Harbor", "Final Fantasy" and "Harry Potter", there seems to be no limit to the stupidity of movie company execs. However, we have been saved by Peter Jackson and J.R.R. Tolkien. I thought about not seeing this movie, as the history of big budget Hollywood has not been too extravegant. "Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring" certainly breaks that mold. Visually, the movie can't be beat. Storywise, there are no holes. But the main thing that got me was that the movie was 3 hours long, yet when it was over, I wanted more. After "The Godfather 2" I was content. After "Scarface" I was content (yet sad that one of my favorite characters had to bite the dust). But I was ready for any amount of time it would take to finish the story. Movies, for me, tend to drag at about 130 minutes. This movie was off and running from the opening titles to the final scene. I was on the edge of my seat, and I feel horrible that I have to wait a year for the second entry in this marvel of movie making. This movie is in my top ten, alright, and it gets the recommendation of 11/10. Big budget Hollywood, you have found your hero. Because of this movie, maybe you'll be forgiven for "Waterworld". Then again, probably not.

title: The greatest film experience of the year!
review:
I was absolutely stunned when I first saw it. The special-effects, the costumes, the make-up and most important of all: THEY STICKED TO THE STORY! I'm one of Tolkien's biggest fans, I consider myself as that.

Everything was almost perfect! Humm okay, there were some things that I REAAAAALLY would have wanted them to have in the movie, like Glorfindel and Tom Bombadill. I'm a little disturbed that Liv Tyler took Glorfindel's place, and said those non-original words 'If you want him, COME AND CLAIM HIM!'. Okay, at least I'm happy they chose an okay actress like Liv Tyler. But I just can't let this thought go: Natalie Imbruglia would have fitted perfect as Arwen. She looks like sort of an elf. Galadriel, who was played by Cate Blanchett, was VERY horrifying. One of my friends, who hadn't read any book of Tolkien thought that she was a witch. I didn't quite like they way they portrayed her. After she had said all those stuff about 'AAH I WOULD BE A TERRIFYING QUEEN IF I HAD THE RING, TREACHEROUS AS THE SEA...' and so on, well, after that, she sort of trembled. I mean, she looked so weak. I didn't quite find Galadriel as a weak person, when I read the books. Hummm... Well, I guess that's how Peter Jackson thinks of her. But please, do not misunderstand me, with all my criticizing! It was wonderful! I cried two times, damn-it! When they came out of Moria, and when Boromir got all those arrows in shot in his chest.. Alas, alas... The film is really a piece of fantasy art! Yummie!

title: If you don't like it I feel for you :)
review: I saw this movie on the opening night, and indeed four times since, every time with different people. In total, I have seen it with 8 other people (scary co-incidence??) and of them, only 1 did not like it. His reasons were banal and he couldn't really explain them so I shan't give them any more space. Sorry Tim! What did I think of the movie? Well, the fact that I've seen it as many times as I have kinda gives it away actually. I read the book straight after I read The hobbit, when I was 10. I loved it. Since then, I have read it three times more and even now it is still my favourite book of all time. When I heard they were going to do a movie about it, I thought, great, until I learned that Elijah Wood was playing Frodo. Oh no, I thought, I can't stand him, though, on seeing it he actually does the part well. Best performance has to go to Sir Ian Mckellan (sp?) he is outstanding, and what's more, he IS Gandalf. All the cast play their parts well, without exception. I loved Liv Tyler and my sister loved Orlando Bloom.... Of course, the real stars of the movie are the effects. Breath-taking. Makes things like Jurassic Park and Star Wars (both, incidentally, too drawn-out and over sequelled franchises) look like Play Days. Pfffft, no really, this movie goes further, harder, faster and better than any other. End of. As for faults, well...If I was Peter Jackson, and I got up one morning and thought, right, I gotta make The Lord Of The Rings into a book today, I would have slipped into a coma. He took on this juggernaugt of epic proportion and pulled it off without any real criticism. I honestly believe to do a better version of the book-to-film adaptation is impossible. On what would they improve? Before screaming at your monitor, answering with your opinions, stop and think: could YOU have done it any better? Thought not. Credit where credit's due, this is a master-piece, no two ways about it. I have as much right as anyone to declare any film I like as "The Best Movie Of All Time", and for that, I choose this, The Fellowships Of The Ring. (At least until I watch the next parts!) Like it or don't like it. It's your call. But I feel for you if it doesn't reach out to you, I really do.

title: Like my imagination.
review: Just to say perfect. Almost perfect. All the characters as I imagined them to be, to act, to talk. Just great. How did they do that. Just the little Hobbit Frodo was somewhat different from how I imagined him to look. The music was overwhelming. I was reluctant to leave the movietheatre after the film ended..I wanted more. That is a good sign.

title: Too good to be true
review: All doubts about skills and imagination of Peter Jackson has gone, he has done a great job in putting the books to the screen! Jackson made just right decisions to take some scenes out from the movie. Also the actors were superb, ie. look the face of Gimli when in the end of movie Aragorn says that "Let's go and nail some orcs" or something like that. EXCELLENT MOVIE!

title: An enchanting, blessing, epic saga
review:
The Lord of the rings: The fellowship of the ring And I quote myself "This is the best movie I've ever seen, and It's probably (maybe the next ones can compare) best movie I will ever see. I wept when I saw this movie, I had constant goosebumps, my part was pounding, it's a first-time-experience that I will never feel again (Yes, even better than sex!), and I can't wait for two more times of that feeling!

Daniel Elijah

title: an injection of adrenaline!
review: a lot of people  have been saying that this is a film which appeals only to fans of the books, what utter bull. i read the books and hated them, however I LOVE THIS MOVIE! my sister is a fan of the books and she and i had a debate about changes made to the story, if anything these are improvements. *****spoiler******* such as the developed romance of aragorn and arwen, to me this improved aragorn's position as a main character, and made me care more about him because he stands more to lose. arwen rescuing frodo from the black riders ok we have enough male heros in this film, not to sound like a feminist, but give the girls a chance. once scene i really did like was when aragorn let frodo go, and was almost tempted by the ring. his inward struggle show his determination not to become isildur, and showed his strength as a future king. the thing that i really liked was that they left out tom bombadil, that was they most boring chapter ever written in a book. this is not just a mindless action movie it is a story of complex emotions, and relationship's between different races. those who say this is boring, what movie were you bloody watching! because it certainly wasn't this one. this is the best film ever made, no not the hype talking. a genuine masterpiece, 10/10 but why do we have to wait so long for the second one?

title: Who cares what the Academy thinks!
review:
As far as I am concerned, the last thing on my mind is whether or not the American Academy recognises LOTR as a "great" film. Let them keep their mediocre 'Star Wars','Titanic' and 'Pearl Harbour' - they are welcome to them.

For all Tolkien fans, this is our Precious, not theirs; a lasting testimony to the great man's ambivalence to Disney-like dumbing down in all of its manifestations. 10 out of 10 Mr. Jackson for bringing the greatest dream ever written to the big screen.

title: Couldn't be better!
review: The next two movies have to be pretty darn good to stand up to the first! Before its' release I thought this might be a great movie, but I never thought it would be that spectacular!  A month after seeing it simply thinking of different scenes leave me breathless.  I don't think this movie could have possibly been better!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: I'm very impressed and enjoyed it immensely
review: Having read the books about 15 years ago I was familiar with the story and characters but not on a detailed level. Nonetheless I was really looking forward to seeing the film and what I saw really carried my breath away. Inspired by watching the movie, I picked up LOTR to read it again and then watched the movie a second time. It was even better the second time around because I was able to look closer at many - but still not all - the details Peter Jackson put into the film to make it as "authentic" as possible. The time and effort the filmmakers spent on that epic production was well worth it. I can't wait to see the film a third and maybe even a fourth time.... Anybody think it's possible to get the second film released earlier?

title: Magic for any Tolkien fan...
review:
Okay, so it may not be accessible to the general public, but WHO CARES? There are millions of Tolkien fans, and they love Peter Jackson. This movie had the whole, packed theater laughing, gasping, and quiet at all the right moments. Great acting (Sean Bean made me LIKE Boromir), great effects, great story, great movie. The trilogy will beat even "Star Wars," I think. There was applause and a standing ovation at the end, and half the audience stayed in their seats through the credits with the magnificent Enya singing in the background. Fans said things like "I've been waiting twenty years for this," and "Holy moly! That was fantastic!"

#1 for a reason.

title: I wish it was Christmas everyday, but I have to wait another year...
review:
I can only recall one other time when I felt so strong about a movie. It was the first time my dad took me to a movie theater, 30 years ago.

The story, although not completely faithful to Tolkien's original, is well streamlined, with a well designed introduction to the history of the One Ring, short and to the point.

The choice of actors is excellent. The landscapes are impressive, the battles are terrifying.

It clearly exceeded my expectations.

If you only see one movie per year, try to see this one.

I wish it was Christmas everyday, but I have to wait another year for volume 2...

title: speechless....but:
review: J.R.R. Tolkien's  "THe Lord of the Rings" is my favorite book of all time. I love the depth, the themes, the setting, and most of all, the characters. I love this movie, becuase though it leaves me thinking about the parts they edited out (small and unneeded) all I can say is: "Wow." Becuase everyone who has read the books knows what an incredible feat this story is. And to cover 2 'books' in three hours is tough without making people angry. So All I can say is "Wow" becuase I love this story, and everything about it. It makes me happy to know that people who have never read the books like the movie, it gives me a heartening feeling. Why? Becuase those people appreciate something that I (or we, I should say) love so dearly. So 'kudos!' Peter and the cast and crew- you really did it. Thank you. Like I've always said: "'The Lord of the Rings' is the only thing I love on this earth that I can't touch."

title: Maybe not the best film ever...
review:
This was certainly the best film of the year.

Like others before me, I will refrain from gushing at a movie which I will be taking the unprecedented step of going to see for the third time at the theatre this Thursday. So, here are the good points and the bad points. The good points outweigh the bad points by orders of magnitude.

Good:

1. It tells the story faithfully even if it departs from complete accuracy.

2. Great acting, especially by Elijah Woods and Ian McKellen.

3. Immense and beautiful scenery, sets and visual effects.

4. Captures, with few exceptions, Tolkien's characters.

5. Appeals to those who have read the book and those who haven't alike.

6. It keeps your attention for the full three hours which is an impressive feat!

Bad:

1. Weathertop scene was disappointing.

2. Gimli's character was underdeveloped and a bit cardboard.

3. Lothlorien passage was incomplete and confusing and Galadriel came across wrong.

In summary? Go and see this movie. Even if you don't like it as much as 90% of the rest of us, you'll never forgive yourself if you miss it. I think it will become a true movie classic of the likes of Ben Hur.

P.S. At one of the sittings, a 6 year old kid in front of me had to be taken out because he was so scared of the black riders. I don't think it's appropriate for kids under 8.

title: Almost perfect
review: I think the only problem with this movie is that everyone has his own thoughts of the world of the Ring. I've found the world similar to my own imaginery world but the cast not always meet the heroes from my dreamworld. For example I've found Legolas and Gimli perfect but I didn't like Aragorn at all. And an other thing that brother me most. If I remember correctly, Arwen appears only in the last book. And her the love scene with Aragorn remembers me a bit Titanic. So it was quiet embrassing. However, it's still the greatest movie of all.

title: Astounding!
review: More exciting, more "realistic", more engaging than anything I was expecting.  I am surprised (and thrilled) that Jackson has managed to be so faithful to the book(s).  And the casting is superb - everyone seemed born to play their respective roles, especially Frodo, Aragorn and Boromir.

title: God bless Peter Jackson!
review: I have read the trilogy twice through.  I was not disappointed in any way by the transition to film.  Watching the first film made me want to re-read the book and go right back out and buy another ticket.  Can't wait for the DVD. I have never anticipated winter more than I do now.  Peter Jackson has shown that great literature can be made into great film without all the Hollywood cliches that are dropped meaninglessly into so many movies.  Long live PJ!

title: A good start to another fanasty trilogy.
review: Let me tell you something. Perfect, Flawless can't be associated with any film. The Special Effects are amazing but I've been saying that ever since The Phantom Menace came out. Many people over rate this film and many people under rate this film. To me it was one of the best movies of the year, but better then Shrek, I don't know about that. It well worth your three hours and 7 bucks to catch this flick, the end caught me off guard becuase I never read the books. Their is a lot of development in this film and it turns off many viewers, but not me a person who treasures the Star Wars Universe and the Matrix is delighted to see development instead of resalution. I can't wait for the next two 2002 is going to be a great year. Getting back on track Lord of the Rings while starting the cycle takes a lot from different movies, Star Wars Saga, Dungeons and Dragons, Braveheart, and Harry Potter. As for best film of all time not even in the top 10.

title: Wonderful, incredible, outlandishly superlative
review: Simply put, the film, in all its facets, fits within my mind's eye over the reading and re-reading of the classic Tolkein novels over a dozen times. Gandalf fits precisely, the hobbits are well selected and performed, Aragorn is a tremendous casting achievement . . . and the beat goes on.  A stupendous achievement!

title: Greater than I expected!!!
review:
I had read 2/3 of the TFotR before I went to cinema! I could not wait any longer! - our need for love - our daily battle against temptations - our dreams - our lack of peace in this world - heroes are not necesarily Batman or Superman! and lots more! all this was joined together! I have to admit that the movie was perfectly optimized for showing the most important of the book in 3 hours, leaving out just those details, which are almost impossible to transform to video!

What are you waiting for: 1) read the book! 2) watch the movie! 3) have a nice day!

:)

title: The first of three promising epics
review: "The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring" is one of the best pictures of the year by an understatment! A visually stunning masterpiece, this movie will no doubt be honored all year long, and fans will be lining up for the next two features. The most amazing thing about this whole movie is the relationship between all of it's central characters. You really and truly think that these guys care for each other and emotion is something that could have easily been lost in a film this size. Yes, it's an adventure movie, a road trip movie to beat all road trip movies! But it comes down to, after all the special effects and beautiful locations, are the characters and how they handle having thier lives turned upsidedown in a horrific way. And as for Peter Jackson, well, let's just say, the guy got it right! God bless him! And a big thanks to the 1000's of people who put this thing on the big screen! And as for those fans waiting in line to see the next one, save me a spot! It's going to be a long two years, but I'm sure it'll be worth the wait!!

title: Simply breathtaking...
review:
From the first moment the movie starts you are immediately captivated by the story that evolves. The cinematography is just amazing, Peter Jackson did an incredible job conveying to us the times of the Hobbits. I believe the cast had excellent chemistry and it's refreshing to see a group of actors who seem to really break into their roles. I'm so happy that Elijah Wood played Frodo, he's a great actor and doesn't get as nearly enough recognition as he deserves. It's also a good breakthrough for Viggo Mortenson who has minor roles in "28 Days" and "A Perfect Murder", Liv Tyler is sweet as Arwen and I look forward to her character expanding in the next two installments. Ian McKellen is just a great actor to watch and really brought Gandalf to life, Sean Bean again is another actor who doesn't get nearly as enough credit as he deserves. Orlando Bloom is a cutie as Legolas, the hobbits are just funny to watch especially Sean Astin's Sam. Cate Blanchett was rather freaky as Galadriel, but I think the way her character signed off to Frodo is just the beginning of our understanding of her.

All in all this is just an amazing movie!!

title: The movie was absolutely PERFECT!!
review: I thought the movie was/is wonderful!! I have seen it 5 times, and will see it at least 2 more times. I'm saving up so I can buy the DVD the fist day it comes out! The way it followed the book so well, and how good all the actors are makes it a PERFECT movie! I will probably never get bored of it.

title: I was inspired.
review: Being from the country where this film was made in and having a kiwi director to make it I had a great sense of pride going into see The Lord of the Rings. In New Zealand you could not get away from knowing that this was going to be big. In the beginning I was spellbound by the majesty and scope of the movie and then was held by a thread on the end of my seat throughout the rest of the movie. This movie inspired me, and brought me to tears with credits and the latest song by Enya, "May it Be". I came out thinking that this was the best movie that I have seen in my life.

title: Boring? Trite? Cheesy?...Give me a break!
review:
I am amazed at the comments of those who disliked this film. Comparing this to The Royal Tenenbaums is like comparing Hamlet to Hello Dolly! Cheesy special effects? War of the Worlds has cheesy special effects by our standards. Star Wars has cheesy special effects. Even Return of the Jedi with its shimmering machines against a matte background is cheesy. LOTR is not. If anything I applaud the ingenuity and creativity of Peter Jackson by not going for the obvious in depicting the hobbits, but for choosing to do it with camera angles instead. The movements are natural.

The story isn't literary? Tolkien has never been highly regarded in literary circles? I'm sorry, but I am not sure what literary circles some people run around in, but there is a reason why the few books that Tolkien wrote endure. His creativity in dealing with universal themes of good and evil, temptation and salvation, and bravery and cowardice have created a new mythology. His writing speaks to the ages...not to a decade.

The acting is superb considering the constraints. True, there is not a great deal of time for character development. I was one of those who was wondering about Legolas. Regardless, characters are clear and believable. Ian McKellen IS Gandalf. Elijah Wood is an excellent Frodo. It is always great to see Ian Holm and Christopher Lee's Saruman was excellent and displayed the depth so often overlooked in the many horror roles of his career. I was most impressed, though,by Sean Astin's Samwise 'Sam' Gamgee. He was both humorous and sensitive as the faithful hobbit whose main duty is to stick near to Frodo. He is Frodo's conscious as well as a voice of reason.

LOTR is not the best movie I have ever seen. It is possibly the best of its type, and this is where I would like to preach to my fellow reviewers. Too often we "Academize" our opinions and forget that each film should be taken separately on its own merits. Comedies shouldn't be lumped together with tragedies any more than a musical with a suicide. Once everything has been accounted for then start the comparisons. The Royal Tenebaums may be a wonderful movie, but is it the best ever of its kind? There will undoubtedly be comparisons made between LOTR and Star Wars, but is it fair to compare one movie's technology with another's when they are separated by twenty years of advancement? Look at things in a more realistic light.

For those who feel Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring is too long I apologize. I grew up in the day of triple features for a buck. I still feel cheated when I pay seven dollars for one movie. And for someone who usually makes a trip to the restroom after 90 minutes, I never felt the urge to leave my seat. My suggestion: don't drink before the movie.

For those who feel that Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring is boring may I suggest that you probably don't really appreciate fantasy to begin with. That's all right, but in the future you may find yourself less bored if you avoid those movies.

Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring is an excellent movie. It has my tentative vote for best of the year because I haven't seen the other possible nominees, but it is a work that will endure, and I can't wait for The Two Towers.

title: A grand epic!
review: This is a film to bring back a sense of wondors to movies. This is escapism on the grandest scale. All but the most unimaginative viewers will feel that they are in Middle Earth and part of a great struggle with unspeakable evil. I read the books when I was 14 and loved them then. The movie captures that same breadth and depth of imagination. This movie is intense though and parents should not consider bringing young children. Likewise it is long and its intensity will wear on the faint of heart. In fact, my only real criticism of this movie is the lack of an intermission.

title: Minor differences with the book
review: They said that LOTR could not be transformed into a movie. Well, for part 1 Jackson did a hell of a job !!! Apart from some minor faults (e.g. Narsil is in possession of Aragorn, Gandalf opens the gate of Moria)the story follows the book in great detail. 3 hours is too short, I am already looking forward to next year!

title: flawless
review: Beautiful film.  Grand in ever aspect.  I didnt even hear any corny lines or anything to mess it up.  I am still blown away, have been since it ended 4 hours ago, and i hope it wont go away.  Go see it!  Before it isn't in the theaters!

title: Best movie I've ever seen!!!
review: Tolkien is my favourite writer and I expected for a long time this movie of Peter Jackson. Now I can tell this is the most emotional film I've ever seen!! Maybe I'm subjective, but movie is so great i imagined before. Now it's a hard time - wait for 12 months to see Two Towers!!

title: The best it could be
review:
This has got to be the hardest story ever to tell in pictures; anyone who's read the book more than once has surely already formed their own mental images of the way Middle Earth and its residences should appear. How do you realize a million people's daydreams? Think about this, too: the movie cost about a million dollars. Titanic cost nearly twice that. Go figure.

SPOILERS HERE:

Personally, I was both dazzled and disappointed. Dazzled because Gandalf, the hobbits, the birthday party, and Gimli all looked exactly as I'd pictured. Rivendell, Hobbiton, and Mordor all one-upped my own imagination and I prefer the director's vision to my own. The script was nearly true to the story (that I've read more than 20 times) and most of the abbreviations were acceptable. The movie, as a stand-alone piece is infinitely more beautiful than the latest offering from star wars.

My disappointments were few, but one in particular was disconcerting. I found myself jarred from total immersion in the piece by some poorly-executed cuts. I found this to be true as the hobbits head for Weathertop with Aragorn, and again when the fellowship heads for the mountain.

The other irritation is the relationship between Gimli and Legolas, a great source of amusement in the books, is not given enough of a pass. In fact, Legolas' role in this movie (I'm sure it will be expanded in the next two, but still) is merely to show off some rather keen special effects (he walks on snow, slings arrows like one of those ball delivery systems for learning tennis) and look absolutely stunningly elfishly beautiful. Unfortunate. The visit to Loth Lorien by the party reveals that the destruction of the ring will not only end the evil in Middle Earth, it will also remove from it the most valued of treasures. This is part of what makes Tolkien's stories so real; it is not all good and evil; the characters have their faults AND their virtues, consequences are not just, "do this, and we'll all live happily ever after", more, a choice between greater goods and lesser evils, with every good thing having that twinge of sadness to it that so mirrors our daily lives. Without this piece, Tolkien's work would have been just another fantasy book on the shelves, and the director's omission, though understandable, was, I believe, a poor choice.

My last beef has to do with Loth Lorien itself. Though beautiful, it felt, to me, and this is COMPLETELY subjective, to be more structured than it should be. Loth Lorien in my mind was the most organic of places, like what you might see if you looked at moss under a microscope. It's a petty beef, though.

:END OF SPOILER I think it definitely deserves best picture, as it has certainly advanced both the art and science of movie making to new heights. Also think Ian McKellen deserves a nod for his portrayal of Gandalf, and absolutely Peter Jackson deserves accolades and a statue for what he's created.

And when it comes out on DVD, I'll be sure to buy two, as I'm guaranteed to wear out the first one in nothing short of a month.

title: Captures the true essence of the books but non-readers of the books will fail to grasp this
review:
As a very longtime fan of Tolkien's work, I can genuinely say this film did not disappoint me in almost any way. True, I was surprised at a few minor details but that has more to do with my own personal interpretation of the books than any mistake made by Jackson or Walsh.

I have noted that a lot of people who have seen the film without reading the books seem to be troubled with some aspects. Many complain about the film being a typical ''Save-the-Elves'' fantasy film. What they fail to realise is that JRR Tolkien invented the fantasy genre. True, he took a lot of elements from Norse, Greek and Egyptian mythology but species that we are now accustomed to in games such as D&D such as Orcs, Elves and Dwarves were invented by Tolkien.

Another common complaint is the slightly shallow ending to FOTR. However, this mirrors Jackson's faithfulness to the book. The movie ends more or less exactly as the first book does. True, it may be disappointing not to have a more conclusive ending but it leaves many things open for the Two Towers in December 2002.

**************** SPOILERS *************** Right, now this bit is only for people who have seen the film. If you go and see it again whether you liked it or not, watch out for some minor details which enhance the quality of the whole picture.

For example, when the Fellowship passes under the two giant statues of Anarion and Elendil, look at the eyebrow of the statue on the right and you will clearly see Gollum spying down on them. If you have trouble locating him, he makes the birds fly off in fright.

Outside that, most of the acting is marvellous as most of the actors settle well into the roles. Alright, so Eiljah Wood occasionally seems somewhat wooden but at other times, he portrays Frodo's melancholy perfectly. Surprisingly, relative unknowns such as Mortensen, Bloom, Boyd and Monaghan easily rise in skill to equal or surpass in acting skill stars like Sean Bean, Tyler or Weaving.

The CGI moments on the whole were successful but the cave troll somewhat disappointed me. I don't know why but its longevity, meant to show its toughness, kinda made the whole scene childish to me.

*************End of Spoilers************

Well, that's it from me. If any fans wish to e-mail me to discuss the movie, I'll be happy to reply.

title: Saw the movie first, then read the book, and my conclusion is...
review:
...that the film is a superb achievement, a wonderful cinematic work of art.

I liked it the first time I saw it, although at 3 hours, it is incredibly exhausting for those who haven't read the book or aren't big fans. At first, when it was over, I almost felt like Jackson and his team tried to do too much with one movie.

I enjoyed it - and appreciated it - much more the second time I saw it.

Everything - cinematography, casting, acting, etc. - is first-rate.

Now, having read the book, I say: How anyone could possibly make a better film rendition of the book, I have no idea. How any Tolkien fans could be disappointed in this movie, overall, I don't understand. The film is JACKSON'S vision of Tolkien - and it is absolutely astounding at that. If you're a Tolkien fan and you don't think that Jackson's vision is the same as yours, too bad. There's only a bajillion Tolkien fans out there; kinda tough to satisfy them all. Considering that the movie can be made only one way, it's amazing what Jackson has done, and I'm glad for him that most people enjoy it. He had an incredibly - almost impossible - task before him, and he more than met it.

It must be understood that Jackson had to walk an incredible tightrope of making a good film with cinematic clarity and brevity while preserving the integrity of Tolkien's work. Practically everything he does in the movie succeeds at this, so much so that it has to be considered one of the more amazing directing jobs in film history. Taking out Tom Bombadil and so many of the songs (goodness, there are SO many songs in the book!) were deletions very necessary for the making of the film, and yet I don't think it insults Tolkien's work in the least. Honestly, considering that Jackson had to deal with Tolkien's immense imagination - once again, a feat many considered impossible - it is tough for me to think of any films that are more impressive from a purely book-to-film translation standpoint.

Contrary to some reviews on the film, the choreography of the film's fight scenes is NOT bad. Just because it doesn't adhere to the "new standards" set by The Matrix, Phantom Menace and all the stuff done by John Wu doesn't mean it was done poorly. Goodness, does EVERYTHING have to look like Charlie's Angles, Crouching Tiger, Musketeer, etc., etc.?! I found it rather refreshing that it did not.

McKellen as Gandalf is perfect - yes, PERFECT. Woods and Mortensen are also particularly outstanding, and I can't think of one weak performance by any member of the cast.

All that said, it is NOT a movie for everyone. Some people just don't like fantasy, others just don't like long movies. Others might not like how it ends (or doesn't end, rather). That said, it is THE movie within its own genre; nothing else comes close. It is to fantasy what Star Wars is to Sci-Fi, what Godfather is to the Mafia, and what Citizen Kane is to newspaper tycoons.

Like it or not, it will probably go down as one of the first important pieces of cinematic art of the 21st century. In the end, Jackson is to be commended for having the vision and creativity to produce what many, including Tolkien himself, never would have thought possible: a worthy cinematic version of "The Fellowship of the Ring."

title: Beautiful adaptation!
review: Peter Jackson made what all directors that adapts books should make: tell the story putting the atmosphere of the book in the film. I have read the book and the film is very close. You can see it without reading the book and vice-versa. One completes the other. The effects are also very good. They are so appropriate that sometimes you don't feel them happening. And this is what makes a good special effect: when it's so natural that you can't see it. The actors are perfect. Christopher Lee has a remarkable interpretation as Sauron. Great actor. I think that the other two movies should come soon. One year is too much time and it can make people lose their interest for the coming movies.

title: A stunning movie in every respect!
review: Peter Jackson got it absolutely right.  His screenplay, based upon viewing the first installment of the trilogy, is a masterful adaptation of a classic work - faithful in spirit and vision without being tediously slavish to the original text.  Add to that superb casting, wonderful production design and photography and New Zealand and the result is possibly the best movie anyone has created in the last 50 or 60 years.  Three hours passed as if they were 30 minutes and a full theatre sat in silent, rapt awe as the story unfolded before them.  A masterpiece!

title: I´m drawn to this film. It is Precious to me!
review:
Yes, I´m going to see this film for the fifth time tonight, which mean I have seen every weekend - Friday or Saturday - since the premiere. The first time I saw it I had to shut my eyes a few times, but on later viewings, knowing where it was scary, I learned to enjoy it. The film is a work of true grit, humour, and best of all, it is not commercial for expensive toys, like the latest Star Wars-movie. I look forward to sit in front row for this tonight. It came to me, me own, my love, my Pre-c-i-o-u-s.

PS: For all the Gollums who say that the film has no ending, I think you should bring som info on the production into your cave and realise that it sets up the next film, somewhat like The Empire Strikes Back

title: They did it right!
review:
Kudos all around! From acting, to directing,to special effects; everything about this movie is fantastic! This movie was done in a way to sate the appetites of Tolkien's many fans, yet thoroughly entertain the uninitiated as well. The screenplay obviously left out many things from the book, but it was done with such adroitness that none of the essential storytelling was lost.

The only thing I did not like about this movie is that I have to wait until next Christmas to see the next one!

title: Excellent movie, almost like reading the book...!!
review: If the novels that in college we have to read had a movie like this there were no necessity to read the book. This movie is almost like reading the book, great acting of Ian McKellen(Gandalf), for me he was the best, deserves and Oscar!! Also, I've read some comments about this movie is bad, but those people haven't read the book. My advice, read the book and then go to see the movie, you will give the movie 10 out of 10 as I did.

title: Delivers on every count!!!
review:
I went to see Fellowship of the Ring expecting not a great adaption of the book, but a great movie. I got it. This films success was sealed when Peter Jackson went for High Drama rather then post-modern hipness and nudge, nudge, winkm wink knowingness.

All the casting was fantastic. You really knew every characters motivations and relationships to all the other characters. The casting of Christopher Lee and Sean Bean was particularly good.

Cinematography and camerawork were perfectly suited to the epic nature of the story. Finally the pace of the film meant that when the big events came they felt like big events. Unlike so many modern films, when the finale comes in this film it feels like the finale rather then just another super edited sequence.

All in all Its not the book. But its a terrific film adaption of the book.

Go see it, so much better then the movies we are used too today.

title: both subtle and astonishing
review: Far, far better than anyone had the right to expect, Jackson's interpretation of the books (so far!) is blissfully free of the sludgy, ponderous thinking that seems to gum up most films in the fantasy genre. There's plenty here to entertain everyone; I've loved the books for years and appreciated Jackson's sensitive transmission of the story from text-narrative to film (not easy with a sprawling text like LOTR). OTOH, my best friend, who loves movies but hasn't read the books, enjoyed it immensely without feeling the loss of any of the material Jackson chose not to use. (Naturally the fans hope the DVD will restore some of that stuff, but we'll see.) The movie has humor and bite and no condescension at all. I can't imagine how Peter Jackson got away with it, but he's made a great, great film despite all the naysayers and despite Hollywood's endemic stupidity. Can't wait for the next two!

title: A superb effort. Obviously done by a fan of the books.
review: A superb effort overall. It is impossible to turn books of this depth into a commercially successful movie and be totally faithful, but this was obviously done by a fan of the books. This is the first movie I have ever gone to see twice in its first run and enjoyed it immensely both times, and wanted more. Totally pleased with cast, and interpretation of locations. I wonder why certain details were not faithful to the book such as: Aragorn with a bow and not carrying the shards of Narsil, why Legolas announced Aragorn's heritage vice Elrond, why Bilbo was not shown in the council, why the the gifts of Galadriel were not covered, why the Fellowship was broken different in many details from the book, etc., but I reserve judgment until I have seen the complete trilogy. I am hoping there will eventually be a "directors cut/long version" a la Dune on DVD of 4-5 hours per movie. I had great fear that the effort would be shoddy or fall short, to do this tale poorly would border on sacrilege to most fans. My fears were unfounded. You can't please everyone completely but I could not legitimately expect to be more pleased.

title: Easily the best fantasy film I've seen.
review: So many of the scenes in this movie were EXACTLY as I pictured them when I read the book.  I didn't think this film could ever be made to live up to my expectations.  Peter Jackson has certainly proven me wrong.  There is so much detail in this movie that many filmmakers would have overlooked.  I am thoroughly impressed by Jackson's efforts.  This is truly a lifetime achievement.

title: A beautifully constructed and visually wonderful film.
review: I have not read any Tolkien before,  so I went to see the movie with an open mind. I was blown away by the truly wonderful scenery, excellent characterization, and incredible special effects.  (How did they manage to get the Hobbits to always appear to be 2 ft. smaller than the rest of the cast?) And The music was perfect - I must get the c.d.  I am very much looking forward to the next episode.  It is a film that stays with you long after you leave the cinema.  Not a film for children, there were bits that scared me, and some very bloody battles which I would not think suitable for under 10's.  My worst nightmare was enacted - walking along a very narrow crumbling stone wall with vast chasms at either side, and the wall begins to break up -terrifying.  Romantic scenes were not too schmaltzy, and Viggo Mortensen - wow, gorgeous or what?  The best film I've seen for a long time.

title: i saw this movie 4 times already...cant wait for 2 and 3
review:
i saw this movie four times already and in all those times, i feel like im still watchin it for the first time... i didnt get sleepy or bored and i still enjoyed watchin it. well i dont know about you guys but the movie, for me, is fantastic.

some people are complaining about the ending... what part of TRILOGY dont they understand? as for me, i love the ending for FOTR. it's one of those endings that you'll never forget easily. it's a cliffhanger that makes u wanna see part 2 and 3 at once! after ive watched FOTR,i really really cant wait to see two towers and return of the king! damn it now i have to wait for so many days to watch 2 and 3!

title: Excuse me while I gush
review:
I will preface my comments by saying that I have read the books, but it has been some years since that time. While movies should be able to stand on their own regardless of the source, there is an undeniable influence when one knows the story already. Now, excuse me while I gush.

This is just a tremendous movie. The story is legendary, having influenced the entire body of work following it. The movie really brings this story to life visually. The special effects are tremendous and almost never get in the way. The casting is brilliant. The soundtrack fits so well with the movie.

The only negatives are that we have to wait until August, 2002, (reportedly) for the DVD, December, 2002, for The Two Towers, and December, 2003, for The Return of the King.

title: The Best Movie I have ever seen!
review:
Not many movies these days can touch a person so much that the world around them changes after seeing it. Truly, this movie is one of these few. And I am not just being over enthusiastic either. This movie is a very well adapted version of the book: though some parts were changed and more left out for time elapsed situations that are unavoidable, these slight differences do not change the overall effect of this film. I have seen it now for my fourth time and, unlike other movies, this one has never and will never loose its appeal.

So many things can be learned from the "Fellowship of the Ring" from just one viewing, but more can be learned on the next. For the guys in the audience the battle scenes are graphic and well done, and for the women in the audience it portrays many touching moments that personally bring me to tears. The main character, Frodo Baggins(portrayed excellently by Elijah Wood) does nothing short but marvel you with his courage that all of us wish we had. To go into a situation only to know that your life will be at stake just for the good of the many instead of the one is a message that this movie stresses throughout its 3 hours (that pass very quickly, by the way). For, as Galadriel says in the movie, "Even the smallest person can change the course of the future." Frodo helps to prove that this quote is true and gives the viewer a new sense of hope to believe and have faith in a time when darkness seems to be lurking just around the corner.

Only one bad thing: the next movie doesn't come out until next Christmas!! All in all, excellent movie, excellent actors, excellent music, excellent director, excellent morals, excellent time!!

title: No cliffhanger? So what!
review:
Fellowship of the Rings is definitely my choice for movie of the year. Having read the books in high school, I was anxious to see what Hollywood would do to this story. Most modern epic "blockbusters" have let CGI and special effects steal the show. For example, watching Star Wars' "droid wars" was like watching a Disney cartoon. The people who brought us "The Mummy Returns" were so busy with the CGI that they forgot to get two decent actors and a script. Planet of the Apes had great scenery but the main character was very boring and unlikeable.

With Lord of the Rings, you get everything you want in a great movie.

1. A great story -- unlikely hero must carry the Ring of Power to heart of all evil and destroy it 2. Visual effects -- Lush, expansive, visionary, new, etc. 3. Script -- Written with intelligence. You can tell the actors actually have something to say. 4. Acting -- No cheesy hollywood jokes for the most part. Ian McKellum and Wood were fabulous. 5. Action/suspense -- You can't get much more action packed than this.

I can't understand why the critics are so upset about the ending. Empire Strikes Back ended with Luke, Leia and the two droids looking out into space and it was the best of the Star Wars movies. Had Peter Jackson left this scene out, we would not have understood the difficult journey that lies ahead for these two unlikely heroes.

I wish Hollywood would take notes from this movie. Get rid of the cheese. Tell stories with some weight. And don't sacrifice the story for the CGI/special effects.

title: absolutely awesome
review: This movie was absolutely awesome. I had doubts about how easily they could convert it to film, seeing as the book is so detailed, but the movie was the absolute best they could have made it, I reckon. It has everything - action, adventure, romance, good versus evil, suspense, great acting. Despite being 3 hours long, I'm giving it 10/10.

title: One of the best ever made
review: Without a doubt this is one of the best movies ever made.  I have read the books many times over many years, and I cannot see a better way to make this movie.  I have met only one person who said that they did not like this film.  The costumes were wonderful.  You could tell that the film makers did their homework.  I loved Bilbo's hole, I loved the mines, and almost every set.  Every character was played to the very best of the actor's ability and you could tell that they put their hearts and souls into it.

title: Truly a Rulling Ring!
review: I have been waiting for this movie for months, and it was worth it! A magnificent film filled with something for everyone: adventure, action, romance, life lessons, tension, and colorful (sometimes cute) characters. If you haven't read the book you will see Tolkien in his best light, as he was meant to be seen. If you have read the books, be prepared to have your wildest dreams come true. Not only is the story well told, but the pictures used to tell it will leave you counting the days for the next movie. The soundtrack is also excellent, with the music carrying you into the soul of the peoples of Middle Earth. This movie deserves every nomination and award it gets!

title: Not exactly the book,but an outstanding film
review: Although this is not an exact movie version of the most widely read (and loved) work of fiction on earth, I have to give Peter Jackson an A+ for his interpretation. He certainly has the feel of the story even though there was some parts glossed over,other parts omitted  (undoubtedly due to time constraints) and some minor changes to the story and characters.If this movie has the effect of causing more than the 50 Million worldwide almost fanatical lovers of the Lord of the Rings to also read the trilogy then Peter Jackson has indeed done a great service.I highly recommend the movie, but to truly appreciate the story, read the entire trilogy and the prequel "The Hobbit".

title: This is really The Lord of the Rings
review: An excellent movie, The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring really deserves the 1st place in any movie ranking, and many awards as well. It's like a dream come true for Tolkien fans to find a movie so similar to the books. It's true, they changed some things (I wasn't very sure about Arwen saving Frodo instead of Glorfindel, but then when I watched the movie it didn't bother me at all), but still, it IS the Lord of the Rings. The introduction was amazing, and completely caught my attention, and the Balrog scene took my breath away. What a wonderful movie!! This is the sensation I wanted to fell with The Phantom Menace!! (but I didn't). I can't wait for the Two Towers (I really hope they won't change the title... as if history could be forgotten just like that...) and Return of the King!!! Absolutely 15 out of 10.

title: My new favorite movie
review: I've read the books, I've seen the film.  In a word..WOW!  LOTR:The Fellowship of the Ring, is my new favorite movie.  I was completely blown away by the characters,  the costumes, the scenery, the special effects.... I know some events and characters from the book were omitted (I'm sure because of the time factor), but the film definitely captures the essence and emotion of the book.   And, even though I knew the story, I was still enthralled with the movie - laughing, cringing, crying, as if the story was completely new to me.  I saw it with someone who had not read the books, and he said it was great!  I recommend this movie to anyone and everyone! Even if you are not a fan of fantasy, I still think you could enjoy this film. It deals so much with human qualities and emotions. There is the potential for greatness in each and every one of us.

title: Epic story telling at its best
review:
J.R.R. Tolkeins books were the first fantasy books I read as a young teenager. At that time, it was a slog to get through the books, and it put me off fantasy for about 5 years. However, I wasn't going to deny myself the film version 20 years later, and this film is a masterpiece!

Throughout the entire film, I didn't want it to end, even when I was begining to fidget (thank goodness for stadium seating being the norm nowadays!). When it did end, the film still haunted my mind and thoughts a week later, so I went and saw it again - a first for 3 hour films and me! Although the special effects seemed to leach the colour from our star actors from the moment their quest began (the only thing that irritated me...), the story is a powerful one and I found it impossible to not be sucked into the whole story. The actors were marvelous, but Ian McKellen as Gandalf deserves to be singled out for praise - his best performance yet! I was also glad that Elijah Wood got the role of Frodo - he is very good in it.

Nowadays it is rare that Hollywood produces a movie with a real story instead of some marketing approved concept - but thank goodness approval was given for this attempt for Peter Jackson to go ahead with his version. I would suspect this will not be surpassed until 3-D/interactive movies are made in the future...

An absolute must see for its sheer ability to sweep you into the story. How, I ask you, can we wait for the two sequel films?!

title: A Breathtaking movie--especially if you haven't read the book
review:
Excellent Movie! It has everything you could ever ask for in a fantasy epic (or any other epic for that matter). I think it's even better if you've never read the book or if you haven't in a long time, because you won't have the tendency to pick on what's different or missing (which believe me...not much was left out!!)

The real star in this movie was the cinematography and the art and set decoration! UNREAL! Also...there was REAL MEAT in this movie...not just one conflict/one battle/one message. You felt like you actually LIVED in Middle Earth for 3 hours!!

The only drawback--you have to wait until NEXT YEAR to see the next chapter!! GRRR!!!! I've even read the books too!! :)

title: It's hard for me to say this...
review:
Alright, listen: I'll admit, I'm a Star Wars geek.

I saw "Phantom Menace" 4 times in theaters and own the DVD and all the Special Edition VHSs. But then I saw "Fellowship of the Rings" on opening day. And it seems all that changed. Star Wars will always have a special place in my heart, but this ONE MOVIE beats them all.

As I said, it's hard for me to say this...

But having not read the books and not even knowing much of the basic plot, I went into this movie with open eyes. And I was totally blown away. I figured LOTR was kid-friendly, with cute little hobbits and dwarves and such. But the movie was so DARK! It's a tale of temptation, of power, of emotion. Not a corny "Harry Potter" (which I saw only for the Episode 2 trailer), but something that pulls at the heartstrings and makes you think. Not only is the plot excellent, but the special effects and acting are extraordinary. I still don't fully understand how they made the hobbits so short (but that will be answered on the DVD, i bet), and I could only find a few obviously bad effects (Frodo in the Council of Elrond). There is only one word to describe the battle sequences: INTENSE. It's just so fast and I don't know how they didn't hurt anybody. I've seen the movie three times and the ending still gets to me.

I don't know. It may be my age (I just turned 18), it may be the changed world, but Star Wars seems a little childish. Don't get me wrong, I'm still excited about "Attack of the Clones", but not in the same sence, nor with the anticipation I have for "The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers."

title: Unexpected, but hoped for
review:
If asked which books I'd take with me on a lonely island, the "Lord of the Rings" would certainly be one of them. I've read and re-read Tolkien's works over and over again and by now I have a pretty clear picture of what Middle Earth is "supposed" to look like (for me, at least). All the more I was anxious to see the movie, not because of the story, but because of the adaptation. And while the movie may or may nor be one of the greatest movies of all time, it is definitively one of the best literature adaptations of all time. The Shire looks lively and "lived in", Bag End presents a warmth and charm that made me want to move in and Gandalf... well, Gandalf is just the way I remember and envision him myself (and many other fans of the book, I guess). McKeller has done an amazing job! My personal hope was not to be disappointed (high expectations). And I wasn't! I had a fantastic time watching it and I am looking forward to Part II and III.

Attention Spoiler:

I have missed the original form of the poem. The adaptation was adequate, but still... Three Rings for the Elven-kings under the sky... unbeatable!

title: 2 cents worth...Fantastic.
review: Quite true to the book in most respects. Some things were exactly as I imagined them to be. A fan's movie, and definitely not for kids under 13. It's hard to understate how impressed I was with this film. Remarkable. It'll be hard to wait a whole year for the next.

title: It's nice to be able to escape our world for 3 hours and visit someplace magical.
review: At first I did not think that I would enjoy this movie.  I had never read the books nor had any idea what the story was about and to be quite honest I really don't like movies that make me have to think too much.  But I figured "Oh well, if anything the special effects must be good".  Within seconds I was completely drawn into the story.  It was beautiful visually and the story line was intriguing.  I actually began to care about these fictional beings.  I felt as if I were traveling with them on this heroic journey and I found myself applauding their victories and mourning their defeats. Like I said, "I usually don't watch these kind of movies", but now I cannot wait until the next chapter of this story is told.  I truly enjoy being able to lose myself for a few hours and enter into a fantasy world full of hope and wonder before having to enter back into reality.  I thank all of you who brought this beautiful story to life.

title: Fantastic in every aspect
review: Wow....that about sums it up. Is there anything wrong with this film at all? Everything just falls into place so perfectly, and the casting could not have been more inspired. Of course, I do wish there was a spot in there for the completely underused yet wonderfully talented British actor Jason Carter, who would've made a stunning Aragorn, but Viggo Mortensen is great in the role too. Elijah Wood has grown tremendously as an actor over the years, and I can't wait to see what else is on store for us as the story continues on the big screen.

title: Pretty like the book...
review:
For those to read and loved the book, a few scenes are missing. For those who didn't, the story is pretty understandable. The F/X are superb, the make-ups are amazing (the Uruk-Hai really impresses), the battle scenes are full of great action, there is romance, scary parts, drama, fun...

What can you wish more?

title: Cinematography is one key to the success of the film
review:
... that is, in my opinion. Do you notice the camera shots? Pretty old-school, huh? No crazy jumpcuts, or strange angles, here. Shots are composed in a quiet manner, with sometimes only a zoom-in for effect (example: drawing in on the ring on a table, signifying the malice it contains without any special effects whatsoever - yet I expected something frightening to happen, all the same).

What this does is draw the viewer in to the film in a very successful, subliminal way. Almost a first-person view, still and quiet and allowing our eyes to fully focus on things. Sure, it made the special effects easier to add into shots, but more importantly, it allowed the story itself to shine through - not a lot of tricky camera angles. Just like the musical score, the shots did not even try to overpower the movie itself, and I really liked that!

What a grand movie! Well-crafted and satisfying!

title: Amazing!
review: There's is only one word to describe what Jackson has done with the world's greatest ever fantasy book: AMAZING. You can take your Harry Potter memorabilia and throw it away because Lord of The Rings is here to stay. The scenery in each scene is magnificent and the acting and costumes impeccable. Roll on "The Two Towers"!!!

title: An experience that will change your life
review: Whether you like Tolkien's world or not this astonishing film will change the course of your like...you'll become an addicted to the world of the elves and you will live forever among them...in the woods... Furthermore the film has put through , as the book meant , many many warning....the effects of power on people..and to respect Mother Nature. Go and see by yourselves...and beware...don't ever...ever take the ruling ring.

title: The Power of The Ring
review:
This film, to me, is the best film ever made. I have been totally taken in by it's magic and have had to go and buy quite a lot of merchandise to satisfy my hunger for seeing it again.

I have seen it twice and I am going to see it again next week. I cannot wait until it comes out on DVD so I can see it always.

Don't really know how I'm going to last until the next installment of the trilogy hopefully site like this and all the publicity will continue to help.

title: staggering, and hauntingly formative film
review: I was never really a fan of the novels. Yet, in the hands of Peter Jackson, I can now see why so many others are. Jackson takes liberties to tell the story and give it meaning; about humanity, and greed. Crafting a different ending, and a terrific feel it is one of the greatest directing jobs of a book that I have ever seen.

title: It's all been said - great movie
review:
Good story, good direction, good acting and good scenery. Originally from NZ, I can't help but feel some ownership (however unjustified) of this film, growing up as I did not far away from where several scenes were filmed, and of course being a fan of Peter Jackson from his early works (Brain Dead et al). Happy to see success where it is deserved, if slightly unexpected. Will definitely see it again soon, and probably also again before #2 comes along. Bring on the Director's Cut DVD!!

10/10

title: my view of the film
review: this was one of the best films that I have seen in the last couple of years. having read the hobbit, and over a period of years read the trilogy of the lord of the rings. not in my case an easy book to read but worth the effort. I was amazed at the way the film mirrored my thoughts on all the characters and scenes. definitely not an easy job considering the power of our imagination. special mention to the actors and special effects brill.............  have no hesitation in recommending this movie. maybe a bit much for the under 12's to sit through.

title: Greatest movie of all times!
review: This is by far the best movie I have ever seen. There are no significant flaws, even after seen the movie several times. It is the only movie I have seen that lasts nearly 3 hours, but do not have 1 boring second in it. The very next day, I went straight to the bookstore and got the book (also worth reading). If you are going to see one movie this year, make  sure this is the one!

title: Clear amazement...
review: The LOTR movie is simply brilliant. Three hours of both pure beauty of the nature and story and unceasing action without "deaf spaces". Some scenes are terrifying and it won't be strange if you'll find yourself covering your eyes. The Ringwraiths, the Cave Troll, the Skurut-Hai, the Balrog - they all are worth acting in your nightmare. Well, Arwen is a small flaw on the bright surface of its perfection, but it is not so serious. If you want it (and I believe you do), go and see it...

title: Go out there and watch it!!
review:
Let me just say; there aren't words enough to describe it...

They've made the impossible - they made the film almost as good as the book (specially if you've read the books) Of course, they haven't got it all in there.. the film should have been about 15 hours or so, but I mean.. That wouldn't be that popular, would it?

You've just have to see this movie, and do it before you miss the chance to do it at the theatre... well go on!!

title: Excellent, Middle Earth lives on...
review:
I was so worried about this film when I heard about it being made. I have read and re-read the Lord of the Rings trilogy many times and I feared that the fine prose of Tolkien would be reduced to the not-so-fine level of Hollywood-esque action blockbuster. I didn't know anything about (director) Jackson and I had a bad feeling that the trilogy might end up looking like 'The Mummy Returns' or completely sap-a-fied like 'Titanic'. Well I am happy to say that I was wrong and Mr. Jackson turned out the best film I've seen in years. I left this movie feeling like I did when I first saw 'Star Wars' in 1977... refreshed, amazed and happy to be alive. The film is utterly flawless, it slightly deviates from the book at times and cuts a few characters like Tom Bombadil but the film breathes the spirit of the book, heavily. I loved it, I give it a 10 out of 10.

Here is a side note: When my girlfriend and I were leaving the theater a group of kids maybe 10 or 11 years old were talking outside with great fervor. One kid exclaimed "I've already started the Two Towers!" and the other kids knew what he meant. I was very happy to see that.

title: Best movie I've seen this year and for awhile
review:
2001 was a horrible year for movies. It brought forth movie like Fast and the Furious, Tomb Raider, Freddy Got Fingered, Final Fantasy, Kiss of The Dragon, Not Another Teen Movie, and Pearl Harbor. These movie made me stay away from my local theater, and forced me to revisit old classics like Godfather and The Shawshank Redemption as a reminder of how good movies can be. Sure there were some gems like Memento and Monsters Inc., yet over all, it was a depressing year for movies. Then came Lord of the Rings.

This movie came as a surprised to me. I was hesitant at first to like it, because of the hype surrounding the movie and mostly because of my own high expectations. I read the books and enjoyed them immensely, yet I expected the movie to be mediocre at it's best. Lord of The Rings not only surprised me, it reminded me of why I go to the movies in the first place. The characters were not bland or dull because the actors put their hearts into their roles. I find myself cheering for them, feeling their pain, their follies, and their triumphs. I find myself immersed in this world created by Peter Jackson, and not wanting to go back to this dreary and ignorant world created by reality. The story was epic and imposing, involving and intriguing. But more importantly, I enjoyed the movie and found myself seeing it again.

This movie didn't hide behind shoddy story, obnoxious characters, or hype. It weaved a tale of individuals opposing a terrible force that threatened their homes, their loved ones and their way of life. I feel sorry for those who can't enjoy this movie. I pity those who don't have enough imagination to appreciate a movie as grand and fantastic as this. Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is the best movie this year because it was not some typical Hollywood special effects extravaganza, but because it had heart. It is a thing missing in most of this year's movies. I give it a 11 out of 10.

title: What entertainment is all about.
review: On the odd occasion I visit the cinema to pay their exorbitant prices for several reasons. To be entertained.To escape from a familiar world to an unknown dimension. To be diverted from the usual mundane cares of earning a living, etc etc. LOTR did this for me in no uncertain terms. I say this unequivocably despite the fact of having been filmed in this lovely land of ours-the NZ landscape never looked so beautiful. Enough has been said about the acting the script the costumes & scenery and I will not belabour the point.But it has been gratifying to read all these positive reviews for a nz made film which has obviously left its mark on so many viewers at this the dawn of the 21st century.Only time will tell if it will live up to those remarks in posterity and not just the box office.

title: It just doesn't get any better than this
review: When I was a child I remember listening to the serialised story on BBC radio and was enthralled. In my imagination I could picture all the characters and locations vividly. Years later the same happened when I read the book. I came to the movie with a little trepidation because it is so easy to be disappointed when you have such strong preconceptions. I was so stunned to see that somebody else must have had exactly the same 'vision' as me because I couldn't tell you one thing that I would have changed...maybe the 'monsters' were a little scarier but the dark riders in particular took me right back to my childhood kitchen with the open fire my mother cooking while I listened to the story on the radio... What pleased me above all was the reaction of the audience. It is a long time since I have heared so many gasps, sighs, cheers and just total absorption by people of all ages but especially the usually so cynical teenagers. Maybe they should make Tolkien compulsory reading in schools.

title: A landmark movie
review:
I was hesitant to see this movie, due to the building hype. The trailers were so excellent, I almost *knew* I would be disappointed. I wasn't, however. I was enthralled... stapled to my seat... feeling my eyes dry out because I didn't want to blink.

I hate to sound like I'm gushing... normally, I'm very picky. However, this movie was over the top in so many ways that it was simply overwhelming. I've read the books, but I did not go to see the book. I went to see a movie based on the books. It did wonderfully in that. The changes/cuts made were immaterial in the end.

The movie itself was truly amazing. The visuals alone were enough to overwhelm the senses. In the face of every carefully chosen and tended location, one felt small, as if caught up in another reality. From the peace of Hobbiton to the peak of Mt. Doom, every scene was unearthly and supremely done.

The actors were well chosen. They carried their roles well enough to never really jar the senses... they maintained the crucial suspension of disbelief. One never thinks about their acting, and they were a good visual compliment to their attitudes. I expected some groaners, but they did suprisingly well. The only one that came close was Elrond, but just force yourself to forget The Matrix, and you'll find him a pleasingly plausible elf-king.

The plot? What can I say? It's Tolkien. It's nice to see a movie go back to good vs. evil for once. It's been a long time since we've been allowed to just sit and watch good guys and bad guys go at it, and not worry about who's who and why they do what they do. This is a movie, despite some moments of violent combat, that a reasonable child should be able to enjoy along with their family.

All in all, this movie is excellent. Fantastic. Wonderful. A bunch of other adjectives I'm not going to bother listing for now. I loved it, and will probably see it yet again before it leaves the theater. Go see it. If you're disappointed, it's because you want to be.

title: An arresting masterpiece (some spoilers)
review:
SPOILERS, though only a few.

I'm partly getting frustrated, having seen the film, about not being able to tell anyone else about it! After all, most people don't want the surprise spoiled.

But in answer to that - what surprise? Nearly everyone I know has read all the books, some of them many times. All I need say is that the film is very faithful to the first book of the series and they should rejoice in the film itself. The film must be, as it was for me, not a revelation of the story, but a revisiting of the story. You know the plot in advance. Not that you must. I have tried to think about it from the point of view of one who has not read the books, nor spoken to someone who has; my wife and I discussed the efficient way the story's background is built into the film. There's a kind of historical prologue at the start which, to the credit of the film's makers, serves not only the purpose of describing the world of Middle Earth, but also projects the audience into the story and is monumentally cinematic in its own right. So even if the background is familiar, you lose nothing by watching the prologue.

Some of the images are ... astonishing. The Fellowship flees Saruman through mines of Moria. The crazy, Escher architecture created by Dwarves and the film's designers who, in turn, created the Dwarves would have been rich enough supposing the mines were occupied by Gimli's 'ale-swilling' relatives. But the film shows Moria in ruins and the audience learns about the fragility of all civilisations, however great their art. I have never been so totally arrested by an image in a film as I was by cathedral-like Moria - save by another one a little later in the same film. The Fellowship canoes down the river Anduin near the end of the film, and they pass through a gorge guarded by two huge and enigmatic statues of ancient kings. Ozymandias by another name.
