review: I didn't think it could ever be done, but Peter Jackson and Co. have recreated the magic of Middle Earth.  I was glued to the screen for the entire 3 hours.  It was the most amazing spectacle of a movie that I have ever seen.

title: A masterpiece in it's time
review:
First I will warn you that I am a Tolkien nut. I've been through the stories of the LOTR in every way so many times I count count. Whether it be the books, the cartoons(lol), the radio broadcasts (minds eye and bbc versions), computer games, you name it. Now I, as everyone else had reservations about what might have gotten messed with as far as story line. But I can now tell you that I have just witnessed the movie event of my life. I have seen Lawrence of Arabia on the big screen and sat in wonder and awe, I can now say the same for LOTR. Those who wonder if the film should be seen, please do see it.

The biggest gripe I have?

******* SPOILER ********

It's so small that most people won't have noticed, but the weapons from the *dozens* of orc weapons that Boromir killed before his death were not included with his body when sent down the river. So being of a serious Tolkien background, and this is my biggest gripe, understand that this movie was fantastic!

title: Boring for those who have not read the books
review:
The first LOTR installment left too many plot lines unexplained, too many characters appearing without contributing to the story. Too much of the richness of the book itself was introduced in a slipshod manner, with the assumption that the movie viewer can makes sense of the bits and pieces and see the larger picture.

To compound the problem, so many plot points, characters - and even the mythology of LOTR - have been stolen and used ad nauseum in other books and movies that the modern viewer would find LOTR uninspired.

This movie should have come out 20 years ago.

Finally, many who do not know the full extent of the trilogy will be sorely disappointed with the ending of part 1.

My advice: read the books instead.

title: One of the Greatest Movies I have seen in a Long Time
review: What can I say this movie was fantastic! I admit I have never read the books but that is what make this movie great. One does not have to read the books to follow the story. As a history buff, I did relize to setting for the story was during the dark ages between the fall of the Roman Empire and the age of enlightment. No time in the film that this was more evident than when the group was going down the river passing the two huge statues. The similarties between the guardians and the roman legions were stunning. As far as those folks, comparing this to Harry Potter let me say this. Forget it! Lord of the Rings is by far superior.

title: Star Wars Comparison
review: I saw Fellowship a couple of weeks ago and it's still on my mind.  I was walking out of the theater and one of my best friend's said "This must have what it had been like if you saw Star Wars in 1976."  I couldn't argue it. It's something I haven't seen in a long time and I can't wait to see it again

title: Marvelous adaptation
review: For any purists who are prejudiced against any version changing Tolkien's words like I was, the only way you can enjoy it is to let yourself enjoy it. There are many changes, some minor, some fairly major.  Overall, though, this is undoubtedly the best live-action adaptation of the greatest fantasy epic there ever will be, so you might as well allow yourself to enjoy what's there, privately rue the changes, but don't let them take away from the great adaptation on screen.  It is a wonderful, awesome adaptation. Enjoy.

title: The best adventure film in years
review:
I've been reading for a while the user comments about this film (wow, they are already more than 400!) and in general, I don't agree with the opinions of those who disliked it.

Half of the people who didn't like the movie say it was perfect as a film but bad compared to the book; the other half says that they liked the movie only because they had read the book, but as a film it was real bad. To me, that proves that they are all wrong. The movie is good (very good) as a film, and it has all the essence of the book.

I agree that in the book you get to know the characters in much more depth, but I think the movie has a good balance between character and environment description. Yeah, right, it could be better in the character department, but it is really good as it is. No movie is perfect, you know.

After reading the user comments, I went to vote for it (gave it a 10) and, well, I'll tell you what I saw: at the moment of writing this comment, more than 6500 people have voted for the film and 80% of them have given it a 10/10! If that isn't special, I don't know what could be.

I've written enough. As many say, you should go and see it, that's the only way you'll really see if it's as good as I say. If you've never liked an adventure film, I don't think this movie will change your mind; but if you ever liked Star Wars, or Star trek, or Indiana Jones, or any pirates or medieval film, any kind of adventure film, I'm sure you'll enjoy The Fellowship of the Ring as much as I did.

Can't wait for the second and third films!

title: ...Wow.
review: In my opinion, this movie captured the entire spirit of The Fellowship of the Ring. It basically stuck to fact (EVEN though Lady Arwen was not nearly as important, and they left out Tome Bombadil) and stuck even more to the soul of Tolkien's classic. I rate this movie a ten

title: Excellent or Good, Have You Read the Books?
review: The Lord of the Rings is all in all a "good" movie.  For those viewers who have not ever read the books I believe it will be a wonderous tale and a feast for your senses.  On the other hand, for those of us who have read the books numerous times and are enthralled with Tolkien's tale, the movie will be decent, but lackluster.  The rich imagery and the little details that set the series apart are not there.  Having read the novels I found myself in the theater thinking, "Hey, what about this part, or they left that out, that sucks."  While it was interesting to watch my imagination played before me, I left the movie feeling that the characters were shallow and not developed enough.  There are exceptions, for instance Sam is the same in the books and in the movie - kudos to Sean Astin - but I believe that several of the other characters were given a different feel and persona.  In summary I say, "Excellent film I you haven't read the books, Good if you have."

title: a m a z i n g
review: my heart nearly exploded, when I entered the cinema. my expectations were huge and I was afraid that this movie will not be able to fullfil them. BUT IT DID. this is one of the best movies I have ever seen. wow. incredible. I can t wait to see the two towers, and the return of the king. FRODO ROCKS

title: At times beautiful, at others a cheapening of a great work
review: The Fellowship of the Ring can best be described as a beautiful film, but at the same time as a missed opportunity at bringing the true feeling of the book to the screen.  Now, it must be said that no film could ever have the depth inherent in the book - the layers and richness in The Lord of the Rings go far beyond the capabilities of film.  Likewise, it would be impossible to fit every chapter of the book into the film and still have a coherent movie, so Peter Jackson was justified in cutting some parts for his interpretation. That said, Peter Jackson's The Fellowship of the Ring could have been much better.  I agree that the characters are wonderfully cast and acted, but the mood of the book is missing in many parts.  Too often, there is reliance on action, and a simplifying of the text.  It is at these junctures that the film falls to the level of typical Hollywood crap.  And it is so sad to see this, when, at other times, some of the beauty and sadness of the book are there. Often the landscapes too, are not right. Not every scene in the book is set on or surrounded by mountains. All in all, there is too much action and not enough focus on the quiet, potent places of Tolkien's world.

title: Mere words fail.
review:
Have seen it twice. Will see it several more times, at least.

Every criticism I've come up with is trivial compared to the scope of what was achieved.

3/4 of Lorian is probably on the cutting room floor. Gimli's best scene in Fellowship, is with Galadriel, for instance. No lembas (elven waybread), no elven cloaks (though the fellowship was wearing them when they left) and a bare mention of the phial.

I can't recall any "added" plot elements. Jackson didn't base the movie on "The Lord of the Rings", he seems to have based it on "The Red Book of West March", "Unfinished Tales", "The Similrillion" and the appendix in the back of the Fellowship.

I found the additional Arwen scenes took nothing away from the heart of the story.

Personally I would have liked Saruman to have been a "counterpoint" to Sauron rather than a lackey.

Perhaps Fellowship should have been two films instead of one, though I would have, happily, sat through a 4.5 hour movie.

Regardless, not since "Gone with the Wind" has a movie been so faithful to its source. 62 years is a long time to wait for a movie to NOT destroy the story it is based on.

One of the best movies I've ever seen. Much better than Star Wars. Ranks up there with "The 10 Commandments", "Ben Hur", "The Wizard of OZ", "Citizen Kane" and "The African Queen". It could be, when the others are released, that LOTR will be the greatest epic saga ever filmed. Time will tell.

Your Grandchildren might well be in awe of you and your children for being amongst the first EVER to see the film, much like the awe you at 8 or 10 would have held for someone who saw "The Wizard of OZ" or "Gone with the Wind" on opening day.

The critical vocabulary does not yet exist to describe LOTR. "Instant classic" does not fully describe it. This is the first "new" film to be made in 85 years and may well re-define how we think about films.

title: Absolute best film of 2001
review:
Seen it 3 times! What a great epos! This is everything beyond my imagination. I did expect something big, but not as big like this! Just wow!

Absolutely best film of 2001!

title: Excellent
review:
I went and saw it the Friday after it opened. I had reservations as to how true it could stay to the book. While it did not cover all aspects of the "The Fellowship of the Ring" it remained an excellent adaptation of the book.

First movie I have ever been to where the audience applauded at the end.

My son and I went back and saw it again yesterday. The first time I have ever gone back and paid to see a movie in a theater. Was just as good the second time as the first.

Now if only I didn't have to wait two years for "The Return of the King."

title: not worth the hype
review: The movie, while entertaining, was disappointing given the hype around it. Several have said this would be the "picture of the year."  I doubt it. While there is a lot to tell, the movie seemed to go for a long time.  The character development seemed a bit shallow.  The timing of events and moods seemed a bit off.

title: This movie is a landmark, an extraordinary moviegoing experience
review: WOW! Ever since I was six years old (ten years ago) and my mom read to me Lord of the Rings, and i saw the cartoons, I was desperate for there to be a live action movie made.  Now that I have seen this masterpiece I am thrilled that a book that means so much to me can come off so good.  When I knew the movie was being made, I decided that I would like the movie no questions asked.  However, as the release date approached I had concerns over how the story would be changed and edited.  HOWEVER, go into this movie knowing that this is an INTERPRETATION of FOTR, not the actual book.  If you watch it with that attitude, you will realize how amazing this movie is.  It is definitely one of my favorite movies of all time, and a landmark in movie history.

title: The Greatest Movie of All Time PERIOD!
review:
This is the greatest movie of all time PERIOD!

Nothing even comes remotely close to this cinematic masterpiece.

The Fellowship of the Ring makes The Godfather look like a cheesy episode of Sopranos and Star Wars look like Pokemon trash.

The acting was superb, the settings amazing, and the special effects top notch. The Balrog is the greatest moment ever seen on screen in the young history of CGI.

Am sure there are few people who wont like it because its 3 hours long, but those are the type of ignorant people who like movies like scream and scary movie, and enjoy 90 minutes of trash with no character development and useful dialog. So pay no heed to those types.

This movie has Oscar written all over it.

Gollum was everything we hoped for and Liv Tyler was perfect for Arwen. The best moment of the movie aside from the Balrog was when they showed Gollum being tortured by Orcs in Mordor. Brilliant.

The Soundtrack was also superb. Chalk up another Oscar in that department.

The combat scenes were some of the best ever seen on screen, sword fighting and archery at its best. Moria was worth the price of admission alone.

My only complaint "and its a small one" is that the movie moved too fast at times. This movie really need to be 4 hours long, as lots of little things were left out from the book, and not enough time was spent in Rivendale and Lorien. Some scenes needed to be played out slower than they were. But the good news is that Jackson has promised 27 minutes of additional cut footage to be included on the Dvd this summer. This movie will just get better and better....and then next year we have part II! Pure Bliss.

Bottom line...

GO SEE THIS MOVIE!!!!!

First timers will like it just as much as fans of the book do. Cinema does not get any better than this.

This movie is so great that is pushes Empire Strikes Back from a 9 to a 7 because ESB is not worthy enough to be one number below FoTR's 10.

10/10 Stars

title: Breathtaking view into Science Fiction
review: This film is one of those landmark films that will undoubtedly go down in history as one of the most thrilling and spectacular films. The fact that they had amazing effects, but that it did not take away from the magical story which they so beautifully brought to life. I would recommend this movie to anyone and everyone.

title: Unbelievably Great!
review:
This movie brought me to tears and it wasn't at the end where they might be expected. It was in the very beginning when they were in the Shire. It was so beautiful and so "right"... all through the movie I was nodding to myself as scene after scene played out as I imagined them... even more real then in my head. Maybe it was helped along by a sense of nostalgia since I haven't read the books in almost 25 years, but at that time I read them over 7 times and as a teenager I had my walls plastered with previous years calendar pictures... let's just say that I was a big fan of the books.

But the movie only added to all this... made it better and more real. I will watch this again when my 19 year old son comes home for Christmas, I am sure that he will have seen it at least once by then as well. Great movie. Touched me deeply. See it, even if you haven't read the books. It is amazing.

title: Read the book, then see the movie
review:
Awesome doesn't do this film justice. It is one of the best movies I have ever seen. However, if you don't read the book first, you might feel a little lost. There isn't much character development, so knowing who everyone is before hand will make the film much better. The movie does stray somewhat from the book, and leaves quite a bit out, but nothing too important. It also has some material that will make it flow better with the other two movies (like stuff you would have found out later anyways in the book, but this way you don't have to wait two years), and some of the story is changed for more continuity. What they did change does not hurt the story whatsoever.

If you see it without having read it, don't bother giving it a lower rating, you aren't worthy.

title: Bestow upon a new epic
review:
The first of the trilogy begins. Not only is it spellbounding, but it catches the soul. It holds a moral we all should receive. You'll have to see the movie to find it. All of the actors were superb. I couldn't pick a better cast. Gandalf was my favorite. Second came all the hobbits. Then, the rest. And if you're choosing between what to see first Harry Potter or Lord of the Rings, well see this first (then Harry if you got the time).

Let me tell you, this movie had it all. A great plot, a geat cast, and a beautiful scenery (New Zealand). I recommend this to the fullest. Let the journey begin.

title: An incredible ride through a fantasy world with adventure that never stalls!
review: I will have to say that maybe, maybe, you have to be a fan of sorcery and magic to appreciate this movie, but I say anyone with an imagination and a taste for adventure will thoroughly enjoy FOTR.  From the moment the movie started I was at aww with everything that graced the screen.  I felt as though I was a little kid again as I sat on the edge of my seat, trying not to blink, in anticipation of what may come next.  The visual aspect of FOTR is breathtaking.  Your fantasy has become reality by using the wonders of CGI.  Let me just say that Ian McKellen (Gandolf) is absolutely amazing. He draws you into the story and has you wishing you could be just as "magical" as he is.  Yes, it is three hours, but it is three hours of adventure from start to finish.  You leave the theater wanting more and wishing you were three and a half feet tall, or had pointed ears, or had a long grey beard. Any way you look at it, this is one of the best stories ever written and it has gone down in my book as one of the best movies I have ever seen.

title: Why have people not liked this movie
review:
I have some of the comments on here about Jackson ruining LOTR. I think nothing could be further from the truth. This movie is in my personal top five, along with Braveheart, Schindler's List and Star Wars. It may not have been perfection, but it came real close. A definite Oscar Winner in the technical areas and I believe should receive Best Picture and Director. It was phenomenal to the Nth Degree. The parts left out were not necessary to the plot. The parts left in were shot beautifully and concisely. Bravo to Mr. Jackson and the cast and crew. I cannot wait for Christmas 2002.

Ahhh 2002. 2 Episode 2s to look forward to.

title: A Wonderful Film.
review: New Line Cinema should be tossing rose petals at Peter Jackson's feet.  A great piece of filmmaking that still lingers in my mind.  Compare it to the sterile "Star Wars:  Episode One" and the achievement is all the better.  I can't wait to see it again.  It's the best of the year.

title: No one could have done it better
review: This movie was great.  I am a huge Tolkien fan and I have been looking forward to this movie for years.  I have seen the movies twice and I highly recommend that others do the same.  I liked it better the second time because I felt like I wasn't critiquing the movie as much and I could just enjoy it.  It wasn't a perfect movie and it wasn't a perfect adaptation of the books, but nothing could ever live up to what I consider to be the best books written by a human author of all time.  Peter Jackson, the cast, and the crew really did a stellar job on this one.  With such a short time to work with they brought forth the main themes of the book, developed the main characters very well, and showed incredible attention to detail.  The whole time I kept wishing they could slow down and show more but I realized in order to make it watchable in a theater they had to keep things moving.  I really hope that the DVD includes a little more footage to help flesh out the story even more.  I thought the omissions from the book were necessary and I think they made the right choices.  The cast really fit my ideas of the characters and the acting altogether was great.  Ian McKellen as Gandalf and Sean Bean as Boromir really stand out in my mind.  I wish they had more time to flesh out some of the minor characters such as Gimli and Legolas as well as the hobbits but you can't have everything in a three hour movie.  I am a huge Star Wars fan but I still think that these special effects were the best I have ever seen.  The Massive battle scenes as well as the CGI characters were utterly astonishing.  But like I stated above, the movie wasn't perfect.  The imperfections though were mainly conflicts with my interpretation of the books.  The Lothlorien sequence I thought was too short and Galadriel went way too crazy.  The other minor imperfections are far outweighed by the combination of the great acting, excellent special effects, strong story line, splendid score, and all around entertainment, and that is what a movie is about, entertainment.  I am so looking forward to the conclusion of this story and I am so glad that the group that put this movie together has done all the movies because I don't think anyone could have done it better.

title: One of the best films I have ever seen.
review: I can't explain to you the feeling I had when I first saw this film.  It came out yesterday and I have already seen it three times.  Forget about Episode 2 & 3, I am sooooooooooooo excited for Two Towers & Return of the King.  Peter Jackson=GENIUS.  He interpreted Tolkien's masterpiece of fiction better than anyone could've ever done it.  If you haven't seen Jackson's HEAVENLY CREATURES, see it now!  Also great are DEAD ALIVE (a.k.a. BRAINDEAD) and THE FRIGHTENERS and MEET THE FEEBLES!  See them all!!!! This film deserves Best Picture, Best Score, Best Cinematography, Best Production Design, Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Actor Ian McKellan, and many more at the oscars next year!

title: Forget all precedents: this is unlike anything you have ever seen...
review:
I went seeing 'The Lord of The Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring' yesterday during a special midnight premiere. And it's hard seeing a 3-hour movie starting at 0.30. But it kept my attention away from fatigue...

'The Fellowship' is a masterpiece... Peter Jackson is a great choice since he apparently honors the novel...

So I am not going to tell you what this movie is like in detail: just go see it for yourself.

The CGI is amazing. Gollum (or what you see of him) is very realistic and so are the monsters, sets, backgrounds, battles. The make-up and costumes are breathtaking, so is the attention for detail, like Arwen's elf-language, props and the detail of the story. The actors are perfectly casted especially Wood as Frodo and McKellen as Gandalf. Teh scenery is diverse and suiting the novel.

I have only one complaint which is the sudden end of the movie. I know I was seeing it for 3 hours but I can't believe I have to wait one full year to see how it continues. This might be a spoiler but the endiing is rather abrupt... there is no climax or anything whatsoever. I would have preferred (THIS IS A SPOILER!) that the movie stopped when Frodo was holding his ring (right after Boromir died), tears in his eyes saying something like: "I wished I never found this ring"...

title: Excellent - the best literary adaptation I've seen.
review:
As long as you regard it as an adaptation, this is just truly an amazing work. I don't think there's ever been a movie that is simply as...epic as this.

A "purist" will find some things to nitpick, and not every scene was adapted the way I would choose to - but every scene made sense; the work holds true to the spirit of the novel remarkably.

Effects were amazing, acting superb, and the score was one of the best I've ever heard.

People have compared it to Star Wars and various other classics, but I'm not sure that Fellowship isn't as unprecedented as Star Wars was in its day.

title: A very impressive and captivating movie
review:
At first I was apprehensive about this movie because of the tremendous media hype, but after seeing it I'm convinced that the praise it has received is not exaggerated. If the other movies in the trilogy are as good as this one, it certainly deserves to be regarded as one of the classics of movie history. The actors are brilliant (especially Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen, Christopher Lee and Sean Bean), the scenery is stunning and the special effects are very impressive.

Despite the length - three hours - it never feels tedious. To be frank, the movie is so captivating that I couldn't help feeling slightly disappointed when it eventually came to an end. I could have sat in the cinema all day watching the story unfold.

Unlike most people I know, I've never gotten around to reading Tolkien's 'Lord of the Rings', the trilogy that these movies are based upon. I've made a few attempts, but I've found the sheer size of the work discouraging. I've been recommended to read the books before watching the movie; I suppose it would have enhanced the experience if I had, but I had no problem enjoying the movie anyway. In fact, it has made me curious about reading the books.

title: Masterpiece
review: Easily the most visually stunning film of the year, the special effects are worth the admission price alone.  Yet even more remarkable is the success with which Jackson and his team have managed the process of adaptation. This has been achieved through two things.  First, casting and performances which are utterly flawless, perfectly capturing the essence of the characters  the loving warmth of the hobbits, the isolated nobility of Aragorn, and the tragic weakness of Boromir.  Secondly, an elegant and economical screenplay which excises, reworks or re-imagines whole chunks of the novel, without doing any real violence to the story.  Indeed, if anything, it is improved by the changes   I certainly found it more exciting, more gripping, and more moving.  This is what an adaptation should be: not a simple translation from page to screen, but a transposition from one register to another, making the film the occasion for a new imaginative experience without losing the qualities for which the novel is so loved. That's no mean feat  and if there is any justice in Hollywood, come Oscar time this spectacularly successful effort will be amply rewarded.

title: Simply Brilliant
review:
Whilst The Fellowship Of The Ring, reconstructs the basics of J R R Tolkien's epic, it's three hour running time, like Brave-heart just flies.

It is not filmed to perfection, if it was it would be 6 - 8 hours long, yet Peter Jackson and company do a fantastic job within a 3 hour time slot.

The casting is top notch, the action jaw dropping, and the locations stunning.

10/10

title: Lord of the Films
review:
I truly thought this movie was one of the best Epic movies I have seen in a few years. What can I say about this movie! I was truly speechless with how well it turned out. Yes the story was different in parts from the book, but in a whole it followed rather well. I have read the books, and I like them, but I knew from the beginning that there would be some changes.

I thought the acting was top notch. Everyone did a fantastic job on the acting. By the end of the movie you come to love the characters and feel for the sorrows and joys. The scenery was incredible. For 3 hours you believe New Zealand becomes Middle Earth and the man-made sets were great. The pacing of the movie was perfect, a little slow at the beginning to set up the movie, but after that it has a wonderful flow to it. I feel Jackson did a wonderful job with the details. It could have been easy to let things slide but he didn't. The Soundtrack compliments the movie wonderfully. The Special effects were top notch and enhance the movie and don't overdue it. Combine the special effects with a great story and you have one of the best movies to come out in a few years.

I truly believe that the Lord of the Rings will Rule the Box Office for the next three years. I will take Elves and Orcs over Jedi and Clones any day. This is a movie that fans of the books, and newcomers will enjoy. Lord of the Rings is truly Lord of the Films for this year.

Jason

10/10

title: Pretty good, but don't drink the latte
review:
I've treated myself to two of the magical spectacles of the season, this one, and Harry Potter, and my money's on Harry Potter, simply because it didn't take itself so seriously, and at such length, as does this first instalment of the Tolkien Trilogy.

Okay, so maybe my big mistake was the large latte at the beginning of a LONG flick, but jeesh, maybe an intermission was warranted?

One feature of this movie that drew me to it, was the thought I missed something when I put the book down in my early '20s, unable to make myself continue, avid reader though I am. My imagination was captured by the t.v. teaser, with Liv Tyler telling Frodo (paraphrased): "this task was given to you -- if you do not not succeed in carrying it out, no one will." What I like about that is its beauty as a metaphor for life, for all our lives, not just those of hobbits and heroes. In essence, we are all given the special task of our own life, and if we do not succeed in our quest to live our own life to the hilt, then no one will.

This film, though, doesn't quite live up to the large metaphors and the deep symbolism I went looking for. It's entertaining, nothing too extraordinary, and it does lag considerably, at times, ESPECIALLY if you had the latte.

title: Embodies all the right themes
review: I just saw this movie today and let me tell you, compared to the books this movie is 100% better. Tolkien, and many people agree with me here, is quite boring. And the fact that someone could present Fellowship Of the Rings so excitingly and fresh, amazes me. Who could be a better Frodo than Elijah Wood? This guy is a great actor with the depth needed to portray this meek hero. But let us nt forget what really sets this apart from just any old special effects flick. Number one it has all the right themes for a story of this magnitude. Those are good and evil, undyielding friendship and devotion, that the little guy is capable of daring feats and where there's a will there's a way. I genuinely love this film, especially how it leaves you begging for more, right at a climax. Between Harry Potter, Star Wars and this...it seems I won't be leaving the movie theater for quite some time!

title: A Good Movie, But A Bad Ending.
review: Lord of the Rings was a really good movie, but the ending wasn't that great. Elijah Wood was great as Frodo and also Liv Tyler was also good. Okay, this movie was REALLY long, it was like three and a half hours, but the movie was really good. The beginning of the movie was great, and so was the middle, but towards the ending the movie got boring. Anywas, I give Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring a 9 out of 10 !! :)

title: not quite
review:
i won't give away the ending but I will say that i sensed a great

disappointment and even anger in the audience with whom I was

viewing the film. certainly we were looking forward to the end of the

movie as the three hours of fantasy eventually begin to exhaust

and then just like that, the movie ended period. A ten doesn't end

like that whatever the ending in the book so I say Lord is a nine.

title: The film to rule them all.
review:
*No spoilers*

First off, I'll admit that I'm a big fan of Peter Jackson's past movies ("Heavenly Creatures" rating as one of my all-time favourites), so I'll try very hard not to be unfairly biased in favour of this movie. However, after seeing Fellowship of the Ring I am left in a state of awe.

Secondly, I've read "The Hobbit" many times (and always loved it) but not the "Lord of the Rings" trilogy. Well, I tried, but it was just too slow for my short attention span (apologies to Tolkein disciples for my sacreligious arrogance). The narrative of the film made sense to me, although I suspect a second viewing will highlight points I missed. At just under three hours it's a long film, to be sure. I don't think I blinked in that time though, I was so engrossed.

The primary responsibility of the film-maker, for a story such as this, should be to entertain. From this perspective, the film works brilliantly. But I think it goes further than that.

The acting is superb throughout. Not one bad (or even mediocre, for that matter) performance. I didn't think American actors could do English accents (does anyone remember Dick van Dyke in "Mary Poppins"?). I was wrong. Elijah Wood (Frodo) was very impressive, demonstrating real depth of character. Sean Bean (Boromir) was a revelation - very low key but developed a scene-stealing performance. I won't repeat critique over the rest of the cast - other comments unanimously echo the sheer acting *class* on offer here.

The dialogue was generally very good, although a couple of lines did make me cringe a bit. But that could just be me being a snob. Whatever.

The battle scenes are magnificent, and BIG. The opening of this film contains battle scenes which dwarf (no pun intended) any I've seen before - they will knock the stuffing out of you.

I have to make a criticism here, albeit not of the movie itself: This film has been marketed in the UK as a "PG" (some scenes may be frightening for children, parental guidance may be required for under 12s) with a footnote stating that under-8s may find it too scary. Huh? I'm 29 and a few scenes almost made me stain my pants. The visceral battle gore, the dark, menacing undertones that pervade the film and the powerful emotional content convince me that this is in NO WAY a "PG"; It should have been marketed as a Cert. "15".

The special effects are astounding. In some respects they're hard to see - they're so well integrated. Only in a couple of (short) scenes did I think "that didn't look quite right". WETA have done the allegedly impossible and *at least* equalled the standard set by Industrial Light and Magic, which is no mean feat. Respect due.

I found the music to be attractive yet low-key; an enhancement to the visuals rather than attention seeking. The sound effects were much more prominent. Brilliantly realised, in a Dolby EX equipped cinema, they hit you from all angles with devastating clarity.

However, the icing on the cake (for me) is the scenery and set construction. *Wow*. Expect the tourism industry to explode in New Zealand. Soaring, swooping shots of the incredible landscapes have an emotional impact that I cannot begin to explain. Sets & props which look absolutely authentic - there are two statues featured that were jaw-dropping in appearance. You *MUST* see this film on a *BIG* screen to do it justice.

I think this film goes way beyond conventional mindless-but-fun entertainment. It has strong artistic merits. I'll state for the record that the critics who have slated this movie by being unfairly negative are generally talking like either anal-retentive gimps with (ironically) limited imagination, or uncultured cretins more suited to watching average brainless Hollywood blockbusters. Just an opinion. ;-)

In summary I'll say that whilst I think there are a few legitimate criticisms of the movie, I understand and accept the reasoning behind them. I wouldn't give the movie a "perfect" rating, although I rate it extremely highly. I strongly urge you to see it for yourself on the big screen.

title: 12 months is too long...

title: This is Unbelievable
review:
My review contains spoilers, so if you don't want to be, err, spoilt, then don't read it.

The Shire seemed perfect to me. Excellently designed and well put together. There is so much detail about Hobbiton in the book, and there are many little details that just want to make me want to jump up and applaud. This was very well put together.

*BIG SPOILER* One very good bit, however, has to the Mines of Moria. Especially where the Fellowship cross the Bridge of Khazad-Dûm. Excellent effects, and the part where Gandalf falls into the black pit is very touching. All sound effects, apart from the sound of the arrows hitting the walls, go, and quiet, sad music begins playing. The sorrow of the group is played will outside with Aragorn telling them to keep going, and to get up, with the rest felling sad, and Frodo with a single tear rolling down his face. Again, a very moving part of the film. *END BIG SPOILER*

The most important part of the Lord of the Rings series books are the characters and their friendships. I think that the casting for LOTR is outstanding, mostly, and deserves congratulations:

When the cast for Lord of the Rings was announced, a few years ago now I think, I remember many mixed views about the casting of Elijah Wood as Frodo Baggins. People saying, `He looks nothing like I imagined Frodo' while other people saying `He looks just like I imagined'. Looking back on the film, I think he was a perfect choice. Elijah seems to have captured the struggle the Frodo faces throughout the journey  deciding which way to go, what to do next. Peter Jackson couldn't have made a better choice.

Another great piece of casting was Ian McKellen as Gandalf  throughout the film, McKellen plays a very convincing Gandalf, and does in fact look exactly as you would imagine Gandalf to be. His acting, like the rest of the cast's, was top notch. Once again, Peter Jackson couldn't have chosen better.

Similarly Aragorn was well casted, played by Viggo Mortensen. He captured the sense of leadership that Aragorn possesses in the book. The bit with him and Arwen does not feature in the book (but is mentioned in the Appendixes), and as I have already said, was not a necessary change to the story.

The close friendship between Frodo and Sam is perfect. Peter Jackson shows them as very close, without going too far.

Merry and Pippin seemed to play a backseat role. The film gave the impression that Pippin was, to some degree, thick and careless, which is not at all true in the books. Both are, however, also well casted, acted and very convincing in their roles. I'm hoping that in the next film they are given better roles (having not read the next book, I must admit I'm not sure how much they are in it).

Sean Bean as Boromir was a good choice. He played the part very well, especially at the end where the threatens Frodo.

Gimli and Legolas also seem, to a degree, to take a backseat  they are always present, but not as noticeable as the other main characters. They are, however, also well casted, and Jackson has remained true to the book with their characters (as he has with the others).

At some parts in the film, I felt a little let down, as if something was not quite right, but by the time I was walking out of the cinema, I felt I wanted to be walking back in to see it again. My review seems to have concentrated mainly on the bad points of the film which is wrong of me. The film is bloody excellent, and the problems I have pointed out are very small and insignificant compared to the triumph that is The Fellowship of the Ring. The film is up there competing with, and in my opinion is better than, Star Wars.

As I wrote to this, I listed to The Fellowship of the Ring soundtrack for about the millionth time in the past two weeks, and it reminded me that all the little problems and inconsistencies are nothing to worry about, and that this is, without doubt one of, if not the, best film ever made. It is worth seeing it: it is worth every minute of your time, worth every penny you pay to see it, worth the huge time we have waited for it. I have but five words to say to you, whether you are a Tolkien fan or not  `Go and see it, now'.

title: Something for everyone...even the fans.
review:
Kudos to Peter Jackson for this film.

I am president of a film club at my university and on campus, about a year ago I passed out flyers for "Meet the Feebles." I had asked students if they had ever heard of Peter Jackson...and most just shook their head. Like the blind prophet who warns of the end of the world, I merely smiled, "You will...You will!"

From "Bad Taste" to "Heavenly Creatures," I have gaped in awe at the NZ director's work. I had high expectations for FOTR, as Tolkien is my favorite author. I had a tinge of fear that this would be made into a 'kids' movie. To my surprise, it is a film that both my six year old and I loved.

Tolkien created the mythos, yet Jackson has given us the most exciting and at times, touching visuals to tell the story.

I'm usually the naysayer, the scoffer of "Titanic," "Jurassic Park," and even "The Phantom Menace." But I can't even pretend to not love this film. There are so many positive reviews, and I can see why. So, yes, I must jump on the bandwagon. But rightfully so.

Thank you PJ.

title: A classic novel turned in to a classic movie!
review: What can I add that has not been said yet? The adaptation of Tolkien's work is very faithful, with even some lines of dialogue which are literally taken from the book, the choice for New Zealand as location must have been Jackson's smartest move. True enough, the characters lack depth, but this is a fantasy story, where the protagonists tend to be one-dimensional good or evil. But even then, actors like Elijah Wood manage to show their internal struggle, adding credibility to their performance. Ian McKellen is simply great as Gandalf, and should be seriously considered as an oscar candidate for best supporting role. Because the three movies have already been shot, we may reasonably expect the two sequels to be of equal quality; it was a big gamble for the studio's, but nevertheless I think this movie will be a classic for ages to come.

title: Peter Jackson: Lord of the Screen.
review:
*SPOILER ALERT*(but not too much).

Well, I finally got to see the most eagerly awaited movie of the year "The Fellowship of the Ring". Admittedly, I felt more than a little apprenhensive about the whole thing. Having read LotR about 4 times since I was a kid, I couldn't help being a little nervous about "how disappointed I was about to become". In my mind, noone could fully live up to the standards of my mind with regards to THE BOOK (no, not the Bible).

As the film began and Galadriels voice filled the theatre, my anxiety came to a full stop. Suddenly, I was there. In middle-earth, bleeding and fighting alongside the very best that world had to offer. I felt full of innocent cozyness in the Shire. I dreaded the Ringwraiths and hated their Lord with all my heart. I fought my way through Moria, whishing that I was as cool as Legolas the Wonder-Elf. Finally, I felt proud to be of the race of Men, with Boromir and Aragorn as my chieftains.

In short: Peter Jackson blew my brains out (not literally, but in a metaphorical sense). How he did it is beyond me. I really didn't see this Director coming. He was quietly tucked away in the category "B-type movies, Geeky films" with Bad Taste and Braindead as cross-references. Now, I have to rearrange my entire "Favourite Movie Persons" gallery. My favourite movie has to go, favourite director as well, Elijah Wood and Liv Tyler have to be removed from my "Hate Them" list and advance quite a bit in my small world of film.

This is easily the best 3 hours I ever spent in a movie theatre. My only regret is, that I couldn't stay for another 6 hours and finish the Thrilogy.

11 out of ten. Peter Jackson (and the rest of folks behind LotR): Thank you very much. TOlkien would have wept for joy.

title: A fitting beginning to an epic story
review:
I have to admit to being a fairly skeptical filmgoer, but this movie had me sitting on the edge of my seat with my mouth hanging open. I like movies that are well, epic, for lack of a better term, and this movie fits the bill. I am familiar with the books, and I think that this film does an excellent job translating Tolkien's work to the screen. Although the movie edits out several points and brings elements that are later introduced in later books (i.e. Strider aka Aragorn), it is done in such a fashion to not offend the book fans.

The cinematography was also excellent, truly bringing to life the rich diversity of the Middle-Earth, far better than I expected. I must tell you, some people may consider this sacrilege, but I consider this film on par with Star Wars for the sheer power of the story and characters. It is certainly better than that piece of crap "Phantom Menace", which makes me highly skeptical about the second film. Lucas had better have some serious tricks up his sleeve.

In conclusion I think this is the kind of grand film that truly represents how entertaining movies can be. It is not a perfect adaptation of the literary classic, but close enough to please the bookworms and the public. Rating 10.

title: Magnificent !
review: Quite simply, everything you could ever want in a movie ! Wonderful characters, heartfelt acting, wondrous locations, scenery and photography. I strongly recommend everyone to see this film at their earliest opportunity.

title: A strange and unique thing
review:
The Lord Of The Rings was not what I expected at all. I had been anticipating a very good film, an epic film, a visually stunning film, but overall it just did not unfold like I had imagined it would. I have problems with this movie, but (and this goes for anyone who really loves movies) voicing them before this particular example seems a little pathetic. The Lord Of The Rings, whether you are groaning or grinning when it has finished, is set to become a modern-day classic.

Peter Jackson has made a unique film here. His bizzare style and eclectic fever has produced something rather beautiful, yet equally abhorrent. The talk of beauty is everywhere and well deserved, it is true that the scope of this movie is simply magnificent. Soaring mountains that thrash icy snow around their peaks whilst tiny beings attempt to navigate the peaks. Dark, hideous and onminous tunnels littered with the corpses of a race annihilated by some creeping foulness. I could go on. The film has character aswell, a bearded wanderer who is wise, gentle and yet full of such an awesome strength and biting tenacity that you simply cannot help but feel utterly mesmerized. Gandalf is an amazing character to see brought to life so vividly. And yes, that is but one example.

As for the effects and action factor, I have never been as stunned and delighted in the cinema as I was during several of these moments, and I mean never. There are scenes in this movie that had me staring open-mouthed in total disbelief. But the action/monster/effects scenes are not presented copiously, they appear now and again, used as and when is necessary. The movie has a story to tell...and that is why it will succeed. I must divert for a second onto an aspect of the film which I cannot stop thinking about...gore, ultra-violence and visions of malignent evil. Peter Jackson, if you haven't noticed, is a twisted man. I myself was ready to be dissappointed by the inevitable fluffiness of any 'scary bits'...I WAS ILL PREPARED. This film contains some of the most rancid and downright wretched freaks you could ever wish to clap your eyes upon. The antagonists in this story are unanimously disgusting...they also mean to hurt people quite badly. Needless to say they are dispatched with such extreme prejudice by the fellowship that the action feels more like some rather disturbing documentary concerning the horrors of war. In other words...adults shall not simply sit beside their children smiling gently as a sword is thrust underneath an arm and an orc drops....instead they will watch in horror as a swarm of hissing, screaming, puke-inducing, sewer filth are stoned, speared, skewered, sliced and ...yes....even tortured before their very eyes. Peter Jackson...how the hell did you get away with that PG rating?

Of course, the film is all the better for the multiple arrow wounds, it delivers the necessary sense of urgency and peril in the story ahead. If I have a negative thing to say, it would concern the score that DOES NOT do justice to the visuals and emotion on-screen, but it is not a bad score either. Another grumble concerns the fact I have to wait to see the next installment, is that a complaint at all? Overall, this film is a grand and epic piece of storytelling...for those who complain of unnecessary plot developments and 'boring sections' I would remind them that this happens to be a mere part one in a trilogy. If Peter Jackson and crew manage to keep consistent then the trilogy when complete will stand alone as totally unique set of movies and they will receive the attention from film-nuts that they deserve....I guarantee it.

title: Exceeds all expectations
review: After eagerly anticipating this film for at least 15 months, I was reassured to find it exceeded all expectations. Ignore the Tolkien purists who will inevitably whinge about incidents and characters which/who have(inevitably) either disappeared completely or been altered/condensed. Remember that telling a story in a film is rather different to telling a story in a novel. What matters is the SPIRIT of the film and here we are in safe hands with Peter Jackson. The world of Middle Earth is stunningly brought to life. The New Zealand Tourist Board must be whooping with joy as their country has never looked so glorious. Visitors will flock in absolute droves. Conversely, there is a real unnerving sense of dense dark evil which you feel draws ever closer to the quiet rolling countryside of the Shire. Mordor and Sauron's agents inspire dread and horror.Strider is quite right when he says that Frodo is "not scared enough". By the end of the film, we all have a much better idea of how scared we really should be. The audience, even those who are familiar with the books, will frequently have their hearts in their mouths in apprehension of what is to come. The tiny Hobbits seem particularly vulnerable, no matter how much fighting spirit they display.At times I was so aghast, I realised that I was forgetting to breathe. The performances of the major characters are marvellous .They throw themselves into the roles with great bravado and are not afraid to display the wholehearted emotions which give the characters and story so much strength. It is difficult to single out performances, especially when some actors have not yet been given the chance  to shine fully, but the two Sir Ian's were exceptional. Ian McKellen's natural authority lent Gandalf the power the role requires and he was able to change in an instant from an affectionate uncle-figure into a truly mighty wizard. Ian Holm gave Bilbo more true pathos than I thought was there in the book; he was rather touching and charming.Elijah Wood was always going to be first choice for Frodo and, even though there will be so much more to come, Frodo's strength of mind and fortitude have been remarkable . His love and affection for Sam and Gandalf shine through in a pure and natural delight. I hope pity and compassion for Gollum will be portrayed half as well in the final two films.I also thought Viggo Mortensen gave a very fine performance as Aragorn. To sum up, the set pieces and battles will take your breath away. You will be thrilled to bits. At(frequent)moments you will be horrified. But overall, you'll desperately want to know what is going to happen to these protagonists as they continue on their lonely and heartbreaking journey.

title: Simpley Stunning !!!
review: Well, where to begin, firstly to all the people out there who are disappointed with the changes ; I can understand your anger/disappointment, but lets be serious folks..it could easily have been a 6 or even 9 hour movie. Plus lets not forget that at the end of the day this is only an adaptation....this then leads me to my next point, this has to be the best book to film adaptation ever! I've read the book numerous times, but to actually SEE the Shire and Rivendell and Lothlorien left me a little stunned. Visually the film is fantastic. I have rated it as a 9.4. The reason it never got a 10 was for the dodgy 'Matrix Style' Wizards battle, Wizards don't fight like that, do they? I hope not. The issue of Arwen at Weathertop also left me a bit flumoxed. Wasn't Weathertop still several days away from Rivendell? Never mind eh! whats done is done. The only really dreadful thing at it all is that I've got to wish a whole year of my life away before we find out if The Two Towers can be even better. The acting is good, the dialogue in parts sticks closely to the book then in a couple of places it lets itself down by a character making a statement which is clearly out of character..I'm moaning to much aren't I. I'm sorry...it has taken me two days to process the visual images that where thrown at me for three of the fastest hours ever. I have never sat in a packed out Theater (I went to the first showing at 11.30am)where no one got up, made a sound, ate anything, crunched anything or muttered through the plot. I had to eat my popcorn in the car on the way home!! The film moves at such a pace it's hard to keep up with the action, the battles are fast and furious. Not overly gory, but I found them a little hard to follow. The Orks are great, the opening shots are good and give a good (if simplified) back ground. I'm going to see it again today. This time I'll be able to sit back and look at the film. May the light of the Valar shine down on Peter Jackson always.

title: Never read the book.... LOTR hard to follow in places
review:
***Spoilers!!!!***

I hate hype... Hype spoils movies...

Anyway.... Just saw the movie and I thought it was OK but having not read the book I found it quite hard to follow in places.

It seems to me that as a book adaption it probably rules!.... But as a movie in itself, I found that it was stunning in some places but sometimes stupid in others.

Some scenes dragged (a couple of the one on one talks were boring) and this ruined the urgency vibe that the movie had built up.

The music was alright in places (especially in the opening credits when the Lord Of The Rings logo shows -cool piece of music) but overall it didn't blow me away like Star Wars, Braveheart or Jaws music did.

The effects were absolutely cool and its great to see some make-up and masks again instead of just seeing stupid computer generated characters (ala ja ja binks). As people are growing used to computer generated crap it was good to see some older style special effects being used for this movie.

The main let down for me was the orcs... They looked great! Totally freaky and nightmarish but by the end of the movie I had the impression they were total wimps. If I was one of the fellowship I wouldn't consider them a threat. A huge group of them wasted like they were those wimpy robot things on that Star Wars phantom menace crap. And their tough leader has his head chopped off. Those guys should be called the keystone orcs or maybe the smurfs. And those rider guys spend all day riding round on their horses and they can't even chase that bird down whose holding onto a small nearly dead person.

Anyway... haven't read the book but still enjoyed most of the movie. Acting was OK but I thought the human guys were pretty crap...

7/10

title: A truly amazing film adaptation
review: I remember when I first saw Star Wars back in 1977. I was only 7 years old back then, and though I didn't really follow the story, I can remember being amazed at the images and characters that were on screen. I can say that that day I saw Star Wars made me love films. Now I am a bit older and I've just seen a film that made me feel like that 7 year old again (except this time, I'm fully capable of following the story and appreciating the small details); for the entire running time of 3 hours, I was in awe. I must say that FOTR is truly an amazing film that displays the power of cinema to take us to new worlds and to experience new adventures. I think it literally is the best example of a fantasy-adventure film that we've seen in a very, very long time. The cinematography, the story, the acting, the score, and the special effects all worked together beautifully to create a truly special motion picture experience. About the only bad part of the film is that, like all films, it eventually has to end. I am really looking forward to the second film in the trilogy. My hat's off to Peter Jackson!

title: Different from the book, the movie is THE masterpiece of our time!
