title: Jackson conned NewLine out of $400million - thank God!
review: Saw this with the wife last night. I will definitely be going back to see it again. There are three things I usually expect from a film such as this : a story, good acting, and visual spectacle. Let me first say that this was probably one of the most visually stunning films I have ever seen. Now let me qualify it by saying that from the three factors(visual,plot and acting), the directing was for me less impressive than the other two. Peter Jackson has coaxed some stunning performances from otherwise ordinary actors. I haven't even started talking about the great actors. Was that really Liv Tyler as Arwen, or did they somehow hire some elf maid from the undying lands across the sea? I want to see more  and I don't care what the purists think. Hell, they could cast her as Luthien if they ever plan to make the Silmarillian. Cate Blanchet was also brilliant. You good see the pride and wisdom of the high elves shine through. Fantastic! Overall nothing less than 10/10 will suffice although the picture is indeed incomplete and I would like to rate all 3 episodes as one film. Now Finally theres just one problem although it doesn't bother me. My wife will not see this film again in a hurry specifically because of the ugliness and brutality of some of the darker scenes. She found the orcs too disgusting to bear- not that I minded. This may however be a problem for the producers as I can see a large section of the population staying away. Therefore I'm pretty sure that this is not a film to break records, although it will definitely recuperate the expense. If they had made the Orcs and co. a bit less gross, then they may have had the super "star Wars" beating hit they were hoping for. Anyway I'm just glad that the films have been made now, so theres no turning back. In years to come this film will standout as one of the alltime classics. Good work Jackson.

title: EASILY the best film EVER made; flawless, otherworldly and heartwrenching!
review:
I could NOT believe what I was seeing and feeling in that theater for my first Lord of the Rings experience...

It was like seeing into heaven...and hell. The staggering beauty and flawless visualizations of the Shire, Rivendell, Lothlorien and the DOOM soaked plains of Mordor-the brutal factories of Isengard and the TERRIFYING and blood thirsty Orcs. WOOOOW!!

The sense of FEAR and DOOM in this is STAGGERING. Sauron is NO contest THE most POWERFULL, EVIL AND TERRIFYING force I have EVER seen in film.

I can NOT say enough. Changed my LIFE. Moved me more than anything ever has.

FLAWLESS acting ALL the way around. Wood and McKellen give THE two BEST performances I have EVER seen. Bean, Lee and the rest were AMAZING too. And Liv Tyler WAS Arwen! YEAH! She was incredible.

Best score, CG and cinematography I ever have seen as well. Moria was beyond words. The Balrog? GREATEST SEQUENCE EVER! Hands down.

The humor was surprising and VERY well done with a sense of lighthearted fun and warmth.

My favorite film of all time and MANY others I know will say the same!

YEAH!!!!!!!!!!

title: Problems I had with the movie
review:
Contains Spoilers Just saw the movie tonight and I'm sorry to say it, I was MAJORLY dissapointed! Yes, the movie was good, but that's because it succeeded in creating an in-depth world true to the book, along with some amazing visuals that certainly made it feel epic. You can't help leaving the theater after 3 hours feeling like you've been on an adventure...because you're overwhelmed by the size! But basically the story was trying to get a ring from point A to point B while fighting some bad guys along the way. The beginning was great with the Hobbit town and party...but once the quest began the story just dragged. Not only that I tend to be nitpicky about things, and after about a dozen incidences in FOTR, I begin to feel let down by a movie. Here are just a few: 1. How did Gandalf get his staff back after escaping from Saruman? And just what was that big owl thing? His pet? Was that butterfly supposed to be some sort of foreshadowing of how he could escape? Why didn't he just eat it? He was in a prison without food, I'm sure! 2. Gandalf hardly used any magic. Why? He seamed pretty useless other than a wise guide. Did he actually cause the stone bridge to break? It seemed so narrow that it would have broken by itself if the monster had stepped on it. 3. Did the dwarf just happen to have another ax? He breaks his ax while trying to destroy the ring, but then moments later holds up a perfect one while replying to Frodo that he has the help of "my ax". A dwarf ax is supposed to be indestructable, since dwarves are master blacksmiths. Their weapon is like an extension of themselves. I suppose I can believe he had another, but it's unlikely. 4. How did the Dark Lord know that Golem had the ring? If Bilbo had it, why didn't they track it to him as easily as they could Frodo? Remember the flashback shows the orcs torturing Golem, he says Bilbo's name and they go after him. First, how did they find Golem when he didn't have the ring, and why didn't they go after Bilbo, since he used the ring to disappear at his party, they wouldn't have had to stop and ask that one worried townsperson where it was! 5. Why did the Shadow riders turn and run downstream when the water came at them instead of straight at Arwen? The dummies deserved to die. If water could kill them, they would be screwed if it ever rained in that lush environment, which it does. 6. Hugo Weaving as Elrond. Somebody tell him he's not the Matrix bad guy with a Britsh accent in this movie. He seemed to me to be so over the top I couldn't stand his line deliveries. 7. How come the dwarf wasn't any help in getting in the mines? It was his cousin, and he talked about the mines. How is it possible he never went there? Why would there even be a secret entrance to a mining area? And why would they let a monster live in the water so close to them? And when Gandalf read the description, he used the word "friend" when he first read the description in elf language, didn't he? Shouldn't that have opened the door? Even if he didn't how dumb to have the password be in the wording itsself, so all you'd have to do is read it aloud! But I digress... 8. In the mines they are surrounded by orcs, but then the orcs all run away when a bigger monster is heard coming. Wouldn't you think this would be a good time for our heroes to keep running? But they just stand there and think..hmm I wonder what could be coming that would scare all these orcs? Let's stand around and ponder this for a moment. Hmmmmm. Oh it's a bigger monster! Run!!! 9. When the staircase it breaking and Frodo and another guy are on it and it's falling toward the other staircase with the rest of our heroes, everybody just stands there(on the edge no less) expecting the staircase to hold when it slams up into it! Fortunately for them it does. The debris doensn't even phase them, either! It would have shattered and sent them all to their deaths! 10. Isn't it cool how the elf always has a pouch stuffed to the max with arrows? He must fire of 40 shots in the movie, and yet at the end it's still full. Maybe he has one of those infinite pouches or something. 11. Too many predictable things happened. Yes, we all knew the giant orc monster would jump out behind the pillar, and that the whip would catch Gandalf, but I guess I'd never predict that Frodo is actually.... 12. Stretch Armstong! Wow! I expected him to jump into the water at the end of the movie in order to save his buddy Sam, who was sinking deeper into the lake, and who's final perspective shot showed the surface about 15 feet about him. But one arm from little Frodo, and he's lifted up into the boat.

Is anyone still reading this? Am I being too nitpicky? I normally enjoy movies, so why didn't I enjoy this one? Please somebody tell me because maybe I'm going crazy, since all my friends are telling me it's the best thing they've ever seen. But I thought the character were all under-developed, the plot was so-so at best, and the pacing was way off! Yes, the battle scenes were awesome, yes the landscape was epic and the colors were beautiful, yes Liv Tyler was actually good, and yes this thing left me wanting to see more! But I wanted to see more because the movie just didn't satify me! I don't want to say I dislike this movie yet, but I'll wait for the trilogy to end before I pass judgement. That leaves plenty of time for people to rip me apart! -----Original Message-----

title: It's DEFINITELY not "horrible"
review:
If you have read the story, perhaps 2 or 3 or 4 times, you knew, going in, that it could NOT be a fully faithful retelling of the book itself. Nope. Can't doit. Nuh-uh. Hell, even if you haven't actually read the books you've seen those ubiquitous 6-inch-thick gift-paks and you know it.

So then the problem is how do you keep that feel and that familiarity and that pull of the story in the 2.5 - 3 hours you got to tell it. And feel like you wouldn't have p***ed off Professor Tolkien.

Well, you do it like like this. Jackson has left in the same feel that the book gives although it is a decidedly 21st century telling. At the end of the movie I still felt I had been through one surprise, struggle, dismay, hope, disappointment after another until finally, at the end, I was left hanging with uncertainty and a ravenous need for the next book.

When' s Two Towers coming out? Can ya buy your tickets yet?

title: The adventure come true
review:
Words fail when I try to describe this beautiful movie. I LOVED the balrog, it was even scarier then I imagined! A lot of people complain about the speed of the movie, but I love that. It keeps you on the edge of your seat till the end. Never before did three hours pass that quickly...

Bravo Peter Jackson for keeping to the story (except for the larger part for Arwen...)

I saw it yesterday, too bad I don't have time to see it again today :-)

title: Definitely on my top ten list...
review:
I saw the LOTR at the first chance I had. I tried to some how find a way to sneak into an early press release, but I had no luck. I'll admit, I fell into all the hype...but when a big movie like this comes along every now and then, it's almost unhelpable. Sadly, 9/10 of those big budget hypes are misses, but I assure you this one is a hit.

I read up all I could on this movie, starting with the books. I had already endured the burden of not reading them before, and after I did so I felt pretty lousy because I had missed out on so much. Then after a whole year of waiting, my time finally came.

I was blown away by this movie. I like to think of myself as kind of a movie person...I watch a lot of stuff and I work at a video store, so I'm well versed. From the first five minutes I had already been entranced by this movie. It has all the right ingredients to take it strait to the top. When I finally left the theatre 3 hours later, I wanted to hop in line and see it again. Unfortunately, I had to go to work...but I will soon return.

I would strongly urge anybody who hasn't seen this movie to do so if you have the time. During the christmas break when you go and have to choose between LOTR, Oceans 11, Vanilla Sky, Ali, or Jimmy Neutron for your kids...I promise you that this one will shine above the others.

title: feeling in the core of action!
review:
You will not waste your money, if you watch it! it deserves to be watched and i guess we must thank to the director in his efforts to bring all complicated pieces together to present a visual show of the year, or who knows, maybe of the decade!

The movie is well furnished with animation effects and extra-ordinary simulations all around. I admit, it sometimes turns into a 21st century computer game! roles are properly distributed among the cast but, playing is not principal purpose of course.

You always feel in the rising tempo of the action, and sometimes it sprains your body, although you know all are crazy computer animations.

So, go watch the movie, you will enjoy.

title: Great!
review:
Up to now, I read the book a few times and I was really wondering, how they could make a film out of it. Yesterday I saw it and it was great! The special effects where great, the pictures AND the adaptation of the book where excellent.

Worth to see it!

title: Outstanding Movie
review: The movie is well worth the price great story, actions and acting.  All of the Fantasy movies rejoice, Fantasy has returned to us in full force. Hopefully this will lead to more Fantasy movies.  This movie was outstanding, there is no words to describe how good this movie is.  Go see it do yourself a favor.

title: I can't understand how anyone could make a better film from the book.
review:
I have read the Swedish translation of the LOFTR trilogy two times and the English original with the JRR Tolkien foreword once. I have read Bilbo and Silmarillon plus some of the articles about the myths and background stories of the LOFTR characters.

As you can imagine I had high, very high expectations of the movie... Is it even possible to make a film from this extraordinary literature? Well, I can only repeat: apart from some very small details, very much ignorable in view of the whole experience, I can't understand how anyone could make a better film from the book.

Some parts of the film, for example when Frodo puts on the Ring and is transported into the dark world, and when Elven Queen Galadriel sees a vision of herself powered by the ring, Peter Jackson (director) has succeeded in scenes which go far beyond anything even I (considered to be a pretty creative person) hadn't imagined. To have that vision, and to be able to transform that vision into a cinematic scene, that, ladies and gentlemen, is trades of a genius at work.

99% of the actors seem to have been born to play their characters; Gandalf (Ian McKellan), Aragorn (Viggo Mortensen), Frodo (Elijah Wood), Legolas (Orlando Bloom), Galadriel (Cate Blanchett) and pretty much everyone else really IS personified in the movie. Is it just good casting or is it the mark of outstanding directing? I don't honestly know.

Alright, as for the parts I did not think quite worked as well as it could, and believe me; I see these things in every movie, and since this film is competing up there with the top films I have ever seen, they are petty details really. 1) Some of the scenes could have been worked on a little more, maybe just one more take. 2) I would have personally preferred some other actors in the parts of Arwen (Liv Tyler) and Elrond (Agent Sm... sorry Hugo Weaving). 3) The digital effects department could have gotten a bigger budget. This is the 21th century, not the early 1990's, and technology have stepped forward from Jurassic Park. Look at The Phantom Menace and Harry Potter... But hey, I don't really care about that; like a said, these are petty petty details.

Thank you Peter Jackson, the actors and the entire film team for making the fantasies come true!

title: Incredible!
review:
I'm not going to write a run-down of the plot which is seemingly what most of the reviewers do here for some stupid reason.. but what I am going to do is just tell everyone flat out... this movie was amazing enough to make me FINALLY (after years of visiting iMDB) make an account and vote a perfect 10 and write this user comment.

The scenery is spectacular, and ever-changing throughout the whole 3 hour movie. After about an hour of watching it.. i began asking myself over and over.. HOW THE HECK DID THEY AFFORD ALL THIS? WOOOW!!!

The CG and special effects are WICKED! This movie is just so awesome in every aspect of movie-making that I'm at a loss of words and thus being a little vague. You HAVE to see this movie to see what I'm talking about... even the best user reviews do it no justice. You think the Lord of the Rings Movie-Trailer was awesome? Multiply that by a factor of 100.. that's the movie.

Despite what some people think... you DON'T have to have read JRR Tolkien's books to understand the plot of the movie. I for one, have not read any of Tolkien's books, and I followed the storyline perfectly! I know a few friends who HAVE read the books, and it is confirmed by them that the movie DOES follow the book, and the movie does an EXCELLENT job immersing even those in the audience who have NOT read the books.

Music is SUPERB and goes perfectly with every scene.

Character development was done with careful consideration and as far as I am concerned, it is perfect.

Regardless of what some people think, the ending of this movie was done EXACTLY as it should be and will provide for an excellent transition into the second movie: (The Two Towers) in 2002.

All in all.. if you're into fantasy type movies.. GO SEE THIS! Even if you're not.. GO SEE IT, just to see what I'm talking about with scenery/music/special fx/storyline etc. This stuff is top-of-the-line present day movie-making technology at work here folks. At least go see it for the sake of appreciating the precision technology used to make something like this! I rated this movie a perfect 10, because it's certainly nothing short of that. If I could rate higher, I'd give it a 15 ... 5 extra bonus points for outstanding screenplay writing!

title: One of the most incredible films I've ever seen.
review: I was one of those people who were absolutely bursting to see this movie. I had actually never read The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, but was inspired to do so after seeing a trailer for the movie last summer. I read all the books in two weeks, and loved them. I really wanted the movies to be great, but was still unsure, and a little nervous about some of the deviations from the plot. But from the moment the prologue began, and the beginning credits rolled, I was absolutely RIVETED! For three full hours I was glued to the edge of my seat - I never wanted it to end! It is truly a magical and visually stunning movie, which totally transports you into its fairy-tale world, from the breathtaking beauty and magic of the elves, to the utter evil and darkness of the Ringwraiths and Mordor. With its propulsive pace, there is never a dull moment in this film - but that is not to say that it doesn't include some really nice, heartfelt moments. Jackson is a genius, crafting this story with incredible skill, passion, and imagination. The script is nice and tight, and there are amazing and heartfelt performances from the entire cast. I particularly thought that Ian Mckellan was BRILLIANT - he added so many dimensions and such fun to Gandalf, it was wonderful. Elijah Wood was the perfect choice for Frodo - sweet natured and heartfelt, Wood is a fine actor. Cate Blanchett was, as always, exceptional, and Ian Holm was marvelous. All of the actors in the Fellowship were perfect, and even Liv Tyler gave a beautiful performance. This is a fantasy movie with REAL magic, and is undoubtedly one of the most incredible films I've ever seen. It is a true work of art.

title: As Good As It Could Have Been
review:
First, there are a few (inevitable) changes from the book that may irritate you if you're the type who wouldn't accept anything less than total adherance to the original story.

The movie doesn't pick up that much steam 'til the fellowship of the ring is officially put together BUT afterwards it becomes everything you would have hoped for (if you read the book or at least bought into some of the hype).

Stunning acting, stunning cinematography. By the time the movie's over, the train is moving full steam ahead and you are left with the impression that it can only get better from there.

title: Different yet fabulous
review:
I had a fabulous time watching this. Having read the books when I was 10 and then once after that, they have a lot of childhood associations for me -- the movie didn't ruin a single one of them.

The pleasant thing about this movie is that it didn't try to stick too closely to the book. The movie is a different medium and demands different dialogue and action in places -- Jackson wasn't afraid to do that and make the movie his own to some extent. Many of the changes he made were good for the movie version. (Although perhaps a bit much of the dark gloomy threatening scenes at Isengard -- but that's just me.)

After seeing and being quite disappointed by Harry Potter & the Philosopher's Stone, I'm extremely relieved with Fellowship -- it shows how a book should be adapted. Also, the actors did a uniformly amazing job -- particularly Elijah Wood and whoever played Gandalf (Ian somebody?). This will be a classic -- do yourself a favour and see it on the big screen.

title: A Thought, A Book, A Dream !!!
review: When I was 9 years old ... I took the Hobbit down from my cousins shelf and read it. From that day on my world changed more than it had ever changed before. Every walk in the woods near my house and every trip to the country became my quest with Bilbo and Gandalf. My heart was with them. My inner belief of the knowledge of good and bad inside me, at such a young age, became an importance to me and an importance to life itself beyond mere mortal imagination. I took down the well thumbed, and well read, Lord of the Rings, and to my sheer joy, embarked on that wondrous journey once again. The film, of course, had much to live up to. Not only had Tolkien managed to conjure up something in my mind that was almost uninterpretable to a screen play, he had instilled an almost unique sense of individuality to the novel that I was concerned, deeply, that it would hardly live up to my expectations. Therefore, I have to admit, that this film was the most imaginative and CORRECT adaptation of a novel that I have ever seen on the screen. Not only did Jackson and Crew recreate the novel, but beautifully recreated for me the childhood world that I had thought lost. This world had everything exactly and perfected from the book.......almost like it was my own mind and imagination that had been projected from my mind onto the big screen. I am usually very critical indeed of wondrous and unique novels being turned out in the cinema, but this admirable film deserves a unilateral 10/10. I could of course criticize the film for a few insignificant things..... but that would be an injustice to what, I am sure, will be the most acclaimed and remarkable film of our time. Sinbad and Jason would be envious but like Gandalf says ...... Sometimes the smallest things have the greatest power .....!!

title: AMAZING!
review: I was not expecting too much, but I was very wrong.... LotR is simply an amazing piece of film-making... incredible scenarios, costumes and special effects, but most of all acting. it is a must see, and I will go to watch it again soon enough!

title: Gone with the Wind for the 21st Century.
review:
There was a marked increase in the production quality of Hollywood films following the release of the epic film Gone With The Wind.

Expect a similar rise in quality in the next few years. The bar has been raised again.

See this movie. It will move you.

title: Goes to show that action-adventure movies can have heart and soul
review: Great performance all around.  Beautiful Cinematography, Set Design...top notch technically.  The screenplay, considering the massive source material, was streamlined but done so effectively.  Sometimes a few lines of dialogue were spoken with the perfect hushed tone but became unintelligible.  The Mines of Moria were fantastic.  Everything.  As some of the reviews have stated, it improved minute by minute.  Thrilling.

title: Fantastic!
review:
I still feel limp. It's every bit as good as other reports indicate - nearly flawless, and the minor deviations from the story make sense in the context of the film. Even at three hours, it seems to rush you through a lot of the story - there's a lot packed into this one film. I don't see how it could be any better unless it were even longer. My only nit is the choice of actor for Elrond, and only because his distinctive voice is recognizably the same as Agent Smith in The Matrix - aside from that, the actors _were_ the characters, and if I've seen them in anything else I couldn't tell you what it was. Sets, scenery, costumes, effects all blend seamlessly - I couldn't believe what I was seeing on the screen in some parts, including little details such as the difference in stature of the characters, which is flawlessly maintained through the entire film.

Some SPOILERS ahead:

Others have reported deviations that don't even exist; their memory of the books is flawed. Examples - Gandalf _was_ snared by the Balrog's whip in the book. Galadriel _was_ tempted by the ring (though in the book it was unclear whether it was real temptation or a demonstration for Frodo - which could also be argued about what was shown in the flick). There is a fair amount of material presented that isn't in the main story from the books, but is included in the appendices and possibly other Tolkien works which expand upon the story of Middle-Earth (the relationship between Arwen and Aragorn is expanded upon in Appendix A).

title: Speechless.
review: I read the books about a year ago, so the book was still fresh in my mind when I saw the movie tonight. I was not only impressed by the visual effects, sound, character dev., plot, etc...but mainly at how close it matched the book. I realize that a few points were modified, twisted, but generally it matched the time line that was set in the book. All things considered I would have to congratulate Mr. Jackson for bringing life to a world so many of us have read and enjoyed. A MUST see on a large screen. Thank you.

title: The Corners Were Cut Just Right!
review: In almost any book-to-movie adaptation, it is inevitable that the scriptwriters will need to cut some corners. Well, I'm glad to report that Walsh/Boyens/Jackson cut the corners just right! The most significant omission is probably Tom Bombadil, who could easily have eaten (smoked?) up another half-hour of the film. Anyway, this work truly stands on its own, and it is terrific. I was worried about the special effects looking half-baked, or the matte paintings looking fake, based on one or two misleading reviews that I had read prior to watching the movie. IMHO, totally false! I didn't notice anything like that. The only revision that I wasn't too excited about was Lurtz, but I can understand why he was added to the story so that there would be a clearer connection to Saruman. Regardless, this production passed muster in every way, and I cannot wait to see the move three or four times more! 10/10.

title: Validation
review:
Simply an amazing movie...the kind of movie that will forever raise my standard for what movies should be.

LOTR seemed to take some of the best of Hollywood blockbuster (stunning visuals, fast pacing, seat-edge action) and mix it with some of the best for award-winning drama (heart-wrenching action, stunning cinematography, wonderful script).

LOTR is the first and ONLY fantasy film to ever have transcended the murky B-grade waters into a true masterpiece of film.

I will watch this movie dozens of times, for the rest of my life.

Thank you, Peter Jackson.

title: The most magnificent piece of film work ever seen.
review: This is by far the most amazing moving there has ever been, despite it's few shortcoming, no other film has or will ever top The Fellowship of the Ring. Peter Jackson set out with a vision, the same vision of Tolkien, i think Tolkien would be amazed with film that has been created.

title: The pinnacle of the movie making art.
review: This is the crowning glory of the cinema. This is what over 100 years of experience making films in America has brought us. This is the greatest movie of all time. It isn't easy for me to admit it but this movie surpasses even Star Wars in grandeur, scope, and story telling. My jaw hung slack on my chest for three hours and my head has been reeling ever since. I am not one to be taken in by movies, not normally, but The Lord of the Rings wowed me at every turn. I've read the books, I know how it all comes out but I still felt like crying at the death of Gandalf. For me that is saying something, I've never cried in a movie before. Peter Jackson is a movie making god. Words can not describe the depth or beauty of this movie (unless of course you count the books, but I'm not J.R.R. Tolkien). How can I possibly explain my delight at seeing the Shire brought to life before my eyes, seeing ringwraiths pursue a terrified Frodo from his home, or Gandalf's battle with the demonic balrog. Everything about this movie demands, deserves, and will get praise. The soundtrack is excellent, the acting perfect, the cinematography, the special effects, the costumes, the sets, the props, environment, the sound, the combination of them all is what Hollywood directors have dreamed of making since the very first motion pictures went into production. There isn't a person on Earth that wouldn't enjoy this movie, and I mean that quite literally. If you have not seen this movie understand that it isn't just hype; this movie is awesome. Even at three hours long every minute manages to be overflowing with actions, drama, and excitement. Seeing is believing though, don't take my word for it, make your own decisions, I know what you'll think however, I was thinking the same thing with my jaw wide open for three hours. Enjoy!

title: To Dream of Middle Earth
review:
Overall, I give it an A. Not an A+ though.

What can I say, it was a feast for the senses and the emotions for someone who has been a Tolkien fan since his early teens.

Could it have been better, no doubt. But I think it's a matter of diminishing returns. What do you cut, what do you add, it's already 3 hours!

Could it have been worse, OH YES!! But thank God and Peter Jackson and New Line, that it wasn't.

I went misty about a dozen places in the film.

It was magic to be transported to Middle Earth for three hours after nearly thirty years of waiting. Well, at least 23 years of waiting since Bakshi's abortive attempt.

******* SPOILERS AHEAD *******

What's great:

  • Sauron opening a can of whup-ass


  • Dragon Fireworks


  • Gandalf Growing in Power Before Bilbo


  • The EYE


  • The "Endless" Columns of Moria


  • Galadriel Transformed


  • Barad-dur With The Lava Flowing from Mt. Doom


  • The Balrog


  • Orthanc


  • Gandalf "Break Dancing"


  • The Bow Guy (i.e., Legolas) 8^)


  • Liv Tyler (yum)


What's not:

  • No Glorfindel


  • No poem from Boromir ("seek for the sword that was broken, not all those who wonder are lost")


  • Council of Elrond "Consternatious Uproar"


  • Gimli's Excitment at Visiting Moria


  • No Remembrance of Mithrandir (i.e., Gandalf) at Lorien


  • No Gifts at Lorien, except one


  • No blindfolds at Lorien


  • The Great River did not look that "Great"


  • Battle scenes are cut too fast


What's very good: EVERYTHING ELSE!!

There were a number of very touching moments in the film, where as I said, tears were welling. Of course I am an emotional person to begin with.

******* MORE SPOILERS *******

One was when Samwise stopped and told Frodo that he was about to go further from home then ever before. I had to pause and ponder at that point what was in store for Sam and what roles he had yet to play. I smiled.

Another was when Frodo jumped into Gandalf's lap, demonstrating his enthusiasm and friendship, but also that touch of innocence that would all too soon be lost.

It was sad to see Gandalf fall. And of course to see Boromir die. But what a delight to see him training Merry and Pippin!! I liked the short love scene 'tween Arwen and Elessar (i.e., Elf Stone, aka Aragorn, aka Strider).

Please go to see this movie and ENJOY!!

title: A year of anticipation and not a bit of disappointment!
review: Excellent casting, across the board.  Visually stunning.  Gripping action. Pathos and wisdom.  It is rare that I have nothing at all negative to say about a film, but this is one of those times!  If pushed, the only complaint I could come up with is that it was not long enough - maybe three hours per book, rather than three hours per part would have satisfied me (there are two books in each of the Fellowship of the Ring, Two Towers and Return of the King).  But as it is, I guess I'll just have to go see it again.  And again.  And again... :)

title: One of the most enjoyable films I have seen in a long time
review: I had high expectations for this film, and I am happy to say that this film fulfilled them.  From the very beginning of the film, the viewer is drawn into the plight of the characters and roots for Frodo and the rest of the fellowship.  The leads, including Elijah Wood and Viggo Mortensen, were very impressive, and several of the supporting players were standouts as well; the characters of Meriadoc and Peregrin come to mind.  The soundtrack was wonderfully haunting, and the battle sequences, while maybe not Crouching Tiger caliber, were incredible nonetheless. This is not to say the film did not have faults.  The female characters' time on screen was fleeting, and Legolas, Boromir, and Gimli had little to no character development.  Despite these flaws, I give the film a 10!

title: Take Notes, Kids. This Is What Ambition Looks Like.
review:
Ever since "Braveheart" came out, the rebirth of the Epic Motion Picture has made its way to the silver screen. Movies like "Titanic," "Pearl Harbor," "Gladiator," and even "The Mummy Returns" try to imitate the vast scope of movies like William Wyler's "Ben-Hur," D.W. Griffith's "Birth of a Nation," and both of Cecil B. DeMille's versions of "The Ten Commandments." Wyler, Griffith and DeMille are considered the architects of the Epic. The spirits of these men, and even James Cameron, Steven Spielberg, George Lucas, and Ridley Scott must make way for the Epic's new all-time master: Peter Jackson.

"The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring" is the best movie I have seen in recent memory. Some may hate this film: People who have been mired in motion picture realism and don't take to epics very well. Normally I would be venomous and outraged that some people would dare attack a movie of such scope and depth, but in this instance, I don't care. The delicate yet masterful direction of J.R.R. Tolkien's classic novel has elevated me into the ether, and all is at peace. It's that good.

Never have I seen an event film that could be so minute, and yet so massive. Take into consideration the battle scenes of the evil orcs against the men and elves. When you see a "Star Wars" picture, ships whiz in and out of the frame, shooting laser beams. They're here and they're gone, leaving no lasting impression. But in Peter Jackson's film, (And I don't know how he does it.) each of these tiny, computer generated figures has a life of it's own. They struck me as characters who had travelled great distances to engage in a war, and had either been cut down, or had risen victorious.

The main actors achieve a delicate feat. The line between the actors and the characters blur, and they're so good that they're practically invisible. There is no force in Ian McKellen's raised eyebrows, Christopher Lee's evil sneer, or Sean Bean's descent into madness. It is all natural, and always stunning. Did these actors know they were creating icons?

The action feels spontaneous instead of being locked into some kind of plot structure where the movie stops for an action scene and then resumes. Everything is in a nice leisurely flow, and requires attention to be paid. Never does this movie pander, or have low expectations of its audience.

Peter Jackson is a director out of New Zealand who has made cheapie horror movies like "Bad Taste" and "Braindead." He has made an Academy Award nominated art film ("Heavenly Creatures") and has had one previous Hollywood effort ("The Frighteners"). While watching these films, I always wondered what he would make if given a real budget, and how it would look. Now I know. Mr. Jackson has shown me places that have eluded me in my wildest dreams, and creatures that dwell in the inkiest corners of my darkest nightmares.

This reminds me of something that Whoopi Goldberg once said: "Movies have to be big, because if they're not big, they're television." And "The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring" sure as hell ain't television.

**** out of 4

title: Superb
review:
This is one of the best films ever made....way better than the original Star Wars trilogy put together and given special treatment.

The effects are amazing.

If you want to check out the director's other work....check out Braindead!! Simply the funniest film with the worst SFX ever made.....he's come along way has Peter Jackson and it's for the better

title: To Be the Greatest Epic Trilogy Ever Made!
review: Forget Star Wars.  This new version of Lord Of The Rings is 100% the best version ever to be made.  There is so much action and wonderful brand new special effects in this film I hardly had a chance to take a breath.  Just when you think the film is about to end, more of the story continues and continues and continues again.  This is wonderful.  The story is unpredictable and the great suspense and anticipation is enjoyable.  The casting of Elijah Wood  as "Frodo Baggins" is perfect.  Mr. Wood puts so much emotion into his acting.  His role is believeable.  The casting of Ian McKellen as "Gandalf".  is perfect as well.  I would like to see an Academy Award nomination here. For anyone who has seen the animated version of Lord Of The Rings (1978) will throughly enjoy this film.   If you have not, you may not want to see it because it might spoil the next two Lord of the Ring films for you.  That is if you do not want to know the ending.  What is so excellent about this Peter Jackson directed film "The Fellowship of the Ring (2001) is that you will not have to wait 2, 3, or 5 years for a sequel.  The next continuing story Lord Of The Ring: The Two Towers will be released in movie theatres next year in December 2002 and the conclusive third film Lord Of The Rings:The Return Of The King will be released in December 2003.  I hope this film will top the record 11 Academy Award nominations.  This film is a wonderful roller-coaster ride and you will be emotionally involved with the great acting of the fine cast.

title: Bedazzling, wondrous, fantastic!
review:
Last night I went to the cinema to see the outcome of 4 years toil by director Peter Jackson, Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, and the others, and I was a little spectical at first. When you've read the extraordinary fine books by Tolkien, your world is changed. There is a world before and after Tolkien, because his universe is so unique and fascinating that it just takes your breath away!

Oh well.. I went to see it and did I get a surprise? YES I did! I've never seen such a fantastic film ever! The whole setting, this marvelous nature of New Zealand is so amazingly beautiful and adds a lot of depth to the film, but that's not all.

The story line in the film is very close to the book, though Tom Bombadil has been left out - a thing that I dislike, but if he was in it, it would have to last at least 45 min. extra! Also, some details have left out and some have been changed and also some added, but hey, when you've read the books will you ever be satisfied? I think not. What made it so good? EVERYTHING! Everything from the visual effects, to the story line and again to the surroundings was.. beautiful.

Elijah Wood as Frodo Baggins (the main character hobbit it you didn't know) plays perhaps the best role he's ever had! I've never liked him before, but now I cannot see any other people playing Frodo. Aragorn, son of Arathorn or "Elessar" is played by my compatriot, Viggo Mortensen, whom I actually really didn't know before, but Viggo Mortensen shows in this film is a great actor and he actually looked quite like how I imagined him :) I could mention them all, but they all play SO good, even the 26,000 soldiers from the New Zealand-Australian army. I mean, what a combat at the beginning of the film - I am impressed.

Go see it, whether you are a fantasy fanatic such as myself, or just a simple, normal person without and geeky hobbies - it IS worth so!

Oh yeah - score: 10/10 (how could it be anything less?)

Wow!

title: It couldn't have been done much better.
review:
Not much needs to be said. I love and have loved the books for years. Obviously changes had to be made in order to adapt the story well for a film but the changes are reasonable for the most part. Considering how much "premise building" had to be done in this first film and how much history had to be told I thought that the pacing was very well done. The cast is excellent and I hope to see some of the characters who didn't get as much time for development really blossom in part 2.

This is the correct way to adapt a long well loved book. "Harry Potter" producers take note. Jackson made 3 hours fly by. Columbus made 2.5 seem like a week.

title: To the Academy
review: It will be interesting to see how Lord of the Rings will do in the Academy Awards this March.  Personally, it is a no brainer.  This is one of the best movies of all time and damn well better receive Best Picture and Best Director.  Especially Best Director.  Say what you want about the film, but Peter Jackson has done one of the best directing jobs of all time.  If LOTR does not receive at least these two awards, I will have lost most of my respect for the Academy.

title: The Good, The Bad and the Ugly
review:
Let me get two things perfectly clear before I begin. First, I am NOT nor have I ever been an Elijah Wood fan, second, I am writing this review while HBO is playing "Battlefield Earth." I am aware that I should turn it off while attempting to write an objective review, but alas, I am lazy. Now, onto the good stuff.

I believe I am safe in saying that this movie is setting the standard in terms of what an epic should be. It has a few minor flaws, but nothing that detracts from it's brilliance.

I could go on and on, but chances are, you've already read everything there is to read on this film, so just pointers:

The Good:

1. As I said, I'm not an Elijah Wood fan, but he does a fine job as Frodo.

2. In terms of make-up: Spectacular. I didn't even realize John-Rhys Davies was in the movie until I got home later. Nuf said.

3. Christopher Lee is absolutely the scariest actor on the planet, bar none.

4. I'm glad Viggo Morteson has finally got a good role. Aragorn was always my favorite character. I mean he was ok in 28 days, but this is better.

5. The acting is top-notch. Everyone was really on. I'm going to assume they kept their level of focus throughtout the entire filming.

6. The locations were gorgeous!

The Bad:

1. The fight scenes are absolutely dreadful. It's mostly shot in close-up, like in Gladiator. You never get a feel for psychology (always important to me). However, the visuals are still spectacular. Only a minor drawback here.

2. Can't think of a number two.

The Ugly:

1. Orcs and their cousins

2. Hobbit Feet - Gotta be a source of infection

3. The Balrog - Sweetness! Looked like a mean old cigarette. One of the coolest CGI characters ever. Too bad it was so dark, but it needed to be, I guess. Sigh.

4. The decapitation towards the end. Best fight sequence of the film. But nasty.

A definite winner, on all counts.

**** out of four.

title: Refreshingly charming, but frustrating (spoilers)
review:
Peter Jackson's _LOTR:TFOTR_ is mystifying, charming, and engaging, yet frustratingly lacking in character development, in establishment of setting, and in passage of time as the film progresses. As a film fan, but not a Tolkien fan, I recommend it for the sheer scope and magic of the film, but definitely do not expect it to be the best movie ever made. You will be taken to a different world and believe you are there, but you will also be left wondering what the heck is really going on with the characters. Luckily the themes of good versus evil, and how one should handle power are not lost among the jumpy plot and poor pacing.

The good: Art direction. I found myself blown away by the fusion of New Zealand landscapes and CGI work. The mines of Moria were incredibly "realistic", and I felt so drawn into the movie in parts like Lothlorien that I forgot that I was in a theater. The sound is excellent throughout, and every establishing shot is like a painting. The acting is great and believable.

The bad: Pacing. The first half of the movie drags and spends too much time with setting up things. The Ringwraith chases seemed disjointed and somewhat pointless. More of that time should have been spent exposing the real threat of the Ring's power. Suddenly, we're in Rivendell, and voila! the fellowship is formed. No backstory for Legolas, Gimli, or even Boromir, and as soon as the fellowship is formed, it seems to break up, weakening the drama.

Still, this film is without a doubt the best of 2001, and may quite possibly be the best fantasy film ever made. For comparison, it beats _The Phantom Menace_ in overall storytelling, and ultimately, the LOTR trilogy shows promise that it may surpass SW Episode's 1-3 in overall quality.

title: Very well done, a tribute to the novel
review: When I first heard rumors that they were going to make a film about the lord of the rings novels, I had my doubts as I have found that the majority of films that have been made based on novels have never lived up to the book without seriously being adapted. As the release day came closer, I began to re-think my perspective on these sort of films, so when I watched the lord of the rings the other day, I must say that it was incredibly done!! It melded live actors and computer effects seamlessly and didn't try to overwhelm you with special effects even though you knew they were there. I STRONGLY recommend this film to anyone who enjoys fantasy or adventure films...this was such an enjoyable experience, from start to cliff hanger ending.

title: Just a little movie magic.
review:
Although there are some minor changes from the book. I feel that they help make the story more compact and easily understood. Especially by American audiences who are no longer used to long scenes of exposition.

At 3 hours in length, I feel the movie had to have some changes and tightening up to make it work. And it does work! The scary bits are very scary. The funny bits are great fun. And Ian McKellan should be awarded an Oscar for best actor.

All in all, it is a wonderful job. 10 out of 10.

title: One of the greatest movies ever, and the best fantasy epic of all time
review:
I had high hopes going into this movie, just like I did with Star Wars: Episode I. Episode I let me down, mainly due to the mass hype building up to it. This, however, did not let me down. Even with all the expectations and mass hype leading up to it, Peter Jackson and the incredible cast have put together one of the most memorable movies of all time. Leaving out the sets, props, costumes and special effects, all of which were absolutely incredible, this film still keeps you in your chair long after it is over, wanting more. Most movies that come from books have a hard time following the book, simply because books usually do not translate well into movie scripts and end up being way too long. The Fellowship of the Ring is one of the few movies I have ever seen that accomplishes both remarkably well. While 3 hours might be a long time to sit for some people, once you start watching, the time flies by. The writers and director should give themselves a lot of credit for keeping the movie flowing so well. If you know the books, then you will see the portions of the film where some of the second book overlaps into this film. Do not be dismayed, though. These overlaps are a necessary and integral part of making the film work. Also, some might question the role of some characters in the movie that seem to have a larger role than in the book. But if you watch closely, you will notice that those few small characters in the movie are a combination of several small characters in the books. All in all, the acting was superb. I could not think of a better cast to portray the characters than those that were chosen. They all fit perfectly into the images I had in my mind of those characters from reading the books. They were elaborate, yet to the point, and showed the true emotion of the story. Bravo, Peter Jackson, Bravo!!

- "One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all, and in the darkness bind them."

title: Epic
review: An epic film masterfully produced.. this is how big films should be. Breathtaking production design, appealing casting and characterizations and a dynamite story all roled into one. Perhaps the best film of the year, this tale based on the story by J.R.R. Tolkien is just the first part of a trilogy that will be released every xmas. Hopefully the next installments can live up to the standard set by the original. GRADE: A

title: The Best Film Of 2001 (Oscar Nomination In The Future)
review:
I'm not going to write a long drawn out review for this film. As you can see, there are plenty of them already in the "Comments" section. What I want to say is, "This is without a doubt the BEST FILM of 2001." Even though there are several other films released this year that deserve an Oscar nod, Lord of the Rings should definitely get a few nominations. The acting in this movie was outstanding. I had to literally check the credits several times to verify that Liv Tyler was Arwen Undomiel. Her whole character and change of voice was mesmerizing to me. I now have respect for her acting talents. Elijah Wood also did a fantastic job. I truly did not think he was right for this part, but he proved me wrong. Sean Astin also did a decent job. The weight gain had me wondering if that was him or not. But the Oscar nomination should definitely go to Ian McKellen for his truly incredible performance.

As for the actual movie and story. I was blown away from this great adventure and how it was told. The visual effects were amazing and very well done. There were a few hic-cups here and there with the editing and special effects, but most of it was flawless. There are a few shocking scenes that may be too much for children 10 and under, but for the most part, this is an excellent family film. I haven't read the J.R.R. Tolkien books, but I will definitely get it and sit it next to the Harry Potter book that I'm trying to finish reading. Great job Peter Jackson and WETA. You've done an incredible job bringing the Lord of the Rings novel to the big screen. I look forward to the next installment.

title: Amazingly done, yet still amazingly disappointed
review:
First I would like to start off and say that this was an amazing movie. I must Compliment Peter Jackson on doing a wonderful job with the film. Now to beefy stuff...There are two ways to look at this movie.

First off, I had the privilege of viewing the absolute first 12:01AM show at my local cinema. I am probably the only person in the theatre that had not yet read the book, which I did on purpose. Since movies take priority over literature in my mind, I don't like knowing the endings of movies and I feel I can judge them better than someone who has rea the book religiously. Also, as a person who takes film and movies (Two very different things) very seriously, it pains me to hear people discuss this MOVIE as the best movie ever. Now like I said, this was amazing to look, but it was sooooooooooo manufactured. Ever since the introduction of computer animation into live action films (granted some pictures require computer generated images i.e. A.I.) the actual "ART" of filmmaking has been lessened with these $100-$300 million dollar movies. If you have read the book (which I still have not), I would strongly recommend this film based upon the reaction of the die hard fans in the audience. It was wonderfully acted, directed, and manufactured.

Now for those of you who haven't read the book, I can't recommend this to you. 9 times out of 10 when I wait to read a book until afterwords, I'm still greatly satisfied when I first view the movie in theatres without prior knowledge to he book. I wasn't as satisfied as I felt I should be. I went into this movie not expecting much but the typical Hollywood "epic", totally manufactured (It was kind of like Titanic meets Legend meets Pearl HArbor meets Willow). If you are an Action movie fan, I guess I might recommend it to you although the sequences are waaaay to far apart. All in all, however, a valiant effort on the part of Peter Jackson (8/10)
