It had really awe-inspiring moments, really "awwww"-inspiring moments, a couple "AAAAH!"-inspiring moments, and many "A HA HA HA!"-inspiring moments. The whole theater seemed to be as enthralled with the film as I was, but I know that's not possible. Noone could possibly like a movie as much as I liked this one, could they? I'm going to see it again and again.

OK, my girlfriend forbade me to say anything even remotely critical about this film, but she's not here now. The only criticisms I had were:

A.) I don't want to wait a year to see the next one

2.) The movie should have been 12 hours long so a lot more seemingly unimportant details could have been included. They had to sort of combine some scenes, and railroad other stuff to present it faster. Most notable: when Frodo puts on the ring, it's not very subtle, in the book it seems to start of with a vague sense of being watched - and when the Fellowship breaks up near the end they sort of combined some scenes. Oh well, had to be done.

III) There were approximately 2 moments where I didn't think the CGI was not perfectly seamless -lets see, that's about 100 fewer times than the next best heavily CGIed movie I've seen... Those were both in Moria.

I was going to say that if they were going to gloss over little details, they could have minimized the Aragorn/Elf (her name escapes me) romance -but in retrospect it was pretty much minimized, and the scene was aesthetically beautiful so scratch that one. That's just my preference anyway...

title: A must see movie
review:
From the moment I saw the stills, I knew that Peter Jackson had created images that had bounced around my head for the last 20 years. I just had to see this one and was not disappointed. Every character, every set,every effect is just how you play the book in your head.

I salute Peter Jackson for finally giving us all what we needed. Lord of the Rings has never been able to be fulfilled by mediocre special effects or animation but gentlemen, we have the technology...

For those few who have not read the book, this film invites you to be entertained and it never fails to deliver on any level.

The visuals, sounds and pace are perfect. The humour is distributed just when you need it and it even made me cry! I don't HAVE to see this film again - I NEED to. I don't have the words to say just how brill this movie is - just go and see it and then you'll know what I mean.

title: Great performances...
review: The acting was very good all around...lots of familiar faces in this one. I am not a 'Rings' fan, but saw this with a friend. It was entertaining and has hooked me for the second movie. Effects and makeup were believable.

title: Better ending than the book
review: I'm glad they incorporated the first chapter of "The Two Towers" into the ending of the first movie. Much better. The changes to the story in general were well done, and did detract too much from the story line. If I had one regret, it was that they did not show the friendship between Gimli and Legolas grow and overcome their ancestrial bitterness into an unbreakable bond like it was in the book. The additions more than make up for it! You get a real sence of the evil at large much more in the movie. Can't wait for the next installment.

title: A perfect adaptation of a great book!
review: Although much of the story had to be changed or omitted due to time constraints, FOTR is a masterpiece of film.  Director P. Jackson brings out a dark quality to the story which only highlights the plot.  The actor's performances are right on the mark with I. McKellen, E. Wood, and I. Holm being the most outstanding.  I have waited for a movie version of this book since I was eight years old.  It has a special place in my soul and my expectations were very high going into the theatre.  I am thankful to say that my criteria were met in every aspect.  All of the key moments in the book were depicted with passion and expert film-making.  Many special moments were left out, but that is simply inevitable.  Finally, a genuine classic film version of a classic story.  This movie is truly one of the best fantasy films ever made.

title: Good thing the holidays are slow for me.
review:
I'm going to have to go back and change all my votes for other movies on IMDB.COM so this movie is rated in the proper perspective.

I'll try to say something different than the usual "it was great", "best movie", "blah blah blah"...which is all true, by the way.

My favorite part of the film is...I'm having a difficult time here....how about the fight at Amon Hen. Yeah, at the end of the movie. That whole scene was beyone thrilling. FYI - don't p*** off Aragorn.

And I really felt sorry for Frodo. It seems everybody wants to kill him for some reason. He gets beat up, stabbed, almost eaten/drowned, chased, grabbed, shot at, run over....and this poor guy has two movies to go!

As for it following the books....no film can exactly duplicate a book. So if you're going to have a hang up over it then you'd better get over it. Judge the film on it's own.

title: You've never seen anything like this!
review: Unbelievable!  I truly have NEVER seen anything like this movie.  You will love it.  However, DO NOT make the mistake of bringing young children to this movie.  It is simply too intense for kids.  Ian McKellen could very well win best supporting actor for this performance.  Elijah Wood was also excellent.

title: beautiful
review: This is the most near to perfect film I have ever seen. I cannot wait until tonight when I will see it again, much less next December when the next one is released. The only reason I didn't run out of the theater and into the next showing was that after another 178 minutes, I wouldn't have gotten home in time to go to work the next morning. This movie is what film making is about.

title: Fantastic
review: This is an amazing film. I felt like I was present at the beginning of an absolute classic.  The scale of the cinematography is extra-ordinary, the Shires are twee and quaint, Mordor is amazing.  It remains very close to the book and the pictures it conjures up are so close to my imaginings, it is uncanny.  Hugely recommended.

title: One of the best movies I have ever seen
review: This movie was great all the way through.  The small plot holes did not affect how good this movie really was.  The way the actors worked together, and the special effects alone make this movie an instant classic.  I highly recommend seeing this movie at least twice.

title: The Greatest Adaptation Ever, The Greatest Movie of 2001
review: The greatest film of 2001, and who knows?, maybe the greatest ever. The adaptation Peter Jackson does is amazing, the best ever. The Middle-Earth is real, with the real sceneries commented in the book, great performance by the actors...its big!!!

title: Definitely worth the wait!
review:
It was always obvious that it would be Steven Spielberg that would make this movie. When I first heard that Peter Jackson should do it, the images that flew through my mind were hobbits mangling orcs with little lawnmowers, brain-eating uruk-hais, and alot of really weird puppets. Later, when I had given it some thought, I knew that he would pull it off, since his greatness lies in his ability to realize his visions, whatever they may be.

I love Tolkiens work. I have read the books over and over again. I have played the roleplaying game, the boardgames, seen the movies, and heard the radio theater version. It's fair to say that I waited for this movie with great anticipation. I was going to watch it with a critical eye, and totally ignore all the usual hype. Here are my takes on the film.

(Possible Spoilers Ahead!)

I was greatly moved the intro. It was fantastic. I cannot believe it is within our grasp to produce such images, but there it is. I had tears in my eyes. Then Hobbiton, I was there. It was exactly as I had imagined it. The hobbits, Gandalf, Bilbo, Frodo, they were not actors. Jackson and his crew have found a way to capture images through time and space, and shows us how it actually looked! There are no other words for it but...Magic.

And it goes on, and on, and on... The images never ends. They just gets bigger and better. Usually a movie have a few memorable moments, but this is not such a movie. This one is shock full of them! Hobitton, Bree, Rivendell, Moria, Lothlorien, Isengaard, everything is there.

Ok, I will quit this raving even though it is hard.

How are the actors doing? Well, sir Ian McKellen as Gandalf delivers a razorsharp performance, so does Christopher Lee as Saruman. Bilbo is fantastic, Frodo is totally believable, as is the other hobbits. John Rhys-Davies as Gimli is pure genius, Legolas are played by this incredibly beautiful guy whom I cannot recall the name of, Viggo Mortensen are a natural Aragorn, and Boromir is perfectly casted. The Oscars comittee will have a busy time this year.

Isn't there anything that is flawed with this film then?

Yes, there is! Sometimes the music makes me think of Titanic. Perhaps there were one or two flashbacks to scenes shown earlier that were superflous. And...*SPOILER* Glorfindel were replaced by Arwen, but then again, how would it be possible to film old Glory? I forgive them for that. Other than that, I cannot find anything negative about FOTR. Three hours seemed like 1,5, and that's a good thing, since the chairs are not always perfectly comfortable in modern theaters, to say the least. I, on the other hand, saw the movie at northern europes largest cinema, with very comfortable chairs, with my boyfriend, with a big bag hot mini-doughnuts and a few cans of cola.

If you are the least bit interested in good cinema, you should not miss this one. I give it 9,0 out of 10. Why not 10? Well, there will be two more, and when they have been released in a couple of years, believe me, it will be 10.0!

title: An emotional journey to Middle Earth
review:
What a sensational film, so beautiful that it transports you to a living, breathing Middle Earth. I cannot think of another book adaptation that has been done as well!

Every actor did a super job and Peter Jackson has created a movie that we should be all grateful for; How unearthly the Elves were not just actors with prosthetic ears and a bow but alien creatures so tantalizingly different. Amazing!

I was struck most of all by the locations that seemed so perfect and I firmly believe that New Zealand's tourist industry has been done great favours.

So take three hours out of your life and take a trip to Middle Earth. You will not be disappointed, for once the hype was right.

title: -= SPOILERS INSIDE =- Not perfect, but far and away the best attempt to date.
review:
I would like to echo the sentiments of so many on this thread, and say WOW! I was charmed by the sheer scope and beauty of the movie, and well impressed with the characters and acting. Though flawed, this movie is the closest anyone has come to putting Tolkien's vision onto the screen successfully.

Parts of the movie seemed rushed, due to time constrictions, but then other parts seemed over-long, slowing down the story. Also, Elrond's obvious bitterness about the failure of the race of Men, while only hinted at in the novels, is blown far out of proportion in the film. Several points in his main dialogue with Gandalf he seems openly angry and deeply resentful. The use of Arwen as an active role was again a deviation from the core story, but not a serious one. Glorfindel was a minor part, and substituting Arwen allowed Peter Jackson to introduce a strong female character early on, instead of Arwen being merely Aragorn's eventual prize. I was very happy with the way the movie ended, at almost the exact timing of the book ending, with just the right amount of foreshadowing needed to pave the way for "The Two Towers" next year.

As I said, most of the deviations and flaws can be attributed to time restriction and a desire on the director's part to simplify some of the story elements. Hardcore fans of the novel will find them a little jarring, but they do not detract in any great way from an otherwise excellent film. Also, it bears noting that "The Fellowship of the Ring" is by far the more drawn-out book of the trilogy. There is a wealth of back-story and history and groundwork that Tolkien had to lay out to establish his world and his characters. The second and third books are more fast-paced, more dynamic, and, with the sundering of the Fellowship, we have several parallel storylines that can be explored as Aragorn, Gimli and Legolas "...hunt some orc.", while Frodo and Sam continue the quest.

As I left the theatre, I heard a group of teens debating on whether LotR would surpass Star Wars in popularity, and arguing the strengths and weaknesses of each series, a pointless discussion, in my opinion. Not only are they representative of two completely different genres, but the story arc is dissimilar. With the original Star Wars Trilogy, Lucas takes us through victorious ending in A New Hope, a bitter near-defeat/uncertain fate ending in Empire Strikes Back, and back to a victory in Return of the Jedi. The Episodes I-II-III trilogy look to be starting the same pattern. Lord of the Rings, however, shows us no victory at the end of "Fellowship". If Jackson follows the books, there is no victory at the end of "The Two Towers" either. There are minor triumphs throughout the books, but no definitive Defeat Of Evil! victory, until the final book.

I give the movie a solid 8/10, for technical brilliance, excellent casting, grand/epic scope and cinematography, but to someone who's read the novels probably 15 times in the last 15 years there were enough inconsistencies to spoil it for me just a bit.

Looking forward to Two Towers in 2K2.

Elphin

title: Three Hours Never Went So Fast!
review:
I have read the books and the movie was no disappointment! Even at 3 hours, much of the book had to be omitted. If you have not read the book do not despair. All the background information you need to understand the plot is nicely explained in the movie.

The characters were wonderfully portrayed. Having read the book I recognized each of the nine instantly. It is obvious that a lot of people who love the books were involved with making the movie. I won't say this is the best movie ever made but it is one of the best!

This is not a movie for young children. There are some very intense scenes that justify the PG-13 rating.

title: Better than a pan galactic gargleblaster!
review: Although I went to see this amazing story come to life on the screen filled with expectation I could never have hoped to believe that the movie would be so explodingly wild, exciting and beautiful! I rated J.R.R. Tolkien's AND Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings a perfect 10. If you don't you must be out of your mind :)

title: You don't see this movie you live it!
review: I can't say enough about this movie.  It captivated me from start to finish. I am a huge rings fan anyway and i was not disappointed in the least.  The acting was incredible and the size relationships was seamless.  I give it a 10!

title: They did it right. Tolkien on screen.
review: With only a few minor and excusable exceptions, they captured Tolkien RIGHT with this movie.  The look, feel, and sound of the book was represented properly on screen.  I truly loved it.  My new favorite fantasy movie ever, and the Best Picture of the year.  If the Academy slights FOTR by denying an Oscar, it will be a tragedy.  Hands down the best movie of the year.  Go see it, you'll love it.

title: Wonderful
review: I really enjoyed this movie.  I thought the cast was wonderful and exciting to watch.  The cinematography was amazing and the film flowed smoothly.  It was a bit slow in parts, but by the time the film ended, I was ready for more.  It holds true to the novel most of the time.  There are a few things added and some deleted, but overall I feel that it stuck true to Tolkien. I would definitely recommend this movie.

title: There is no way this movie could have been made any better.
review: From the opening scene of Gandalf's ride into the Shire to Frodo and Sam heading off alone towards Mordor at the end the film had me riveted to the screen. Peter Jackson has done such a tremendous job with 'The Fellowship of the Ring' that it's going to make waiting a whole year to see the next installment very difficult. All my fears of how bad this movie could be were dashed in the first 5 minutes and I just sat back and marveled as the movie unfolded at how well Peter Jackson brought images and scenes to life that I had only been imagining for decades. All the demons of Mordor are realized in frightening detail (and ugliness) as was the naive innocence of the hobbits. All the great places of Middle Earth, The Shire, Elrond, and Lothlorien, are brought to life with breathtaking detail and beauty. This is a movie that needs to be seen on the big screen. A must see for all fans of Tolkien's epic.

title: Easily the best film of all time
review: This film has everything a film lover could wish for. Excellent story, superb effects and awesome acting. Peter Jackson has made a film that will be talked about for years to come. Quite simply it is the "PERFECT" movie.

title: What a film
review: I went to see this film on the opening night and i loved it. It is the best film i have seen since The Matrix. I can`t wait to see the next one. I didnt think any one in the film gave a bad performance. It is one of those films that could be watched over and over again and i will be doing.

title: Awesome film.
review:
This film at once celebrates everything that has been achieved in this artform since the first moving pictures flickered into life while defining the standard by which all films will be judged from now on. The day after seeing the film I am still searching for words to do it justice. For the first time, special effects are so real that you simply accept that what you see on screen is real. You are completely immersed into Tolkien's world and propelled along on the most amazing adventure imaginable.

I don't think I will bother going to the movies anymore - I can't imagine anything topping this...except the next in the trilogy perhaps.

title: Wow!
review:
I've been reading Lord of the Rings over the years. I have seen many a movie based on a book turn out disastrous. Regardless of the deviations from the original source material, this book captures, at least for me, the heart of the Fellowship of the Ring.

This was a singular event in my personal cinematic experience. I fully expect to only have 2 additional similarly emotional experiences in the remainder of my life - and that would be the final two parts of this trilogy.

I was talking to someone last night and I was asked - what other book has the depth, richness, and general appeal to be made into such a film event. We were at a loss for additional candidates.

My expectations for this film were fully met. After I have seen it a few more times , purchased the DVD (along with a player), and done the same with the next two films of the series, I will feel like I have reached the pinnacle.

title: Worth the wait
review:
Seldom in life is something so strongly anticipated not a disappointment. This film is one of those rare occasions.

The editing of the story from book form to film is masterful. If I had known in advance how much streamlining would be done, I would have been concerned. But it was handled so well, that you have to think hard to see what was cut.

I did think that Elijah Wood looked too much like Wynona Ryder in Girl Interrupted, which led me to wonder whether Angelina Jolie would be playing Gollum.

Bravo, Mr. Jackson. You film met and exceeded the expectations of 35 years of waiting for this film. Can we move up the dates on the next 2?

title: Et Eärello Endorenna utúlien - From out of the great sea to Middle Earth I have come
review:
I walked into the Lord of the Rings: the Fellowship of the Ring with really high expectations, and I walked away having had all of them fulfilled. The incredible satisfaction of seeing Orthanc towering above the Gap of Rohan, the pristine beauty of Rivendell, the sad, solemn enchantment of Lothlorien, all of these were portrayed with incredible detail and realism. The amount of work that went into this film is simply astounding.

The Dark Riders were incredibly scary and the balrog- oh my, the BALROG. I won't give away any secrets, but the character that scared me most in the film, more than Gollum (who makes several shadowed appearances), more than Sauron, more than the Uruk-hai, was Bilbo. Ian Holm does a more than realistic job of portraying the old hobbit, he does a terrifying job of it.

The Shire is amazingly green and homely, while the mines of Moria are equally vast and majestic. The river at Amon Hen is unreal, and all of this was filmed in New Zealand. New Zealand is Middle Earth, there is just no two ways about it. Caradhras is incredible, likewise the city of Minas Tirith (which we glimpse briefly) is ancient and beautiful. The film has very high production values and it shows. The detailed cities and realms are beyond description in some cases. I can't wait to see Treebeard and the Ents.

The Elves are enchanting, beautiful and sad. The Dwarves are steadfast, loyal and hardy. The hobbits are frightened, small, but very determined and possess courage beyond their size. Men, men are honorable, but their faults run deep as well. The film does an excellent job of portraying the separate races. Another point worthy of note is how well the wizards (both Gandalf and Saruman) are done. They are played by impeccable actors and the duels between them are the finest battles you will see.

I could write reams more about this film, but in reality, all I have to say is, "Go and see it.. now. Go and buy a ticket and watch it. And then, watch it again the next day. There is too much and too little in this film that you cannot miss it. See it today. It's worth it."

title: Breathtaking
review: A simple review: the film is breathtaking in its scope and depth. It may not be exactly what Tolkien imagined but I would think that it comes very close, and as a film it succeeds on all levels. The viewer does not merely watch but participates in Frodo Baggins' mission, and not once but many times he is overcome with emotion. This could very well be the most beautifully realised film this, or any, year and it deserves all the critical praise it has been getting. And more... I want to see Peter Jackson up on that podium in March! This is a grand cinematic gift that deserves to be recognised. It is the first time I have been truly enchanted watching a movie since I was a kid.

title: Where's the 15 ?
review:
I'm looking for the 15.... I wanna give 15/10 for LOTR.... It's the most incredible thing I've ever seen in my life !

Thanks Peter Jackson ! Thanks God...

title: Almost spot-on
review:
Well, I've been waiting twenty years for this film to be made, ever since I first read LOTR when I was 12.

I've been a frequent visior to fan websites this last two years or so and knew before sitting down in the theatre what had been changed.

Generally, I thought the film was very good. It certainly could not have been made before as a live action film - the techniques necessary have only recently been available.

The casting has turned out to have been fairly astute, with special mention going to Ian McKellen, Sean Bean and Viggo Mortensen. The scenery was terrific with Barad-dur, Minas Tirith and Isengad fabulously realised obviously paying homage to existing artwork painted quite a few years ago. Only Moria was a bit of a disappointment, being a little too bland and not giving the impression of what it was - not just a mine but the largest Dwarven city in Middle-earth. The world of the ring (i.e. when you put it on!) is fabulously depicted and clearly shows how the corrupting effect of the ring could be cumulative.

Now onto the section of the review which deals with my impressions of the changes made within the film, both positive and negative - SPOILERS BELOW!

The Bad

--------

1) Liv Tyler during the flight to the ford and the river scene. I can understand the requirement to appeal to a wider section of the audience, and have nothing against her replacing Glorfindel (much) - but on the whole this was a big mistake. Frodo's nightmare journey to the ford and his subsequent defiance to the Nazgul is simptomatic of the hidden strengths of his character. Additionally, not having Elrond conjure the river and Gandalf embelish the waves is also irritating. 2) Galadriel at Egladil. In the book when Frodo offers her the one ring, she does not light up like an extra from a cheap science fiction series and need a quick nap afterwards, her attitude is very self-mocking and she dismisses it quite easily with a laugh. She has already made her mind up on the subject long before. There is also NO mention of Nenya at all - WHY???

3) While the Balrog was well animated - fautlessly in fact, it's too big! Gandalf subsequently wins by throwing his enemy off the mountain - will this be changed also?

The Good

--------

1) Aragorn - In the film, Aragorn questions himself a lot.

He is deathly afraid that he has inherited his ancestor's (Isildur) weakness for the ring and will fail the fellowship because of it. This also makes sense as to why he has not made himself known to Denethor before. 2) Boromir - In the film he explains the reasons that drive him to push himself so hard, his Father's approaching dotage and his fear that Minas Tirith will fall soon.

I have a few other minor niggles, such as why this new Uruk-hai character feels the need to run in slow-motion and roar every five seconds but as a whole I am glad this film was made and look ahead with enthusiasm for the remaining two installments. Lastly, in the UK the film was given a PG rating with advice that the film "may be unsuitable for children under 8" - this is very irresposible on the part of new line. There are clearly scenes in this film that will give nightmares to children under 12.

Ah well - now waiting for the DVD to come out :)

Happy Christmas all

Dan

title: It sure leaves an impression
review: Dense, intelligent, exhausting, mythic, and awe-inspiring. I fear it will take several viewings to get the genuine impact of this film, but my initial reaction is that this will be added to the collective unconscious of humanity. It will probably last. In the way that many of the classics have. I suspect I will be watching this thing and its sequels on brain-memory chip, or whatever the heck storage technology we have 50 years from now. And remembering how I felt back in December of 2001 when I first stumbled out of the theater.

title: A nanosecond of betrayal, 3 hours of glory (some spoilers)
review:
The first time I saw this film I must admit I felt pungent feels of betrayal, for just a nanosecond, before appreciating why the causative scenes had been changed. The fact that the time-frame has gone from a few years to a few days through me. Other aspects however gleefully reminded me of what a great thing the silver screen can be.

Take for example Gandalf in his fury, growing in size and menace (and Galadriel for that matter). In the book, for those who are become overly complacent reading it, there is a tendency to put fuzzy edges on some of the nastier bits: the film orcs were nastier than I imagined; Bilbo's sudden "Gollumisation" at Rivendell REALLY made me jump; Gandalf's fall in Moria (though you know he is Maiar, and can't be killed as such); the perception of the world by one wearing the ring - scary!; and I guess my mind didn't do justice to the scenery. I have climbed in many places from Snowdonia (Wales) to Kathmandu. It is these places I see in my head as they travel, but none compare to the majesty and beauty of New Zealand!

Finally a word on the Actors: Elijah Wood encapsulated the absolute, gut-wrenching weariness of bearing the ring. The Constant evil, the weight, the menace and the whispering! Its effect on Boromir was marvellously played out by Sean Bean, and Sean as Samwise was the true steadfast, strong (and probably highly intelligent, yet humble) companion. Ian Mckellen - what a STAR! He is now Gandalf in my own mind!

Well done PJ, EW, EM, SB, VM, IH et al.

title: See it twice, NOW!
review:
The film is magnificent. Some die-hard book fans may have problems though as I did. The first time I saw it, I had a problem with some of the inaccuracies, and a few other minor beefs. See it a second time and those problems seem to erase themselves, as you can then judge it on its own merits rather than a comparison to the book.

This movie will only get better with time. Flawless imagery, soundtrack, acting, battles. The book took a hard cut, but it couldn't be avoided w/out resulting in a 6 hour first film. I am greatly looking forward toward a Director's Cut with some of the scenes cut for time's sake. The audience would have stayed longer- the 3 hours pass like 30 minutes!

title: You've got to see it
review: It's not the best movie I've ever seen, but probably the most impressive. There was only one bit I thought was done badly, most was done brilliantly and some bits were awesome. They managed things in the film I didn't think they'd even try and I wish I had been less impressed by some of the effects as they were so good I was distracted by working out how they were done. In all, I felt it was too short and would have happily watched hours more.

title: Too much hype...
review:
Hi everyone,

I have read The Lord Of The Rings trilogy about 10 times so I knew the storyline before I went to see the movie. Purposely I watched very few trailers and TV spots so as to give the movie a fair chance. I was not surprised though with the product of the Director's efforts. I found that the acting the Hobbits did was poor, they seemed sometimes to be wacky just for wacky's sake. The camera angles used to show the height difference between Gandalf and Hobbits was awkward, the cut of the tape was almost visible! I feel bad because the movie had spectacular scenery and stayed true to the book, even in its ending. For 3 hours and $8.00 I was angry about the ending. I knew that the Fellowship was to break up, but for the screen to go blank as it did garnered gasps from the crowd and even a few boos. I can't wait for the next two movies, they will be much more interesting than this first one, it just sets the table. Almost like the dirty tricks played by Star Wars Episode I.

title: What a disappointment!
review:
LOTR: FOTR is not a bad film. It's moderately entertaining and it'll pass the time adequately. But it certainly isn't what we, the movie buffs and Tolkien fans, were expecting. Some comments:

If you're going to make a movie about Middle Earth, make it look right. The scenery is very nice, and so is the set design, but many of the pivotal scenes look just plain cheesy. The matte paintings that seem to be a prominent feature of almost every exterior scene (and Moria) are generally poor. Check out the non-moving waterfalls in some of the particularly cruddy Rivendell exterior shots, just as an example. They just didn't feel *real*. I never passed beyond that boundary of suspension of disbelief. Now, this may seem like a trivial complaint, but it made me realise that I was watching a mere movie.

And speaking of sucky CGI effects, most of the monsters were remarkably unrealistic. The film seemed to suffer from the "Mummy Returns" syndrome - thinking you can get away with lousy effects if you speed it up enough and use lots of annoying camera angles. The cave troll was a particularly good example of this - a potentially exciting action sequence ruined by poor CGI and irritating/confusing camera work.

Examples of CGI cheesiness: -The fireworks at Bilbo's farewell party, -Many of the exterior scenes featuring landscapes (the real thing) and ruins/buildings (a very obvious CGI/matte inclusion). -The cave troll. Very poorly animated - the filmmakers speeded up the action to try to hide this. It didn't work, though!

What was with the jumpy cinematography in the battle scenes? It was just plain annoying.

Too much Saruman! They must have gotten Christopher Lee really cheap, because there were endless swooping helicopter-view shots of him and his orcs, none of which added anything to the film. His role has been greatly expanded from the book, without any real benefit to anyone.

The filmmakers obviously thought that we were stupid, because they seemed to spend a lot of time refreshing us about just how Sauron lost the ring. Get used to the prologue's shot of the ring on his dismembered hand because you'll see it a lot.

And in case you're wondering why this is a three-hour movie, it's because a large portion of it consists of close up shots of the Ring, either on various tables or on Elijah Wood's palm.

The casting was generally good. Sadly, though, the key character, Wood as Frodo Baggins, seemed to spend a lot of the film either looking confused or looking scared; somewhat lacking in character development. I loved Ian McKellan as Gandalf - very charismatic and likeable. Aragorn, Boromir, Legolas and Gimli were very well-cast, and added a lot to the film. Pity about a simian-looking Hugo Weaving as Elrond. And what was with Liv Tyler in there anyway? And as for Cate Blanchett as Galadriel - she was just plain creepy. Why make some of the elves look like escapees from "Planet of the Apes"?

I think the filmmakers got orcs and zombies confused. The orcs in this looked a lot more like the undead - dripping flesh, etc. Especially those serious gravity-defying wall-climbing moves they were doing in Moria!

The main Uruk reminded me of Darth Maul - looks vicious and gets about five minutes of teeth-baring screen time.

The film felt gloomy and dark, without the hope and the spirit that pervaded even the darkest moments of the books. Lorien, instead of being a place of beauty that Frodo would loved to have returned to, was just creepy.

Where was the character development? What did the characters get out of the story? At the end, what made Frodo a different hobbit to his persona in the beginning? In the book, quite a lot, but in the film, nothing. What drove any of the characters? The film gave us lots of insight into their interactions with CGI monsters, but that's about it. The characters in the film were defined only by the cleanliness of their hair rather than the unique people they were in the book.

The pacing was poor. Sharp action sequences combined with long, drawn-out dialogue and "mystical" moments. Just as you were getting used to one aspect of the film, another one appeared jarringly.

On the other hand, there were some exceptional moments and some true cinematic highlights: Ian McKellen as Gandalf was towering. His sheer presence made some of the more tedious scenes worthwhile. His quirky humour made the character come to life. I was expecting Legolas to be an effeminate blonde elf, but Orlando Bloom plays him with vitality and charm. He's also extremely physical - this is the sort of archer you'd like to have on your side. Viggo Mortensen creates a memorably physical Aragorn - he really *is* Strider. But the acting honours in the fellowship belong to Sean Bean, who is a tormented yet ultimately noble Boromir. He's possibly the greatest revelation in the cast. Ian Holm is also worth a mention, playing Bilbo. He has a very memorable and startling moment with Frodo in Rivendell.

I loved the tension of the Moria scenes. Peter Jackson created a true sense of claustrophobia and desperation. Very true to the book.

I also loved the creation of the Shire. The sets were wonderful and very realistic. Pity that trend didn't continue.

The Nazgul were excellent - the sound effects were really stomach-turning. The Moria and Balrog sequence (apart from the orcs) was pretty good - with an excellent sense of impending doom. The sequences where Frodo wore the ring were brilliantly done, and really conveyed the sense of danger.

The soundtrack is really good, and appropriately used.

Now, don't get me wrong - LOTR would be a much better film if you went in there expecting a lot less. It's not intrinsically bad - it's just the small things that take it from being great to being merely mediocre.

title: Truly a masterpiece ...
review:
Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is by any means a true masterpiece. A masterpiece in vision, filming, set, special effects-technique, sound, music ... you name it. Words can not describe the magic I saw in it, it is simply one of the greatest film experience I have ever had - and I've been around since 1960 (come on - I went f.i. to a premier of the first and original The Planet of the Apes).

The Fellowship of the Ring will surely go down in history as one of the greatest films ever made. Everybody MUST see it (and I am sure everybody will). Congratulations Peter Jackson, cast and crew. If you are ever in the neighborhood ...

And I have to say to those few sorry souls that do not see or find the pure magic within this movie: I really, really feel sorry for you...

title: Courage is in the innocence of the Hobbits.
review:
Roger Ebert's vision of Middle Earth did not exactly match with Peter Jackson's. He believed that the Hobbits took the side stage to more powerful characters and action. Though there was plenty of action and other characters very powerful, there was little doubt to me that this was Frodo's story. Not only does the story open and close with shots of Frodo, but from start to finish it maps his growth. We watch him lose his innocence slowly step by step with trials that would strip most of us completely.

Wood is wonderful as Frodo and pulled me completely into Middle Earth. I found that I was not anticpating the next fight/confrontation/battle of swords and sorcery, but the how Wood handled the battle within. His eyes showed us more than most dialogue. I can not say enough about how Frodo was portrayed.

What Peter Jackson did best was incorporate the smallest of details so that we would not forget the magic of Tolkien's story and how he weaved symbolism within effortlessly. Two thoughts that would not leave my mind were that the greatest of power can come from the smallest of things and that courage is not in the feat we commit, but is within the apprehension with which we have before committing it.

See this movie to be entertained and inspired.

title: Breathtaking Just how a film should be made
review:
I saw LOTR pt 1 last night and it took my breath away. Yes I have read the book (at our school it was the benchmark for fast reading, my record being 5 days) the bits of the book that were edited out were wisely chosen, of course I was a bit upset at the removal of Tom Bombadil, but I admit some people may not have understood the meaning of this part of the book. And also the change in the scene of the Flood at the ford near Rivendell. But Peter Jackson has captured the spirit of the story completely, I have never felt so much terror in a cinema than the scenes when Frodo puts on the Ring, it was a whole new take on the putting on of the Ring ( I had previously assumed that he just saw his surroundings) The Balrog in the mines at Moira was spine-tingling and the scene where Galadriel shows Frodo a glimpse of what could happen if she accepts the Ring from him was pure nightmare. The film explains perfectly why Frodo is the ideal ringbearer, he hates it more than men admire it for its power and would be glad to be rid of it. What scared me most was the scene at Elrond's where Bilbo asks to hold the Ring one more time, and when he gets nasty toward Frodo you see how much of a hold this Ring possesses over its previous slaves. Christopher Lee is a superb choice as Saruman the White, quite fitting for the Hammer horror actor to portray the sinister leader of the Wizards. Sean Bean is great as the warrior Boromir, I wonder if Peter Jackson had seen his portrayal of Sharpe? The most surprising character was Sean Astin as Samwise, he is utterly convincing as the gardener who is dragged into the adventure.

In short, a five star film with five star performances all around, Peter Jackson captures the essence of Tolkien's epic.

title: Still stunned by perfection
review: One day ago was the greatest day of my life.  I went to see what I saw as perfection.  I was in Middle Earth.  It is a movie that will change your life.  I am still riding the high the movie gave me.  I hope this high lasts forever.  Finally a movie has come to us that brought us a true fantasy world.  I shivered, I cried, I laughed, I cheered, and I cheered.  I did not want to leave the theater, I wanted to watch it again and again.  I better get a loan for how many times I want to see this movie.

title: Breathtaking
review:
Wow. I saw TFotR yesterday and am about to see it again. It's actually the first movie I will see more than once at the cinema.

Peter Jackson and the whole cast and crew did an incredible job. I actually felt like I was really there. That was something Tolkien in his IMO way over-rated book never could. I've read far better books than LotR but I've rarely seen better movies. This whole "yeah, nice, but not as good as the book"-babbling by those "fans" can easily be ignored. It's the same as with "Dune" which is an great movie but also gets bashed by fans of the book it is based on. The book was nice but the movie was better.

And I especially want to point out Cate Blanchett, Ian McKellen and Christopher Lee as they were so perfect for their roles as Galadriel, Gandalf and Saruman.

I gave this 10 out of 10 and can't wait for 2002 when it will continue.

title: too hasty
review:
Ai...

I have read Tolkien's book one year ago and was very impressed. I didn't expect the same fot the movie because it''s simply not possible.

It is possible to shorten the story and make it an excellent movie. Peter Jackson had a chance but just missed!

The movie could not take me, why not? I think its because of some choices of PJ. Making a movie of this book, the first you have to ask yourself is: what feeling does the book give me and how do I bring this in the movie!?

This first part of the complete story in the book gives introduction to various characters and takes care that you will love the characters. Also the story let you feel that the trip Frodo is making is long and hard. Third, you're going to love Middle-Earth and don''t want it to be destroyed.

In stead of these goals Peter Jackson focus is on battle and escapes. He gives you nice landscapes and pictures but wasted a lot of movietime with battles in stead of subtle tense.

I believe that in the next parts the movie will be better because Peter Jackson is more a person who would have liked these parts with lots of fights.

Overall, 8/10

title: It seems a long time til next christmas (possible minor spoilers)
review:
This has got to be the best movie I've ever seen. The landscapes, filming, locations, special effects and castles, the entire audio-visual expression defies description. It has to be seen. Considering the expectations and hype, Peter Jackson and his team has done an admirable job of adapting Tolkiens epic saga to film. And even though the movie cannot be completely true to the book (it has to stand on its own), I think the creative freedom they have given themselves works very well.

Ian McKellan is perfect as Gandalf, the Balrog of Moria is excellent, and the opening sequence is a masterpiece in filmmaking.

10 out of 10.

Regards, Per Axel

title: An extraordinary achievement
review:
This film was by no means perfect. Occasionally the SFX looked slightly rough, or the (new) dialog dipped dangerously into the realms of cheese. The linear nature of the travelog meant that there was a slight sense of and then, and then, and then...

However, all of that can be forgiven. Like the Godfather, it offers an aesthetic experience far beyond cinematic storytelling - you are absorbed into a sensory experience that will, if you allow it, transport you entirely out of your own world, into one that is a subtle blend of Tolkien's Middle Earth, and Peter Jackson's own imagination.

title: One of the best epic films ever made.
review:
Ok, I am not a die-hard J.R.R. Tolkien fan, and I have not read any of the books yet. Just wanted to get that out of the way.

With that said, let me add that this is one of the best movies to hit Hollywood in a while. It has everything: action, drama, comedy, thrills, chills, memorable performances, and great visuals. This is the formula for an unforgettable epic, and I for one cannot wait for the second and third installments.

I could be nitpicky and comment on how the hobbits really didn't look as short as they were supposed to look. I could complain about the lack of certain character expositions. But you know what, while those were things that I noticed about the movie, it didn't bother me one bit. Let's face it folks, the movie is never as good as the book. I know this, for I read many books before they become movies. I chose not to read any of the Lord Of The Rings novels before I saw the movie, for I wanted to experience the film with no pretenses.

This movie is a great example of Hollywood living up to its potential. So many times does Hollywood make crap, especially when it comes to event pictures such as Pearl Harbor and Armageddon. In LOTR (Lord Of The Rings), we get the perfect juxtaposition of great storytelling, with the effective usage of special effects. LOTR uses lots of CG effects to create some of the most breathtaking landscapes, and some of the most harrowing images of evil, ever created in film. LOTR also has many great performances: Elijah Wood (Frodo Baggins) does a fantastic job playing the reluctant, conflicted hobbit who must bring the ring to its destruction. He plays it with such emotion and grace that I found it nearly impossible not to feel for him. Ian McKellen (Gandalf) plays the 7 foot tall wizard with poise and dignity. You never question his character for a minute. Let me just leave it at that. Supporting turns for Sean Astin and Viggo Mortensen (Samwise and Aragorn, respectively) are right on target, and often moving as characters both devoted to Frodo in their own ways. Look for other amazing supporting performances by Hugo Weaving, Christopher Lee, and Ian Holm.

The music matched the various moods of the film, and was not overbearing as other epic soundtracks can be sometimes. The score is merely a storytelling tool, and it is used well in this film. I would rather have a more restrained score in this movie, as many of the images in this movie are soft and muted, utilizing certain earthtones and shades of green. If John Williams scored this film, chances are we would have a loud, striking musical score that would probably eclipse some key elements in the film. Not that John Williams isn't a master at what he does, but this movie is not Star Wars or Superman.

Bottom line, if you want to see an amazing piece of Hollywood magic, if you want to be swept up in an wonderful epic story, or if you just want to see something that is worth the 7 bucks you pay to get in the theater, go see this movie as soon as you can. If you have read the book(s), try not to expect too much of this movie, as this is just a movie, and you may trick yourself into not liking it if you think about it too much. Sit back and enjoy a classic epic film series in the making.

I give it a 10 out of 10.

title: The best film of the past 10 years
review:
For someone who has never managed to read the book. I entered the cinema with an open mind. My only expectations were created by the trailers and the excellent score I purchased weeks prior.

Fellowship of the rings is excellent. The acting is flawless with all those involved making truly believable characters who you really care about. The special effects are breathtaking and work with the story rather than as an expression of "look what we've done" that has blighted recent films and the scenery is fantastic. The score by Howard Shore is brilliant and really adds to the sense of wonderment you get when watching the film.

After seeing a wide range of films this year including all the blockbuster movies I can honestly say this beats them all by a mile. If you have an imagination and want to be totally immersed in a film for three hours of your life go and see this film.

My only criticism.... 12 months till the next one.

10 out of 10. Awesome, Outstanding, Wonderful,Fantastic, the best.

title: Breathtaking
review:
Totally breathtaking - dispite some deviation from the book, this film managed to capture the atmosphere of Tolkien's world excellently.

However, without the Two Towers and Return of the King, it feels incomplete.

The next two years are going to drag..

title: Perfect in every way
review: I've been a fan of The Lord of the Rings since I was little and have read all the books. The film brought them to life exactly as I had seen them in my mind. Beautifully put together holding true to the story from start to finish an amazing experience. It was a dream come true. I just wish I could see the next one tomorrow.

title: A masterpeice of epic proportions!
review: Wow - this must be the best movie I have seen in years. After 3 hours I felt like it had just started and I wanted it to go on to tell the rest of the story there and then. Quite honestly I think it could have done with being made into a longer movie, possibly 4-5 hours with a break in the middle as there was enough plot and adventure to fill that.

title: The best film. EVER.
review:
Words simply do not do this film justice. Peter Jackson has crafted exactly what Lord of the Rings (and fantasy movie in general) fans have been looking for for years.

In recent memory, movies have not been kind to the fantasy genre. Dungeons and Dragons. Ewww. Jackson makes Middle Earth a very believable place, where not everything is pristine and clean, and every person is completely believable. Viggo Mortenson makes an amazing Aragorn the ranger, Elijah Wood is both pitiable and courageous as Frodo Baggins, Ian McKellen is perfect as the quintessential wizard Gandalf, and Sean Astin gives old Samwise Gamgee that endearing nature that any reader of the LOTR series has come to know and love. The doomed Baromir is expertly portrayed by Sean Bean, and even Liz Tyler, an actress I have always liked but never really respected as a thespian, gives an outstanding performance.

The key, however, is in how Jackson so obviously loves and respects the series to make everything so believable. The faithfulness to the book is at an unprecedented level, and the details are nailed perfectly, right down to the way the elves, humans, and dwarves have different fighting styles. This is easily the best fantasy movie of all time, with only Willow to even compete, and, as my summary presents, simply the best film of all time.

title: Thank God I've read the books.
review:
No, not because it's a horrible movie (which it isn't), but simply because waiting 8,760 hours for the sequel The Two Towers is cruel and unusual punishment. Waiting 17,520 hours for the last installment Return of the King is torture.

Going in, I thought I knew how Gandalf was. I thought I knew how Frodo was. Boromir, Strider/Aragorn, Gimli, Legolas, Samwise Gamgee, Pippin, Merry. I was wrong, Peter Jackson was right.

I thought I knew what the Uruk Hai looked like. I didn't, but Peter Jackson did - and his vision is MUCH scarier. Same goes for the Balrog and the Orcs.

Some people mentioned, that this was the biggest special effects extravaganza EVER. Maybe it was, but I only noticed two special effects: Gandalfs fireworks and the Balrog. I KNOW the actors aren't really 4' or 7', but in this movie it's not special effects, it's just real.

Acting? Nope - didn't see any of that either. When people are themselves, they don't act - they just are.

I'm tempted to say "wow", but that doesn't do this movie justice. Neither does anything I've written thus far. The only thing that does this movie justice is seing it - but seing isn't believing; what I mean is, I've seen this movie, but I can't belive it worked, I can't believe that it's this good, I can't even belive it lasted three hours (felt like fortyfive minutes), last but not least, I can't believe I have to wait 8,760 hours to watch the sequel.

Someone should kidnap Peter Jackon and hold him ransom for the other two movies.

title: I thoroughly enjoyed this movie
review: I have just finished watching the first movie of the series and am very happy to report that it was everything I had hoped for. While I missed a few characters that where in the book but not the movie (eg. Tom Bombadil)I know that it would not have been possible to put everything in a movie. Sam's relationship with the pony, how he rescued him, things like that. But over all it was a great ride and wonderfully filmed.  I was thrilled  to see how they made the Hobbits look so small.I wanted to say also the casting was just excellent. The actors looked like I had imagined when reading the book. I am presently re-reading the 3rd part and will find it difficult to wait until next December for part II. Since the story gets darker I know that the next 2 films will be even more exiting.  Good work to the director and all the players.** "One ring to rule them all, One ring to find them, One ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them. In the land of Mordor where the Shadows lie.''**

title: Lord of the Rings was disappointing and over hyped
review:
In all likelyhood, my opinion will be the minority, but I feel I need to provide some balance against all the buzz. Having read and enjoyed the books when I was younger, I knew the film would be epic - and it was. However the film fell short (in my opinion) on a number of levels. Even with 3 hours to work with, there was little character development and virtually none of the details that the books provided. When characters died, I did not feel any empathy or loss. Too much time was spent on broad camera angles. For example, during the birthday party there was very little personal interaction amongst the characters, it was 5 minutes of general party shots and dancing. Throughout the movie we were bombarded with spectacular views of the landscape, which is all well and good, but it left this viewer wondering what these characters really were like. Another example is the fight scenes, granted they were well done but there was little detail to the actual combat and I never really felt that the characters were in danger. I never was on the edge of my seat, however I did jump once or twice.

Net net, the movie was enjoyable, not very compelling, and in my opinion only an average movie at best.

title: Brilliant, beautiful - Failure
review:
I watched the most anticipated movie of my life last night, one I had waited 26 years to see. I desperately wanted it to be the best film of all time and was afraid that my expectations were too high. Now I have seen it, my feelings about it are very ambivalent. The feeling about it depends on where I am coming from, am I watching simply as a cinema goer or as someone who loves the books.

As a movie, it is awesome. The acting fails in one place only and that is Galadriel. I felt that Cate Blanchett was stilted and that her character was too dark. She only became decent after she had past the test. For the rest, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen, Elijah Wood and all the rest excel at their roles. The scenery, the filming and the CGI were all breathtaking. As a movie I feel that this will take at least two Oscars - Original Score and Effects. It may well take Best Film, Best Director, Best Supporting Actor, Best Writing - Screenplay Based on Material from Another Medium.

I have no reservations about the quality of this film and Peter Jackson deserves every scrap of praise that he has received.

So why my reservations. A torturous analogy I tried after seeing it was that while the book was roast beef with all the trimmings, the movie was only roast beef. It had all the main ingredients of Tolkien's meal, but lacked the trimmings to make it as memorable as the book. Too many of the small details which make the book so absorbing were missing. Yes, I know that to include it all would have made the film too long, but was it necessary to include all the stuff about the creation of the Uruk-hai (not in the book) at the expense of other more important elements of the novel. It also seemed to me that in the film Saruman was simply a servant of Sauron, whereas in the book he had his own agenda.

To recap the film was brilliant, it was beautiful, but it failed to capture the essence of the written version. Also, as an afterthought, let me add, it was infinitely better than Bakshi's version.

It is not best film of all time, but it is one of the best. It is probably the best fantasy film of all time, taken on it's own merits and the FX are the best to date.

What rating would I give this film, I don't know. It depends how I view it, on it's own merits or as an adaptation.

On it's own merits 9/10. As an adaptation 6/10. I'll be kind and roundup - overall 8/10

title: High Art
review:
Cinematic high art!

Captivating and mysterious, the tale has begun, and there's been no tale like it in the history of moviedom.

I assumed that LOTR:FOTR would be a movie you could compare to all the other fantasy movies of the past, but alas, that is not the case. There are no other films to compare it to, because it is a unique and uplifting film with no equal to speak of.

Rating this movie is not possible. You can't rate a movie with no equivalent to compare it to.

Citizen Kane, The Wizard of OZ, Casablanca, The Godfather, Pulp Fiction. They are all movies that changed the art of movie making, and they left their audience with a real sense of wonderment. A grand achievement of their creators, and LOTR:FOTR is no different.

Movie history, has been accomplished.

title: M-A-S-T-E-R-P-I-E-C-E-!!!!!!!!!
review: not just the most beautifully shot movie of all times, not only (finally) a classic for the genre of fantasy, not only an artistical masterpiece, not only incredibly tense and epic, but finally a real adaption of the LORD OF THE RINGS! This is the best thing that has happened to me in my life and a dream come true! praise Peter Jackson and his folks for what they have accomplished ! Thanks to everybody that helped. And remember, we still got two coming!!!!!!!!!!

title: Makes me wanna read the books
review: As it states in the title, I have not read the books- just The Hobbit and that I read twice hating the characters both times I read it. Certainly puts ANY fantasy movie to shame. I don't think this will be a big blockbuster. Nerds don't bring a lot to a box office. However, It will be set as THE fantasy movie to be measured by.

title: Can't wait for the next book
review:
Yes it's not the same as the book but what film ever is. That said I was amazed how some of the descriptions put in the book came to life on screen. Frodo looked wimpish probably due to the actor playing the part. I always imagined him a bit more tough looking but create portrayal. The film does not jump across the first book like I imagined it would, yes it does speed along but are we going to sit and watch 6 hours on screen instead of reading a book, I don't think so.

I have read the books at least 6 times and watch the animated version over 10 times so I am possible biased in my views, but I can't wait until next week during the xmas holidays to see it again and will but it as soon as it is available on DVD.

The Orcs are brilliant and the elves just magic, I thought the dwarf may have been less hairy and a bit more earthy looking, but the characters were almost like I imagined.

As I say Can't wait until the two towers is released and the the final episode.

Go and see and enjoy it as a movie and nothing else

title: Bravo Peter Jackson!
review:
As a die-hard fan of the book I was prepared to be disappointed, I couldn't visualize Elijah Wood as Frodo and was highly sceptical of an enhanced role for Arwen. However, most of all I was fearful that it would end up being 'Disneyfied', the darker undertones sanitised, leaving only a sickly sweet potboiler.

Thankfully I was wrong, the film isn't perfect but it is so close! Peter Jackson and his team deserve the highest praise for their boldness of vision, their determination to make the fantastic appear commonplace and the unbelievable as possible.

The acting is top notch, with Sean Bean snatching the honours, from my point of view, giving a very rounded and polished performance to perhaps the most complex of all the initial characters. The special effects, fight sequences, costumns and locations are all generally excellent. However, I would reserve the greatest accolade for the screenplay itself. Jackson has taken tremendous liberties with his source material and yet it all works. Every change is justified and helps the narrative flow or the visual style. In fact I would go so far as to say that I actually prefer the screen interpretation of Aragorn to the one in the book.

Downers - yes, there are a few cheesy lines, but most of these are lifted straight from the book, but at no point does it get overly sentimental as so many Hollywood blockbusters do. The hobbits overly quick acceptance of Strider is a little rushed and the failure to convey that significant periods of time are elapsing between the events that unfold on screen are minor quibbles. Personally I think the movie is too short and hope that the web rumours of an extended unrated directors cut prove to be true one day.

In summary this is a must see film and personally I am envious of anyone who sees this film with out any knowledge of the book, to be swept along by Peter Jackson's vision without knowing what comes next must be close to cinematic bliss.

title: Superb, Excellent, Overwhelming, Surreal, Real and an allround highly enjoyable adventure!
review:
This film is the greatest film accomplishment I have ever seen.

The adaption from the epic book, written by J R R Tolkein, was done suprisingly well. Even though people moaned about how it cut things out, the parts cut out were parts that should have been cut from the movie, because it would be boring otherwise. The acting was highly impressive and totally captivating. The sets and scenes... well... its the beautiful landscape of my country (New Zealand) what do you expect (p.s. the scenes are amazing). The costumes and props will easily talk emmy and grammy awards and Peter Jacksons direction style shone through and made the movie vibrant, and alive. It seemed so real and captivating. It made me feel I had just been on an adventure. I loved it, my all time favourite. A definate cinema and video must see! 10/10 :-)

title: It's simple. I saw the first showing & I can't wait until the next film!
review:
It's simple. I saw the first showing & I can't wait until the next film!

The acting, the plot, the visual feast...oh my!

I will go and see it again with friends and family. It was so refreshing to see characters from my youth brought to life with such creativity & character.

For those who have not read the book, keep in mind there are 2 sequels planned and this release is only the first 'book'.

title: EXCELLENT! A True Spectacle!
review: What a terrific, magical movie! The almost 3 hour film flew by and the wonder of the book was fully captured on screen. Please go and enjoy what has to be one of the best movies of all time! Can't wait for Part II.

title: They did it, they finally did it.
review:
Being a long time fan of Tolkien, I was anxious to see what Peter Jackson had in store for us. Though my expectations ran very high, I was not let down. The seemingly impossible task of putting Tolkien magnificent world of Middle Earth to the big screen let us all wondering if the screen would be big enough.

After the not entirely successful animated version from 1979 by Bakshi, most Tolkien readers was left with the hope that someday, in the all too far future, someone would finally have the vision, the technology, the drive and the money to do it right.

Peter Jackson put up the vision, New Line Cinema put up the money, the rest is before our very eyes becoming movie (/literary?) history. Alan Lee's stunning artwork has been brought to life perfectly. Though some might disagree, which they are entirely entitled to, that the story has been altered, it has not been changed in any way that disturbs the essence of Tolkiens masterpiece. Many people are very sensitive to this type of alteration, but Peter Jackson has changed only subtle things that would make for a movie better suited to represent the original intent of the author.

Basically, everything in this movie works. The plot is well told and engaging. The characters are perfectly believable (I particularly enjoyed Sean Bean's rendition of the all too human Boromir and not enough praise can be given to Ian McKellen for his bringing Gandalf to life). The scenery is perfect too the degree that I suspect they have found a passage to Middle Earth. The rhythm, mood and flow is also no less epic, homely and intense, when called for.

All in all, perfect is the word that come to mind. Well, done mr. Jackson and associates! We look forward to seeing the first one repeatedly until the next one arrives.

title: Visually stunning, boring in parts, but I will see it again!
review:
I've not read the book so didn't know what to expect of the story.

First the negatives

The pacing and plot disappoint, 2 hours of build up then 1 hour of action then a rather abrupt ending that feels more like the end of a paragraph than the end of a book.

The score: I hardly remember it. Perhaps because it was so well integrated into the movie, or perhaps because it was dull.

The 2 "comedy" hobbits are bearable, but buffoons. They teeter on the cliff that leads to annoying valley.

The positives

The film looks beautiful and the scale is huge.

The FX are fantastic, but I *expect* things to look this good.

Vigo Mortensen and Sean Bean are great in their roles.

While it feels 3 hours long, at no point did I want it to end.

So far, a 7/10. On a second viewing I think it could rise to a 9/10.

title: Greatness!
review: Rarely does a movie move me so much. Never, and I mean never, has a blockbuster type movie ever lived up to the hype till now!! From the opening credits to the closing credits a fantastic epic in every sense of the word! Absolutely a must see, see again, and own on DVD! It's hard to express the sheer awesome-ness this film provides. Amazing special effects intwined in Oscar-calibur acting! Ian McKellen is simply amazing as Gandalf! I have never read the original Lord of the Rings, but after seeing this great movie I went straight to the book store and bought the entire trilogy with a giddy excitement like I was in grade school!!! It will be a long wait until the next installment, however it gives me plenty of time to read the Lord of the Rings and let the experience of seeing the Fellowship of the Rings sink in....and sink in deep with the cherished favorite films of mine! 10 out of 10 all the way!

title: beautiful
review: Absolutely beautiful... Wonderful script..the changes in the story are appropriate... Superb casting... have no fear in seeing this movie, you will not be disappointed.

title: Passionate film making at its best, god bless Mr P.J.
review: If you don't know the story go see it, if you do you will love it. My girlfriend is a big Rings fan, I myself was not so aware, but was a huge fan of Peter Jackson. It is a must see, I have seen it twice in the 15 hours since it publicly opened in New Zealand. The first time was brilliant, and the second time was an experience; you wont notice the 180 minutes run time. I strongly urge you to see a real fantasy movie and tell that John Hughes idiot to go back to Home Alone, Harry potter was just ok, I know it was a kids movie, but so is the LOTR.

title: My voting criteria
review:
My three criteria for voting were:

do I want to see the film again? will I buy the DVD when it is released? does it make me want to read the book?

Answers in order:

Yes, Yes and No (but it did make me want to re-read the book) and I now want to read the Silmarillion.

My only negative comment "the book is better!"

title: Just like a dream come true
review:
I've been a fan of Tolkiens books since I was about 12. I was kind of nervous about the new movies, but I like Peter Jackson movies since "Braindead" & "Heavenly Creatures". So I thought "Hey, let's give him a chance".

Then it happened - the "New Line" symbol disappeared - the movie began And about 3 hours later I had to face reality again, and it was very hard to leave Middle-Earth.

My conclusions from watching "Fellowship of the ring" are: 1. - It is impossible to make a movie exactly like "The Book" 2. - You will never see a better adaption of "The Book"

I think everyone involved in the making of the movie made a fabulous job.

It was a big risk for New Line to make this movie - I hope in the end it will pay off, because sometimes these risks have to be taken to bring movies to a new level. And this movie is definitely a new level, so everyone go watch it !

title: EXCITING!
review: "A long expected party", yet a long expected movie. Thank you Peter Jackson for bringing to the screen our immortal dreams. I watched it only yesterday and was deeply impressed. Words ain't enough, though; you simply have to watch it and feel the breeze of Middle Earth! I adore Strider and Frodo really; see who you will like! The film may differ from the book but the soul remains and that's what really counts!

title: I'm still blown away
review:
I got out of this film about 3 hours ago, and I'm still reeling. I have the feeling that I'm going to be reeling for many years to come. I saw a classic tonight- one that evokes the way I first felt when I saw Star Wars. But, somehow, it's better than Star Wars- it holds more weight on its own, it's got so much heart. Technically, the film is a marvel- great acting, story, special effects, blah blah. That's all well and good- a lot of movies have that. But this film blows them all away because it has an emotion, a moral core that seems somehow unapproachable by most Hollywood pictures. Maybe it's Tolkien's spectacular setting and writing, or Peter Jackson's love for film and this work in particular, but this movie transcends what movies used to be before tonight.

Astounding. Spectacular. Lovely. Epic. Heartbreaking. Beautiful.

That's all the words I can muster for now.

title: Amazing.
review:
I have always loved this story and i have read the books a few times. As everyone else i have my own picture of how shire, rivendell and all the other places looks like, what amazed me was that many of the places in this film looked almost exactly as i imagined.

This is a 10/10 film, it's a perfect interpretation of the best fantasy story ever written.

title: Very good!!!
review:
****Some Spoilers***** This review is really intended for people who have seen the film, or have at least read the book. All anyone needs to know who has done neither is to do so A.S.A.P

I have been looking forward to another attempt at a film adaption of the Lord Of The Rings, and I'm not disappointed.

I have followed the gradual seepage of info on this film during it's production with interest and well before its release I was happy with the final casting, the actors seemed to fit the bill well, and guess what, I was right!! (Although I find Liv Tyler a little bland, it didn't matter because Arwen is a relatively sideline character anyway)

Orlando Bloom, as all the reviewers were saying, does ooze style, while Viggo Mortenson, Sean Bean and Ian Mckellen are able to pull off their unusual scripting, typical and appropriate in fantasy films, without ever seeming cheesy. At times McKellen is particularly outstanding. But I found Elijah Wood a real surprise. Not having seen much of his other work I wasn't sure what to expect and I was pleased to see he fits into the role perfectly, progressively showing inner feelings and depth as the character changes during the film. The other Hobbits were sidelined somewhat during this film, Merry and Pippin being used as a bit of comic relief more than anything else, but I expect from what I know having read the books that this will change somewhat in parts II and III, especially for Sean Astin as Sam, displayed rather strongly at the end of the film in a scene where I actually began to shed tears ( yes i felt a little sad at my age but what the hell), the friendship between sam and Frodo will undoubtably be a greater element in the sequels. And Sean even manages to pull of a semi-accurate English country accent to good effect.

Action wise the film excels!! Again a key element is the style in Legolas' use of a bow and arrow, while the swordplay is inde fast and furious, without having to resort to ripping off any Matrix stylee effects as too many films in recent years have done. Despite what another comment says I would very much liken the action to Gladiator, possibly even better. The other strong point is the orc design. There position is more clearly defined in this film than I remember in the book, in terms of what they are and the attention to these and various other creatures beyond their just being the foe adds more fear in their presence, much like the stylistic animation did in the animated film.

Visually the film is stunning, and CGI is used much better here than in most films of recent years that have rendered exotic landscapes for films, perhaps because it seems more sparing, using a lot of genuine New Zealand landscape to keep a real feel to Middle Earth.

If I have any real quibbles(?) with the film,its in minor details. While I expect obvious liberties with plot and story events for the transfer to film, most of which seem acceptable, I wasn't too keen on the representation of scenes in either elf city. The Council of Elrond seemed too vague, all the feeling of real planning and heavy decision making was lost, and Elrond seemed to have too little command of his own council. (also, Arwen should never have stopped the riders when it was a representation of the extent of Elrond's powers within his kingdom). Similarly in Lothlorien Galadriel's part seems redundant of necessity to the story, the meeting seems all too short to convey anything.

Again, one other minor point, although I know this is looking ahead more, but it would have felt better to have had a little more of Gollum in the backstory, and in the nearness and intensity of his pursuit of the ring during the journey of the fellowship. But this all becomes more important when he meets Frodo and Sam in Part II.

Overall though, the action and atmosphere of the film are the most important elements. Here Fellowship of the Ring really succeeds and it is here that people will be truly entertained. While people not really into fantasy might not be as adamant about the films strengths as others, I see no reason why everyone can not appreciate the films entertainment.

title: So much more than I hoped for.
review: I went into the theater expecting to see a ho-hum adaption of an incredible book.  I came out more excited than ever to see the next two.  I was completely gripped from the beginning.  Though slowed at first, I got caught up and was in suspense when characters were threatened, and cried when they hurt.  Masterfully done by Peter Jackson.  I had no knowledge of him before this came out, but, I will now follow his career carefully.  Also, I was impressed by Orlando Bloom, who plays Legolas.  I immediately came home and checked out his other credentials. Over all an achievement.  I have already spread the word to my friends. It is three hours long, but well worth it.

title: The first film I've ever seen that has lived up to the hype
review:
OK, so I've read the books, the Silmarillion and I've got the 13 hour radio play from BBC on tape. I am a Tolkien addict, and I went to the movie with huge expectations. Even so, The Fellowship of the Ring ensnared me right from the first frame.

Usually when my expectations are as high as they were for this movie I get really disappointed, but Peter Jackson delivers his stuff in such an impressive manner, that I still get goosebumps on my skin when I think back on some of the scenes.

If you only could see one film this year, this should be it.

title: Mindblowing
review:
I went to a special screening of The Fellowhip of the Ring yesterday, and i still can't describe the experience. Not a single person moved until the last credit faded from the screen..

This is one of those movies you want to see again and again. The locations are superb, just like the casting. The CGI is amazing, it's so extremely detailed you believe they actually "hired" some of the creatures straight from middle-earth.

I'm already counting the day's until The Two Towers hit the screens

If you like fantasy, go see this movie. If you don't like fantasy...Well, you will after seeing The Fellowship of the Ring.

10/10

title: Don't read too much about the film before seeing it!
review:
Quite simply, stunning!

From the special effects to the superb acting to the haunting soundtrack, this film deserves all the praise that has been heaped on it and more.

I first read the books only a couple of years ago, and was thoroughly drawn in into the semi-historical world Tolkein devised. This was something I had never experienced before, and not since; a book where the background is so detailed and carefully constructed that there isn't a scrap of doubt in your mind as you read that this place existed and these events took place.

You can perhaps imagine, then, my joy when I heard only a year later that this wonderful story was to be made into a film. I watched the trailers avidly and strove to uncover extra little details of the filming. I read every preview and review of the film I could lay my hands on before seeing the film. And in this was my great mistake.

For, you see, though this film deserves all the praise that it has received, it also deserves most of the criticisms. The sad thing is that I doubt that I would have noticed, or even cared, about most of the little niggles if I had not read about them beforehand. Hence I will not repeat them here, and I would urge you strongly not to read many more reviews before seeing this film - the fewer reviews you read the more you will enjoy this film.

And you will enjoy the film, trust me. It was emotionally powerful in places and had some of the best action scenes I've seen in recent years. The adaptation from the book is one of the best I've ever seen, and the scriptwriters deserve to win awards. There are parts more believable than others and parts more accessible than others, but as a whole, the film will leave you gasping, and wanting more.

See this film - just try not to spoil it for yourself by reading too many reviews!

title: IT JUST BLOODY RULED!!!! IT WAS AMAZING!!! (it has some minor spoilers)
review:
Ok let the fun begin! :-)) As I said the movie ruled! It was like if someone took Tolkien's book and made perfect images out of it and scrolled them in front of a big screen with narration! Everything was perfect!
