Afterall its difficult to imagine Boromir and Aragorn killing dozens of Orcs because they had such small introductions into the main plot.

No doubt the cinematography, the action sequences and especially the CGI work in the film was amazing, but again I say it, LOTR is a story, its not a video game.

Still I think that it is a major effort and for sure Peter Jackson did do a better job than many would have. But still, after watching Fellowship of the Ring, I am anticipating the next Star Wars even more. Somehow George Lucas has better grip on storytelling and narrative.

None the less, a magnificent cinematic acheivment.

title: I was enchanted
review:
This is by far the best film I have ever seen. I'm gonna tell you right away; I haven't read Lord of the Rings (working on it now though, and loving that too) but I soon learned that I had been missing out on something great.

Anyway, the film. From the first scene to the last I couldn't take my eyes of the screen. Everything about this movie was stunning. The landscape was perfect, the actors were superb and there was never a dull moment. While we were taken down into mines and up to the top of towers, I got a feeling I was actually soaring.

My mark for knowing that I really love a film, is that I remeber certain scenes from it. With this one, I remeber practically everything! I can play any scene I like in my head (allmost) and I'm counting the days 'til "Two towers", which I don't dubt will be just as good. I just hope I can finish the book in time:)

My fave scene would have to be Frodo beeing re-united with Bilbo at Rivendell. And also, when Sam jumps into the sea to follow Frodo to Mordor...gotta love that Sam.

If you haven't gone to seen this film in at the cinema yet, you better get your butt over there coz you have no idea what you are missing! Even though I'm gonna buy it on video, I am certain that it will be nothing like the thrill I had of watching it on a big screen. But honestly, go see it...what, are you still here????

title: Don't miss it!
review:
Wow ! This movie sure takes your breath away right from the first minutes of the film. The battle scenes are awesome and the director sure did a hell of a job recreating the unique atmosphere of the books. Of course some things in the movie differ a bit from the book but those are neglible because he has stuck to the story 100%.

Go see it !

title: AMAZING
review: I think that there is no better movie out there in movieland. Here is my two cents. I think there is no movie out there that is based on a book with so much detail. I think the movie had everything you could want. I've read all the books and I loved them. And maybe the movie more. I don't think it gets better. Only if you wanted to sit in the theater for ten hours and have the movie follow the book right to the last word. Everybody should all read and see the movie for themselves. But this is only one man's opinion. All I can say is, The Fellowship of The Ring was done perfectly, from the battles to the acting--and let's not forget the landscape. AMAZING!!!!!!!!!

title: Much better than the book
review: I am not a fan of the Lord of the rings books. I read them in high school and although I loved the action, I felt JRR.Tolkien spent too much time describing the leaves,trees grains of sand etc..... I went to see the movie because I like the general story. I was pleasantly surprised at how good the movie was. I will definately own it when it comes out on DVD. Beautiful cinematography. Very true to the book without the long descriptions. Anyone who has not seen this movie is missing a real treat.

title: Memorable... But Classic?
review:
One wonders whether the amount of net users in a frenzy after leaving the cinema pushed this to such a high spot in IMDB history. Don't get me wrong, it is a good film... a very good film. I found myself thinking about the film for days afterward - which is usually a good thing. But watching it - it lacked a completeness (and not just because it was the first part of a trilogy). It tended to get lost - chase - pause - chase - pause - chase - pause etc. No build up.

I've not read the Trilogy (only the Hobbit), and can't comment on the book to screen translation, but I question this film's position among the epics and classics of all time, especially when we look back on it in five years.

title: Words dont express...
review: Words dont, neh, words CANT express the truly awesome power of this films phenomenal greatness. The hype does not live up to the movie. Ever since I heard about this coming out three years ago, I have been waiting...and let me tell you, I AM NOT DISAPPOINTED! Without a doubt one of the greatest and most powerful movie ever made!!!

title: FOTR stands for Fantastic, outstanding, terrific, rejoiceful movie.
review: For more than a year I have been a member of imdb.com. A few months later I found out that they have a top 250 list for the best movies of all time rated by the public. When I looked at the list, I saw The Godfather at No.1 which has always been highly praised. I always now check out the top 250 daily to see if that has changed. Results: It hasn't. But when the first movie of The Lord of the Rings trilogy came out, things were about to change. The Fellowship of the Rings came out whopping The Godfather out of first place with a 9.7 rating. Godfather's rating: 9.0. For quite a few weeks FOTR remained as the most highly rated movie of all time. But when I looked up again one day, it was at No.2 with a 9.1. Godfather with a 9.0. Anyway, I'm one of the first to say this, but I'm dissapointed that it's not No.1. It may not be the best movie of all time, but it does deserve to be no.1 a lot longer than it was on at no.1. But I have to say I'm actually debating whether it's my favorite movie of all time because when I came out of that theatre the first time, I kept saying to myself, "that movie is the grace of cinema." I mean who ever is says that this is a bad movie, what are you smoking? I can't think of one bad thing to say about this movie. I mean I would hate to admit this, but Tom Bombadil was a waste of three chapters and there was no reason why they should of had him in the movie. I mean he was just pointless. But let's get to the good stuff. Half the stuff in the background was cinematography not computer generation. Elijah Wood was mistakenly called Elijah when he was born. His real name should be well, Frodo Baggins. Sean Astin as Samwise Gamgee was also fantastic. Every actor and actress did very well. As for the movie itself it was great at very aspect, acting, plot, action, drama, happiness. The movie had it all. The action I have to say to is that it was much more suspenceful than the book. It was very well done especially the last battle sequence. The best acors as i say again were Elijah Wood, Sean Astin, Ian Mckellan, and Viggo Mortenson. But as for the whole movie, it's one of the best movies I've ever seen. FOTR deserves a 10/10. And I'm really looking forward to the two sequels especially Return of the King, which right now is my personal favorite book. If FOTR is not nominated, I will lose all my respect for the academy. P.S: One of the best sword Mano e Mano's I ever seen in a movie at the end which is done by the leading orc and Strider (Aragorn) You wiill not be dissapointed with thus movie!!!!!!!!!

title: Absolutely fantastic, the greatest adventure I've ever been on!
review: In only my dreams could I have seen such a wonderful place.  This film brought me to tears on how good it really was.  I honestly expected the best and received better.  Only Jackson could of brought this film to life the way he did.  Congratulations!

title: Even more boring than the book...
review:
SPOILERS AHEAD! I have to admit that I am stumped over the love many people have for this trilogy of books. I plowed my way through The Hobbit, and have been trying to read Fellowship for about a year. Never made it past the Council of Elrond. Maybe I would have more of an appreciation if I read these books as a kid. The main problem I have with this story is that there is no suspense. You always know that someone or something is going to show up and save the day. But I decided to see the movie anyway, because everyone I knew raved about it. Plus, I did want to find out what happened at the end, since I could never make it through the book.

So, today I wasted three hours watching this horrendously boring movie. I first looked at my watch about 45 minutes in, and looked at it every fifteen minutes for the rest of the movie. I would've left, but I paid $9 and I kept thinking that it had to get better. What's the problem? Where do I begin...

1. No character development, as in the books. Who cares what happens to these guys? Not me. I was rather thrilled each time Frodo was stabbed, because I kept hoping maybe he'd die and throw a twist in the story. Nope.

2. The plot is based on the following: travel, battle, Frodo thinks he can't do it, someone tells him how important it is for him to do it, travel, battle, Frodo thinks he can't do it, someone tells him how important it is for him to do it, etc., etc., etc. Can you say boring? Furthermore, they never seemed to have any trouble during the battle scenes. I don't know, but those bad guys looked pretty tough. Doubtful that this goofy group could beat them.

3. Cheese factor is very high. Example: Arwen: "Do you remember the first time we met?" Aragon: "I thought I had strayed into a dream." Gag me. The rest of the dialogue is equally as corny. The women's voices (Arwen and Cate Blanchett) have a weird echo around them. Also lots of slow motion/close up scenes, that are supposed to tell us how the character is feeling, but instead are laughable.

4. The music was specifically placed to inform the audience when a dramatic moment was occurring. Without the music, it's doubtful we would have known, since the story simply kept repeating itself. With the repeat, it was difficult to know when a big thing was happening vs. a little thing.

5. 8 people have the power to kill an army of bad guys. This doesn't bother me in Star Wars, but it bothered me here, especially since the Hobbits have no fighting skills.

6. Stereotypical characters who mess things up and get the group into more trouble.

7. Too long. Way too long. Scenes were dragged out for much too long, for "emotional impact." This movie simply never felt like it got moving. When the first credit came onto the screen, I ran out of that theatre. Couldn't wait for this movie to end.

I will never watch this movie again, nor will I return to see the rest of the installments. Once was enough for me. Huge disappointment.

title: Very good film, if a bit overrated....
review:
Lord of the Rings' first installment, The Fellowship of the Ring, is an enchanting film to behold. Well directed by Peter Jackson, some of the set pieces and fight scenes are simply breathtaking. They have to be seen to be believed. However, it does have its share of flaws too. Overlength is its main problem, it never seems to end. As you can see with the average rating this film has, Fellowship of the Ring is quite overrated too. How this film can rank above such action classics as The Road Warrior, Mad Max, and Jaws is beyond me. Although not the best film of the year (my pick for best of the year is Memento), this film definitely holds its own in terms of book to screen adaptations.

Rating: 8/10

title: very good
review:
The reviews have said everything there is to say, so briefly, LOTR had just about everything in a film you could ask for, barring the laughing out loud humour, which it didn't need anyway & the time went be relatively quickly.

It's certainly not deserving as it's position of No2 of all time though. It lost marks for being a little too long, for being a stand alone film & a tiny bit too fantasy/sci-fi for my own enjoyment.

I've never touched any Tolkien, or even fantasy book in my time, but I prefer it that way, as I had no idea in the slightest what was coming next or indeed will do.

But all in all one of the best films in years & possibly my favourite 'Epic' or battle film ever & I'll be in the queue for the sequel.

A high 8/10

title: Great special effects, and very exciting--not my favorite, however
review:
I really enjoyed the movie. Seeing it in the theater was a neat experience, and I loved the special effects, scenery, and acting.

Having never read any of the books by Tolkien, I can't say much about that, except that my friends who did read the books thought it looked a lot like they imagined it, but that they did cut out quite a bit (but most movies that are based on books have many differences).

It was good that there was no swearing or immorality...There was a lot of violence, but not the same bloody gore as some movies have. Even though Tolkien was a Christian, the story is not really "Christian," and I don't agree with the use of a "good wizard". It is good against evil, with the good side winning in the end. Enjoyable, but still not my favorite movie.

title: Excellent but not No2 of all-time(!!!)
review: This is an excellent adventure but I think imdb has been... hijacked by fans of Tolkien in this case. At the moment I'm writing this the film is rated as the No2 movie of all times in imdb.  I am a science-fiction fan, I recently bought the book, I even played the board game (and liked it) and this was admittedly a movie with very good casting, excellent photography and scenery and a script that breezes through the 3 hours it lasts. Yet, I think that it lacks the depth or... inner magnitude that I would need to see in a movie to rate as a 10/10. For me an 8/10 or max. 9/10 is more than fair enough. As a sidenote, I cannot understand how the Lord of the Rings trilogy has been categorized into "SCIENCE-Fiction". There are 2 words in there you know and in my view this is simply "FICTION". Excellent but still plain "fiction".

title: Ignorance is bliss...
review:
I love this movie. (Please read, this is not your typical review) =c)>

I admit, "The Fellowship of the Ring" is not the best movie ever made. It has it's flaws, it strays from the book. But, I must admit, it is a very good movie. One of my favorites.

Here are some things I have noticed from the people I know, who review this movie:

A) "I didn't like the ending..." Hmmm, how many times have you heard this? I don't get it. How can you judge the ending, IF YOU HAVEN'T SEEN IT YET. "The Return of the King" is the ending. Unlike "Indiana Jones," "Star Wars," and any others, "The Fellowship of the Ring" is NOT a stand alone film. I'm sorry it isn't. It is the first third of a massive story. Do not judge the film based on the first third.

B) "Well, if this is the first third of the movie, how come they don't release it all together? Aren't they just trying to make more money by turning it into THREE films?" How bout this as an answer: Would YOU wanna sit in a theater for 10 hours watching one movie? I don't think so.

C) "It is too different from the book." Well duh. Of course they have to change some things, that is the entire point of cinema. It is an interpretation of a writing. May it start as a book, or a script, movies are always an interpretation of one form of writing. I have yet to see a film that is EXACTLY like the shooting script.

D) "There is not emotion. It is just based on special effects." If you don't feel the emotion, read the book. Even the image of Sauron touched me emotionally. After reading the book, you know SO much about the characters, their desires, their pasts, their futures, etc. (Which is something that can NEVER be completely realized on film), that the book is like a companion to the film. They work together to form an emotional bond. And, about the special effects? How else are you gonna make the creatures and landscapes look like Middle Earth? Are you gonna breed REAL orcs and trolls? No, of course not. The Special effects in the film are neccassary to move the story along. Without the special effects, Tolkeins most memorable scenes could have never been created.

Ok, so there are a few things I've noticed. So please, keep these in mind. This is a very good film, I have no doubt about it.

title: I Implore You
review:
I'm not going to do a review simply because there's so many of both negative and positive opinions, that I can't really add much that hasn't already been said in either context. But to call this the worst movie as many seemed to have done? It seems like many users here are simply upset that at one stage, LOTR was above The Godfather in the ratings and had a hefty advantage at being number one. So naturally, being the biased idiots that most human beings are, people began voting it down and trying to use the worst of excuses in order to justify their unfair ratings. LOTR has 1,800 users who've rated it as a 1 / 10, whereas The Phantom Menace has 1,970.

Can you honestly tell me that it was voted down so badly simply because it's the worst movie of all time as opposed to a few fanatics being upset at seeing it as the #1 movie of all time as according to the IMDB users? Whether or not this is the greatest movie of all time depends on individual taste. If you're a fan of Tolkien, a fan of fantasy in general, or simply can appreciate hard work that's come together so well, you'd be hard pressed to actually find any fault or justifiably hate this movie. It's without a doubt the best movie in a long time (Note: I loved The Shawshank Redemption, and even though I love LOTR, TSR remains my #1).

To say it's undeserving of the praise it's gotten and that it's not worthy of being number one is simply idiotic. Face it. Is it harder to manipulate the audience's sympathies through actors being mopey and upset and getting an Oscar (ala American Beauty, or many of the possible nominees for this year's Oscars), or is it harder to create an entire believable world and to do it well? You have your Willows, and you have your Gladiator's and LOTR's.

Whether it's to your personal taste or not, whether you truly believe it's the number one film of all time, don't put the remarkable work of hard working actors and directors down simply because you'd rate it a seven instead of a ten. Don't vote it down simply because you want The Godfather to remain there, or you want Citizen Kane to climb up, or whatever. Instead. Recognise it for the masterpiece of its genre that it is, and judge it on its OWN merits, rather than comparing it to others and trying to justify your inexcusable hatred and bias.

title: Breathless
review:
The only bad thing about this movie, for all intents and purposes is that it ends. Waiting for the next one will be painful. This movie was full of emotion, more so than even I figured Jackson would be able to pull out of us in the audience. I wish I could completely blank my memory or the books before seeing this, so I can be in the shoes of the un-initiated, but oh well.

This is easily the best movie I have ever seen, expecting to be topped only by the sequels.

I can't wait for the DVD either... I hope the rumours are true about adding back in some cuts scenes and the possible "R" version. 3 hours is not too long to sit for such a great story.

I saw it twice in the theater and can't imagine getting bored of watching it over and over.

The extremely small amount of flaws (most flaws I hear from people have more to do with the story or the fact that they didn't realize that part one doesn't FINISH the story) still couldn't warrant me not giving it a 10... so I did give it a pretty solid ten.

A masterpiece.  The Fellowship of the Ring edges above The Matrix and Star Wars as my favorite movie.  Peter Jackson brings the land of Middle Earth to live in a sprawling three part epic in which the fellowship (the hobbits Frodo Baggins, Samwise Gamgee, Meriadoc Brandybuck, Peregrin Took, Legolas the Elf, Gimli the Dwarf, Boromir of Gondor, Gandalf the Wizard and a mysterious stranger called Strider/Aragorn) must embark on a perilous quest to destroy the One Ring.  Kudos to Peter Jackson for his acomplishment of bringing J.R.R. Tolkien's masterful book into an unbelievably great movie. Peter Jackson's companies Weta Workshop and Weta Digital do an excellent job in creating the evil orcs and other such creatures and for creating the armor and weapons.  Sir Ian McKellen gives a memorable performance as the Wizard Gandalf.  From his battle with Saramun the wizard to when he shouts "You shall not pass" to the devillish Balrog,  McKellen gives an Oscar-worthy performance.  Childish actor Elijah Wood also presents a nice performance as the main character Frodo Baggins.  Orlando Bloom kicks major ass as Legolas the Elf and Sean Bean is worthy as the greedy then possesed then nice Boromir.  My favorite performance is Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn/Strider.  One of FOTR's strong points is its incredible special effects.  The CGI effects are very nicley done.  There is one thing that will make the hairs on the back of your neck stand up is the singal image of Gollum and his bone chilling voice, "My precious..."  FOTR is a very great movie and should be cherished for years to come.  ***** out of 5 stars. FOTR

title: thoroughly disappointing.
review: i had such high hopes for this film, and could not have been more shocked at how awful and hollow it was. the storyline was rushed and it took much away from the movie because it never allowed the opportunity to really delve into the characters. i also really felt more of the beginning of the story should have been portrayed as you never get that tolkien essence of a new beginning of not knowing what lies ahead and the innocence of the hobbits. far too much time was wasted on needless scenes revolving sauroman and arwen. finally, the camerawork was disappointing. in such beautiful landscapes as this there is definitely no need for so many facial close ups.  the scenery could easily have spoken for itself. now i can clearly say that there was not a single good film in 2001.

title: 9/10...need I say more?
review:
First of all, a review on the book itself: simply put, reading Lord Of The Rings is what got me started reading the whole fantasy genre.

Second, I loved the movie, and would have happily sat there for longer than 3 hours to watch it, if possible. Many people have posted complaints that there has been many changes in the movie. This is a valid point, in fact I have one of my own, which is the fact that the movie lacked, which I thought were critical character developments, such as for example, the developing friendship between Legolas and Gimli. Although, I do understand the point of this completely, as we can't expect filmmakers to give us one movie that is over 6 hours long. I would also like to point out that HARRY POTTER, the movie, was made almost exactly the book, and for some reason (I can't point out exactly what), the movie lacked the depth of the book, and was in my opinion: overrated.

In conclusion, the movie was an amazing example of how far special effects have come today. The cast of characters were more or less how I imagined them. The casting was superb. This is definitely a movie to watch over and over again.

Also, as a sidenote (to the powers that be), I will definitely be looking forward to future fantasy films, especially if adapted from my favourite books/series. But until then, I will be waiting breathlessly for the next two installments of this wonderful movie.

Overall rating: 9/10

title: Easy to admire, but flawed
review:
Fellowship of the Ring is a sincerely-crafted fantasy that benefits from earnest performances, beautiful scenery, and an epic scope. But the movie suffers from problems with pacing and focus, and a lack of movie "magic". FOTR is packed to the gills with story, at the expense of getting on with the story. Every scene was expertly crafted, but the sense of urgency in the action of most scenes ran counter to the urgency of the movie to move forward. The journey the Fellowship is on travels one place, then another, then another, then another, then another, etc. It becomes as tedious and exhausting to watch as that last sentence was to read. This also applies to the action scenes. There are so many of a similar nature, they begin to lose their impact. Finally, though sincerely played, I never felt endeared to the characters to care enough about their fates.

I have a feeling that this movie would play much better as a mini-series. But don't misunderstand my overall impression of the movie. I felt the need to address these flaws due to what I feel is the hyperbolic gushing of Trilogy fans, but I did like and respect this movie. It is in no way one of the top 50 movies of all time, but is certainly one of the 10 best this year. I give it 8 out of 10.

title: second viewing even better
review:
I had to see FotR again just to find out what I saw the first time, and what I saw the first time was amazing. I was so excited I missed important information given by one character about another, or about the plot, but the second time, everything made sense. And, it was still a fast 3 hours. The people I was with keep telling me they think it was good. Really good. First time round I gave it a 10. I still do.

This is a tight production; the acting is riveting; the FX are cool. Ok, it isn't minutely perfect, some cuts were made too quickly e.g. Aragorn surveys the landscape of Lothlorien then it seems the Fellowship is trooping through the woods. Just what was Aragorn thinking, or about to say. Great place? Nice to be back? then oops they have the Cold Welcome from the elves. One can guess, from reading the books; but maybe the cut will be on the DVD.

I have a single complaint, and that would be the forgettable trailers beforehand. I hope something better comes along or it will be a long wait for a good movie, til The Two Towers comes out. Meanwhile I want to see FotR again!

title: Loved it! Best film ever!!!
review: I'd go see this film everyday if I could!  What a wonderful cast and amazing scenery. Throughout the film, I laughed, I cried, I was frightened.  It brings about many emotions and you really get attached to the characters. Loved it, just loved it!

title: It was great. Wasn't bored once.
review: I would recommend this movie highly. I believe that the novel was accurately depicted (as accurately as possible in a 3 hour movie....the movie would have to be way longer to include it all). While watching it, it did not seem like 3 hours, and kept my attention the whole time. The only precaution I have is taking young children to see it. A 9 year old girl told me she hid under the covers after seeing it, but then again, my 8 year old brother thought it was great.

title: I'm Swimming against the current!!
review:
I know that I'm swimming against the current, but Lord of the Rings is another in a string of long special effects movies with little depth of character development and long,long spectacular violent scenes. This should be called "Monsters, Inc." For people who love the Rings Trilogy, this level of one-after-another "excitement" may be just what you were looking for. This movie went on forever...and just think there's more to come. Lord of The Rings marks the most mud, slime, drooling, ugliness, and bad dental work that I have seen in the cinema. I'm glad that they were able to use the same troll idea and figure from Harry Potter. I'm also glad that smells were not spread into the theater, since all of the characters, except Frodo were unwashed...years worth of filth. How did Frodo keep such a clean face?

Is this and other films' extreme length an indication of film quality? I don't think so. Interminable films do not equal great films. I'm interested in less phlegm, drool and ugliness,and more fine acting, tighter story lines and plot variation that holds my interest. I wouldn't want to see this again, so I guess I am glad I saw it once...ONCE IS ENOUGH. Sorry, but I'm proud to be in the tiny minority that couldn't wait to leave the theater before the credits rolled.

title: Absolutely outstanding!!!
review: I grew up in the time of epic motion picture making, when vision, daring and showmanship brought us "Ben-Hur," "Lawrence of Arabia," "Spartacus," and a host of others.  Sadly, that type of vision seemed lost in today's monumental budgets and miniscule stories.  And then came Peter Jackson... What audacity to tackle J.R.R. Tolkien's famous classic, especially as a live action film!  And what talent to pull it off!  He combined an expert cast, superb cinematography and top-notch special effects to re-create the beauty and terror of Middle Earth.  Howard Shore's music score with help from Enya is dramatic and emotional.  Obviously, the film is a masterpiece, standing head and shoulders above a ton of films over the past few decades. But the real tragedy about this incredible piece of movie-making will be the lack of awards it will attract.  If the Oscars were fair, it would obviously win the award for Best Picture, but the voters ironically do not vote for originality and vision.  Never mind, this film will be a classic for years to come.  And, I am anxiously waiting for next Christmas!

title: THE BEST MOVIE OF ALL TIME!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review:
WOW!!!!!!!!! THE BEST MOVIE I HAVE EVER WITNESSED!!!!!! ANYBODY WHO WOULDN'T LIKE THIS WORK OF ART IS LUDICROUS!!!!!!!!! MY INSATIABLE APPETITE FOR THIS MOVIE IS OVERWHELMING, I HAVE SEEN IT 4 TIMES ALREADY AND WANT TO GO AGAIN AND AGAIN AND AGAIN!!!!! Anyone who hasn't seen it yet had better get their lazy butt off that couch and into Peter Jackson's film epic of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Fellowship of the Ring. And there are TWO more coming!!!! I can't wait!!!! I was on the edge of my seat the entire movie!!! It's pretty sad but I already know alot of the lines from the movie. Simply breathtaking.

Enthusiastic Tolkien Fan Singerwen221

title: it IS possible to turn the book into film
review:
If you've read the book - go see the film. Very rarely has there been a really good screen adaptation of something so "verbal" as Tolkien's LOTR. I could not believe how well they visualized all the fantastic creatures, landscapes, events, etc.

Personally, I'm a bit disappointed by the portrayal of Galadriel (elven queen) - in fact the whole Lothlorien sequence -, but that is just a couple of minutes out of hours of excellent theatre. My favorites are the landscapes (Mordor in the beginning, Rivendell, Anduin river, the Moria mines!!!), closely followed by the evil creatures: even the ringwraiths (all the more terrifying in the book because they only exist in the spirit realm and cannot be seen) have been rendered quite adequately (to say the least).

Can't wait to see the second and third parts.

P.S.: judging from the negative readers' comments: having read the book(s) definitely helps to enjoy the movie more.

title: Incredible special effects, poor character development
review: This movie has incredible special effects and the cinematagraphy is excellent.  Watching the movie is more like a trip to watch a gallery of incredible pictures as opposed to getting wrapped up in a movie.  At almost 3 hours long, you would think they could have developed the characters a little more.  It seems like this movie is more concerned with making mention to as many parts of the book as possible and not going into depth about anything.  If you get up and leave after the first hour, you won't miss much.

title: Years of waiting was well worth it!
review: After reading the "Lord of the Rings" trilogy, I could not imagine a movie telling the story better than the actual books. I was stunned to find myself loving the movie even more than the amazing words. The movie had effects and pictures I could not even dream up in my wildest imagination.

title: Skeptics: Don't Be Hasty!
review:
=====To all of those who found this first movie lacking substance, depth, heroines, character development, plot, etc: for your own sakes, please, don't be hasty. *This is only the beginning!* You are about to get cinematically rocked like you've probably never been before.

=====Please indulge me: You are sitting at the dinner table and guess what? You have not yet been fed. You've only just finished your soup or salad. Are you still hungry? Well, I wonder why? And are you going to leave *now?* If you haven't eaten at this restaurant before, believe me, you have no idea yet what you are in store for.

=====I've read the books at least 4 or 5 times through the years.

With what I've seen on the screen recently, I am on the edge of my seat as I have never been in my life. I've witnessed that the pieces are now in place as I once believed I couldn't have hoped for, and the proportions of what are yet to come are nothing short of phenomenal. We are about to witness the most mind boggling cinema in history.

=====I beg you, don't kid yourself over the next couple years. You will likely eat your words when this grand-daddy-of-a-bearded-lady sings.

=====I am so grateful to be a part of this.

=====Shawn.

title: STINKER!
review: A much better read than a flick. A gross rip-off. Everything from the book is there but presented most poorly. And that music; it just plays and plays and plays some more, but why? Most distracting. For sure millions upon millions will go to the theater to see this film, but will they be there for the second and third installments? I don't think so,Bob.

title: The biggest rival ever for Star Wars
review: You don't need to be a Tolkien's reader or fan to enjoy this movie, because it could be interesting for anyone. I mean everybody has heard abuot the especial effects, the money they spend, the extras, the time it took, etc., but when you're watching the movie you just get involved by the strong and attractive environment of the movie, because behind the epic adventure you find a story that is based in human feelings like loyalty, friendship and others. In addition, the actors are just great: Elijah Wood is here with his most important role and he made his best demonstration of how high he can get. Ian McKellen gives life to Gandalf in a wonderful way and everybody else is in a good level. In general this is an amazing movie wich will make you enjoy the three hours it takes, and not just that you will finish longing for the next.

title: Great visuals are undermined by rushed pace
review: Peter Jackson, who must be one of the greatest visual directors working today, does as much as he can with the sheer volume of material that he has to fit into one movie (albeit in 3.5 hours), but , due to the overwhelming detail of Tolkien's epic, produces a frenetically-paced, somewhat unidimensional, film. In the end, it feels as though every scene was comprised of the good guys being hunted or exposed to a different foe, each of which is "of great power", as Gandalf describes it in his best sage's voice The casting and performances are, unfortunately, the other weakness of the film. Gandalf, Bilbo Baggins, and Sharuman do decent jobs, but I have to question the choices of Elijah Wood, a selection surely  based exclusively on his elfin physical traits, and the leader of the elves, the "Hello, Mr. Anderson" guy from The Matrix, a chronic overactor who turns his characters into parodies of themselves. Fortunately, the bad guys are the stars of this movie, and, with them, Peter Jackson does an excellent job.

title: The most epical story on screen
review:
There have been mixed reviews of "The Fellowship of the Ring", but more than 3/4's of them have been in the movie's favour. Without regard to the critics, this is the best film I have ever seen. (I'd have to point out that I am only 17, I haven't seen "The Godfather" but I do go to the cinema nearly twice a month!)

It is a truly beautiful film - the special effects are literally jaw dropping; the swoops of the camera are amazing and leave you breathless! The acting is perfect, Ian McKellan portrays Gandalf exactly as I had thought of him in the book, and although Elijah Wood didn't look very hobbit-ish (however, the special effects do help, however _little_ they may be ...) he was a brilliant Frodo.

The magnificent score by Howard Shore compliments the film, when the music swells you can -feel- it, and it adds to the film's journey of your emotions.

I have never cried so much at a film - it is simply so beautiful - the strength of the friendships within the Fellowship, the downfalls ... you're there with them, the viewer is experiencing the character's feelings and what they are going through on-screen. I was literally choked at the beauty of it all, and left the cinema emotionally exhausted.

Some of the things they left out, like Tom Bombadill I was a little disappointed about, but others, like the dialogue (which is very lengthy in the book) which shows the development of friendship between the Nine, would have made the movie far bigger than it is. Besides that, the acting of the characters said more than any dialogue could.

The exclusion of females in the book is a little disappointing, and I was glad that Peter Jackson included the love story between Arwen and Aragorn. (which, contary to what people think, IS included in The Lord of The Rings story - it is in the Appendix at the back of the book)

I've already written far more than I intended, but no amount of words can say how beautifully MAGNIFICENT this film is - the only thing you can do is go and see it, watch it in the cinema, in it's finest form, and "strap yourself in". A true epic.

title: At last!!! The legend has come to life!!
review:
The first time I came out of the theater after watching this brilliant adaptation, I felt totally satisfied, mentally and spiritually! I will go on to describe different categories of the movie in some detail in the hope it will help others better understand this timeless story.

First of all, if you do not like fantasy at all. DO NOT SEE THIS! This is as fantasy based as you can get. After all, it is thought by many to have been the definition of fantasy epics ever since the books came out in the 50s.

The landscapes, movies sets, environment,etc., are all spectacularly done. Hobbiton looked exactly as I had imagined it, considering all the work they put into making that set, it came out the way it should. New Zealand was probably the perfect place to create all the imaginary lands that we will see. Bree looked like it should, a small, rough village. Rivendell looked great, the Mines of Moria were of course spectacular. I thought Lothlorien looked very nice. Some people complained about how we didn't see hardly any of it. But on my second time watching I did notice more of it then the first time. And I thought the river area in the ending scenes was perfect for the events that happen there. I think Jackson did good by Tolkien and couldn't have been done any better.

I thought every single actor did a very heartfelt, wonderful job. Elijah Wood made a wonderful Frodo. Ian McKellen makes a stupendous Gandalf the Grey. Viggo Mortensen makes Aragorn come to life. I thought Sean Astin made a nice, very loyal and simple Samwise Gamgee. Dominic Monoghan and Billy Boyd did a good job as Merry and Pippin, although in this movie they were mostly the comic relief which isn't a bad thing, but they did do a couple of important things in the book which would have been nice to see but that is a minor complaint. Ian Holm is Bilbo Baggins! Also, Christopher Lee is Saruman! I have always liked Christopher Lee and I can't wait to see him in the next two movies, and Episode II! I was disappointed not to see Brad Dourif as Grima Wormtongue, but then I haven't read the book in awhile and I'm not sure how big a role he plays in this stage of the story. Even though I would have preferred the movie to stay more faithful to the book, I can't complain about Liv Tyler's Arwen. For one thing, she really isn't in that much of the movie. Secondly, I have noticed a few people complaining about the romance between her and Aragorn as being stupid or unnecessary or simply thought it wasn't in the story. Well, for your information she is in the books and they are in love. I thought it made sense in a way to expand her role a little bit. And lastly, she played the part very well. Hugo Weaving did a fine job as Elrond. Sean Bean did a great job as the conflicting character of Boromir. Cate Blanchett did a great job as the piercing and mysterious Galadriel. Finally, John Rhys-Davies and Orland Bloom were the perfect Gimli the dwarf and Legolas the elf. Some people have said they thought John Rhy-Davies was wasted in this role. They need to understand that this isn't a John Rhys-Davies film. In this film he is supposed to be a dwarf! And that is exactly what he is! You just couldn't get enough of the archery skills of Legolas.hehe The perfect cast for this story!

Peter Jackson was very faithful to the story. It was inevitable to have left out the minor details and a couple of the somewhat important parts in the story. But as others have already said, if you were to include everything the movie would probably be around 9 hrs. long! The story began just like it should. It proceeded at the correct pace, even though some people didn't like this, that is just the way Tolkien wrote it. And it ended almost identically to the book which I actually liked. Some people didn't like this and others thought that they screwed up with the ending. My advice is to read the book, and it is meant to be a cliff hanger. I can sympathize though, because I don't want to wait a year either!

I thought the sound effects and music were well done and were perfectly suited for the movie. The special effects were simply great. Fortunately, the movie still felt very realistic, and it just takes you into its world! I have to say that I loved the Balrog!! When me and my dad saw the animated version years ago, the Balrog in that film didn't match his imagination and it didn't really match mine either. But this time, I thought the Balrog was perfect!!! Another thing that has bothered me is that some people have said that this is simply just a movie full of fighting or its "walk, fight, walk, fight". I have to disagree because:



SPOILERS!!

1) The opening fight sequence barely lasts 2 to 3 minutes. 2) Unless you consider; the little tiff Gandalf and Saruman have, the brief semi-fight sequence between Strider and The Black Riders, the chase scene of Arwen and Frodo by The Black Riders, the duel of the wizards on the snow peaks, and the encounter with the sea monster at the gate of Moria; actual fight scenes, the next one doesn't show up until they are well into The Mines of Moria. And, even that isn't that long. 3) The next and final fight scene is when Boromir dies and Merry and Pippin are captured. This is probably the longest fight scene in the movie, but there's plenty of good interaction in the middle of it which means it isn't all mindless fighting, and even then it isn't too long. 4) So if you add up everything I have just said: 3+2+3+4+3+3+7+10 is approximately 35 minutes of fighting! And in my humble opinion, some of that isn't a real mindless battle scene! 35 minutes out of 3 hrs. does not make the movie one big fight fest, in my mind.

Anyway, I just wanted people to understand that this movie is mostly about substance with a minimum of actual violence. I hope this movie wins some awards later on! I can't wait next year for The Two Towers, and the year after for The Return of the King!! This will be one of the greatest trilogies of all time!

title: "All that glitters..."
review:
I first devoured these books when I was 10, and I have read them seven or eight times since. The inhabitants and issues of Middle Earth are important friends from my childhood, and the trilogy's sensibilities are part of my adult makeup. The full quote "All that glitters is not gold, not all those who wander are lost," has been an apt theme for my life. (Since the quote is not in the movie, I'm sure only the readers are reading on at this point!)

Which is all to suggest that the bar was pretty high for me in these movies. And it is with a very deep sense of gratitude and relief that I can say the Fellowship of the Ring has passed...summa cum laude.

I reject the most effusive commentary here. I've only just seen the film, and just seen it once, so whether or not it surpasses Citizen Kane, or whatever is being implied, is premature. However, it is as fully realized a vision as I could have demanded.

For the book lovers, the movie will not have the same rich detail and nuance. But it shows and tells the story masterfully. The upwriting of Arwen Evenstar's role is seamless and well-played by the very young actress. In fact, all of the casting is astounding, especially Bilbo, Gimli, Gandalf, Saruman, Boromir, Galadriel and Samwise. And the actors live into their characters well.

The least successful for me is Frodo. Elijah Wood is excellent, but too young. Throughout the film Frodo is shown as the holy innocent, while in the book he is an eccentric bachelor approaching middle age, a generation older than his hobbit companions. Maybe this is just important to me as self-description...but then maybe it was important to Tolkien too. Adventures do not happen only to the young.

In any case, this was probably an inevitable casualty of a moviemaker's responsibility to sell tickets, but it changes the story just a little. To Jackson's and Wood's credit, a bit of the steel (or mithril) in Frodo's character begins to assert itself at the very end of the movie...but it is a bigger part of the book from the beginning. I trust it will be an important part of the other two films.

But that's a quibble. One other quibble is that the mallorn woods of Lorien were too dark. But overall I thought the special effects in the movie showed true vision and excellent craftsmanship. All the details of plot that really matter are presented in a logical and manageable, if rapid scale. The characterizations have been well written. I didn't really notice the score or shots much, but I tend to catch those things on second viewings with any movie.

I thought the back-story synopsis at the beginning was genius, a far better way to exploit the medium than having Gandalf and Frodo talking it all over in front of the fire. It throws us right into Middle Earth, a place where history is never far below the soil.

Mr. Jackson et al.: thanks for showing the entire birthday party, right down to the Proudfeet. Thanks for containing both Aragorn and Strider in one man, and hats off to Viggo Mortenson for surpassing my expectations. Thanks for allowing a 3,000-year-old elf to look ageless, even at the risk of confusing the non-reader audience. Thanks for those waterfalls in Rivendell, and for bringing Orthanc and Moria to life. Thanks for distinguishing the Uruk-Hai (in fact, I think the movie does this better than the book...making me look forward to The Two Towers a lot). Thanks for Gwaihir's flight. Thanks for using so much of New Zealand, already familiar to me as the planet's most beautiful place.

I have a long list of other things I'm grateful for...but I'm going to be too busy heading out for a second viewing!

title: On Arwen and Aragorn
review:
Many people seem to criticized the relationship between Arwen and Aragorn in the film, The Lord of the Rings. Although it is correct that Arwen did not save Frodo after he had been stabbed by the Lord of The Nazgul, the King of Angmar, the love story is indeed part of Tolkien's book. It is discussed in brief in Appendix A p1032 and completes a symmetry in the tales of middle earth.

There were three marriages between elf and man. Beren and Luthien, Idril and Tuor and finally Aragorn and Arwen. Idril and Tuor gave rise to the line that includes Elrond but also his brother Elros who chose to live as man unlike Elrond although part human chose to live his life as an elf. Elros gave rise to the Kings of the Edain and Aragorn is descended directly from Elros. As such Aragorn is in fact related to Arwen although many generations of men and women lie between them. The marriage thus re-unites the blood of human and elven kind, restoring the Kings of Men.

Love stories form an important part of the Silmarillion, a book written by J.R.R Tolkien but published after his death by his son Christopher, perhaps the most important being that of Beren and Luthien. As such it seems to me that the inclusion of the love story is in keeping with Tolkien's image of middle earth. Jackson has intelligently not copied the book but instead (and with great success) has projected Tolkien's tale recast in cinematographic form.

In including the love story (left mainly to the appendix in the book) and promoting her role Jackson has perhaps told a tale better set in the history of middle earth, ironically, than the book.

title: Great, but not as great as the book
review: I liked the film a lot, almost as much as I did like the book. I could hardly wait for it to be shown. Although I do have some second thoughts about it: The set is wonderful and very worth showing, but I still think there is just a bit too much of those air shots, which steal a bit of time for showing the characters. If the camera stayed a bit longer with them we could learn more about some of them like Sam, Gimli or Legolas (remember that almost 30% of the story was originally told from Sam's point of view). Still, I think it's a wonderful movie and can't wait for the next two. I guess we will get to know the characters well enough when we see tho whole story.

title: The Best Series!
review: I have to say without doubt that this is the best visual and audio treat I've encountered.  The size, scope and content of the movie make it a classic, instantaneously.  From the first moment in the film to the end credits, the entire audience is riveted.  I've not seen a movie that was able to do that with such conviction!  The audience breathed together, felt together, and watched in utter, blissful harmony.  I especially liked the scenery, and I am comforted by the fact that all three movies will be of the same quality as the first.  I eagerly await the release of the next two movies!

title: Exactly...
review: how it should have been made. You couldn´t hope for more! Unfortunately it´s a while between the movies are showing, but that was the way the books worked as well (for those a bit older than me)... Enjoy this movie, but make sure to read the books first! /Stefan

title: How could anyone score this a '1' ? - but over 1800 have...
review:
It's a long time since I saw 'The Godfather'. A better movie than LotR(Part1)? Probably, but there again I would pump for Shawshank as being No1 myself.... Godfather had tremendous style - Shawshank ...well had everything in my book. But what does LotR(Part1) have that puts it in the same bracket as these illustrious companions for so many people?

It's extremely beautiful to look at. It's well acted. It is based on a great story. It's got action, comedy, romance, violence etc....the works(...plenty of people of covered this already...). Personally, I felt the inter cutting with the Gandalf/Saruman story worked very well - I didnt have a problem with the Glorfindel sex change. The council of ELrond I think was a failure, but twas only a moment in the context of the whole. The three hours flashed by - and Ill have to go and see it for a second time - not something Ive ever wanted to do before. It makes a real impact - visually, and soundwise, and it is obvious why so many rate this one right up there.

But (yup - there is a but coming), I was left with some feelings of disappointment come the end. I had a feeling I was going to be after reading all the reviews on IMdb before going. Nothing could live up to that kind of hype. Most of my issues with LOTR(Part1) were that it was just that - a (part 1.). You couldnt judge the book just reading the first book - nor can you do the same with the film. The architecture of the story AS A WHOLE has breathtaking scope. But taken in isolation the architecture of the first book just doesn't support the screen play for a film that well. There's no 'arch' shape - a going , a coming home. Its more of a washing line - a series of events that occur on a journey. Scary, beathtaking, beautiful to look at, and exciting events to be sure, but there would have to be more to warrant the top film award for me.

At first - I was sad at this. I really wanted this to be the Holy Grail of movies. But then I thought about the next two, and that the film to judge would have to be the composite of all three. I suspect that the next book the Two Towers has a better chance to stand on it's own feet as a movie, but the third will have the same problems as the Fellowship. We shall see.

It is an un imaginable prospect to sit down and see the three huge moveis back to back, but perhaps only then can we really see if the whole makes sense. The first part is a great start, and I can only look forward with anticipation to the completed work

title: This film is a classic
review: This movie just grows on you. Each viewing reveals more detail and a greater appreciation of what a classic movie this is. Have now seen the movie as often as I have read the book. Since we are all programmed to think in pictures must say I prefer the film to the book. There are parts of the book that I think should have been included in the movie but do not know how a 9 hour movie would go down with an R18 rating. I for one hope the DVD release includes obvious cuts that were filmed and we allowed to hit the pause butoon for breakfast and second breakfast. I for one think this is the movie of the decade so far. I am sure the second episode from my point of view will eclipse this first instalment-just hope treebeard and the ents live up to the expectations I now have. Peter Jackson has achieved with the FOTR more than I expected. I now expect TTT to eclipse the first instalment as this is merely a warm up to more magic.

title: Groundbreaking!
review: I'd like to say this is probably the most spectacular movie I've ever seen. Peter Jackson really demonstrates how to make a $100 million movie and not get 'Water World.' It's so visually pleasing, and never feels like it's being shoved in your face... as a fan of the books, I felt the adaptation was tremendous. The cast was wonderful, and I hope they get as much recognition come Oscar time as Peter Jackson will.

title: It was everything I imagined.
review: From the Shire to Rivendell, Galadriel to Gandalf, this movie truly nailed every image I had in my head while reading the book.  There is nothing I can say that is negative about this movie.  In terms of a book to movie adaptation, this is the closest to perfection there ever has been.  I just don't have the words to describe the effect this had on me.  Truly amazing. The casting was perfect, as if these people were born to play the characters.  I am in awe, and will count the days until I can go see this again, as well as when I can go see The Two Towers.

title: Beyond my expectation! A great movie!
review:
I have read "The Lord of the Rings" twice. I have always loved the rich imaginative detail and adventure of the books. How can they make this into a live action movie? Too many particulars about characters sizes etc! Well, they did it! Moreover, they went beyond my imagination on some parts. Rivendell was actually realised on film. The council of Elrond was better than I imagined - great look and feel. And I really loved the portayal of Sauramon and the look of Isengard. Awesome! I am glad Jackson placed an importance on Isengard..because in the books you don't really know what is happening there until later.

My only fault with the movie deals with the whole Lorien/Galadriel scenes. Not enough Gimli/Galadriel/Legolas interactions. Plus, where was Samwise when Frodo looked into the Mirror? I realize time was a factor but it was really missed.

However, excellent job. Entertaining! Great acting! Great special effects. And the whole Moria scenes from start to finish were class A!

title: Forget the Golden Globes, we know PJ is a genius!!!
review: I have not gone to the theater to see a movie repeatedly since Star Wars in 1977. Until now. I went last week for the third time to see a film that has captured my imagination and my heart. Is it a perfect film? No, of course not - nothing is, but Peter Jackson's labour of love has given birth to a movie that will set the standard of excellence for many years to come. For those who moan that it's a stupid, boring story with nothing but travel and fight, travel and fight, your ignorance is showing. Precisely how would you describe any great epic such as the Iliad other than a journey broken by bits of action. There are people whose brains appear to be lacking in sufficient imagination and/or curiosity to appreciate any sort of make-believe, whether it is Fantasy, Science Fiction, or Muppet movies. And quite frankly, those oh-so-serious people tend to be boring and pretentious and definitely NOT anyone I wish to spend time with. Yes the Godfather is a great piece of cinema, but it's not my favorite movie of all time. I'm not certain I could pick just one, but LOTR would be in the top group. This movie grabbed me and took me into a world that I had only imagined before, but it was a world I recognized immediately as Peter Jackson obviously loved the book as much as I did. There were relatively few actors in this film because Peter found the REAL Gandalf and Aragorn and Frodo and managed to convince them to help him make this film. I want to visit the Shire and live in a hobbit hole because they really exist - we know that now. I do doubt that the Academy Awards will honor Peter and company as they should be honored, but that is the way of the world. I do know that millions of people will find themselves transported by a brilliant work of filmmaking.

title: Brilliant film, two more viewings and I have a new personal record. It will happen!
review: I have seen this film seven times now, and I am sure I can see it seven more times. It is moving, violent, action-packed, scary, funny - everything a great movie should be. I highly recommend it to people who are fans of junk like The Phantom Menace.

title: Breathtaking
review:
It's amazing just how the film works so well bringing the book to life with minimal deviation from what was hardly written as a screenplay. The sweep, the verve of the thing had me gulping throughout three hours that whizzed by. Elijah Wood perfectly captures the 'haunted' quality that I always imagined Frodo had, and the other characters are just as impressive - I had my doubts before the film re: Viggo Mortensen, but they were allayed immediately. Can't see the point of 'beefing up' Arwen's role, given there's hardly any extra scenage for her bar replacing Glorfindel - maybe in Two Towers & Return of the King.

Have to mention the short cut to mushrooms and the trolls' glade... nice touches for Tolkien fans

Can't wait to see it again!

title: Great Portrayal
review:
After watching the films and not once feeling bored throughout the whole 3hours and 15 minutes. I thought that Lord of the the Rings: Fellowship of the ring was one of the best portrayals of such an influencial novel that has ever been created.

Throughout the film, the audience was shown unsurpassingly the emotions or each character and the superb scenery which again is unsurpassed by any film.

title: Godlike!!
review:
The movie of the century left me breathless.... I saw this movie in a 500 seat theater all sold out. In the beginning the crowd was loud and irritating but right after the first screen appeared everybody was quiet ;-)) You could hear a needle falling on the floor in matter of speech Even at the end of the movie people stayed in their seats.

My advice: go see this movie or you'll regret this for the rest of your life.

title: Pretty good.
review: First off I'd like to say I am NOT a diehard LOTR fan, or even a fantasy fan. I tried it, but never got into it. Anyway, "The Lord of The Rings" was an awesome movie. But there's a big difference between 'awesome' and 'great' I was truly shocked that this movie is .1 behind "The Godfather". To me, it seemed kind of like "Gladiator", with its violence. In fact, the what (in my very humble opinion) saved this movie was Jackson's great directing and changing of a (from what I've heard) entirely different world to make it simple enough for newbies while being enjoyable at the same time, and a great performance by Elijah Wood. But better than "The Godfather"? Give me a break. "The Godfather" not only gave brilliant performances, but also had a beautifully intricate plot. It's Coppola at his prime. To recap: "The Lord of The Rings: Best movie adaption of a book? No doubt. Best movie ever? In my Top Ten. But not the greatest.

title: I wish the film had been a bit longer
review:
As a person having read the books I wish the film had been a bit longer. Now on some spots the film moved too quickly from one scene to another. I couldn't help feeling the editor had been asked to make the film shorter and as a result some gluing shots were missing. Can't wait to see the director's cut on a DVD.

Anyway so good was the film I sat the first 120 to 140 minutes glued to my seat before my buttocks got so numb I noticed I have to change my position;-).

title: Special effects epic.
review: "Lord of the rings" was as good as has been said.  It is not a perfect movie though.  I found the effects to be very well done but somewhat distracting. There seems to be this way of having a camera sweep over the effect so you get an idea of the scene but never really focus or linger on any particular object.   I enjoyed the lingering shots inside of Bilbo's cottage and the effect of making Gandalf seem so much larger than the Hobbits around him. That was well done.  Ian Holm looked tiny compared to Gandalf.  The other monster type effects were too fleeting for me.  Quick cuts of moving figures looked just confusing for my slow eyes.  I enjoyed the shot of Arwen's horse galloping at full speed far more than dark, jumpy shots of Orcs, Goblins, and Uruks.  Nonetheless the movie was successful in portraying a believable, fictious world.  The crossing the bridge in the Mines of Moria was impressive also a lingered shot of Gollum was good. The movie is long, lots of fidgiting after 2 hours, and violent but not particularly gory.  I would recommend it.

title: Best they could have done
review:
A superb interpretation of an almost unfilmable book. Hats off to Peter Jackson for this movie. I enjoyed every moment, from the quiet beauty of the Shire to the majesty of Rivendell & the horrors of Moria.

The only niggles I have are that Gimli & Legolas appeared to be rather flat characters and you don't get any sense of the bond that grows between them (tradionally Dwarves & Elves do not get on) and Lothlorien seemed a little rushed. However the reworking of Arwen into the story worked wonderfully.

And Sean Bean as Boromir !!!!!! How to turn a fairly unsympathetic character in to a tragic hero !!!!

The film ended on the perfect note as well.

Must see it again soon.

title: The most amazing blockbuster in ages...
review:
The Lord Of The Rings has done much for New Zealand; it injected at least a hundred million dollars into Wellington alone last year (which is a lot of money here.) Anyway, it is rumored that you can play Six Degrees of Separation with connections to LOTR and it will always connect! Whether or not this shows how huge the film is, or how little our country is I don't know. But, for us all to see our country's and people's work up on the big screen early this morning thrilled me in a way I can not describe in words.

The film combines everything from the grandiose explosions of Pearl Harbor through to the shaky hand-held majic of Pi, in a way that makes sense and eases the viewer into the horrific back-story that must be delved into. After a rather placid first hour, the story begins to heat up horrifically with the entrance of the terrifying Black Riders. The sound of their screams, harls, and snarls is reminiscent of Jurrasic Park's T-Rex roars but with the harshest tone imaginable. To enjoy this film at it's best; go to the nearest cinema that enjoys the pleasures of the latest sound systems, as you will notice the difference when your seats start to shake with the Timpani crashes of Howard Shore's epic score.

The score is truly epic, and easily outweighs the lacklustre score of Harry Potter as does the special effects, the story, the acting, and the direction. So therefore if this is the second film you see this year, you'll be glad you saved the best until last.

The film should be admired on it's constantly building-up of flare and ambitiousness; it starts simply with a lot of romantic Close-Ups and lingering Lond Shots of the lush Shire, but by the two-and-a-half-hour mark, you've been treated to glorious slow-motion, rapid horse chases, and many a heroic face. The acting is wonderful when combined with everything that did make me gasp for breath, and the scene that stuck out in my mind was a part of the Bridge of Khazud-Dan (or something like that) that was absolutely heart-breaking (If you've read the books you'll know what I mean).

I should change that last passage though; (If you've now seen the books, you'll know what I mean) because this movie unlike Roger Ebert's obviously over-streched imagination, was exactly how I imagined it. Every detail that Tolkien ever described was there, leaving me with my last satisfied thought.

All in all, well done to everyone involved, and I hope everyone with access to a cinema gets to go see this near-perfect movie.

title: Jackson not Tolkein - This won't bring the fantasy experience to the masses.
review:
I had looked forward to this film for many months so I had high expectations going in. I had enjoyed the animated version in the past (sadly never finished by Ralph Bakshi though there are sequels available in the US) and felt confident that as with the animated film the basic story would be the same as the book but the look and acting would be improved to give a much clearer version of Tolkein's magnum opus.

Well the look of the film matched my expectations from the incredible opening battle to the lustrousness of the shire. The mine of Moria seemed oddly shaped for a mine however, but it did look spectacular all the same.

Unfortunately I feel Jackson attempted to stamp his own vision on the project. Obviously with an enormous book like LOTR then you have to chop a lot out, however this is let's remember the most popular book on the planet next to the Bible so I feel it's fair to say that Tolkein has written a pretty ng good yarn that doesn't require to be jazzed up.

The dialogue should have remained the same but reduced, instead it was changed and changed unnecessarily also the film had too many unnecessary action scenes and computer generated monsters. The characters of Frodo's two cousins changed from stalwart friends to amiable but stupid buffoons (one with an out of place Scottish accent).

Strider/Aragorn was changed from a tough and brooding haunted figure to an action hero. Who would be scared of the Ring Wraiths when Aragorn can easily kick the crap out of a bunch of them?

LOTR was about subtlety on every level. A deep and very long book which had a lustrous rich history. The first part of the book can be cut into it's basic plot (it was done before by Bakshi) but when it is changed for change's sake then it is reduced to yet another screenplay and ultimately The Fellowship of The Ring is yet another action movie.

This should have been the film that put fantasy on the map but instead I am sure many people must be wondering what all the fuss is about. The great thing about fantasy is the ability to lose yourself in another world, a realistic world in some ways but a different one from ours. This never happened in the film therefore it was a disappointment. Enjoyable enough on a certain level (but then again so was 'The Mummy') and yes it did look lovely but ultimately this just wasn't Tolkein.

PS: For a true fantasy film look at John Boorman's Excalibur which tells an often repeated tale in a beautiful manner but with proper respect for the source material.

joe-middleton.

title: Lord of the Rings, the Second Best Movie of all time Um. No.
review:
I have heard so many things about this movie it is unbelievable. I have seen this movie twice, read the books, and I can say for sure that it is not the 2nd best movie of all time. It is also ridiculous that this movie won the AFI best picture of the year against ten other briliant spectacular movies.

The first time I saw the movie everyone in my group was half and half on the opinion of weather they liked the movie. Some people thought it was dreadfull and were upset with me for making them see a 3 hour movie that they thought was "stupid." Others thought the movie was wonderfull but no one thought it was the best movie of the year. I thought the movie was average but when other people wanted to see it I thought I would give it a second chance.

The second time I saw it was a different experience. I liked the first half of the movie better but I thought the battle scenes towards the end were ridiculous. The acting was average but some of those "1-liners" were stabbing me in the heart. For instance, "Let's hunt some Ork" was my vote for the most ridiculous line in the movie.

I thought the special effects in the movie were amazing but the music and the acting were average. My favorite character was probably Frodo Bagins or Gandalf. I thought the movie relied on too much action which the book did not. Some people I heard said they were bored by the dialogue. That was my favorite part (besides the ring wraiths) in the whole film.

In short I do suggest you see this movie. Some of you will probably hate it, and some of you will probably like it, but none of you I doubt will worship this movie...even if you've read the books.

title: A faithful translation of the book but futile for adepts
review: I've read the book 5 times, so going to the film was a serious risk.  It's a real tribute to Peter Jackson that I didn't feel I should not be watching this.  He followed the book faithfully (leaving out numerous side plots, songs, poetry and secondary characters, but that was inevitable).  His imagery concerning the landscapes was extremely faithful to Tolkien. Especially Rivendel and Moria were excellently visualised.  Most of the characters also corresponded to what you would expect after reading the book.  But then the question arises:  Why make a film at all, if all it does is slavishly illustrating the written word?  I would expect a film to add an extra dimension.  Of course, Jackson would have been crucified if he had dared to impose a personal view on the story.  Thus, maybe it was not necessary to make this film.  I don't feel I would have missed anything if I hadn't seen the film.  But if as a result of seeing the film people will be stimulated to read the book this would surely justify the film. I also have a few comments.  I don't want to start nitpicking about what has been kept and what has been left out, but I wonder if Gimli will be given more depth in the sequels.  He was supposed to be overwhelmed by Galadriel and to develop a strange complicity with Legolas.  But in Lothlorien Gimli was hardly given any attention. Most characters were well cast.  Especially Saruman, Gandalf (I had imagined Sean Connery in that role but Ian McKellen does a great job) and Frodo. In my imagination, Boromir looked like Steve Reeves with long blond hair and Elrond like Paul Newman in the 1960's and Galadriel was more ethereally beautiful (Kate Blanchett is certainly pretty but not heavenly so).  Well, that's everybody's private preference.  But it was a pity that Sam, Merry and Pippin were not given any more pronounced personalities. Two things I did not like.  One was the casting of Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn.  I know many critics gave him very good marks, but to me he doesn't look the part.  He's not tall enough and he doesn't express the depth and the suffering that goes with the character.  His face is almost empty, he's just going through the motions.  Liam Neeson in The Phantom Menace came much closer to the essence of Aragorn, and of course Max Von Sydow in The Seventh Seal: he would have been the ideal Strider.  The second is the music.  Too recognisable bur especially: too much like church music.  Many times it terribly distracted me from the film: I had the impression to be at Communion or something.

title: Justice to Tolkien's imagination
review:
When I went to see the Lord of the Rings , I was in no doubt that I would be disappointed. The book definitely had to be better than the movie , however well made the movie is . 3 times after seeing the movie in the theater I stand corrected.

The movie is an excellent adaptation of the book. It remains very faithful to the book. However there are small changes which I feel are necessary for a taut screenplay.The character of Tom Bombadillo has been avoided and some of the slower parts of the book have been made more exciting , the Nazgul pursue the hobbits more closely , Arwen heads the flight to the ford , the romance between Aragorn and Arwen doesnt blossom so early in the book . Other than these small changes , an amazing adaptation of the book.

Firstly the visuals are breathtaking. The Shire , the mines of Moria , Rivendell and Lothlorien ..brilliantly executed. My favorite is the mines of Moria . The transformation of Isengard from a green meadow to the dark work shops of Saruman is amazing. The cast is competent and everybody lives their roles . Frodo and Gandalf are really good. The make up for the elves is really cool too . Watch out for Legolas with the bow in the last fight.The narration is rivetting and keeps you engrossed.The little bit of history up front, about the 1st war and how Sauron loses his ring is apt and will help people who haven't read the book follow the movie better. Kudos to Peter Jackson and the entire crew. This movie will be "How to write an adapted Screenplay 101 " .

I hope this movie takes it's fair share of Oscars .. Definitely the best trilogy( if the other 2 are as good ) to hit the screens since Star Wars.... I just can't wait for the other two parts... Go ahead see the movie at least a couple of times on the big screen ...

title: The definition of epic
review:
Well, I went to the late show of this film expecting Star Wars, and I have to say it ALMOST fit the bill. I think my main problem was that I knew the hero's objective (throwing the rings into the fire) wouldn't be reached by the end. I knew they'd have to cut off at some other prominent seeming point, and so, several times, I was wondering is THIS where they'll end it? (I've never read the books, besides The Hobbit.) So my several near-ends: 1.The Fellowship is actually formed and forged in Rivendell. (By the way, as Hugo Weaving said, "The ring must be destroyed," I distinctly heard the guy to my right add, "Mr. ANDerson.") 2.When Gandalf dies in the mines and they emerge on the other side. After all, another great sweeping vista and a sense of completion/loss. 3.When they leave the elf-witch's kingdom on the boat with the army on the rise. (I REALLY thought it was ending here.) So, by the time the film had actually ended, it felt kind of anticlimactic to just have Sam and Frodo embrace on the mountaintop.

This is really a film about worlds and monsters, and there's probably something missing since instead of our imagination creating these things out of Tolkien's words, we experience them instantaneously, though miraculously, on the screen. The Shadow Demon, the giant orc beast in the mines, Sauron, the tentacled monster of the swamp, the Ring Wraiths (my god, what intensity!), the Golem, the Orcs, and Saruman's day army were all incredible creations, as powerful as the details put into the worlds these travelers went through. Personally, I thought the acting fine, especially by Mortensen (reminding me of a Han Solo type for some reason), Sean Bean, Ian Holm, and Ian McKellen ("YOU SHALL NOT PASS!!".) I didn't quite find myself engrossed in Frodo's character: he has far yet to come, and he needs to get a little ANGRY. Even Liv Tyler did a great job, and the Elvish language is gorgeous. The best thing I can say about this movie is that it's good enough to make me go out and find a copy of the Two Towers to read over the holiday. Make the best out of the times we find ourselves in.

title: An overall, nicely done film.
review: I have read all 6 books of "The Lord of the Rings" (except the 7th book which is the appendices) and all I can say is they are GREAT and the best books I have ever read!!!!!!! I actually should say BOOK because in its entirety this truly is just ONE story and let me remind you people it is NOT a trilogy!!!!!!! Those who have read the books will understand and realise that! Even Tolkien himself said how he was annoyed at how people began to call it a trilogy. Of course the movies make it look-out to be like one but it isn't. I plan on reading "The Hobbit" after (yeah I know its suppose to take place before and one should read it first) and think it might be very interesting. What I liked about Tolkiens work was how you do not have to read "The Hobbit" to understand what's going on in "The Lord of the Rings". They pretty much are two very different stories and what one has to remember is "The Hobbit" is a PRELUDE and NOT a PREQUEL for "The Lord of the Rings" that we must understand. Well Peter Jackson's movie was very well done and most of the actors were more than perfect for the parts. I personally enjoy how i pictured the characters and the realm of Middle-Earth much better than the movie but I think that's how it has always been. This movie did lack some character development: Merry and Pippin did not seem to have much film time. That bothered me cause if you have read the books you should know that these two become very important characters! But we will have to wait and see with that one. This next one bothered me the MOST and many other Tolkien fans who have READ the book. Why did they leave out the great Tom Bombadil, AGAIN!!!???? One would of thought they would of learned the big mistake Ralph Bashki's 1978 version of the story made!!!! I know some people do not see him necessary to the story but I certainly do. Even though he was not in the book long or was a major character, in my opinion if it wasn't for him the hobbits would of never made it out of the "Old Forest", never got the courage or spirits needed to complete the quest, and never gotten the swords they posessed! But whatever at least the "cave trolls" weren't left out. Another thing that really bothered me was when Frodo get's stabbed by the Ringwraiths, it is GLORFINDEL who rescues them!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! It is NOT Legolas (1978 version) and it is NOT ARWEN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Why can't you people get that straight!!!!??????? And why didn't Frodo get to do his famous song at "The Prancing Pony"!!!????? That was one of my favourite parts on the '78 film and they left it out, and Butterbur's character was reduced enormously of course. Why did they leave out some of the best characters??
