title: Great, but if anything, TOO faithful
review:
Disregard the squealing of rabid Tolkien zealots moaning about the lack of Tom Bombadil(!), hobbit sing songs(double !!) and very minor story tweaks, just sit back and soak it all up. Peter Jackson has done an amazing job shoehorning JRR's quaint, old-fogeyish medieval soap opera into an exciting and impressive epic that flies by and left this cynic aching for more.

I read LOTR as a young pup, and am genuinely curious as to how Jackson is going to handle the next two parts. The Two Towers...how are the Ents(intelligent trees, no less) going to be handled? Are they really necessary? There is something a bit neverending story about trees running around the place and this could be a bridge too far for all but the most receptive cinemagoers. The big Siege could be special though...especially as i read somewhere that the orcs could be packing gunpowder and flamethrowers devised by Saruman.

Return of the King...JRR totally lost it here, reams of densely packed psuedo-beowulf gibberish that wrap thing up in a totally dissatisfying manner. I hope Peter Jackson had the courage of his convictions and made the many changes that I think are necessary, as even the most staunch of Tolkiens fans must realise, no matter what happens, the books are still there.

Anyway, Ive seen FOTR twice and loved it. If i was to be picky(and i understand applying logic or reasoning to probably the definitive Fantasy story is an effort in futility), I would say that although there is a feeling of dread and uncertainty I dont recall in the books, I still feel the main characters are just too invulnerable. Strider for example...takes on 5-6 ringwraiths casually, god knows how many orcs, an entire legion of Uruk Hai...the fight scenes quicky become dull when we realise the uruks or whatever might have huge superiority of numbers but nevertheless shuffle clumsily in single file toward our heroes (including an effeminate hairdresser type and a small, stumpy old man with an axe)and are summarily dispatched with minimal effort. The Uruk-Hai in particular...Jackson spent a while building these bad boys up (and they do look particularly fearsome) but apart from their hardcore leader, seem to post almost no threat whatsoever to the fellowship. Did I see hobbits killing Uruk-hai? Saruman...back to the drawing board mate.

Last Criticism...I thought the score was pretty forgettable. I loved Leonard Rosenman's discordant, clashing music for Ralph Bakshi's animated LOTR and thought the lack of a "money" theme might (very mildly) affect this film's long term classic status. Anyways...Great acting, great fx, good story...give Peter Jackson more money and a copy of David Gemmell's "King Beyond the Gate".

title: A little sceptic
review:
Well, what can I say? I was disappointed, there's no doubt about that. A lot of details throughout the film made me question the motive of making it; was it an attempt to make LoTR immortal, or was it just a way to make a huge profit?

If thought of as just a film among others, I have to say that I was impressed and thankful of a GREAT fantasy movie. The genre sure doesn't include many...

If viewed in the light of it being a screen version of one of the greatest book in the history, I - as I said - was very disappointed. I can understand the need of shortening down the action in one way or another, but in some cases I felt as if the writer/director had totally changed the spirit of the book. That is, from MY point of view...

Loved the characters, the scenery and the choreography; not so very impressed by all the shortcomings. A great film, but not THE greatest. :)

title: No milestone of filmhistory!
review:
This movie is getting too much hype. The special effects may be awesome but that's about it. The story develops too slowly. I already felt uncomfortable after the first ten minutes as Frodo and Gandalf blathered about the good ol' times. The script is poor, the dialogues are even poorer, the movie doesn't create an eerie atmosphere, the movie lacks suspense, the humor is average, the end is appaling etc.

You have to wait more than an hour to see a great battle including the showdown with this big Goblin or whatever it was. Unfortunately, the movie can't keep its pace afterwards. This was the single highlight!

Don't listen to people who try to convince you that LOTR is a fantastic movie. It's a simple mainstream movie and nothing more...

title: Just a Complete Movie - From 1st Scene to The Last
review:
Although the readers of Middle Earth may not agree with me, I think this is the most complete movie ever made. Its good at the start, and when the ball really starts rolling (you'll know this part when you see it), it becomes a masterpiece.

The special effects of this movie must have set a new industry standard. The Phantom Menace's special effects are child's play in comparison to what is seen in Lord of the Rings.

Lord of the Rings captivates the audience like no recent movie. The casting was superb, and the soundtrack matched the movie scene for scene. The movie will leave you begging for more ... definitely one to watch over and over again.

title: The movie is better than all the trailers and commercials
review: When I first saw the advertisements for the movie, I wasn't excited about it at all, to be honest. After all, with Harry Potter smothering the theaters these days, who would want to see another fantasy movie? Besides, I have never read the trilogy (I have always thought it was too dark and serious). But on january 1, my wife suggested we see the movie. She didn't take much to convince me because I was sort of into watching a mindless action movie whereas I didn't have to think so hard. All my doubts about this movie would soon disappear like ash In the first half hour of the movie, I was transfixed, completely captivated by the excitement of moviemaking and storytelling. Before I knew it, it was over, with a cliffhanger ending that had my wife and I in a fit of anger (but happy that it was so good). Yes, it was tremendously enjoyable. I left the theater without that feeling of seeing a megabuck, all action, all special effects, and a no-brainer of a movie. Instead, I left feeling awarded with a great literary feast for the eyes and mind.

title: FANTASTIC
review:
I've seen LOTR twice and I have to say that this is one film that was worth the wait(Unlike as many have already said Phantom Menace). I have read the Book 3 times and thought that Peter Jackson and team did a NEARLY perfect job.

**SPOILERS**

There are a couple of things I would have changed about the film. The main one being the ending were Aragon has a discussion with Frodo and is tempted by the ring. This isn't in the book and doesn't make much sense in the film. Why would Aragon willingly let Frodo go off on his own when it seems certain that Frodo needs Aragon to protect with all thats going on. It was a bad change. Didn't mind Tom Bombadil, Arwen changes. Gandalf hanging on and nobody running to his aid didn't happen in the book either and bothered me.

**END OF SPOILERS**

Overall a marvelous film. Just go and see for yourself if you haven't already done so. Aragon, Frodo, Gandalf, Boromir and Legolas were all brilliantly portrayed. Anyway go see it!

10

title: Wonderful Movie
review: After reading several bad comments, I guess the only thing that makes sense to complain about is the length. If you're an impatient person, three hours can seem very long. But if you appreciate the beauty and majesty of a movie like The Lord of the Rings then you will love it. Each part of the movie had me hooked, with my eyes glued to the screen. I loved Frodo's meek courage and Sam and the other hobbit's good-natured attitude. Striders guidance and protection over Frodo was great. So if you have the patients and appreciate fine literature and great works of art come and see The Lord of the Rings.

title: It's not the same feeling
review:
For more than a year I had expected the movie, and when it started I heard my heart jumping in expectation of what was coming. I saw a beautiful depicted Shire , or "Contea" as I first read the book in Italian. But slowly the magic became to fall as the story turned away from the original plot. I understand that is not the same public, and that some changes had to be made in order to put such a huge art work in the big screen, but I can't forgive that the lives of the characters, that give the book the greatness that it has, where just sketched in the movie.

Reading the book is like joining the fellowship, getting to know the other members, their history, their talents and flaws, and the motives behind all their action. In the movie, you just know their names and where are they from. About Gimli you just get that is a dwarf, because he screams it always that he can, but you never get to feel like a mate in your own company, like the "big", brave guy, ready to give his blood to defend his company.... and that's just an example. The cast was great: looking at them you really get who they are. I specially liked Gandalf, looks very very wise and brave, and specially liked Araghorn, my favorite character in the whole book. This actor looks just like it has, rude but sensitive, with the charge in his back of having to lead his people to the victory but with a terrible family curse. Another one i liked was Elrond, that looks like he's got, and ancient warrior, wise enough to choose between immortal and mortal live, and wise in all his choices.

Looking from another point, the world of the movie is great and the combination between real landscapes and SGI gives you the best view of this incredible world. The armies, UAO!, the encounter between mordor army and Gilgalad's and Elendil's armies is just epic!

So, I got one of the two things I wanted from the movie: I got the world drawn in a brilliant way, inhabited by dumb people that lives only for this chapter of their lives.... could be worse.

title: Fantastic Film
review: Simply put, the most facinating, well made film I've ever seen.  Follows the book almost exactly.  Effects are well done and the movie moves along without any dull moments.  After 3 hours of watching it I wanted more. The first movie since The Matrix that made me want to go back and see it multiple times.  Can't wait for the sequels.

title: Middle Earth and its characters come to life!
review:
I came away from "The Fellowship of the Ring" feeling that I had finally gotten a chance to actually see the world and characters of Tolkein's classic. Middle Earth is beautifully recreated, and the characters are true to life.

I suspect that viewers who haven't read Tolkein's books will have a little trouble at first figuring out what is going on. I would suggest, if at all possible, that they read the prequel to "Lord of the Rings" - "The Hobbit" - before going to see "The Fellowship of the Ring". They should also be prepared for the fact that "Lord of the Rings" is really a single story that spans 3 books (and now 3 movies). Consequently, the end of "The Fellowship of the Ring" is like the end of a chapter rather than the end of a story.

Fans of the books will notice that some material has necessarily been cut to keep the movie from lasting 6 hours (instead of 3). And, while the basic plot line of the story has been preserved, those who are familiar with the books may be irritated at times by minor but needless inaccuracies in the movie, and by the lack of an accurate sense of the amount of time that is passing at certain points in the story.

But, all in all, I suspect that fans of the books will be glad they went to see the movie, and that those viewers who haven't read the books may be inspired to do so once they see the movie.

title: A great movie....
review:
Peter Jackson has done a fabulous job of transforming one of the most read and loved books of all time into a wonderfully enjoyable movie. His directing and casting is fabulous and transfers all the qualities of Middle Earth from page to screen.

Of the casting, i think that without a doubt Sir Ian McKellen will forever be Gandalf. His presence and poise, elocution and execution of the role is almost beyond belief! Viggo Mortensen as the rugged Strider/Aragorn is another stroke of genius. Very un-pretentious but quietly regal. And as for Elijah Wood as Frodo, amazing. But for me the star is Sean Astin as Sam. I was a little apprehensive how Hollywood would treat Tolkien's depiction of a servant in Sam, but the brotherhood that obviously exists between Sam and Frodo is pure and strong!

Certainly the cinematographer will receive and oscar for this epic!

As for those who were disappointed with the film, perhaps your expectations were too high? As a representation of Tolkien's classic it is a fantastic movie, but as a generally appealing movie? I think it still suffers from the marginalisation that goes along with being in the fantasy genre.

Nevertheless, a wonderful adventure! Roll on Dec 2002!

title: People are Generally Dumb.
review:
I saw The Fellowship of the Ring without reading the book beforehand, and with only a vague recollection of the 1970's animated version of The Hobbit (horrible!). I knew the basic gist of things, ie. The ring was bad, the ring had to be destroyed, the ring made you invisible. I also knew a little bit about the hobbits just from word of mouth. I was expecting to be entirely clueless through tLotR, as I had no knowledge of the book.

I was completely blown away, however, that the entire movie actually made *sense* to me. Sure, I didn't know much of the history of Gloin and Gimli, or Moria, or who the heck Dain was, but those were all fairly trivial things to the overall plot of the movie. They obviously did a great job in making it understandable, the only improvement I ask is that they let you learn people's names. I couldn't even remember who Gimli and Legolas were, and confused Boromir with Pippin when talking about it afterwards, because they hardly ever used names in the movie.

The next day I went out and bought the entire LotR 'trilogy', plus The Hobbit, and went home to read. I finished both The Hobbit and The Fellowship in less than a week, and was rather pleased with both of them. The Hobbit answered my questions about the dwarves and Moria, and the Fellowship gave me the names. Sure, the movie cut quite a few of the fun parts from the book, but people need to stop being dumb and realize that the movie was already 3 hours long, and much of the stuff in the book that was cut wasn't all *that* important. Also, Arwen Undomiel/Evenstar was given a more.. influental role because it help make the movie appeal to more people, and it's much less boring than Frodo riding alone.

Overall, while I hold the book at a higher level than the movie, I have to say that the movie was about as close as possible, and that no one on Earth could have made it better. It's not my favorite movie, but it makes my top ten list at about 4 or 5.

On another note, I hold nothing against people who didn't enjoy the movie, that's their opinion, but as for those who complain about the ending, I think you're all ignorant fools. It's not a single movie! It's a zarkin' trilogy! The movie was 2 1/2 hours long, and they *have* to leave you wanting something, or you won't come back next time! Get a life, please.

title: It could have been SO bad, and it was SO good.
review: I guess I have to begin by saying that I have read the books, (I've lost count of the times), and I was (am) a real Tolkien geek, particularly in my teens, some years ago now. In the 70s I was favorably impressed with Bakshi's attempt (I know, I know, I'm sorry) but I think some parts were well done, for the money they had available, and I think Bakshi's heart was in the right place. The cutesy versions of The Hobbit and Return of the King were terrible. When I heard of the attempt to be made by Mr. Jackson (who?) to do a live action version I was, to put it mildly, not looking forward to it, although I knew I would feel obligated to go, and be tortured. Well, the first film is here, I went, and I loved it. I knew some parts would have to be modified, but the job they did was a miracle. It's not perfect, like the books <g>, but Mr. Jackson satisfied this Tolkien fan. To nitpick, I thought that the scenes in Farmer Maggot's field and Bree were not led up to or explained well, the Black Riders might have been explained better, and the stay in Lorien seemed to me a little too new-agey for me. Could I have explained it better? No way, at least not without adding a couple of hours, and most people seem to understand just fine. To those who haven't read the books, I think they make the movie better, whether you liked it or not. I wonder what it would be like to read the books for the first time after seeing the movie(s). This is probably not the best film of all time, it will doubtless come down a few places after the novelty has worn off, but I give it a solid 9.

title: Nothing but praise
review: Loved the movie.  Want to see it at the theatre again and again, until the DVD comes out and I can watch it at home.  Everything about it was just so magnificent, the details, the character development, the surroundings. The Elfin kingdom was so beautiful, the Hobbit village was adorable, Gandalf was amazing, just like all the characters.  Cannot WAIT until the second one comes out!

title: masterpiece of cinematic wizardry
review: seemless camera tricks, okay computer graphics, beautiful sweeping shots, exceptional timing of reactions, subtle sound effects underly the obvious ones, brilliant acting (esp. gandalf). in regard to the books: a few characters missing, time frames a bit jumbled. I was on the edge of my seat most of the way through. by the time the credits started to roll, i found my eyebrows stuck on "high".

title: Completely and utterly blown away!!!
review:
This film is without a doubt THE best film ever made!! Star wars?! what a rip off! You can see where Lucas obtained his 'vision' for his saga! Obi Wan - Gandalf. Luke - Frodo. Han Solo - Aragorn. Leia - Arwen. Comparisons will inevitably be drawn.

I went into this film completely cold. Hadn't read the book. Hadn't even been on the hype wagon until a few months before it's release and I must say, I was blown away. Unfortunately, on my first viewing, there were some rather rude children, and adults talking and laughing throughout, and this distracted me from the film. I have since seen this film 3 times, and it just gets better!

Ian McKellen should get an Oscar for his portrayal of Gandalf the Grey, some actors are born to play some roles, and with McKellen, you looked at him and though that he WAS Gandalf. The same goes for Viggo Mortensen. He played, well he didn't even play Aragorn, again he WAS the character.

FEW PLOT SPOILERS AROUND!

When I first went to see this film, I thought that the whole film would be about the fellowship going to FIND the ring, I had no idea that they HAD the ring and were safeguarding it for it's destruction. So this was a surprise to me.

Peter Jackson!!! What a job! he's only made 5 films and he can create something as beautiful as this! The SFX are fantastic, bordering on flawless. (and I hate these SAD people who actually watch the film and pick out the mistakes, that really BUGS me. Get a life you people!!!) Where was I...? Oh yes, Jackson. If he doesn't win Best Director, then something's wrong. I know it's an event film, but what was Gladiator? And I love that too!

The costume department, and make up effects guys should get nods for their outstanding accomplishment on this film.

The orcs, goblins, troll's etc were very scary especially the leader of the Urac Hai, he scared me witless, and the scene between him and Sean Bean and Viggo was filled with intensity!

The comic potential was used well too. Much needed in a film that is this dark. I think Legolas was a great character and I enjoyed the initial hatred between him and Gimli, towards the end the relationship became somewhat mutual. This film has opened during a time when the forces of good and evil ARE fighting. It's a strong reminder that everyone, regardless of their race or religion should unite to overcome such forces. It's the triumph of the 'little people' over the overwhelming evil. Good timing, even though it's coincidental. We all need escapism at the moment, and what better place to go than the world that Tolkien?Peter Jackson have created for us!!!

The film did drag when we were introduced to Galadriel. Blanchett, who I admire as an actress seemed a little too laid back and monotonous for my liking. Mind you , I havn't read the books, so who am I to judge, but as a film, she didn't hit the right chord with me.

Above all, this is a male film, and I felt that the love story didn't damage that feel, some friends have complained that Arwen doesn't even appear that long in the book, so why boost her character? I felt it worked.

There is so much to say about this film.

Elijah Wood? didn't go overboard on him, but he was strong, and I believe he is developed further - as will all characters! - in the Two Towers.

HUGE PLOT SPOILER HERE!!!! What happened to Gandalf, It took 5 mins for it to sink in! how could that happen? it was the biggest surprise shock I have witnessed since the killing off of Marion Crane in Hitchcock's Psycho!! Good thing that I didn't read the book!

Can we all wait another year for this epic story to conclude? no way!!! I'm going to read the book all in one go - I'll give myself a few weeks, locked away with a bottle of Jack Daniel's and some biscuits and enjoy!!!

All in all, this is a beautifully realised and splendidly shot film. I'm going to watch it for the fourth time in a week.

Go and believe the hype!! If you ARE disappointed, check yourself into the nearest loony bin!!!

13/10. what more can you say.

title: Brave New World
review: The film has begun and ended a chapter of fantasy films. Until the LOTR trilogy is complete, it has set the standards of fantasy on a epic scale that no other film could even begin to reach. The richness of detail is just screaming to be uncovered, and to live in Middle Earth would be heaven, or just catch a plane to New Zealand, either will do. The Lord of the Rings could be compared to another film I know (some may know what I am talking about) but I would rather not. It is like comparing diamonds with glass. And that is why it is pure genius. Peter Jackson, I salute you.

title: Good Begining Fast with some exceptions B+ A- Rating
review:
(WARNING: THERE IS A TINY SPOILER IN THE REVIEW... VERY SMALL BUT NECESSARY)

Review of The Fellowship of the Ring -DarkCloud

The movie began better than I had expected. Since I read the book, I knew the prestory, but one of the people I went with did not... Thus, while I found the introduction easy to understand, my friend needed some explination about the names and the relationship between characters. The beginning was well-filled with action, and when Gandalf came to Hobbiton, it went fairly well... However, Bilbo Baggins, although acting well when he first met Gandalf, sort of fell flat as the movie went on. They did a good job of making hobbits seem smaller than the humans by casting tall humans, but the hobbits did not really look like "hobbits", however the Dwarves looked well... The Goblins and Orcs looked Reasonable, but the Balrog looked too much like a reject Magog from the Heroes of Might and Magic computer game. The elves did not look sufficiently different from humans, or from each other. Arwen looked much like Galadriel and each of their names were only mentioned once, thus it was hard to tell whether Galadriel was Arwen at one time... *.* The only main thing they cut out was Tom Bombadil. And the only minor thing they cut out that was not a major "change" was that Gandalf did not battle at Candlekeep. However their little "addition" and "change" with Arwen, truly made the movie fairly annoying. Instead of Gandalf saving Frodo from the Nazgul, Arwen appears, with little or no explanation. She then saves Frodo by crossing the river and sends the river down on the Nazgul... Then Gandalf appears and Arwen disappears after talking to Aragorn (Strider)? I understand the need for "romance", but please, don't mess with Tolkien.

Other than that, the only other confusing parts of the movie was when the Party reached Lothorioen and met Galadriel and her husband. The trouble here was Galadriel looked much like Arwen and her husband looked MUCH like Elrond... Thus, the idea was given that Elrond and Arwen rode ahead of the party somehow???? It made no sense- eventually I figured out it was not Arwen, but Galadriel and thus Elrond couln't have come...

However, Galadriel only mentions her name once!

The other problem with Galadriel was her temptation by the ring which was confusing, unnecessary and unexplained. It could have been cut.

And, one annoying detail was the misty "ring" sequences when Frodo puts on the ring and is transported into the mist. Those sequences were merely annoying.

Overall the story was quick, execept for a few 'dramatic' moments such as the drawing out of Boromir's death and Samwise under the water. The acting was so-so... Frodo, Gandalf, and Saruman did extremely well, whereas I believe Boromir could have looked a bit more haunted. Bilbo could have been improved.

The story was kept to better than most adaptations which I have seen, and the additions of the back story at the beginning of the tale was necessary.

Also, they did a good job of setting up the Ents for book two with Saruman burning trees.

Overall, I would rate the movie about a B+ or A-.

However, when I left the movie, I heard someone behind me remark (I doubt he had ever read the books) "That was crap." referring to the ending... Now of course, we could not expect the producers of the movie to make the ending better, but, this lead me to think that perhaps they should release one movie every 6 months, just so that people will remember what happened in the last movie and the movies won't have to be summed up. Also, it would allow people to feel 'fullfilled' sooner. For, the person making the remark seemed unfulfilled. (I also noticed at least 2 people walk out of the movie and not return)

However, some, such as my friend who had never read the books, rate it higher than the Harry Potter movie, and have pledged to read the books due to how interesting the movie was.

I look forward to the sequel and a possible prequel (the Hobbit) ;)

-DarkCloud

title: Amazing.
review: I thought the era of magic and miracles on film was long over.  FOTR is the Lawrence of Arabia of the 21st century. There are so many fantastic things about this production it's hard to know where to begin.  Chiefly, I have to say that the script and the acting (not the effects, although they really were excellent) was what made the movie. Sir Ian McKellan and Ian Holm both deliver chilling, inspiring performances. I never thought I'd say this, but I may actually have to start taking Christopher Lee seriously!

title: An amazing epic with fantastic visuals.
review:
Peter Jacksons adaption of JRR Tolkien's classic book (which I've read once and liked a lot - although I wouldn't read it again) is an amazing movie. Jackson made all the right choices adapting this baby, for example cutting out that lumberjack fellow who would only have slowed down the already leisurly moving picture. The Kiwi director showed an amazing visual imagination that matches Tolkiens descripitive style. He also added a very unique lighting, some lights seem to come out of nowhere but the images they create are all timeless - and worthy of the fantasy genre. Jackson mixed this stylized approach with down-to-earth imagery (dirty fingernails, lots of mud) to create a fantastic collection of images that can only be described as astonishing. One just always has to remember that this is Jacksons imagination of Tolkien - it might not be our own. I for one had a slightly different idea of Wheathertop but hey, that's of no importance, is it?

I look at what's on screen and am just amazed. The movie, as a film and as an adaption, was everything I wanted it to be: Epic, dark, violent, long. Some people I've talked to said it lacked a hero. Well this isn't "Star Wars" (this isn't a rant - "The Empire Strikes Back" is my favorite movie of all time), this is fantasy, this is Tolkien, this is the story of a hobbit who doesn't want to be a hero. That's the emotional core of the movie - and it works, especailly because Elijah Wood is surrounded by such great actors as Ian McKellen, Christopher Lee and newcomer Orlando Bloom who made quite an impression on me. I've never seen anyone charge an arrow that quickly. Amazing.

Final words? Great entry into a great trilogy. The "Moira"-scenes are something of the best I've ever seen on screen. Those complaining that it's too long suffer from attention deficit disorder: These three hours are worth every second, just look at the screen and enjoy this new world. It's my tie-in for best movie of the year (with "Amélie") and I salute you, Peter Jackson.

Rating: 10/10

title: waiting for it to arrive at a _really_ big screen
review:
It is a very good film adaptation. I've only read the last dozen or so comments, so I don't know if anyone else has mentioned this yet. Tolkien wrote LOTR and intended it to be sold as a single novel. His publishers did not think it would sell otherwise, and therefore had him divide up into three. The reason why the film ends without resolution is because the book ends without resolution. It is an installment.

There is no way to "fix" Fellowship to have a "real" ending because the arc of the story was never written to include sub-conclusions: climaxes to individual events, yes; concluded storylines, no. ALL of the major events culminate in the last book. Tucked in amongst this is the sense of a history immeasurablly more vast than what we know. This history actually exists in Tolkien's writing, and is easily researched if you enjoy reading a scholar's attempt at writing history backwards (skillful, and often brilliant, but so realistic as to be realistically tedious).

We are constantly exposed to the edges and the ends of other people's stories. Whether under Moria or in the woods of Lorien, we are encouraged to recognize the massive scope of history and that history is an interweaving of separate stories into a perceived whole. In this story, the One Ring is the unifier. It brings the disparate storylines together and breaks them apart again.

In epic, history, and real life, massive issues have wide ranging influence. This war of good against ultimate evil is world-shaking, and there is no way that 9 companions riding around the deserts of Mordor can be the only ones affected or responding to Sauron's threat. The companions join and disperse and rejoin and redisperse in new configurations. It is all a very conscious, even stylized, mimicking of an organic process.

With respect to the film, this interweaving of past, present, and future is preserved, if often condensed and truncated by necessity. It really is a very long novel, with diversions which often lead nowhere in particular. I think those who find the characterizations in the novel to be weak are mistaking their simplicity and idealization for lack. Read the Song Roland, or better yet, Beowulf, for the kind of history he drew from.

My problems with the film are primarily about shades of meaning, minor points of characterization. The only one which matters is the scene at the Prancing Pony when Frodo accidently dons the ring. In the book, Frodo is tempted by the ring and succumbs through vanity and pride. The difference is small, but significant, as Frodo should not seem to be always strong against the ring, but rather always struggling. A minor point, when compared to the otherwise very faithful film. Yes, there are issues about class and race in the film as in the novel. Tolkien was emulating an Anglo-Saxon environment (Eomer, Theoden King, etc), as well writing from a British monarchist context as a highly educated academic.

Nonetheless, I loved it. Yes, I would have liked to see more of Frodo's adventurous and Sam's poetic spirits, but too much was already crammed into 3 hours, and there is no way to 'touch' upon everything. Now, if it would just get to that really big screen at that really big theater with the fantastic sound system (if you are in Manhattan, you'll know the one I mean), instead of the 4X6 postage stamp I saw it on at my local multiplex!

title: Of course the book is better! BUT THIS MOVIE IS GREAT!
review:
First, I just have to say one thing, to all of you who gave this movie a vote score of "1". Of course the book is better! Book and movie are two completely different ways of telling a story. And the book will always be the best. But..... This movie is so very well directed. It has all the important aspects of the book, and what we see in the movie, is an absolute minimum that HAD to be in it. If Peter Jackson should have pictured more of the book, the movie would have been much longer. In fact, they had to cut 1 hour from the directors cut, so it wouldn't be to long for a cinema version. (The extra hour will hopefully be in the DVD release). And considering, it will even be two more films, for a total of 9 hours with exceptional and incredibly well directed movies, it deserves all credit for being true to the book. Of course, some of you will say, well.....the movie may be good, but they should never made it. Well, I can't help you, but I've read the book plenty of times, and I love good books and movies. And this movie, is definitely one of my favorites. The fantasy genre was desperate for a good movie, and now we have one! I'm glad I can enjoy this movie, not thinking of the obvious, like "The book is better". Of course it is :)

I'm sure J.R.R Tolkien would love it to :) He would even helped creating it! He's such a great man!

title: Amazing
review: Well first up, this movie deserves a 10 from me. However, I'll try to be critical without being unreasonable.. The movie captures the story of Tolkien's mind with overpowering realism. For the most part it matches exactly with my imagination, which is a real work of art if you can pull that off, and not because of my imagination :). Anyway, the cast is great, the scenery is great, the cgi is great, the monstrous the story is great, the action is amazing and the karma is positive throughout. If you like D&D, this is the sort of thing you'd want to see everyday, but you don't because it would give you an instant overdose of goodness, if there is such a thing. The one critique I want to mention, is that aside from the little errors (eastereggs?) in the movie that are allready mentioned everywhere, the movie does not give you enough time to live with the characters.. there is little room for empathy. But that is at this point the only flaw I can find for a movie that is a transition from a masterpiece by Tolkien himself. If you don't know exactly how it's gonna turn out, such a movie would be a director's suicide, yet, the fact that it is here and that is so good is proof that this director knew what he was doing, and what he wanted. He knew the public was fond of Tolkien and would be extremely critical about it... I'm going to conclude with my present sentiments, which are that waiting for the next one for a whole long year will be torture, but then again, so was Frodo's voyage.

title: Absolutely brilliant!
review:
When I first read "The Fellowship of the Ring", I thought the book was unnecessarily descriptive. There were lots of chapters, such as "In the house of Tom Bombadil" or "The Old Forest" which I thought completely boring, for they could have easily been removed from the book and the story would not have been altered in any way. Now that I have watched the film, I totally enjoyed the way Peter Jackson (the director) manipulated the book in a way that would seem more entertaining to the audience, bringing suspense and thrills to anyone, even though you have read the book already, such as the scene of Gandalf and Saruman. The photography is magnificent, and the screen adaptation deserves an oscar. Do not miss this film. If you are doubting upon which movie to watch when you are at the cinema, do not hesitate, and go and see "The Fellowship of the Ring".

P.S. On a more personal note, compared to the adaptation made to the book of Harry Potter and the Philosopher´s stone, this is a hundred times much better. I would even dare to say, that The Fellowship of the Ring as a movie, can actually beat the book. I´m not exaggerating it.

title: Definitely worth seeing over and over again!
review:
I read Tolkiens book a year or 9 ago I think for the first time (in Dutch). It took me a while to complete it but in the end I was proud to have finished such a masterpiece. Three years later I bought the original English version and I have read that one at least 3 times still enjoying it to the very last word. The fact that I read the book a couple of times was a holdback for me to see the film, I was afraid I would be disappointed. Now that I've seen it, I can only say 1 thing, you definitely have to see the film!.

I enjoyed every minute of the 180 and for me the film could have been twice as long. In my opinion the film represents the book quite well especially some characters like the Nazgûl, Legolas and Gandalf and also the impression of the environment is one of beauty.

This is the first film ever where I have the desire to buy some merchandise just to be reminded of the film now and then (I bought a nice Nazgûl mug) and I am also planning to see it a second a third and maybe a fourth time!

title: A near perfect rendering of the literary imagery and story
review: A truly moving film even if you have read the trilogy before as I have, 4 times.  Great acting.  These actors looked and acted just like I have imagined them when i read the story.  The director has definitely succeeded in focusing on the important parts of the tale.  This trilogy is being done much better than the kiddie film Star Wars 1.  The Lucas trilogy is taking to long to produce and is mainstream marketed to an extent that it feels very cheap and un-ballsy. Can't wait to see The Two Towers.

title: Great movie, but it's not the book
review: I saw this movie a week after it opened, and thought that it was quite possibly the best movie I'd ever seen. I felt this way for two reasons, one, I hadn't read the book. Two, I hadn't payed much attention to the hype. When I went to see Harry Potter, I had read all the books, and followed the news of the project's development carefully. After seeing the movie, I thought it didn't keep to the book well enough, and so, even though it was an excellent movie, I was disappointed. When I saw Lord of the Rings, I enjoyed it immensely and I have since started reading the book. The movie is significantly different, but I think it captures well the feeling of the book. It also does a better job at conveying a subtle terror that the book merely hinted at. I went in to the movie without any expectations and came out thinking that it is a crime if it doesn't win Best Picture. The acting was amazing, the casting perfect, and the story well-told. So whether it follows the book exactly isn't important, watch it as a movie unto itself, not as a movie made from the book.

title: The best movie since "Gladiator". No, better!
review: I cannot say enough good things about this movie!  Even if you've never read the book, the movie captures the story line so closely you would be missing nothing.  There WERE a couple of scenes from the book that were missing, especially my personal favorite with Tom Bombadil, but I did not feel that the omissions detracted from the story line in any way.  The dialog was verbatim in many places, and the characters were right on the money!  What struck me most was the verisimilitude; you could almost believe that Middle-Earth really existed.  I highly recommend this movie to everyone, whether you're a Tolkien fan or not.  After seeing this movie, you will be.

title: One of the best books of all time becomes one of the best movies of all time
review: I sat down for this movie for 3 hours, I did not notice the time. I entered this magical world and came out in awe. One of the best movies I have seen since Star Wars. The fantasy world was depicted brilliantly,the characters were all to remember. The acting was great, the action was great and special effects were not even noticeble, because it blended into the movie perfectly. The scenery in New Zealand was beautiful. I read the books, and loved them, the movie was as close to the book as you can get. Anyone who complains about the movie not being a good adaption should never watch another movie again.

title: Not perfect certainly, but better than I expected...
review:
I first read these books in the early 70's over a weekend. I remember being unable to put them down. Soon after that I hoped they would make a movie of it, and sure enough they did but it was a ridiculous animated film. I knew this film would not be perfect but like most hard core Rings fans was happy that it made at all.

I am rather surprised at the choice of Director but the results are better than expected. Obviously considerable effort was made and it shows. Bilbo and Gandalf are played well and I really enjoyed the first half hour. Some people complained that the movie was too long, well, I could watch a nine hour movie of The Fellowship of the Ring.

Some of my complaints:

1. Musical score - Very uninspired, does not compliment scenery (which was excellent). Listen to the opening music of Shrek (the piece without vocals), and imagine that music in LOTR. 2. Action scenes - Too many angles, too much darting about, looked like a video game. 3. Dramatic tension - Not enough, we are rushed from one scene to another. Perhaps you could not fit it within 3 hours. 4. Dialogue - Good, but a little more of the poetry of the book could have been conveyed.

I look forward to The Two Towers and the Return of the King and feel that they will be better than the first film.

title: Excellent movie, a certain classic!
review: This is an excellent movie that will only get better as each of the other two movies is released in the next two years.  I've read the books several times and love this movie.  My family has never read the books but they love it, too (they now want to read the books!).  This is a movie worth seeing several times, that will never grow old and dated, and will definitely be a DVD to purchase. Now, for the long wait until next December. Still, releasing three movie sequels (especially of this caliber) in three years is pretty darn impressive!

title: Great fantasy
review:
I am not an avid fan of fantasy. Generally I couldn't give a damn about little pixie people running around fighting dragons and talking about magical crowns. Even through all this prejudice I must say that I adored LOTR, and what the director acheived. As far as I am concerned I don't think it's the best movie ever. But I understand people saying that, because the scope and grandure of it is magnificent. The scenery is amazing, the characters picked well, storyline good (it is after all, extremely close to the books plot) and the overall mood captures perfectly what the books create. I have a small hatred of sentimentality, and the music and a few scenes started to lean in that direction, but I decided to give them a break because what's a few seconds of crap for a whole three hours of good stuff? Frodo was pretty well done, I mean I never found the hobbits totally enthralling. They were there, they said a few things, but it was mainly what they did that counted. The film really made them a little bit more interesting, despite the smaller parts. I was really pleased they cut out the Bombadil part. Countless of innocent, struggling readers have arrived there, and many of the even the most valient fall. It's blimming boring. I'm sure that it has some intelligent inner meaning and helps to define the later plot, but I didn't really find it.

On much much less of an intelligent note, was there anyone else who rather fancied one or two of the characters? I say Legolas,but there are some weird people who value Frodo more. No, I say, that gormless expression will never win my heart. If you are especially deprived you might find Gimli the one for you. Hey, whatever floats your boat.

title: Oh, COME ON. It was GOOD.
review:
I simply cannot believe the sheer amount of people insolently yelling and screaming about this being 'the worst film ever'. Sure, it may not have followed the book to a T (and no, I haven't read the books) and it was somewhat flashy. But what on earth did you expect?

FoTR was a wonderful fairytale adventure, and probably the only other fantasy film to give me the same butterflies I got watching Excalibur for the first time again. It is indeed contrived, the story rather stereotypical etc.. but people must understand, this IS the original. The story from which most of modern fantasy writers draw a certain degree of inspiration from.

I know almost no-one will read this, as there are nigh on 1000 comments already. But I am actually offended that people thought this didn't deserve even a fraction of the praise it got. It was just magical.

Allan.

title: It's not that great people.
review: Ok, look at what place LOTR is on the top 250 list and tell me if it truly deserves to be there. I mean come on, this film didn't grab me all that much. Sure it has some nice action and good visuals, but frankly, the character developement SUCKED! I really didn't give a s*** when i watched Gandalf die (and yes, i've read the book). I didn't feel PROUD of Frodo Baggins like I should have when he and Sam left the Fellowship at the end. How can you call this a better fantasy film than STAR WARS??? Come on! How can you forget the evil wrath of the terrifying Darth Vader, or the slick "mr. coolguy" attitude of Han Solo? There are no characters like this in LOTR, and i don't think it deserves a 10/10 by any long shot.

title: Over Rated
review: How on earth does this film sit at #1? Or how did anyone manage to endure 3+ hours? I found this film to be FLAT, With direction no better than a Disney MOW. Well that's just me I guess.... If the Oscars give this one more than sfx, I will be surprised, to say the least....common folks, think about it....

title: I think this is just the best film I've ever seen. Period.
review: What can I say?  Wow. Many big films in recent years I have kept expectations down, and therefore was able to enjoy them for what they were (i.e. Episode I).  This one, I couldn't do it.  I had heard such great things that I had my expectations well up.  It met and blew the doors off them.  I really wasn't too sure about some of the computer effects that I had heard about, but they were all (or almost all) seamless.  The acting was incredible (Ian McKellen and Christopher Lee, obviously, but the others were also very good), as was the casting.  In fact, it may sound like gushing, but I can't think of a facet of the movie that I wasn't impressed with.  Can't wait to see Part 2 and 3. I just hope one of them, at least, bypasses Titanic for total sales.  It certainly deserves it.  The level of devotion to their trade obvious in all involved surpasses any I've seen before.

title: Excellent movie!! It sparked my interest in the books!
review:
I have now seen this movie three times. I rarely go to the theater to see any movie, and I've never gone more than once for any single movie, so the fact that I've seen this one three times in three weeks should tell you a lot. I had never been interested in the stories before, but I have already begun reading the first book (I refuse to read the other two until I have seen the movies; I don't want to ruin any surprises). I thought the cast was excellent. I was really impressed with Elijah Wood and Sean Astin, but the entire cast did a great job of making the characters real and believable. The scenery was absolutely breathtaking. My 9 and 8 year old daughters have gone with me each time, and actually sat spellbound through the entirety of every showing, a miracle for them! I know that some people are disappointed at the many things that had to be cut out, but the movie is already three hours long (although it certainly didn't seem like it, not even the third time). I think Peter Jackson did an excellent job making what must have been some very difficult decisions on what to cut and what to leave in or alter.

I have to admit, I've become a little obsessed. I bought the soundtrack the next day and have listened to nothing else since. My kids are already asking when we will go see it again. I told them maybe next week. : )

title: Words Fail Me
review:
This is not a review, but just a comment...

I've just seen the film and i'm speechless. I must admit i've been eagerly anticipating the films release and have read the book - once! I don't consider myself one of the biggest fans, they read it constantly. I won't write a review, not only because there are already thousands online already but simply because I can't. I can't find the words that will do justice to this unbelievably good film.

This film must be a reviewers nightmare.

Simly put - There has NEVER been a film like this!

title: Excellent film inspired by, but not truthful to, the book.
review:
The Lord of the Rings is my favourite book, and I have longed for a great while to see it put into a worthy film. Despite the fact that many major changes were made to the story, this film lives up to that title in spirit.

I would have liked to have seen the hobbits singing Shire songs at the Prancing Pony, to have seen Legolas get his due credit for meeting Frodo's party after their encounter at Weathertop... and to have seen Gandalf get his due credit for transforming the river into a stampede of white horses, would have preferred it if Saruman would not have been portrayed as being in league with Sauron, when really he really wanted to try to use the ring against him, and I really would have appreciated it if Gimli and his party would not have been portrayed as being ignorant of the fact that Moria was a ruin, and I would have liked it if Frodo had - as in the book - told no one of his plans to go off alone... all of which were changed, along with a lot of the characters' motives and emotions.

I would have loved to see an exact replica of the books on film, but I see how the changes help the film to be effective in new ways. While the singing at the Prancing pony emphasizes the nievete' of the Hobbits, the lack of it emphasized how intimidated they were. Arwen is to marry Aragorn... it's nice to see her character being developed on the screen. Saruman's shift to the dark side simplifies the conflicts... so that emphasis can be put on the Fellowship and the corrupting influence of the ring. The "realization" on screen that Moria has been overtaken helps to create an overwhelming sense of despair and dread, and Frodo's exchanges with his fellows - regarding his plans to leave - really deepen the characters and shows how wise, perceptive, and bonded this Fellowship is.

Middle Earth, all of its characters, locales, peoples, creatures, and cultures are right there on the screen... which alone thrilled me... but also on screen was the heaviness of the impending doom, the dark, awful reality of the ringbearer's task, the steadfastness of the simplest folk, and the love, honor, respect, strength, and wisdom of the characters involved. There is so much a purist could criticise in this film, but I prefer to praise the faithfulness of the portrayal to the spirit of the story. I gave it a 9.

title: A Fantastic Movie Experience.
review: I did not read the books and I really enjoyed the film.  I went in with no expectations, because I did not read the books and still thought the movie was very good.  The story is very good, and the action is great.  The acting is very good.  The entire film was excellent.  I would recommend it to all. Yes, there are a few portions of the film which are a little slow to develop the story.  However, it works wells with the film.  Also, I have one friend that actually hated the film and she said the film was geared for teenagers. I strongly disagree and think she may be on a cheap drug.  The film is a 10 out of 10 in my opinion.

title: A compelling blend of movie magic and true emotion
review: The Lord of the Rings, easily the most hyped movie to come out in 2001, largely came through for its audience.  The sets and locations are mammoth in scale and create an impressive backdrop for the world of the film.  The performances are honest and forthright.  Although I enjoyed this three-hour adventure for the fantastic romp that it was, placing it #1 among all movies in the imdb poll seems a little much.  What happened to simple stories, good acting, and solid camera work?

title: It's about human nature, set in a fantastic story...
review:
I have never read J.R.R. Tolkien's books, but it's obvious from watching the Lord of the Rings that the movie attempts to put everything it can from the book onto the big screen, and it works.

The Lord of the Rings is really about the nature of humanity. Tolkien breaks up human nature into four races, the Elves, who represent our most noble aspects and possibility of quiet greatness, the Dwarves, who represent our baser instincts, our drive and courage, Humans, who represent our flaws and potential, and finally the Hobbits, who represent our innocent and communal nature.

From there, Tolkien erects this fantastic world in which to set his story, which is excellently portrayed in the movie not by narrative history, but in live-action scenes with backdrops never to be seen again in the entire movie, just to retell history, or visit a certain city along the journey of the main characters.

The shere breadth of the film is incredible. Tolkien didn't write his book with the limitations of film and budget in mind, so he crafted incredibly diverse realms, and these are beautifully portrayed in the movie.

Ian McKellen brings his presence and experience to bear, and indeed all of the actors do a good job at their assigned roles. Not just adequate, but good.

The bottom line is that the movie is done well, perhaps faithfully, and certainly worth viewing or purchasing on DVD in its own right. Those afraid to see it for "spoiling the book" are making a mistake. Even if the movie isn't exactly like the book (and what movie can be?), it's the best movie I've seen since Saving Private Ryan. Better than Gladiator.

It's a fantastic tale, you'll enjoy it.

title: Steady on there folks!
review:
There seems to be a massive polemic developing between those who are familiar with the book and the neophytes that have never been exposed to JRRT's work.

To the ones who are au fait with the book and have negative comments to make I would say this, The LOTR is a massive tome and in my 5 times of reading it I have come up with different images, emotions and thoughts. Peter Jackson has done what anyone would do in his situation and that is emphasise his own perspective. I personally loved the film, probably because I identified with a lot of what was emphasised but I was disappointed with some of the omissions. However I reckon there was enough left in to hold true to the spirit of the tale without running the film into 6-7 hours. I know there are fans (and I'm probably one myself) who would flock to see this, but it's a trifle elitist to hope that Hollywood would start making films just for the hardcore, multiple-readings, got-no-girlfriend (oh woe is me) fanatics

And to those who say it's the best film ever, I can't agree. It's brilliat and will blow you away, but read the book and steep in Tolkiens imagery and landscapes and you will be REALLY blown away. For the best film ever you have to go with something you need to think about as well as surf the wave of excitement that is FOTR.

title: Good movie, but not great
review: I was a bit dissapointed about LOTR. It is a good movie, but not that great. Hopefully the next two films will be better though. Almost all I know who saw Lord of The Rings, said the same thing as me, so I am astounded that it has gone to number one here on the Internet Movie Database.

title: Let's not say that it is anything like the book, please.
review:
(Spolier)

I'm a fan of Mr Jackson. I'm a fan of LoTR. However I cannot say that I am a big fan of the movie Mr Jackson has crafted. Certainly it is an 'enjoyable' film per se, but it is nothing like the book (elements are in there, but it doesn't even attempt to follow Tolkien's original plot at all). The fight scenes are laughable - it's like watching a Lethal Weapon movie - and the continuity person should be given a good spank.

I could forgive all of these things (to repeat: It is an enjoyable film) if everyone didn't bang on about how it was a faithful adaptation of the book. It isn't. Not even close.

Summary: A good fantasy movie with superb special effects (even the Dungeons and Dragons style battle between Saruman and Gandalf, and the battle between the cave troll in Moria - which didn't happen like this at all in the book); it's generally fairly well acted (even Pippin as the Scottish hobbit); however I cannot forget the terrible way in which Cate Blanchett was asked to portray Galadriel - it's hard to imagine Gimli being smitten by the hard-nosed, malicious b*tch as portrayed in the movie! Most critically for me is the way in which the movie suffers for having assassinated the original plot (Aragon's sword being in Rivendell and not in his scabbard, Arwen not Legolas rescuing Frodo at the Ford of Bruin (spelling??) and so on and so on; I won't bang on about the continuity problems. I look forward to Part II: at least I'm geared up for a movie *based* loosely on Tolkien's masterpiece, rather than a faithful adaptation of it.

title: FANTASTIC !
review: Seen it 5 times now and still as good as ever. Tears swelled up in my eyes upon seeing Hobbiton come to life in the film. will never forget its acting and story and not to mention the soundtrack throughout. U can use as many superlatives as u want and they still do not do it justice. I would bet gl is shaking in his boots................

title: Good if you've read the books, Reasonable if you haven't.
review: Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a good fantasy story with great special effects.  However, it is also a third of a complete story, of which I do not know the conclusion. For these reasons I can see why people who have loved the books and know the complete story would love seeing the tale put onto the big screen. But, I am not familiar with the story and have sat through 2 Hrs, 58 Minutes of a reasonable fantasy film which left me feeling let down.  For this reason I would suggest that anyone that has not read the books think about if they want to sit through this, not know what happens next or how any of it concludes until the other 2 parts have been released in the distant future.

title: Visually spectacular.
review: Although the film was generally superb.  I felt that it was dissapointing in some aspects.  The book does not lend itself to film adaptation, and the climactic point is too far from the end.  The way in which the book has been trimmed alows the pace of the film to be maintained, without loss of continuity.  Some of the battles are of a truely epic feel.  On the whole, I really enjoyed the movie, and I feel sure that parts two and three will be even better.

title: Must see movie of the year
review: I have personally not read the Lord of the rings book, but after watching this movie, I have decided to go out and buy myself a copy.  This film is exactly how you expect a fantasy adventure film to be.  Great performances all round, stunning SFX, no cheesy lines.  In short a flawless, if long movie.  Go see this film now!

title: One word: Perfect...
review: I'm in love with this movie.. It's awesome! Acting, Fx, story, woah!! I love the prologue (incredible scenes battle!), the shire, but the best it's in Moria.. the balrog! gasp.. I can't believe it! The most beautiful scene for me is Boromir teaching Pippin and Merry ..
