title: NO SPOILERS-----This film is the best movie ever for the masses
review:
People who have not read the book, are in awe of this movie. I watched people around me during the movie (glances, of course I missed nothing of the movie itself), and their reactions said enough. The story is of course is magnificent. The translation to the big screen is done very well. Action scenes are much more intimidating, and the little intro explains to people a lot which would not fit into the movie dialogue itself. All the actors are great, especially the dwarf, which will make you laugh for sure. Gandalf stands out too, Sir Ian McKellen we have to thank for that. The masses who are too lazy ( or dumb ) to read the book will now have the best story ever delivered to them in easy form. Although its a long sit ( 3 hours ) the time will fly by, and at the end you will be VERY disappointed this part is over, and VERY agitated because you'll have to wait another year for part 2. My advice: GO READ THE BOOK!

Big ups to Peter Jackson for taking the necessary time to perfect this movie.

title: BEST MOVIE OF THE YEAR
review: This movie was better than any movie that came out this year.Pearl Harbor special effects do not compare to anything like this, plus Pearl Harbor was dumb.There aren't any movies that have came out this year that compare to this one.I think this one should win best picture of the year because it had good acting,good story,good effects,and was good for everyone.Not everyone will agree with me that this was the best movie of the year but thats ok i feel how i want you feel how you want about that new stupid movie Not Another Teen Movie or A Beautiful Mind.

title: Absolutely fantastic!
review:
Awe inspiring fantasy which had the cinema in a hush. Beautiful to look at. A true spectacle. Tolkien's descriptions are brought to life in glorious technicolour. I left the cinema on a high after being in a state of high anxiety for three hours at the plight of the hobbits. And I fell in love with the eyes of Elijah Wood.

Top marks to the rest of the cast too, especially Mortensen and McKellen.

title: Makes Harry Potter look anemic!
review: A roller coaster ride from start to finish.  Good thing Harry Potter came out first as word of mouth comparison to this film would have been disastrous.  The Fellowship is definitely an adult film to be enjoyed even by those who have not read the books.  My movie-going friend and I await The Two Towers and The Return of The King wishing they would both come out this year

title: One ring to rule them all, One ring to find them, One ring to bring them all and in the Darkness bind them
review:
The Lord of the Rings. I've seen The Fellowship of the Ring for the first time yesterday (I'm already planning another visit) and I can only say that this trilogy (It has been shot already) is going to be an epic the size of Star Wars.

****************** - Possible spoilers from here - ********************

The story for those who do not know it: Once long ago the rings of power were forged. Three went to the elven Lords, seven to the dwarves and nine to the human kings. They were tricked by Sauron the 'Prince of Darkness'. He forged another ring so he could rule all the other rings. He brought the world destruction and troubled times. Eventually an alliance between Elves, Humans and Dwarves was able to stop Sauron, but the ring wasn't destroyed.

Thousands of years later when Sauron began to rise again a hobbit named Bilbo Baggins came along and acquired (stole) the ring from Gollum (a creature who had the ring in his possession for hundreds of years. In this time the ring had totally corrupted the creature, who now couldn't part from his "Prrrrecious" anymore). The ring heard the call of its master and decided the time was right to be found again.

Now 60 years later Bilbo (at the age of 111. The ring had prolonged the life of the old Hobbit considerably) still living in his beloved shire plans his final farewell. He wants to leave the shire to go spend his final days with the Elves of Rivendell and finish the book about his adventures. He uses the ring to disappear from his birthday to be able to leave quietly. Gandalf persuades him to leave the ring behind.

Frodo then gets the ring in his possession, but Gandalf tells him to keep it a secret and to hide the Ring, feeling some things not right

His suspicions were triggered, when Bilbo became very angry when he asked him to leave the ring behind. Bilbo even called the ring his "precious". The corruption had started to consume Bilbo too.

Gandalf then leaves Frodo to do research on the rings of power. Time goes by and one day Gandalf returns. He now knows for sure the Ring is the one ring and it must be destroyed. If not, Sauron, will be able to destroy the world once again. Even now his Fortress of Barad Dur is rebuild and his armies are growing. His Nazgul (ring wraiths) are already out looking for the ring, being drawn to it whenever its power are used. They already know that someone named Baggins who lives in the Shire has the ring. A race against time starts.

This is just the beginning of the movie(book). The Hobbits gain the aid of the humans (Boromir and Aragorn), an Elf (Legolas) and a Dwarf (Gimli), Gandalf and two other Hobbits from the Shire (Peregrin and Meriadoc). This is the Fellowship of the Ring that has to bring the ring to Mount Doom in Mordor in the center of the realm of Sauron. Only in the fires of Mount Doom can the ring be destroyed. The second half of the movies sees the Fellowship on the road traveling through the mines of Moria, and the forests of LothLorien (both great adaptations from the book) hunted down by Orcs in the process. The two following movies will tell the rest of the journey of the Fellowship of the Ring.

My opinion: I expected a lot of this movie after reading all the other reviews, but what I hadn't expected was to see a book really come to life this way. Everything was very recognizable from the Shire to Rivendell, to the mines of Moria and the land of Loth Lorien.

It's sad to see some things from the book missing in the movie. Like the missing Tom Bombadil. They also changed a number of scenes (probably to keep the movie going and keep it interesting). For instance the intro to the movie is not entirely faithful to the story. Bilbo didn't just find the ring, he tricked it out of the hands of Gollum. Gollum was in fact a Hobbit before he became the creature he is today. But it's probably all done to make sure that the intro isn't a movie in itself. I wasn't really bothered by it, though.

The movie starts very fairy tale like but quickly turns very grim when the race starts to flee from the Nazgul. The first part of the movie is very tense because of these chasing Nazgul. The mines of Moria in the second half of the movie have also been done very well. I really love what they did with the Balrog. A great burning, flaming monster. Throughout the movie we also see the surroundings of Isengard (the home of Saruman the wise) change from a lush and green land to a barren waste land dotted with mines and growing Orc armies.

The film doesn't slow down once during the entire 3 hours of running time. You will actually jump from your seat several times throughout the movie as well. They've put a couple of nice scares in there.

I'll quit now. It's just a very good movie and I'm going to see it again. And I already know I'm going to buy the DVD too when it comes out. I'll give this movie a 10 out of 10. I usually don't give tens to movies, so...........

title: Have we been to the same film?
review: I just cannot understand some of the comments I've read here, I must have seen a different film. Most bizarre of all has to be the chap who complains bitterly about the lack of an ending to this film; where have you been?! There has been no misleading of anyone, this is the FIRST PART of a trilogy for goodness sake!! I don't want to spoil anyone's enjoyment of the next film, The Two Towers, but I don't think that will have a definite ending either (shock, horror!). This film is magnificent, one of the best I've ever seen. The fact that it doesn't always fit exactly with my imaginings or those of anyone else is irrelevant, we're all of us different and this is the interpretation of one man, Peter Jackson. I don't think it will be a million miles away from most people's interpretation anyway. 10 out of 10 for Mr Jackson, and roll on the next in the series.

title: GREAT MOVIE!
review: i loved the movie! it was AMAZING!!!!!!! the characters really brought life to the film! you really feel like your actually in the movie....its a rare feeling, getting tired after the movie because you feel like you were dodging arrows and running away from the orks!!! :) its simply amazing and you have to experience it yourself

title: Fantastic - Can't wait for "The Two Towers"
review: Having read "The Hobbit" and the entire trilogy, "Lord of the Rings", I was completely satisfied with Peter Jackson's big screen version of the first book, "The Fellowship of the Rings".  The second the credits started rolling, I was ready to walk out and dish out money for the second movie. It is a shame to have to wait an entire year for the next one.  Not owning a DVD player at the time, I have vowed to buy one in time for the release of this movie in DVD form.  I can't wait for the DVD of this movie or the second movie or the third movie.  You get my drift.  It was FANTASTIC.

title: Astonishing and beautiful, frightening and distant
review:
So what is there to say other than that this is perhaps the most awaited film of all time?

Most of you have read the books, been lost in the wonderful tales of Middle-earth, only to come back to our world to realize that maybe the difference between our worlds isn't that big.

Finally, 50 years after the books were written, we get to see a seriously taken adaption into the world of films. First of all, I was very delighted when I first heard that Peter Jackson would make the films. I'm sure, if some great hollywood director would've made them, the films would become a disaster. But what am I saying then, that the film is good? Well, yes, it is!

First we get to know the world of Middle-earth through a really nice prologue, where all you need to know is explained. Then we get thrown into the beautiful landscapes of Shire, where we meet the hobbits and good old Gandalf, to discover that the actors chosen for the roles are perfect. And as more of the characters come into play, we see that almost all actors and actresses are great.

The film has an overall dreamish feeling, and I really like that. When you read the books, you feel a lot more related to the hobbits than the rest of the different races of people. The elves are (inhumanly) beautiful and have a lot of power and grace, the humans are very noble and proud, and so on. So, in the film, we get to see everything through the eyes of the hobbits. Those are things that lay beyond their ways of living, and therefor hard to understand. This saves the film a lot. I'm sure I'd get frustrated if all those beyond-our-imagination things had just been thown at my face without a single explanation of what it really is. So by making those sequences feel a bit distant and hard to grip, you get saved from the frustrations as well as long and hard to remember explanations.

Another great thing about the film, and one of the reasons why I'm so happy that Peter Jackson made it, is that the darker sequences are sometimes really frightening and have a bit of a psychological horror-film feeling to them. This proves that Jackson has a great sense of how you make things frightening, as this isn't easy at all. For example, I wasn't really frightened when I watched "Scream". Large knives and scary masks simply doesn't frighten me anymore, after having seen lots of hollywood "scary movies". Though, when I watch David Lynch's "Lost Highway", I get really frightened, and this type of psychological horror is also used in "The Fellowship of the Ring", though in a lighter scale.

But, as in all other films, there are some problems. First of all, I'm sure I'd be a lot more happy if I hadn't read the books before I saw the film. Yes, it's a great adaption of the book, but some things just kept annoying me. Some of the characters (read: Merry and Pippin, among others) were very poorly introduced. And some of the changes in the adaption made me a little dissapointed. But, then again, if it had been completely truthful to the book, it had been a very long and boring film.

It's hard for me to give this film a fair rating before having seen the two to come. But it is one of the better films I've seen, and I know that, when all three films are out, they will have a special place in my movie collection. Applause and a huge thanks to Peter Jackson for making this film not just another hollywood mastodont, but a great film with its own life and feeling.

8 out of 10

title: Fantastic film - go see it if you've got an imagination
review: It must have been a daunting task to reproduce Tolkien's fantasy in film. So what an achievement this film is.  When it came to an end I looked at my watch and realised that 3 hours had passed in total enjoyment.  My only criticism it that I've got to wait another year to continue the story - too long!

title: The first 5 minutes were enough for me
review:
Five minutes into the film, I felt something I had never felt with any other film; I had seen enough...

I was ready to give Peter Jackson the Oscar then and there it was THAT good. Let's face it, with how many films can you, after only five minutes, say "that's enough, this film is truly something wonderful."

Jackson's capable hands have achieved a near flawless adaptation from book to film - remaining loyal to the text while bringing the legendary to life. From the epic battle scenes to the tranquil Shire to the ominous tower of Saruman. The real and surreal were blended together to create a whole new form of visual effect - ultra-reality!

This is a movie I want to see again - even though saw it only two weeks ago - it's just too long to wait for The Two Towers :-)

title: Truly mindblowing
review:
Having never read the Lord of the Rings trilogy, I wasn't quite sure what to expect with this film. I had avoided all the hype, refused to read any reviews by the so called "experts" (who often get it wrong, in my book) ... and waited until the day came to see it.

At three hours long, it is quite heavy going, but from the start to the finish, it is truly a fantastic film. From the fight scenes - which must have been a nightmare to direct, but looked so good; to the emotional stuff with regards to Gandalf, and the amazing strength of the friendship between the Hobbitts (which was excellently done - had me teary several times); to the brilliant computer graphics - often difficult to tell what was real and what isn't; the strong storyline; the superb acting - everyone involved deserves huge credit for the realism they brought to the role; the brilliant characters - so easy to identify with, and everyone will have a favourite for whatever reason; and some of the simply breathtaking scenic/landscape shots - it really is, as Ron from Harry Potter would put it, "bloody brilliant."

I really couldn't find fault with this film. It is one of the best I have seen in my lifetime; miss it at your peril ! It is one of those films that will be talked about for a long time to come.

To all those who wonder whether Harry Potter or LOTR is the best film this Winter... well, the fact is that the two films are completely different. Both have good points - but it's impossible to compare them. Just enjoy !

At the end of it, you have to remind yourself that it isn't real. It is that easy to get completely immersed in the story. It's almost a let down that it isn't real !

Admittedly - it is not for everyone. So people don't like lengthy films, no matter how good they are. Or some miss crucial bits and then are baffled by the plot. Or maybe they just don't like using their imagination a bit. Because you do need to use your imagination... some bits do defy belief - but that is all part of the magic !

Gets a very big thumbs up from me ! Go see - if you have an open-mind, and appreciate the effort that's gone into the film, you will enjoy it. Make sure that you don't drink much, and go to the toilet before hand - because you cannot miss a second ! My only complaint would be how uncomfortable the seats in the cinema were... and how long we have to wait for the next instalment !

title: Fabulous adaptation, great movie.
review: This movie was a great adaptation of the book, there were very few significant changes. As a movie is was very entertaining, giving violence for the blood-seekers, beauty and romance for the ladies, humor for the litle comedians, suspense for the "please-make-me-shake"ers. It had everything a movie needs to be great. Though the ending may have not been "satisfying", thats just because that's how the books split. It left interesting cliffhangers and if they tried to resolve it in one movie, the whole trilogy would have to be in one movie... some people don't seem to understand that it is a trilogy. "The movie didn't do anything in the end" they say, but that's because the other two movies will. Great movie!

title: Good but not Great!!!
review:
Movie is long, but keeps a somewhat good pace. Pace at times seems slow. I recall seeing Gladiator and remember what a soul that movie had, this movie lacks the intense soul of a film like gladiator.

Effects are ok but not great, standard stuff but not ILM quality. Acting was great, everyone put in a solid performance.

One major thing that was missing was a good music score, music soul was lacking throughout the movie, this alone would have brought the movie up a notch.

title: Superb acting brings the book to life
review:
A magnificent film! For once hollywood has managed to leave the story intact (well almost). This interpretation of a magical book is superb, the actors have really worked hard to bring the fantasy alive. The sensitive use of special effects really enhances the story and are not overdone. I can't wait for the next installment, if they have re-created the 'Ents' as well as they re-created the 'Balrog' then we're in for another treat.

Well done!

title: Excellent!!
review:
Being one of those cynics who feel that these sort of films are for those who have followed the saga for years. I WAS PROVED WRONG!! This film has the effects of a masterpiece and is more so with the acting talents of Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Sean Bean and many many more....

The film is therefore given credit to the work of Peter Jackson, who creates the hobbit land and all it's slender. The only problem that i had with the film was the 'fight' between the two wizards, it just seemed a little far fetched to see two old men knocking each other with huge wooden sticks!!!

Although, it holds the mystery which is needed for the sequels! CAN'T WAIT FOR 2002'S AND 2003'S FILMS OF THE TRILOGY!!!

title: Defining Film of the Fantasy Genre
review:
After seeing Peter Jackson's magnificent Fellowship of the Ring, my wife was so awestruck all she could manage for a while was "Wow". Fellowship of the Ring is amazing, not only a good film but something that will define the genre for years to come.

Jackson took the proper approach and concentrates on characters. The relationships between them drive the film more then the quest to destroy the Ring does. They never seem silly or trivial from Gandalf's role as mentor to the friendship between Sam and Frodo. My wife was most taken by the scenes between Boromir and Frodo. I've always liked Sean Bean and it was great to see him deliver in the complex role of Boromir.

Thank god New Line had faith in Peter Jackson and his choices. For a director known for small, gory horror/comedy flicks he certainly does deliver the goods. Although I can't wait for The Two Towers I'm more eagerly anticipating the day when I can load all three films into the DVD player and bask in the glory of Lord of the Rings as one complete film experience.

title: The best 7 bucks i ever spent at the theaters!
review: I think Lord of the Rings is a gem. It was really awesome, the special effects were so good, i could hardly tell the difference. I Loved the way all the characters looked.....just as i imagined them. The weaponry was so cool too. They had so many sweet swords.... i was like a kid in a candy store. The movie had a good plot too....... i was dissapointed when it ended cause i wanted there to be more of it lol. I cant wait until the sequels come out. One Ring to Rule Them ALL!

title: Loved it-- but let's get perspective on a few things
review:
Yes, I thoroughly enjoyed this movie. I feel a little sheepish because I think I'm obsessed with it right now (or maybe I'm just obsessed with Legolas). If pressed for my rating, I'd give it a 9 or even 10/10. My face hurt from smiling for 3 hours at things I'd finally seen realized on film.

But, some perspective on many things I've read in the user comments.

Do I feel this is the greatest movie (or even ONE of the greatest) movies of all time? Not necessarily, but do any of you really give a flying Balrog? If not, why are you surprised or indignant that LOTR "took over" spots from "The Godfather" or "The Shawshank Redemption"?

For heaven's sake, this is IMDB, not the American Film Institute. Taking nothing away from IMDB, which I find to be an invaluable resource for looking up movies, actors, directors, and keeping up with popular culture--I don't come to IMDB for critical mass from readers. IMDB is simply looking at user ratings from people like you and me, and frankly, I don't trust any of you (the feeling should be mutual--my gosh, for all you know, my 2nd favorite film of all time might be "It's Pat").

Bottom line is that this is a film that most viewers are enjoying, either for its faithfulness to the book, its stunning cinematography, the sense of adventure, or yes, even the cute boys. If you think this film sucked, I won't insult you..but I do feel a little bit sorry for you that you couldn't let go and enjoy it.

title: One of the best films I have ever seen!!
review: I went to see this movie with my wife, and my sons, age 14 and 19 on Christmas Eve. I thoroughly enjoyed it as escapist's entertainment. One of the best films ever!! I thought the effects were great and the story somewhat easy to follow. It should be taken as is, a great way to escape the world and visit another place and time. My boys loved it, my wife said it was okay...maybe if George Clooney was in it. I don't enjoy movies much in the theater, usually bad seating and sound...so I can't wait to view this on DVD, where I can relax with surround sound. I recently purchased the Lord of the Rings Trilogy books, so I am looking forward to getting up to speed and enjoy the upcoming sequels. I recommend it highly !!

title: Maybe not "the best", but certainly one of the best.
review:
I don't think any movie, not even the Godfather is free of critics, yet I was still surprised to see the endless list of IMDB commentators who hated this movie. After reading some of the comments, you'd think the movie was comparable to Superman IV. Granted, it might not have been the best movie ever made, but to call it "trash" or a "waste of money" is not only grossly unfair to the movie and its producers, but equally gives very little merit to IMDB's rating system.

For starters, I thoroughly enjoyed this movie. I've read the series several times throughout my life and went into the theatres two weeks after it opened hearing mixed reviews, yet still having high expectations. To say that my expectations were blown away is an understatement. Visual effects aside, the movie evoked the same emotions and the same feelings that were generated when I read the book. For this reason, even though parts of the storyline were altered or cut (necessarily), the movie was a fantastic success.

Would I call it the best movie ever? Probably not. I can't even answer the question, "What's your favorite movie of all time?" But, I can confidently say, as many already have, that it's the BEST motion picture for this genre EVER. I noticed that most of the critics of this film hate the fantasy genre, find a lack of character development, or thought the movie was unbearably long. Yes, it is long. Yes, it has a ton of characters. But let's remember that this is an adaptation of a story of epic proportions. It wouldn't do the story any justice to cut the length, and the only way characters can be developed is by prolonging the movie even more. I thought the movie was perfect the way it was, and for what it tried to do. And for that, I give it a 10.

title: Fantastic!
review: This movie had me on the edge of my seat from the beginning. Despite being 3 hrs long, time flew by. Despite not having read the book, I fully enjoyed the movie. The acting in it is terrific, especially by Elijah Wood. The effects are brilliant, and the storyline is one the most exciting I've ever seen! I definitely reccommend it to anyone!!

title: EyeOpening!!!
review: Seeing this movie opening day could not have been better.  The theater was packed and at one point the entire audience was clapping due to a scene that kept us on the edge of our seat.  The casting was amazing, the scenes, backgrounds, and effects were awesome...I could not have been more impressed. A MUST SEE!!! AND A MUST OWN!!!

title: Bye bye Harry Potter, Hello Fellowship
review: I don't know about anyone else, But movies made from a book, usually do not follow very well.  But, this movie was excellent.  Just how the characters came to life and how they were described.  The "Fellowship opf the Ring" even gave a short explanation to how the ring came to the shire, since there are alot of people who don't remember or never read "the hobbit".  I think this movie was better thqn Harry Potter and was more precise with the book.

title: Good, but not great
review: Okay, let's start by saying I'm not going to comment on how well or badly the movie followed the book. I never liked comparing films to the medium they came from, just judge them on their own merit. So with that in mind, LOTR-TFOTR is okay, not great by any stretch. It's basically a 3-hour chase and fight scene movie, with a few moments of character development thrown in here and there. And at 3-hours of running and fighting, that gets to be too long. I'm not against long movies if their stories warrant it, but this doesn't. After watching it I left thinking, "okay, just how much did I learn about these characters?" Not a lot, really. Do I care if Frodo succeeds in his quest? Am I interested in the relationship between Aragorn and Arwen? And what about the other two hobbits that were captured? And Gandalf? I'd have to say that my answer would be no. This film didn't keep me interested in the characters (except for Gandalf, maybe) enough for me to wonder what's going to happen to them. What keeps this movie moving are the characters running from one menace to another. And after what seems to be the twentieth fight scene, you almost wish they'd get killed and be over with it. I've read other reviews that mention this is the first of three books so you have to forgo any character development and get the story moving. This is completely wrong. If you don't care about the characters in the first movie, why bother to see what happens to them in the next? Are we supposed to resign ourselves to the fact that this is a trilogy and we have to see all three to fully appreciate them? No. This is a movie, and it should be judged the same as any other. There are trilogies that the first installment stands on it's own, with or without the others. Ever hear of The Godfather?. And if the answer is, well, it's true to the book and that's the way the book is, I would answer then that's the fault of the book. I know this not to be true. The book is full of character development that Peter Jackson forgo for action. And as for the special effects, I didn't think they were that great. In today's age where you can film a shot in your basement and make it look like you're on top of Mount Everest, spectacular effects are too much common-place. And honestly, some of the scenes had the obvious look of computer-generation to them. No matter how good the special effects are, your eye can still detect something's wrong. No I didn't hate the film as you might think. It was entertaining in some areas. I think the look of some of the different lands in Middle Earth had a nice feel to them. I just don't think it was that great of a movie.

title: Perhaps the best movie ever made.
review:
Peter Jackson has produced perhaps the finest movie ever made. The Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring is a beautiful, rich movie filled with wonderful performances and excellent special effects. But it is Tolkien's story and character building that make this such an excellent movie.

I am particularly impressed with Ian McKellen's performance as Gandalf. What an incredible actor! But it's difficult to single out any specific actor in this movie, as everyone turns in an incredible performance. There was no one in the movie who didn't become their character. At no point was I disappointed with anyone's portrayal.

I rated this movie a perfect 10. This movie reminded me why there are blockbusters. All other movies that I have seen in the past few years absolutely pale in comparison.

title: Introducing a new generation to Middle Earth
review: I first read "The Hobbit" and LOTR at about age 14, and have re-read them many times since then. I took my 10-year-old son to see FOTR last night and we both loved it. Yes, there were some things missing and unexplained in it, but I still plan to see it again in the theater and buy the DVD when it's available. There was no way to include EVERYTHING and remain within the time constraints. I told my son about some of the scenes that were left out and explained the sudden appearance of Bill the pony. He had a lot of questions and I was delighted to be able to help pass the story on to a new generation. Now he wants to read the books, starting with "The Hobbit", so I'm going to buy him his own set to enjoy for years to come.

title: One ring to bring us all to an incredible world...
review:
I went to the theater for "The Fellowship..." with the highest expectations I've ever had about a movie, because of the enormous quantity of adds and news about this historical event film. Three hours later, I had noticed that the movie had ended and I was almost crying. It was beyond my expectations...I felt like I was floating.

It is the perfect combination of a Hollywood Big-Budgeted production, with a small independent movie vision. And you really, I mean REALLY, can tell that it was made with a great love to the amazing work of Mr. J.R.R. Tolkien.

I'm not going to tell you any spoilers, or if it is an excellent motion picture or just good or anything. It is my duty to inform you: You SHOULD see it. Period.

title: Somewhat disappointed
review: The movie was very entertaining, but, did not follow the book well at all. The overall story line was preserved but the individual scenes failed to adhere to J.R.R.'s orignal story.  Time constraints had a large effect on that, I'm sure.  I'll watch it again when it comes to the $1 movie theater...

title: Travel, fighting, travel, fighting....why not!
review: Excellent graphics, a tad theatrical acting and way too much travelling and fighting. Wonder how the last one will turn out. "We demand blood, more blood". Nevertheless, story from the book is converted very Tolkien'ish. No doubt it's a classic, but it definitely need two good follow-ups for keeping this status. Making of and special-features will be greatly awaited on the coming DVD.

title: A 6 course Meal
review:
I sat a little too close to the screen to have been able to fully appreceate this incredible adventure. I'm just going to have to go right back out and see it again. I wouldn't want to cut anything even though it is a little long. It isn't perfect....The Dwarf didn't even get under my skin, which I'm sad about. But Frodo was wonderful as was Aragorn and Gandalf... I liked the Women too.... I don't think this story quite lends itself structuraly to what we are used to in Cinema today and given that I commend Peter Jackson for his extraordinary job. The sets were fantastic, the landscapes perfect, the creatures brilliant, the direction spectacular.

I can't wait a year for the next one... that's heartbreaking.

The only thing I'm really sorry about though, is the fact that I'm not in it.

title: Astounding job!
review: This is quite possibly the finest book-to-movie translation I have ever seen.  The acting was wonderful, and the casting even better (Legolas=perfect).  The scenery was wonderful - and with multiple scenes taken STRAIGHT from the text...  I was simply amazed at the faithfulness. I'm eagerly awaiting the rest of the series.

title: Best Fantasy movie/Book Trilogy to ever, and will ever exist. Harry who?
review:
I had begun to read Fellowship of the Ring before I saw the movie. I finished the first, 70 page chapter before I went to see the movie. I begged, and whined, and moaned, and groaned, and nearly chewed an arm and leg off to beg my mom to take me to go and see it. I had every intention to go and see it when it first came out. Here was my chance! So my mom decided to FINALLY take me with one of those expression that almost seem to look like "You better not ask me to take you to see a movie like this EVER again until you can drive!" I had no regrets what so ever. I had seen Harry Potter and the Sorcerers Stone with my grandma. My grandma loved it. I thought it was okay. I had somewhat liked the books. My grandma loved the movie obviously enough.(Harry Potter) Me and my mom get to the theater. Get our tickets, order our pop and popcorn(and candy for me) and make our way into the WRONG movie room. Well, wrong timing to be exact. I had wondered why in Gods name nobody was in it. My mom asked the Usher what the hold up was, and he laughed and told us we were an hour early. Despite me and my moms blonde moment, we rushed the the correct showing RIGHT when they started the previews. Amen for that hold up. The Spider-Man Tailer was amazing, just like the Amazing Spider-Man himself(and that good looking actor they'll have play as him) Can't wait to see that flick. So as LOTR starts up, I was instantly hooked, already knowing what the first chapter part of the movie was to be about. Within two hours of the movie, my mom leaned over to me and whispered to me this was the "BEST MOVIE" she had seen in a long, long time. When we walked out after the three hour and 10 minute movie, my Mom told me she had never seen a movie that great. I too will ULTIMATELY agree this is THE ABSOLUTE BEST MOVIE(and book that I'm reading) THAT I HAVE SEEN IN MY ENTIRE LIFE!!!!!!! So if what I dragged my mom into, and not wanting to be part of, and loving what she saw can't convince you....nothing can. This is the best movie I have seen in my lifetime.

You couldn't pick a better actor to play the Hobbit Frodo Baggins. Way to go ELIJAH! Way to go Fellowship cast!!!!

HARRY WHO?!

title: "My" best picture? (Spoilers)
review:
I have to say that FOTR gets better with multiple viewings, which is my criteria for a favorite picture. The 3 hr length did not detract at all from my enthusiam, whereas the 80 min of Blair Witch was the most torturous 80 min of my life (not really, I used fast forward a lot;). I couldn't sit through The Godfather (heresy!!;), but had no problems with Lawrence of Arabia or GWTW. And I actually enjoyed Tomb Raider (arrgh!!).

The reality of IMDB is that this is a "fun" site for movie buffs. There is no real 10 or 1 movies (some people may actually like Plan 9 from Outer Space, or hate The Godfather), nor can you rate a movie with a simple 1-10 rating system. How about a 50-100 question rating system? That may lend more credibility to the ratings, or not, but rating a movie won't be as simple or as fun anymore.

--SPOILERs---

By the way, in the book, when Galadriel is offered the ring by Frodo, her transformation in the movie was described in the book, almost to a tee, and her dialogue was taken out of the book nearly verbatim.

The time compression was an issue, but PJ only had 3 hours to shoehorn in as much of the story as he could.

Those who lament Boromir not carrying into TTT should note: he appears only for a page or so in the first chapter of TTT stuck full of arrows and dying. It made sense in the movie to conclude his role in FOTR. I did imagine him more porcupine-like with 30 arrows stuck in him in the book, but I guess the 3 or 4 tree trunks they shot into him in the movie had the same effect.

I couldn't imagine any other way the movie could have concluded. Showing Frodo and Sam walking off towards Mount Doom was I thought the best you could do, other than showing a preview of TTT immediately after the movie "...scenes from next year's episode..."

FYI, the principle filming for FOTR, TTT, and ROTK wrapped early last year at an estimated cost of $270 mil. FOTR to date has brought in over $300 mil worldwide in 2 weeks. TTT and ROTK are a done deal, believe me.

Anyway, FOTR "rocks!" Peace.

title: Phenomenal!
review:
This is without doubt one of the best films I have ever seen, and has inspired me to buy the books so I can find out what happens next!

Practically everything about the film is perfect - it's a bottom-numbing 3 hours or so, but it literally flies by. As a cinema fidgeter I was concerned that boredom and discomfort would set in, but I was gripped from the word go.

The casting and locations are amazing - the hobbits are exactly as you imagine them to be, and the difference is sizes of the characters comes across very well.

Elijah Wood stands out for his performance as the young Frodo, who finds the weight of the world on his shoulders. He uses his amazingly expressive eyes to convey his feelings, so that the audience are with him from the outset. The other hobbits are also excellent, especially the "comedy double act" of Merry and Pippin.

Nothing jars - everything is perfect. Peter Jackson really deserves recognition for his vision, and I hope he gets it.

I can't wait for the next installment this Christmas!

title: Overwhelmed by special effects, but still a great movie.
review: This is the movie event of the year. I have not seen a movie this big since Titanic. This is a real gem. I hope it will win awards not because it deserves it, but because it will make it more precious. For once, a movie with no funny sidekicks to ruin the drama of this intense story. This is the real thing, perhaps the best fantasy movie to date. Of course, i am being overly enthusiastic about this experience, and i do occasionally go overboard with excitement. But let's just say that i have tried to look for flaws in this movie and hardly saw any. It surpassed my expectations.

title: Peter Jackson has really done it!
review: I know that some people really and truly hate the fantasy genre. Others only like films that are incomprehensible - "if I can't understand it, it must be true art". But I have yet to speak to a real live human being that hasn't loved this movie. He has managed to craft something that brings a great and complex world to life with images and words and people and creatures and sounds. I have seen it twice now and I was even more impressed the second time. Did it follow every exact incident from the book? - no and nor did it need to. The Harry Potter film was cute and clever, but in trying to be exactly faithful to the written word, lost some of the wit and heart that the book possessed. Peter Jackson brought the spirit of Middle Earth to the screen, not just the characters. Thank heaven that New Line had the wisdom to choose this director and the guts to give him the resources. I watched David Lean's Lawrence of Arabia again recently, and I truly believe that Jackson's work will make the same kind of impact and be as deeply respected twenty-five years from now. For those of you who are unable to enjoy Lord of the Rings, I pity you.

title: Probably the best fantasy-epic I've ever seen on the big screen..
review:
Last Wednesday it was the night of nights. For the first time ever, I went to see the movie true fans were anticipating for a long time. And I've hardly read the book when I was like, 10 or 11, but this movie felt like a recognition of something I was forgotten for a long time.. Truly magnificent acting jobs by Elijah Wood, Sir Ian McKellen, Hugo Weaving (very underrated, he needs so much more screen time!!) and of course Christopher Lee. Lee is so much of an on screen presence, he truly steals the show as the evil Saruman. Legolas Greenleaf (portrayed here by the magnificent Orlando Bloom) has way too little screen time as the noble and heroic Elf. He remains focused (and kool!) in the most stressed moments of the movie.

The ending kept me yearning for more, and right after I saw the movie, I wanted to go home and read more in the book of the Fellowship of the Ring. Can't wait for the Two Towers!!! Thank you Peter Jackson for such an terrific job, I can't tell in more words how great this movie is, unforgettable...

title: A Great Fantasy Film
review:
I am not going to repeat all the standard praise for this very impressive fantasy film but I would like to point out that all this discussion about which the greatest movie of all time is all a little redundant. It is impossible to compare a fantasy movie like Lord of the Rings to a crime drama like the Godfather. I have enjoyed both movies - but they are very different. One movie is a piece of mystical escapist (though intense) fun the other is an insight into the twisted workings of a maffia family and the real nature of power. They are such different films that evoke very different experiences for the viewer why do people even try to compare them? It is more possible to compare like with like (whether by genre or theme) - i.e the Godfather with Donnie Brasco or Lord of the Rings with Hawk the Slayer (giggle).

The whole business of stating whether a movie is any good is as a very subjective affair. For instance there will be ten year old girls out there who think the Dirty Dancing is the greatest movie of all time. In my opinion the Shawshank Redemption is nowhere near as good a movie as its movie database score suggests - and the older you get the sillier that film becomes. Plenty of people will disagree with me - and that is reflected in the movies high standing. Doubtless the Lord of the Rings score will decline a little but I doubt the film will plummet out of the top 100 - it is a genuinely decent film and not a turkey like Titanic or the Phantom Menace.

I think one of the main reasons that this film is so successful is that it has clearly been made with integrity. This hasn't been primarily developed as just a dumb downed money spinner (i.e. Pearl harbour) but is a true labour of love. Peter Jackson really seems to understand his source material and at times even adds to it - look at his treatment of the ring as almost a character in its own right and as a source of corruption. It's his obvious respect for the book that has won over most of the legion of Tolkien fans plus prevented the movie becoming yet another purile sword and sorcery flick.

One other thing - I do think that this is easily the greatest fantasy film made. It is far more involving then the now rather bland and dated Star Wars films. In fact the films true fantasy competition comes from the movie Excalibur - which, in style, Lord of the Rings most resembles. In my mind there is no question that Lord of the Rings has surpassed this old fantasy bench mark and the wait for the Two Towers will seem endless.

title: Best movie I've ever seen, and I've seen a lot of movies
review: I came with three friends to see this movie, and all four of us left agreeing it is the best movie we have ever seen. I was disturbed when a commentor below said it would become an obscure movie that will go alongside movies like Willow and The Dark Crystal. Last time I checked, those movies aren't streaking towards earning 300 million or more dollars and becoming #1 at the IMDB top 250. If over 70% of the people who have seen this movie left feeling the movie they saw was a 10 out of 10, then obviously this is a very good movie. Those who don't like it probably hate it without reason, or they have an agenda. Anti-Tolkieners. I was never a big fan of Tolkien either, but I recently read the books, and they are very good.

title: Look underneath the surface for greatness
review: 1st of all may i say that i have never rated a movie a 10 nor a 1.  I dont believe in such extremes.  Before i break the lord of the rings down i should also comment that the hype of the movie has seemingly attracted many people who have no buisness watching this movie.  And therefore, whouldn't have any buisness reviewing it.  People who crave sunday morning cartoons are more likely to rate "the cider house rules" lower than others.  the same logic applies here, and it is a two way street.  OH and one more thing, whats with all this talk about greatest movie ever......i dont understand...THERE IS NO GREATEST MOVIE EVER.  not citizen cane, not the godfather, nor lord of the rings.  Heck, somebody in mississippi probably thinks "weird science" is the greatest movie ever.  And who fights over movies, the only people that have the authority to talk smack about who's got the better movie is the people who made them.  Anyway, the lord of the rings is a strong movie, why strong...the other words, great, grand, fantastic, are played out and dont truelly chracterize a moive.  Strong on the other hand represents its ability to succeed in many differant areas. Why strong, i dont have alot of time to watch moives, nor the time to see one twice...but somehow it got me in there twice...why?...most people rate movies based on action, effects, and sometimes acting (even though most people arent qualified to judge acting)  I on the otherhand suspect other elements besdides the surface factors.  Acting is key, i felt the acting in some areas of the movie transcended hollywood acting (acting that isn't great but good enough to keep people from gagging). everyone was supurb...their use of subtext made you feel the characters more than hear their spoken words.  This alone puts it ahead most movies budgeted over 100 mill.  Another element consistantly overlooked is multidemensional characters....people are booing at the fact that some arent as well rounded as others....only because they werent introduced in some grandoise fashion. The principle characters gandalf, frodo, and Aragorn are introduced well...the others, there are too many of them.  Most of them don't have roles large enough to desearve large attention.  However with the attention that was given ,especially Boromir, it was used well.  Boromir was a speicial character for me.  I felt the inner conflict within him.  how he was torn between forces beyond his control and ultimately gave in to the ID of his personality only to snap out of it in time to die in honor.  It is the characters that the movie is about and i felt empathetic toward them. When gandalf died so did my heart.  When Boromir died i was proud that he tried to redeem himself.  Without strong characters you dont have a strong movie.  Finally, the most powerful element of the movie was once again something beneath the surface.  The themes of the movie were mature (theme: what the heck was the movie about underneath the screen, resolution, pixels)...This movie dared to express ideas concerning the human condition rather than simply give us great visuals and large sets, and all those meaningless nothings that people rate movies on nowadays.  And these themes, how man is weak, how evil turns people against themselves, how even smaller people can be the bravest, the tru pain of losing someone, the fear of the unknown.  the themes of this movie are so well expressed, real, and so deep, they pierced my soul so far as i was able to look past hobbits, dwarfs, and elf's to see humans and how we really are and i was utterly drawn to it and as i left the theater i dont know why, some of the story telling was off, plot holes ext. ext. some parts did drag a bit blah blah blah blah.....I HAD TO SEE IT AGAIN...after seeing it again I......HAVE TO SEE IT AGAIN.  Lord of the rings is not the greatest movie ever made and to its credit no movie is the greatest ever made, everyone has their own great movie.  However, this movie is a symbol of great storytelling....in that it is what is underneath that is why it is so great and with movies like these they only get stronger over time.

title: The Best Film of the Year
review: This year, despite a lot of griping, has had some very high highs.  And some very low Pearl Harbors.  Despite all, and several movies that I enjoyed a lot ("Royal Tenenbaums," "Gosford Park," "Shipping News" is very enjoyable if formulaic [and cowardly when they avoid the part of the book that talks about religion], Michael Winterbottom's "The Claim" is for consideration this year I think, "Beautiful Mind" is Ron Howard's best work maybe ever, "In the Bedroom" with Sissy Spacek just acting the hell out of it), it was clear to me after about 20 minutes, and clearer after three hours, that the best film of the year is "Fellowship of the Ring."  I concede that it feels like we're in fast forward quite often but them's the brakes.  The casting is perfect, yes even Liv Tyler, the accents are perfect, even the necessary moments of comic relief by the so-far very marginalized Pippin and Merry are perfectly handled.  The Mountain Troll made Harry's Cave Troll look like Jar Jar Binks (do they really think that looked real?), every exterior topped the ones before, New Zealand was to this film what Tunisia was to Star Wars. The idea of having Christopher Lee as the film's sub-narrator like a dungeons and dragons version of Prospero's Books should get the pic a screenwriting nom and Christopher Lee a Supporting Actor nom, if not the little trophy.  My only real criticism of Elijah Wood is that he has no pores.  Even the negligible beefing up of Arwen was only sensible, and probably something Tolkien would have done himself if his daughter had made her request for a strong female character one book earlier (speaking of which, start buying stock in the actress playing Eowyn.  She's australian I think, I saw her name somewhere, she'll probably be opposite Hugh Jackman in a romantic comedy in no time), and really, in the appendix to the Lord of the Rings, it is what he does: he toughs her up in retrospect.  Bombadil and Goldberry, the Barrow Downs, most of Lothlorien, etc. sad to see you go, and it was annoying that they gave away the Palantir right away.  They pull off the height differences quite well with old fashioned depth of field, and even though it sometimes feels like you're watching someone else play "Gauntlet," the fight sequences are visceral and effective.  The score is a bit like Orff fighting Handel to the death at times but when I'm not annoyed by an Enya song something has been packaged right. If New Line gets the guff, they should ditch the three year plan and bring out Two Towers directly opposite "Spider-Man" which, to be honest, looks like crap (are we supposed to be excited that the spider-man figure looks like it was animated from a crayon box?  same thing as with all the Lucas effects in Star Wars I and the horrendous special edition trilogies.  You know, there's a reason why people used to use puppets: it's because they exist in space). I'm showing my lack of insider savvy there, for all I know New Line paid for some of S-M.  Anyway, as they found out, if they'd opened on as many screens as Harry Porter and the Wizard's Rock they may very well have beaten it, as they well deserved to.  If they don't want to do that I think that reopening it in theatres in the summer will get it another huge run at the box office at least (yes it will be nice on DVD but really if ever there was a film to see again and again in a theatre), maybe format it for IMAX.  Without droning too much more I will say that for me it is Jackson's (and I think that all the credit goes to Jackson, this is his film all the way) seamless integration of effects into the story, of everything into the story, that gives it the drive to keep you watching, but what makes it Best Picture material is the moment where Sam (Sean Astin) very undramatically reflects on how he is about to be further from home than he has ever been before.  Things like that, being able to encapsulate such an emotional kick in one quick moment.  And look for the director himself giving a Hitch-style cameo as a drunken face on the road to the "Prancing Pony" in Bree.  Fellowship of the Ring, the best picture of the year.  And only now will I admit that I'm going to see "Ali" tomorrow, and that "Black Hawk Down" doesn't even show here for two weeks.

title: Majestic
review:
There are so many comments circulating about this film, I'll just make one simple one:

There were several scenes in this movie that were EXACTLY as I had imagined them in my mind when reading Tolkien, years ago.

I have never come across a movie that has felt like a projection of my mind onto the screen in certain scenes like this.

Certainly there have been movies where I have thought, "That's a great interpretation of what I imagined..."

But in Lord of the Rings, some scenes were just perfect. It was really scary in that respect, actually!

title: Great film
review:
Lord of the ring: The Fellowship of the ring is truly a great film which will please both reader and non-reader of the book.

As a reader and a fan of the books, I really commend the director for this wonderful job. It is not exact the same word by word of the book. However, it has done a miracle thing. It has kept the spirit and the message of the book! It also be able to pass this wonderful spirit of the book to the movie. Unlike Harry Potter, which I am also a big fan of the book, that has tried to keep everything/every scene from the book but fail a bit short on keeping the feeling of the book.

All the actors have done a great job. Elijah Wood as Frodo is even better than Frodo in my imagination.

This movie has both Drama and action.

Three hour is not long enough and I want to see more.

title: Never thought a movie would beat the original Star Wars trilogy!
review: I am very impressed by this movie; it is not very easy to impress me.  I have worked at Blockbuster Video store for many years, I received  five free movie rentals a week through those years.  In seeing so many movies I have become perhaps too critical of whatever movies I now see.  And I am very impressed with The Fellowship of the Ring.  I have never been able to single out my "favorite movie" before; I have always had to give a list.  That has changed; I enjoy watching this epic and I look forward to the rest.  Also, I am happy to find out that some movies can still move me on an emotional level.

title: best interpretation of LOTR, maybe not best movie EVER
review:
Just a side note before I start my review and monolouge of disbelief for all those who hate this movie; no, I am not a rapid Tolkien fan, and yes, I registered on this site just to type this commentary. I thouroghly enjoyed seeing this movie three times, and while I do think it drags in a few places, my fear that this movie would dissapoint was certainly unfounded. I was happy with Jackson's interpretation of some of my favorite prose, but there were many details that did not meet with the vision I had of Middle earth. Certainly, the film was dark. There were many times when I cringed because I felt that Jackson's Fellowship had mangled the somewhat merrier and more joyful world of Tolkien. As I've said, several minute details, specifically the strangely stoic potrayal of elves, and the overly cruel depiction of the world outside of the Shire (mainly Bree) did not match with what was in my mind (just to name a few). However, the attempt to satisfy so many people and such a widly diverse audience, and still pay an almost anal attention to detail is heroic. I was unsatified with several aspects of the film, but then again... so is everyone who saw it! Everyone has their own interpretaion of Middle Earth, or lack of one, and it would be an infinitely difficult task to make a version of LOTR that would satisfy everyone. Jackson would have had to make a differant movie for every single person on earth to make EVERYONE happy. In making even one version for everyone, Jackson has outdone what many modern directors are too incompetant to do. So, I say, everyone should stop whining about it and appreciate it for what it is. For those of you who thought it was horrible, I'd say that I don't understand that viewpoint at all. As for faults with the story, all a person had to do was listen and look. It was all cleanly laid out at the beginning with the brief background story. All one had to do after that was to observe the story as it continued. It's very simple. As for those who think it is a worthless piece of trash, I wonder who they work for. No, seriously. Only politicians or members of a cult are capable of such mindless hatred. To write such bad reviews, they would have to be trained to do so, and be sent out by some sort of demon on earth. Some reviews on this site were obviously written by this cult. Ignore them. Those people would rather see movies of the sort that are made solely by profit-driven studios posessing no inspiration or vision, but an idea of how to please a mob with mindless cliches and make quick profits. This is mainly because members of this cult can't tell the difference between mediocrity and a quality film. Finally, I'd like to say that I am happy seeing Tolkien in live action, and not in the form of some mindless cartoon. It's not my Middle Earth, but it's a noble attempt. It's not the best movie either, but, then again, the best version of LOTR has been available for almost 50 years. Go and read it.

I'd give it an 8.5/10.

Jackson's Lord of The Rings may not be the best movie of all time, but The Empire Strikes Back is

title: Enslaving
review:
I have heard people ranting on about the flaws in this movie. One such statment that made me chuckle to myself about the ignorence of the person comenting, was about the scenery. I cannot remeber their exact words, but they were some where along the lines of: "The scenery wasnt real enough".

Thats funny, it is real!

This movie, in my mind, is far greater than any movie i have ever seen in my so far short life. The music captured the tension of certain scenes as well as innocence, danger, victory and impending doom of a 'Balrog'. The music was more than just an aid for the movie, it was part of it. As the camera swept over the (real) landscape as it follwed the company, the music threw you in there too.

The genius of Peter Jackson is inspiring to say the least. Throughout the 3 hours of brillance, i was captivated, that my mind was literaly enslaved and i felt i was there. I felt i was an orc charging through the mines of moria after the fellowship, i felt i was part of the fellow ship, walking beside Gandalf, toiling up the snowy mountain.

I have also heard people saying other things of critisim towards The Fellowship of the Ring, like it is too long and doesnt have an ending. First of all, the book is over 1000 pages long. If it was all made into one movie, it would be longer than it already is. If it was to be shorter, ther would have to be more movies, more anti endings and more dissapointed people.

For around three hours, I was held to the edge of my seat and my eyes fixed to the action on screen. I felt i was no longer in a movie, but actualy in Middle Earth, and that is a powerful feeling. I recomend it very strongly, and all those who say it isnt worth it, i dare you to try and do better.

title: Stunning, truely stunning
review:
Amazing cinematic experience. Truly what the cinema is meant to be about: fantastic visuals, amazing and believable acting and characters, and a engrossing story.

A must see.

title: Best three hours I EVER SPENT!
review: I've been waiting YEARS for a great fantasy film with elves, swords, and the like. It's about time someone did it RIGHT! Excellent film. They even managed to do it without a cute furry animal(s) to sell MILLIONS in the retail market. HURRAY! Anyone who has not read the books (like me) can enjoy it EVEN more by not picking at "missing" segments and comparing it to the full story. I think three hours is long enough, thank you very much, and it was sliced PERFECTLY. Don't be surprised if this is one of the great film accomplishments of out time, simply extending the success of the book.

title: Simply Brilliant
review:
Absolutely amazing. I'm almost lost for words. I find it very hard to imagine how this film can be topped - ever.

I've been a Tolkien fan ever since I read The Hobbit when I was 8. I then read the Lord of the Rings when I was 10, and have re-read the books pretty much every year since. So I was understandably concerned about how the film would stand up to my own imagination.

They couldn't film the whole book. The film would have been about 15 hours long if they did. But overall the feel of the books was maintained in fine style.

There were a few things I thought they should have left in? I think Sam looking in the mirror should have been there, and it was a shame to leave out the Barrow Wights. But I liked the way they managed to modify the Shire to Rivendell section to speed it up, but without losing too much of the feel of the books. If they'd done that part in it's entirety it would probably have been 3 hours long in itself.

I thought Galadriel was very good. I always felt she was quite a dangerous and powerful character, especially if you've read up on some of the history in the Silmarillion. The BBC radio production and the animated version didn't seem to touch on that at all which was disappointing, but I think Peter Jackson got it just right.

The Gandalf/Saruman confrontation was good. I think they had to beef up the threat of Saruman a bit, otherwise there wouldn't have been any significant bad guys to keep the masses (non-Tolkien readers) interested. Christopher Lee was excellent I thought.

Liv Tyler (Arwen) was better than I thought she was going to be, and it worked quite well with her replacing Glorfindel, as in the books he's hardly mentioned again apart from at the council.

I thought the humorous touches were very good as well. And Sean Astin was really good as Sam, it'll be interesting how he develops the character in the next two where he's more in the limelight.

Shame the next one's a year away. :(

title: An Excellent all round film
review:
As a film in its own right it is nothing short of a Master Piece. Peter Jacksons name will go down in Film history along with Spielburg, Lucus and Scorsese.

The main problem I am finding with the trilogy is that I have to wait a whole year to watch the second film.

I am glad that I am not a parent with each film coming out just before Christmas.

title: Three hours of bliss.
review:
There are lots of words to describe this film but if I were limited to one word to sum it up, that word would be WOW!

I spent most of my time watching this with my mouth open.

There were a couple of scenes in this movie where I was touched, and a couple of scenes in which I was chilled to the marrow. Not bad for an old cynic, who thought that I'd seen it all.

I'm going to see it again as soon as I can.

title: Didn't like it - sorry
review:
I side with the nay-sayers on this one. The film is tedious to watch (another reviewer has noted the action-talk-action-talk pattern the screenplay follows), the swirling visuals (especially in the fight scenes) are sick-making and confusing, and considering the literary basis for the film the script is decidedly illiterate.

A great disappointment, especially as I took my son promising him a magical cinema experience. He simply didn't know what was going on. I'm afraid the next two will have to recover their costs without our help.

title: That's it
review:
This is really an amazing movie. I read the books before and I am very pleased about the quality achieved here.

Especially the sections up to the council meeting and the passage through the gates of Moria are excellent. I also want to express here is the appearance of Liv Tyler as Arwen. She really does great, I am impressed.

10/10 without doubt.

PS : To those with negative comments : you dont say things like like "oh, this is a "carry the ring from point A to B", "how did aragorn defeat all those orcs" for a FANTASY movie... got it ??

title: Absolutely Breath-taking
review: Ok, before I go any further, I have not read the original books by Tolkien, but I know enough of the story to know what was going on. This movie, however, truly draws you in. There were points in some of the fight scenes where I stopped breathing and the panoramic shots increased my desire to visit New Zealand twelve-fold. The effects were awesome without overpowering the story, and the small details, particularly with the grace of the elf, Legolas, were well done. Definately worth seeing!

title: Greatest of all time?
review:
Given that, for the moment, this film ranks at the top of IMDb's Movie list, there has been a bit of debate in the reviews about whether "The Fellowship of the Ring" is the best film ever. (It probably won't stay that high; I would bet it eventually settles in at No. 3 or 4). Most people would say no, because most people have chosen a favorite already and are hesitant to stray from that conviction. "Shawshank Redemption" is a common, and wholly deserved, choice for many. While I also hesitate to say this is the best film ever, I can say this: I am hard pressed to think of a better one. There are several films which stand on the same level ("Shawshank," "The Empire Strikes Back," etc.) but none that I can think of which are clear and away better than "Rings." It is unquestionably the best work in the (admittedly small) genre, but this is insufficient praise when you consider that it competes with "Dungeons & Dragons", "Mortal Kombat," and "Krull" for that honor.

So praise goes to the individuals that made this film the triumph that it is. First, to Ian McKellen for covering the entire range of Gandalf, from the playful hobbit-friend to the imposing and powerful wizard. To Elijah Wood, for his best turn yet as Frodo. All four of the hobbits, indeed, captured the comfort-loving and adventure-wary attitude of Tolkien's hobbits perfectly. To Viggo Mortensen, who literally lived in his armor to capture the essence of Aragorn. To Christopher Lee, a long-overdue helping of praise for his portrayal of Saruman (his recitation of the power of Sauron's eye is just chilling). To John Rhys-Davies, not nearly as underdeveloped as Gimli as some would say. He just fit to character, never letting us forget the temperament of a dwarf. Having read The Two Towers I assure that his role will expand. To Orlando Bloom, a natural elf if I ever saw one. (Someone pointed out that in Caradhras he tiptoes across the top of the snow while the others slog through it - I have to go back and watch it again just to see that!) To Howard Shore, whose soundtrack gets better with each listening - it's the best one this year and should take home the Oscar and the Globe. (I was all suited up to hand that award to John Williams for "Harry Potter," because it had one jingle - you know the one if you've seen it - that was memorable. Shore's score has at least seven such themes.) To WETA, the special effects house, I can't say enough. The effects are the best in any film. This can be realized at the same time you realize that John Rhys-Davies and Elijah Wood are both close to 6' tall. Many of the seamless conversations and events of the film were acted in front of a blue screen, with characters interacting with wooden posts and the like. All is flawless on screen.

And most of all praise goes to Peter Jackson, an admitted fan of the trilogy. He had the vision to reshape Tolkien's story just enough to make it a masterpiece of cinema - the removal of Tom Bombadil was ideal, he being the character in "Fellowship" least connected to the rest of the story, who comes and goes and leaves the characters more or less unchanged, and the barrow-wights, which was so forgettable a portion of the book that I scarcely remember it. Also he had the temperance to leave the most important aspects of the story unchanged, such as the encounter with the Balrog (listen to Ian McKellen say that word in the movie. Classic!) and the Lady of the Wood.

The film is littered with the details of Tolkien's Middle Earth, and makes perfect sense to one outside the fandom - I had not read the novels until after I had seen the movie twice. I don't think it's crystal clear to some people that this is the first of three; a few people in my theater who were in shock when it ended with so little resolved, but that's a minor grievance and hopefully that information will spread faster than the film. Of course, that's a pretty tall order with a film like this.
